title: Bill Due-Date Tracker
description: Help families see every upcoming bill and its due date so they stop paying late fees.
requirements: Accept commands: add, update, delete, list, mark-in-progress, mark-done
Store tasks in a JSON file with id, description, status, createdAt, updatedAt
List all tasks or filter by status (todo, in-progress, done)
Handle a missing file and invalid commands gracefully
stretch: Add due dates and a priority flag
overview: Help families see every upcoming bill and its due date so they stop paying late fees.
tasks: Store tasks in tasks.json in the current folder. Each task has id (number), description, status, createdAt, and updatedAt (ISO date strings). Create the file with an empty array if it does not exist.
task-cli add "text" creates a task with status todo, the next free id, and prints: Task added successfully (ID: n).
task-cli update id "text" changes the description and updatedAt. task-cli delete id removes the task.
task-cli mark-in-progress id and task-cli mark-done id set the status to in-progress or done.
task-cli list prints every task. task-cli list todo, list in-progress, and list done print only tasks with that status, one per line as [id] description (status).
Unknown commands, a missing id, or an id that does not exist print a short error message and exit with code 1 instead of crashing.

examples.title: Command session
examples.code:
task-cli add "Buy groceries"
task-cli add "Write report"
task-cli mark-done 1
task-cli list
task-cli list todo
task-cli delete 9
examples.output:
Task added successfully (ID: 1)
Task added successfully (ID: 2)
[1] Buy groceries (done)
[2] Write report (todo)
[2] Write report (todo)
Error: task 9 not found

notes: Use only the standard library of your language (for example process.argv in Node or sys.argv in Python).
Never keep tasks only in memory: read the file at the start of each command and write it back after changes.

title: Webhook Aggregator for Payment Providers
description: Combine payment provider webhooks with retries and idempotency so merchants never miss a payment update.

overview: Combine payment provider webhooks with retries and idempotency so merchants never miss a payment update.
tasks: verify_signature(secret, body, signature) computes HMAC-SHA256 and compares with hmac.compare_digest.
POST /webhooks/<provider> rejects bad signatures with 401 and otherwise enqueues the event and returns 202.
process_event(event) skips events whose id is already stored (idempotency) and returns 'processed' or 'duplicate'.
Retry failed jobs up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s).
poll_orders() fetches a third API every 60 seconds and merges records by order id into one table.

examples.title: Sample checks
examples.code:
import hmac, hashlib
sig = hmac.new(b"k", b"{}", hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
print(verify_signature("k", b"{}", sig))
print(verify_signature("k", b"{}", "bad"))
seen = set()
print(process_event({"id": "e1"}, seen))
print(process_event({"id": "e1"}, seen))
examples.output:
True
False
processed
duplicate

notes: Always verify the signature on the raw request body, not re-serialised JSON.
Respond fast (202) and do the work in a worker.

contrast(fg, bg) should return (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) with L1 the lighter, rounded to 2 places.
level(ratio, large=False) should return 'AAA' at 7 or more, 'AA' at 4.5 or more (3 for large text), otherwise 'Fail'.
Check five colour pairs from a sample page and list which fail.
Replace each failing colour with the nearest passing one and recheck.

examples.title: Ratios
examples.code:
print(contrast('#000000', '#ffffff'))
print(contrast('#777777', '#ffffff'))
print(level(4.48))

notes: Normal text needs 4.5:1 for AA; large text needs 3:1.
Gray #777777 on white is a classic fail, #767676 passes.

title: Move Files Between Finance Offices
description: Use ssh, scp and rsync to move records safely between a finance office's machines.
requirements: Copy files with scp and rsync
overview: Use ssh, scp and rsync to move records safely between a finance office's machines.
tasks: Log in with ssh user@host (use a VM, a cloud server, or localhost with sshd running) and run whoami and pwd.
Run one remote command without opening a shell: ssh user@host 'uname -s'.
Copy a local file up with scp notes.txt user@host:/tmp/ and a remote file down with scp user@host:/tmp/notes.txt ./copy.txt.
Sync a folder with rsync -avz ./site/ user@host:/tmp/site/ and run it twice to see that the second run transfers nothing.
Write the commands you used in ssh-cheatsheet.txt with one line of explanation each.

examples.title: Remote command
examples.code:
ssh user@host 'echo hello from $(hostname -s)'
rsync -avz ./site/ user@host:/tmp/site/
examples.output:
hello from myserver
sending incremental file list
./
index.html

sent 412 bytes  received 38 bytes  300.00 bytes/sec
total size is 120  speedup is 0.27

notes: Host name, byte counts, and speeds will vary on your machine.
A trailing slash on the rsync source copies the contents, not the folder itself.

title: SSH Keys for a Payments Engineer
description: Create a key pair so a payments engineer logs in to servers securely without a shared password.
requirements: Install the public key on a server
overview: Create a key pair so a payments engineer logs in to servers securely without a shared password.
tasks: Generate a key with ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C 'you@example.com' -f $HOME/.ssh/lab_key.
Check that lab_key (private) has mode 600 and lab_key.pub (public) exists; show them with ls -l.
Install the public key with ssh-copy-id -i $HOME/.ssh/lab_key.pub user@host.
Log in with ssh -i $HOME/.ssh/lab_key user@host and confirm no password prompt appears.
Add a Host block to $HOME/.ssh/config so that ssh lab works as a shortcut.

examples.title: Config shortcut
examples.code: ssh lab 'echo logged in as $(whoami)'
examples.output: logged in as user

notes: Never share or commit the private key, only the .pub file.
ssh refuses a private key whose permissions are too open.

title: Two Bank Sites on One Server
description: Host two community bank sites on one server using Nginx server blocks.
requirements: Create two sites with server blocks
overview: Host two community bank sites on one server using Nginx server blocks.
tasks: Create /var/www/site-a/index.html containing 'Site A' and /var/www/site-b/index.html containing 'Site B'.
Create /etc/nginx/conf.d/site-a.conf with a server block: listen 8081; root /var/www/site-a;.
Create /etc/nginx/conf.d/site-b.conf the same way on port 8082 with root /var/www/site-b;.
Validate with sudo nginx -t and apply with sudo systemctl reload nginx.
Test each site with curl and show both answers.

examples.title: Test both sites
examples.code:
curl -s http://localhost:8081
curl -s http://localhost:8082
examples.output:
Site A
Site B

notes: For domain-based hosting use server_name a.local; and add hosts file entries.
Always run nginx -t before reload so a typo cannot take the server down.

title: Custom Error Pages for a Payments Site
description: Add friendly 404 pages and redirects so customers who mistype a payments address are helped.
overview: Add friendly 404 pages and redirects so customers who mistype a payments address are helped.
tasks: Create /var/www/site/404.html containing 'Page not found'.
In the server block add error_page 404 /404.html; and location = /404.html { internal; }.
Add location = /old { return 301 /new; } and create /var/www/site/new/index.html.
Run sudo nginx -t and reload.
Verify with curl -i that /missing returns 404 with your page and /old returns 301 with a Location header.

examples.title: Check codes
examples.code:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost/missing
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n' http://localhost/old
examples.output:
404
301 http://localhost/new

notes: Use 301 for permanent moves and 302 for temporary ones.
Keep a copy of the working config before editing.

title: Compression and Rate Limits for a Payments API
description: Tune Nginx with compression and request limits so a payments API stays fast and fair.
requirements: Set caching headers for static assets
overview: Tune Nginx with compression and request limits so a payments API stays fast and fair.
tasks: In nginx.conf (http block) add gzip on; gzip_types text/css application/javascript application/json; gzip_min_length 256;.
Serve assets from /static/ and add location /static/ { expires 30d; add_header Cache-Control 'public'; }.
Add limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=perip:10m rate=5r/s; in http and limit_req zone=perip burst=10 nodelay; in your location.
Verify gzip with curl -sI -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' and the cache header on /static/style.css.
Trigger the limit by sending 30 fast requests and count the 503 responses.

examples.title: Check headers
examples.code: curl -sI -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' http://localhost/static/style.css
examples.output:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/css
Content-Encoding: gzip
Cache-Control: public
Expires: (30 days ahead)

notes: Other headers such as Date and Server will also appear and vary.
Do not gzip already compressed files like jpg.

title: Look Up Records for a Bank Domain
description: Read A, CNAME, MX and TXT records for a real bank domain to confirm it is set up correctly.
requirements: Look up A, CNAME, MX, and TXT records with dig
Trace a lookup from the root
overview: Read A, CNAME, MX and TXT records for a real bank domain to confirm it is set up correctly.
tasks: Run dig example.com A +short and record the IP.
Run dig www.github.com CNAME +short and dig gmail.com MX +short, and dig google.com TXT +short.
Run nslookup example.com and compare its answer with dig.
Run dig +trace example.com and list the servers it visits in order (root, TLD, authoritative).
Write dns-notes.txt explaining what each record type is for.

examples.title: Mail records
examples.code: dig gmail.com MX +short
examples.output:
5 gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com.
10 alt1.gmail-smtp-in.l.google.com.
(more alt servers follow)

notes: Real results change over time, so your values may differ.
The number before an MX host is its priority; lower is tried first.

title: Point a Payments Domain at a Server
description: Create an A record that points a payments domain at a small merchant's server.
requirements: Create an A record for your server
Load the site by domain name
overview: Create an A record that points a payments domain at a small merchant's server.
tasks: Get your server's public IP (curl -s https://ifconfig.me) and a domain at any DNS provider.
Create an A record: name app, value your IP, TTL 300.
Check it with dig app.yourdomain.com A +short until it returns your IP.
Make Nginx or a simple python3 -m http.server answer on port 80.
Load http://app.yourdomain.com with curl and show the response.

examples.title: Verify record
examples.code:
dig app.yourdomain.com A +short
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://app.yourdomain.com

notes: The IP shown is a documentation example; yours will differ.
Propagation can take minutes, depending on TTL.

title: Resource Monitor for Payment Servers
description: Warn staff when payment servers run low on disk or memory, before customers see failed payments.
requirements: Report CPU, memory, and disk usage
overview: Warn staff when payment servers run low on disk or memory, before customers see failed payments.
tasks: Create check.sh with a THRESHOLD variable defaulting to 80.
Read memory use from free -m (used divided by total) and disk use from df -P / (the Use% column).
Read CPU load from /proc/loadavg or uptime and compare to the number of cores from nproc.
Print one line per resource like MEM 42% OK, or WARN when above the threshold.
Add a cron entry */5 * * * * /home/user/check.sh >> /var/log/check.log.

examples.title: Run it
examples.code: ./check.sh
examples.output:
CPU 12% OK
MEM 42% OK
DISK 91% WARN

notes: Values will vary; the format must match.
Exit with status 1 if any resource warns, so cron and tools can detect it.

title: Find Payment Errors in Live Logs
description: Find errors in live payment logs with grep, tail and awk so failed payments are fixed quickly.
requirements: Use tail to watch a log live
overview: Find errors in live payment logs with grep, tail and awk so failed payments are fixed quickly.
tasks: Create access.log with at least 10 lines in the format 'IP METHOD PATH STATUS', for example '10.0.0.1 GET /home 200'.
Watch new lines live with tail -f access.log while appending lines from another terminal.
Find all server errors with grep ' 500$' access.log and count with grep -c.
Count requests per status with awk '{c[$4]++} END {for (s in c) print s, c[s]}' access.log.
Show the top 3 IPs by sorting and uniq -c.

examples.title: Count statuses
examples.code:
printf '1.1.1.1 GET /a 200
1.1.1.2 GET /b 500
1.1.1.1 GET /c 200
' > access.log
awk '{c[$4]++} END {for (s in c) print s, c[s]}' access.log
grep -c ' 500$' access.log

notes: awk may print the status groups in any order.
tail -f stops with Ctrl-C.

title: Health Endpoint for a Savings App
description: Add a health endpoint to a savings app and monitor it from outside so outages are noticed fast.
requirements: Check dependencies such as the database
overview: Add a health endpoint to a savings app and monitor it from outside so outages are noticed fast.
tasks: Add GET /health to your app returning JSON {"status": "ok", "db": "ok"} with HTTP 200.
Run a trivial query such as SELECT 1 against the database; if it fails return HTTP 503 and {"status": "fail", "db": "down"}.
Write monitor.sh that calls curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' on the endpoint every 30 seconds.
Print a timestamped UP or DOWN line, only when the state changes.
Stop the database and show monitor.sh reporting DOWN.

examples.title: Healthy and failing
examples.code: curl -s -w ' %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:3000/health
examples.output: {"status":"ok","db":"ok"} 200

notes: When the database is down the same call shows status fail and 503.
Keep the endpoint fast and free of authentication.

title: Manage Payment Services With systemctl
description: Check and control payment services with systemctl so customers' payments keep flowing.
requirements: Start, stop, enable, and disable one
overview: Check and control payment services with systemctl so customers' payments keep flowing.
tasks: List running services with systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running.
Pick one service and run sudo systemctl stop, then start, then restart.
Check boot behaviour with systemctl is-enabled, then run enable and disable.
Read systemctl status and explain the Active line and the last log lines.
Write the commands and what each does in services.txt.

examples.title: Check state
examples.code:
sudo systemctl stop cron
systemctl is-active cron
sudo systemctl start cron
systemctl is-active cron
examples.output:
inactive
active

notes: On some systems the cron service is named crond.
enable only changes boot behaviour; start changes the current state.

title: Run a Settlement Script on Boot
description: Make a settlement script run when the server boots so merchants are paid after a restart.
requirements: Create a unit that runs it at boot
overview: Make a settlement script run when the server boots so merchants are paid after a restart.
tasks: Write /usr/local/bin/hello.sh that appends 'booted at ' plus date to /tmp/hello.log, and make it executable.
Create /etc/systemd/system/hello.service with [Unit] Description, [Service] Type=oneshot and ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/hello.sh, and [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target.
Run sudo systemctl daemon-reload, then sudo systemctl enable --now hello.service.
Check with systemctl status hello.service.
Reboot and show the new line in /tmp/hello.log.

examples.title: After reboot
examples.code: cat /tmp/hello.log
examples.output: booted at Sat Nov  7 09:15:02 UTC 2026

notes: The date text will vary; each boot adds a line.
Add RemainAfterExit=yes if you want the service to show as active after the script ends.

title: Containers for a Payments Team
description: Pull and run images and expose ports so a payments team tests changes before customers see them.
overview: Pull and run images and expose ports so a payments team tests changes before customers see them.
tasks: Run docker run --rm alpine echo hello and see the output.
Run docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 nginx and open http://localhost:8080 with curl.
List running containers with docker ps and all with docker ps -a.
Stop it with docker stop web and delete it with docker rm web.
List local images with docker images and remove one with docker rmi.

examples.title: Run and test
examples.code:
docker run -d --name web -p 8080:80 nginx
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8080
docker stop web && docker rm web
examples.output:
(container id)
200
web

notes: The first line is a long container id; it varies.
-p host:container maps a host port to a port inside the container.

title: Volumes for Ledger Data
description: Keep ledger data safe with volumes so a container restart never loses transaction records.
requirements: Mount a volume and keep data after removal
Use a bind mount for development
overview: Keep ledger data safe with volumes so a container restart never loses transaction records.
tasks: Create docker volume create data and run docker run --rm -v data:/data alpine sh -c 'echo saved > /data/f.txt'.
Start a new container with the same volume and cat /data/f.txt to prove the data survived.
Run docker run --rm -e GREETING=hi alpine sh -c 'echo $GREETING'.
Bind-mount your current folder: docker run --rm -v $PWD:/app alpine ls /app.
Explain in a note when to use a volume and when a bind mount.

examples.title: Data survives
examples.code:
docker run --rm -v data:/data alpine sh -c 'echo saved > /data/f.txt'
docker run --rm -v data:/data alpine cat /data/f.txt
examples.output: saved

notes: Removing the container does not remove the named volume.
Use docker volume rm data to clean up.

title: Multi-Stage Build for a Payments Image
description: Shrink a payments service image so it deploys faster and uses less cloud cost.
requirements: Build a large image and note its size
overview: Shrink a payments service image so it deploys faster and uses less cloud cost.
tasks: Create main.go with a hello world program and a single-stage Dockerfile FROM golang:1.22 that builds and runs it; build it as app:big.
Record the size with docker images app:big.
Rewrite the Dockerfile: FROM golang:1.22 AS build with CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /app, then FROM alpine and COPY --from=build /app /app.
Build it as app:small and run it to confirm the same output.
Write the two sizes and the percentage saved in sizes.txt.

examples.title: Compare sizes
examples.code: docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.Size}}' app
examples.output:
app:small 12MB
app:big 850MB

notes: Sizes shown are examples and will differ.
Only the final stage ends up in the image.

title: S3 Bucket for Customer Statements
description: Store customer statements in an S3 bucket with simple permissions so only the right person sees them.
requirements: Create a bucket and upload files
overview: Store customer statements in an S3 bucket with simple permissions so only the right person sees them.
tasks: Create a bucket with aws s3 mb s3://YOURNAME-lab-2026 (names must be globally unique).
Upload with aws s3 cp hello.txt s3://YOURNAME-lab-2026/ and list with aws s3 ls.
Confirm Block Public Access is on with aws s3api get-public-access-block.
Create a link with aws s3 presign s3://YOURNAME-lab-2026/hello.txt --expires-in 300.
Open the link with curl before and after it expires and note the difference.

examples.title: Presign and fetch
examples.code:
aws s3 ls s3://YOURNAME-lab-2026/
curl -s "$(aws s3 presign s3://YOURNAME-lab-2026/hello.txt --expires-in 300)"
examples.output:
2026-11-07 09:00:00         12 hello.txt
hello world

notes: Date and size will vary.
After expiry curl returns an AccessDenied XML error.

title: IAM Policies for a Payments Service
description: Give a payments service only the permissions it needs, and test that limit.
requirements: Create a user with a policy limited to one bucket
overview: Give a payments service only the permissions it needs, and test that limit.
tasks: Create the user with aws iam create-user --user-name lab-user.
Write policy.json allowing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::YOURNAME-lab-2026 and s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::YOURNAME-lab-2026/*.
Attach it with aws iam put-user-policy --user-name lab-user --policy-name one-bucket --policy-document file://policy.json.
Create an access key and test with that profile: listing the bucket works, listing another bucket fails.
Enable MFA for the user and note the steps.

examples.title: Allowed and denied
examples.code:
aws s3 ls s3://YOURNAME-lab-2026 --profile lab
aws s3 ls s3://some-other-bucket --profile lab
examples.output:
2026-11-07 09:00:00         12 hello.txt
An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the ListObjectsV2 operation: Access Denied

notes: Never use the root account for daily work.
Delete test keys when you finish.

title: Managed Database for a Payments App
description: Launch a managed database for a payments app and restrict network access to protect customer data.
overview: Launch a managed database for a payments app and restrict network access to protect customer data.
tasks: Create a db.t3.micro PostgreSQL instance with aws rds create-db-instance (or the console) and a strong master password.
Create a security group that allows port 5432 only from your app's security group or IP, and attach it.
Set PubliclyAccessible to false if your app runs inside the VPC.
Connect with psql -h ENDPOINT -U postgres -d postgres and run SELECT version();.
Write a small script that connects and inserts one row, then try from a disallowed IP to show it times out.

examples.title: Connect
examples.code: psql -h mydb.abc123.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com -U postgres -c 'SELECT 1 AS ok;'

notes: The endpoint is a placeholder.
Delete the instance when done to avoid charges.

title: Summariser for Financial News
description: Summarise financial news with a language model so readers quickly understand changes that affect their money.
requirements: Send an article to an LLM for a summary
overview: Summarise financial news with a language model so readers quickly understand changes that affect their money.
tasks: summarize(text, sentences=3, tone='neutral') should build a prompt asking for exactly that many sentences in that tone and return the model's reply text.
build_prompt(text, sentences, tone) should be a separate pure function so you can test it without calling the API.
Read the API key from an environment variable and exit with a clear message if it is missing.
If the text is longer than 8000 characters, split it into chunks, summarise each, then summarise the joined summaries.
Accept a file path and --sentences and --tone flags with argparse.

examples.title: Prompt builder
examples.code: print(build_prompt('Cats sleep a lot.', 1, 'playful'))
examples.output:
Summarize the text below in exactly 1 sentence(s). Tone: playful.

Text:
Cats sleep a lot.

notes: Model replies vary between runs, so test the prompt builder, not the reply.
Never hard-code the API key.

title: Prompt Templates for Bank Support
description: Build reusable prompt templates for bank support replies and test them for accuracy.
overview: Build reusable prompt templates for bank support replies and test them for accuracy.
tasks: Write three templates in templates.json, each with named placeholders like {topic} and {audience}.
render(name, **vars) should fill a template with str.format and raise KeyError with a clear message if a variable is missing.
run_all(name, inputs) should call the model for each input dict and return a list of (inputs, output) pairs.
Save results to results.csv with columns template, inputs, output.
Test with at least 3 different inputs per template.

examples.title: Render
examples.code:
templates = {'explain': 'Explain {topic} to a {audience} in two sentences.'}
print(render('explain', topic='DNS', audience='child'))
examples.output: Explain DNS to a child in two sentences.

notes: Keep templates in data, not scattered through code.
Outputs vary; keep them for comparison across edits.

title: Invoice Field Extractor
description: Extract amounts and due dates from messy invoices so small businesses pay on time.
requirements: Ask for JSON output from messy text
overview: Extract amounts and due dates from messy invoices so small businesses pay on time.
tasks: extract(text) should prompt the model to return only JSON with name (string), email (string), and amount (number).
parse_and_validate(raw) should json.loads the reply and check required keys and types, raising ValueError with the reason.
Strip code fences before parsing, since models sometimes add them.
extract_with_retry(text, tries=3) should resend the error message to the model on failure and raise after the last try.
Test on 5 messy emails or notes and print a pass or fail count.

examples.title: Validator
examples.output:
{'name': 'Ann', 'email': 'a@x.com', 'amount': 12.5}
missing key: email

notes: Test the validator with fixed strings; model output itself will vary.
Cap retries so errors cannot loop forever.

title: Account Card Props and State
description: Build an account card list to practise props, state and events for a banking app.
requirements: Build a card component with props
overview: Build an account card list to practise props, state and events for a banking app.
tasks: ProfileCard({ name, role, avatarUrl }) should render the name, role, and image from props.
Add a Follow button; clicking toggles a followed state and changes the label between 'Follow' and 'Following'.
App should hold an array of at least 4 people and render one ProfileCard each with key set to a unique id.
Show a count in the page header such as 'Following 2 of 4', updated when buttons are clicked.
Style cards in a responsive grid.

examples.title: Behaviour check
examples.code:
1. Open the page: header reads 'Following 0 of 4'.
2. Click Follow on the first card.
examples.output: The first button reads 'Following' and the header reads 'Following 1 of 4'.

notes: Keys must be stable ids, not array indexes.
Do not change props inside a component.

title: Fetch and Show Exchange Rates
description: Fetch exchange rates and show them with loading and error states so people see current prices.
overview: Fetch exchange rates and show them with loading and error states so people see current prices.
tasks: Use https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users as the data source.
Keep state for data, loading (starts true), and error (starts null).
Fetch inside an effect on mount; check response.ok and set an error message if not.
Render 'Loading...' while loading, 'Something went wrong' on error, otherwise a list of names with key=user.id.
Test the error state by changing the URL to a bad path.

examples.title: Expected UI states
examples.code: Load the page, then break the URL.
examples.output:
Good URL: 'Loading...' then 10 names starting with Leanne Graham.
Bad URL: 'Loading...' then 'Something went wrong'.

notes: Set loading to false in both success and failure.
Cancel or ignore the response if the component unmounts.

title: Loan Application Routing and Forms
description: Build a multi-page loan application with validated forms so applicants don't lose their progress.
overview: Build a multi-page loan application with validated forms so applicants don't lose their progress.
tasks: Add routes /, /contact, and /thanks with a navigation bar, using React Router or your framework's router.
Build a contact form with name, email, and message fields.
validate(values) should return an object of errors: name required, email must match a simple pattern, message at least 10 characters.
Show errors under each field and block submit until valid.
On success navigate to /thanks and display the submitted values.

examples.title: Validator
examples.code: console.log(validate({ name: '', email: 'bad', message: 'hi' }));
examples.output: { name: 'Name is required', email: 'Enter a valid email', message: 'Message must be at least 10 characters' }

notes: Keep validate a pure function so it is easy to test.
Pass data to /thanks through router state or a shared store.

title: Protect Payment API Keys
description: Call a payments API using a key kept in environment variables so merchants' keys are not leaked.
requirements: Use a .env file excluded from git
Show a clear error if missing
overview: Call a payments API using a key kept in environment variables so merchants' keys are not leaked.
tasks: Create .env containing API_KEY=your_key_here and .env.example with API_KEY= and no secret.
Add .env to .gitignore and confirm git status does not list it.
get_key(name='API_KEY') should read os.environ (after loading .env with python-dotenv) and raise RuntimeError('Missing API_KEY. Copy .env.example to .env and set it.') if absent.
call_api() should send the key in a request header, never in logs or printed output.
Run without .env and show the clear error.

examples.title: Missing key
examples.output: Missing API_KEY. Copy .env.example to .env and set it.

notes: If a key was ever committed, treat it as leaked and rotate it.
Do not print the key, even partly.

title: Pagination and Rate Limits for Market Data
description: Fetch all pages of market data while respecting rate limits, so investors see complete information.
requirements: Fetch all pages of a result
overview: Fetch all pages of market data while respecting rate limits, so investors see complete information.
tasks: fetch_all(url) should request page after page (for example ?page=1,2,3 or the Link header's next URL) until a page returns no items.
Read the X-RateLimit-Remaining header and sleep until X-RateLimit-Reset when it reaches 0.
On HTTP 429, wait for the Retry-After seconds, or double the wait each time starting at 1 second, up to 5 retries.
Return one flat list of all items.
Test against https://api.github.com/repos/python/cpython/issues?per_page=30 for 3 pages.

examples.title: Backoff delays
examples.code: print([backoff(n) for n in range(5)])

notes: backoff(n) should return 2 ** n.
Set a maximum page count while testing so you do not hit limits.

title: Compose File for a Payments Service
description: Write a compose file that runs a payments service with the right ports and environment settings.
requirements: Write a compose file for one service
overview: Write a compose file that runs a payments service with the right ports and environment settings.

Start it with docker compose up -d.
Check state with docker compose ps and logs with docker compose logs web.
Confirm http://localhost:8080 answers and that docker compose exec web printenv GREETING prints the value.
Stop and remove with docker compose down.

examples.title: Check the service
examples.code:
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec web printenv GREETING
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8080
examples.output:
hello
200

notes: Compose also prints container creation lines first.
Indent YAML with spaces, never tabs.

title: Networks and Volumes for a Payments Stack
description: Connect payment services over a private network and persist their data safely.
requirements: Add two services on one network
overview: Connect payment services over a private network and persist their data safely.
tasks: In compose.yaml define db (image postgres:16, POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secret, volume dbdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data) and app (image alpine, command sleep 3600).
Declare the top-level volumes: dbdata:.
From app install the client or ping and reach the database by the name db (ping -c 1 db).
Create a table in db, run docker compose down, then up again, and show the table still exists.
Run docker compose down -v and show the data is gone.

examples.title: Resolve by name

Hide the menu below 600px using a media query and show it when the nav has class open.
Toggle the class and set aria-expanded true or false on the button with JavaScript.
Make Tab reach every link, and close the menu on Escape.
Test at 1200px wide and 375px wide.

examples.title: Toggle
examples.output: At 375px the links are hidden; clicking the button shows them and aria-expanded becomes true; clicking again hides them and it becomes false.

notes: Use a real button element for the toggle, not a div.
Focus outlines must stay visible.

title: Gallery of Product Cards
description: Create a gallery that opens each financial product image in a lightbox so customers compare offers.
requirements: Open a larger image in a lightbox
Close on Escape and outside click
overview: Create a gallery that opens each financial product image in a lightbox so customers compare offers.
tasks: Build a CSS grid of at least 6 images with alt text.
Make each thumbnail a button or link so it can be focused.
On click show a fixed overlay with the large image.
Close on Escape and when the overlay background is clicked, but not when the image is clicked.
Return focus to the thumbnail after closing.

examples.title: Close handlers
examples.code:
overlay.addEventListener('click', e => { if (e.target === overlay) close(); });
document.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Escape') close(); });
examples.output: Clicking a thumbnail opens the overlay; Escape and clicking the dark area close it; clicking the large image does nothing.

notes: Every image needs meaningful alt text.
Stop the page from scrolling behind the overlay while it is open.

title: Light and Dark Mode for Banking
description: Add a theme toggle that remembers each customer's choice, so banking screens are easier to read.
overview: Add a theme toggle that remembers each customer's choice, so banking screens are easier to read.
tasks: Define colour variables on :root and override them under [data-theme="dark"].
Write setTheme(name) that sets document.documentElement.dataset.theme and saves it with localStorage.setItem("theme", name).
On page load read localStorage and apply the saved theme, defaulting to light.
Add a button that calls setTheme with the opposite theme.
Reload the page and confirm the theme persists.

examples.title: Console check
examples.code:
setTheme('dark');
console.log(document.documentElement.dataset.theme, localStorage.getItem('theme'));
examples.output: dark dark

notes: Wrap localStorage in try/catch since it can be blocked.
Use variables for every colour so nothing is missed.

title: Keyboard Navigation for a Payment Site
description: Make a payment site work with only a keyboard so people with motor disabilities can pay bills.
requirements: Navigate a site using only the keyboard
overview: Make a payment site work with only a keyboard so people with motor disabilities can pay bills.
tasks: Unplug or ignore the mouse and use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space across a page.
Write a table of problems: element, symptom, such as no visible focus or unreachable.
Fix at least three: restore a focus outline, use button instead of div, correct the tab order by removing positive tabindex values.
Retest and mark each row fixed.
Take before and after screenshots of the focus style.

examples.title: Problem log
examples.code:
Element           Problem                    Fix
Menu div          not reachable by Tab       change to button
Search link       outline removed            add :focus-visible style
Modal close       tabindex=5 order wrong     remove tabindex
examples.output: After fixes, Tab moves through the page in visual order and the focused element always has a visible outline.

notes: Never use outline: none without a replacement.
Native buttons and links work with the keyboard for free.

title: Screen Reader Walkthrough of Checkout
description: Test checkout with a screen reader and list what is announced wrongly, so blind shoppers can pay.
requirements: Test a page with a screen reader
overview: Test checkout with a screen reader and list what is announced wrongly, so blind shoppers can pay.
tasks: Turn on VoiceOver (Cmd+F5 on Mac) or NVDA and navigate a page with headings, links, a form and an image.
Write down what is announced for each element.
List at least three problems such as a link announced as click here, an image with no alt, or an input with no label.
Fix with proper markup: descriptive link text, alt, label for.
Retest and record the new announcements.

examples.title: Before and after
examples.code: click here See pricing
examples.output: Before: link, click here; image unlabelled; edit text. After: link, See pricing; image, Sales by month, rising; Email, edit text.

notes: Announcement wording differs per screen reader.
Fix with native HTML first.

title: ARIA for Financial Forms
description: Use ARIA labels where HTML is not enough, so screen reader users can complete financial forms.
requirements: Add roles and labels only where needed
overview: Use ARIA labels where HTML is not enough, so screen reader users can complete financial forms.
tasks: Build the same control twice: a div with role="button" tabindex="0" and a real button element.
Show what the div version still needs: key handling for Enter and Space.
Add aria-label to an icon-only button.
Use aria-expanded and aria-controls on an accordion trigger.
Test all with a screen reader and list differences.

examples.title: Native vs ARIA
examples.code: Save
examples.output: Screen reader says: Close dialog, button; and Save, button. The div needs extra JavaScript to react to Enter and Space; the button does not.

notes: Wrong ARIA is worse than no ARIA.
aria-label replaces the visible text for assistive tech, so keep it short.

title: SSH Config for Finance Servers
description: Create shortcuts for finance servers so staff connect securely without mistakes.
requirements: Set user, port, and key per host
overview: Create shortcuts for finance servers so staff connect securely without mistakes.
tasks: Open or create $HOME/.ssh/config and set permissions to 600.
Add at least three Host entries with HostName, User, Port and IdentityFile.
Connect with ssh alias for each.
Run ssh -G alias to confirm the settings used.
Add Host * with ServerAliveInterval 60.

examples.title: Config and check
examples.code:
Host web
  HostName 203.0.113.10
  User deploy
  Port 2222
  IdentityFile $HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519

ssh -G web
examples.output: Among many lines: hostname 203.0.113.10, user deploy, port 2222, identityfile $HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519

notes: The first matching value wins, so put specific hosts before Host *.
Use your own server addresses; those shown are examples.

title: Secure SSH for Banking Servers
description: Disable password and root login on a banking test server and check the change works.
requirements: Test a new session before closing the old one
overview: Disable password and root login on a banking test server and check the change works.
tasks: Confirm key login works first with ssh user@host.
Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config: PasswordAuthentication no, PermitRootLogin no.
Run sudo sshd -t and fix any errors; it prints nothing when valid.
Restart with sudo systemctl restart ssh, keeping your current session open.
Open a second terminal to test key login works, then confirm password and root login are refused.

examples.title: Tests
examples.code:
ssh -o PubkeyAuthentication=no user@host
ssh root@host
examples.output:
user@host: Permission denied (publickey).
root@host: Permission denied (publickey).

notes: Never close the working session until the new one succeeds.
The service is named sshd on Red Hat family systems.

title: Install and Read Nginx for Payments
description: Install Nginx and read its config so a payments site stays online for customers.
requirements: Find and read the config files
overview: Install Nginx and read its config so a payments site stays online for customers.
tasks: Install with sudo apt install nginx and check systemctl status nginx.
Open /etc/nginx/nginx.conf and find the include lines for sites-enabled or conf.d.
Find the root directive of the default site.
Edit index.html in that root to say Hello from my server.
Run sudo nginx -t then sudo systemctl reload nginx.

examples.title: Check
examples.code:
sudo nginx -t
curl -s http://localhost
examples.output:
nginx: the configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf syntax is ok
nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test is successful
Hello from my server

notes: Paths differ by distribution.
Always run nginx -t before reload.

title: Gateway Logs and Status Codes
description: Find requests and errors in gateway logs and explain status codes so failed payments are understood.
overview: Find requests and errors in gateway logs and explain status codes so failed payments are understood.
tasks: Find the logs, usually /var/log/nginx/access.log and error.log.
Request an existing page, a missing page and a page that returns 500 (point a location at a broken backend).
Use tail -n 5 on the access log and match each request to its status.
Find the matching error log lines.
Write one sentence per status code.

examples.title: Requests
examples.code:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost/
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost/nope

notes: Access log shows every request; error log shows problems.
500 is a server fault, 404 a client mistake.

title: TTL and Propagation for a Bank Domain
description: Change a bank domain record and explain propagation so customers reach the right site during a change.
overview: Change a bank domain record and explain propagation so customers reach the right site during a change.
tasks: Create an A record for test.example.com with TTL 300.
Query with dig +noall +answer test.example.com and note the TTL.
Change the record to a new IP.
Query repeatedly against 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 and note when each returns the new value.
Explain why some resolvers returned the old IP for a while.

examples.title: Query
examples.code: dig +noall +answer test.example.com
examples.output: test.example.com. 300 IN A 203.0.113.10

notes: The TTL shown counts down on cached answers.
Use a domain you control; example.com cannot be edited.

title: www and Redirects for a Fintech Domain
description: Add a www record and redirect it to the main domain so customers always land on the real site.
requirements: Redirect www to the main domain
overview: Add a www record and redirect it to the main domain so customers always land on the real site.
tasks: Add a CNAME record www pointing to the apex domain, or an A record to the same IP.
Configure the web server to answer for www.example.com with a 301 redirect.
Verify DNS with dig +short www.example.com.
Check the redirect with curl.
Check that the apex still returns 200.

examples.title: Redirect check
examples.code: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n" http://www.example.com
examples.output: 301 http://example.com/

notes: Use your own domain name in place of example.com.
A CNAME cannot be set at the apex itself.

title: Netdata Charts for a Payments Server
description: Install Netdata and explain its charts so staff see when a payments server is struggling.
overview: Install Netdata and explain its charts so staff see when a payments server is struggling.
tasks: Install using the official kickstart script and open http://localhost:19999.
Find CPU, memory, disk I/O and network charts.
Write one sentence per chart explaining what it measures.
Generate CPU load with stress-ng --cpu 2 --timeout 60s and watch the CPU chart rise.
Take screenshots before and during the load.

examples.title: Check
examples.code: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://localhost:19999/

notes: Netdata listens on port 19999 by default.
Do not expose it to the internet without protection.

title: Log Rotation for Transaction Logs
description: Configure logrotate so transaction logs never fill the disk and stop payments.
requirements: Configure logrotate for an app log
overview: Configure logrotate so transaction logs never fill the disk and stop payments.
tasks: Create /etc/logrotate.d/myapp for /var/log/myapp/*.log.
Set daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, missingok, notifempty.
Dry run with sudo logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.d/myapp.
Force with sudo logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.d/myapp twice.
List the directory to check the files.

examples.title: After two forced rotations
examples.code: ls /var/log/myapp
examples.output: myapp.log  myapp.log.1  myapp.log.2.gz

notes: delaycompress leaves the newest rotated file uncompressed.
Use copytruncate if the app cannot reopen its log.

title: journalctl for Payment Services
description: Filter payment service logs by unit, time and priority to find why a payment failed.
overview: Filter payment service logs by unit, time and priority to find why a payment failed.
tasks: Show logs for one unit with journalctl -u ssh.
Limit by time with --since "1 hour ago".
Show only errors and worse with -p err.
Follow live with -f and trigger an event, such as restarting the service.
Save a command list with a comment for each.

examples.title: Commands
examples.code: journalctl -u ssh --since "1 hour ago" -p err --no-pager
examples.output: Lines in the form: Jan 10 09:00:01 host sshd[812]: message. If there are no errors, journalctl prints: -- No entries --

notes: Output varies by system.
Priorities run from emerg through debug; -p err includes err, crit, alert and emerg.

title: Restart Policies for a Payments Worker
description: Test restart policies so a payments worker recovers from crashes without dropping payments.
requirements: Try always, on-failure, and no restart
overview: Test restart policies so a payments worker recovers from crashes without dropping payments.
tasks: Create /etc/systemd/system/crash.service with ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'sleep 2; exit 1'.
Test Restart=no: start the unit and check systemctl is-active.
Change to Restart=on-failure with RestartSec=1; reload with systemctl daemon-reload and watch it restart.
Change to Restart=always and note it restarts even on clean exit 0.
Record observations in a table.

examples.title: Restart=no
examples.code:
sudo systemctl start crash
sleep 4
systemctl is-active crash
examples.output: failed

notes: With on-failure or always, systemctl show crash -p NRestarts shows a growing number.
Stop the service when done.

title: Dockerfile for a Payments Web App
description: Containerise a small payments web app so a shop can run it on any computer.
requirements: Write a Dockerfile for a small app
overview: Containerise a small payments web app so a shop can run it on any computer.
tasks: Create app.js with an HTTP server on port 3000 that replies "hello from docker" at GET /.
Create a Dockerfile: FROM node:20-alpine, WORKDIR /app, COPY package.json first, RUN npm install, then COPY the rest, EXPOSE 3000, CMD ["node", "app.js"].
Create .dockerignore listing node_modules, .git, and *.log so they are not copied into the image.
Build with docker build -t hello-app . and run with docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --name hello hello-app.
Verify the container responds and stop it with docker stop hello.

examples.title: Build and test
examples.code:
docker build -t hello-app .
docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --name hello hello-app
curl http://localhost:3000/
examples.output: hello from docker

notes: Copy package.json before the source so Docker can cache the npm install layer.
If port 3000 is taken, map another host port such as -p 8080:3000.

title: Debug a Failing Payments Container
description: Use logs and exec to find why a payments container fails, so customers can pay again quickly.
overview: Use logs and exec to find why a payments container fails, so customers can pay again quickly.
tasks: Run a container that exits at once: docker run -d --name broken alpine sh -c "echo starting; cat /missing.txt".
Use docker ps -a to see the exit code, then docker logs broken to read the error message.
Start a healthy container (docker run -d --name web nginx) and open a shell with docker exec -it web sh.
Use docker inspect web to find its IP address, image, and mounted volumes (use the --format flag for one field).
List networks with docker network ls and show which containers are attached with docker network inspect bridge.
Write a short debug.md noting the cause of the failure and the command that revealed it.

examples.title: Find the failure
examples.code:
docker run --name broken alpine sh -c "cat /missing.txt"
docker logs broken
docker inspect broken --format '{{.State.ExitCode}}'
examples.output:
cat: can't open '/missing.txt': No such file or directory
1

notes: docker logs works even after a container has exited.
Remove test containers with docker rm -f broken web when done.

title: Push a Payments Image to a Registry
description: Tag and push a payments image to a registry so the same tested version is deployed everywhere.
requirements: Push and pull it on another machine
overview: Tag and push a payments image to a registry so the same tested version is deployed everywhere.
tasks: Build a small image locally, for example docker build -t myapp:1.0 .
Tag it for your registry: docker tag myapp:1.0 YOURUSER/myapp:1.0 (or ghcr.io/YOURUSER/myapp:1.0).
Log in with docker login (use an access token, not your password).
Push with docker push YOURUSER/myapp:1.0 and confirm the tag appears in the registry web page.
On another machine (or after docker rmi), run docker pull YOURUSER/myapp:1.0 and docker run it.
Also push a latest tag and explain in a README line why pinning 1.0 is safer.

examples.title: Tag and push
examples.code:
docker tag myapp:1.0 YOURUSER/myapp:1.0
docker push YOURUSER/myapp:1.0
examples.output:
The push refers to repository [docker.io/YOURUSER/myapp]
1.0: digest: sha256:<hash> size: <bytes>

notes: Digest and size values will vary.
Never commit registry tokens to git.

title: Free-Tier VM for a Payments Demo
description: Launch a VM for a payments demo, check its cost, and shut it down so no surprise bill appears.
overview: Launch a VM for a payments demo, check its cost, and shut it down so no surprise bill appears.
tasks: Launch a t2.micro or t3.micro EC2 instance with Amazon Linux and a key pair, in one region, tagged Name=practice-vm.
Connect with ssh -i key.pem ec2-user@PUBLIC_IP and run uname -a to prove it works.
Open Billing and Cost Management and Free Tier usage; note the hours used so far.
Stop the instance and confirm the state is stopped; note that storage still costs a little.
Terminate the instance and confirm the attached volume is deleted.
Write a checklist.md with the resources you created and confirmed gone (instance, volume, elastic IP).

examples.title: CLI state check
examples.code: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=practice-vm --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].State.Name' --output text
examples.output: terminated

notes: Instances stay listed as terminated for about an hour; that is normal.
Allocate no Elastic IP unless you release it, since unattached ones are billed.

title: Billing Alerts for a Cloud Account
description: Set budget alerts so a small fintech never gets a surprise cloud bill.
overview: Set budget alerts so a small fintech never gets a surprise cloud bill.
tasks: Enable billing access for IAM users and CloudWatch billing alerts in account settings.
Create a monthly cost budget of 10 USD named monthly-guard in AWS Budgets.
Add alerts at 50 percent actual, 80 percent actual, and 100 percent forecasted spend, sent to your email.
Confirm the SNS or email subscription so alerts are actually delivered.
Test by lowering the threshold to a tiny amount (such as 0.01 USD) and checking that an email arrives; then restore it.
Record each alert and its threshold in alerts.md.

examples.title: List budgets
examples.code: aws budgets describe-budgets --account-id 123456789012 --query 'Budgets[].BudgetName' --output text
examples.output: monthly-guard

notes: Billing data can lag by hours, so test alerts may take time.
Budgets alert you; they do not stop spending by themselves.

title: CloudWatch Logs for a Payments App
description: Send payments logs to CloudWatch and search them to answer customers' payment questions.
requirements: Create a metric from a log pattern
overview: Send payments logs to CloudWatch and search them to answer customers' payment questions.
tasks: Create a log group /practice/app and a stream with aws logs create-log-group and create-log-stream.
Send at least 5 log lines (some containing ERROR) with aws logs put-log-events or the CloudWatch agent.
Search with aws logs filter-log-events --filter-pattern ERROR and confirm only error lines return.
Create a metric filter named ErrorCount on the pattern ERROR in namespace Practice.
Generate two more ERROR lines and confirm the metric shows a count in the console.

examples.title: Filter errors
examples.code: aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name /practice/app --filter-pattern ERROR --query 'events[].message' --output text
examples.output: ERROR db timeout    ERROR payment failed

notes: Message text and count depend on the lines you send; metrics can take a minute to appear.
Set retention (for example 7 days) so old logs do not accumulate cost.

title: Tokens and Limits for Financial Documents
description: Count tokens in financial documents to see when a model's context limit could cut off the answer.
requirements: Test a long input near the limit
overview: Count tokens in financial documents to see when a model's context limit could cut off the answer.
tasks: Write count_tokens(text, model) in Python using tiktoken (or the provider token-count API) that returns an integer.
Count tokens for five inputs: an English sentence, a long word, code, emoji, and non-English text; print a table of characters versus tokens.
Build an input slightly under and slightly over the model context limit and send both.
Record what the API does over the limit (error or truncation) and which part is dropped.
Summarise findings in findings.md with the characters-per-token ratio of each input.

examples.title: Token counts
examples.code:
import tiktoken
enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
for t in ["Hello world", "internationalization", "def f(x): return x"]:
    print(len(t), len(enc.encode(t)))

notes: Counts differ per tokenizer; always use the one matching your model.
Remember that the output tokens also count against the window.

title: Temperature and Prompts for Bank Support
description: Compare answers while changing temperature and system prompts so a support bot gives steady answers.
overview: Compare answers while changing temperature and system prompts so a support bot gives steady answers.
tasks: Write ask(question, system, temperature) that calls a chat API and returns the reply text.
Run one creative question at temperature 0, 0.7, and 1.5, three times each; save all outputs to results.json.
Run one factual question with three system prompts: none, "Answer in one sentence", and "You are a pirate".
Compare results in a table: how much do outputs vary per run, and how does tone or length change?
Write observations in effects.md with at least one example per knob.

examples.title: Run a comparison
examples.code:
for t in [0, 0.7, 1.5]:
    print(t, ask("Name a color.", "", t))
examples.output:
0 Blue.
0.7 Green.
1.5 Teal, like a quiet lagoon at dawn.

notes: Your outputs will vary; the point is the pattern, not these exact words.
Change only one variable at a time.

title: Streaming Answers in a Money Terminal App
description: Stream model answers token by token so people get money answers without waiting.
overview: Stream model answers token by token so people get money answers without waiting.
tasks: Write stream_chat(prompt) that calls a chat API with stream=True.
Print each text delta immediately with print(chunk, end="", flush=True).
Print a final newline and the total number of chunks received.
Catch KeyboardInterrupt, print "[stopped]", and exit with code 130 without a traceback.
Catch network errors and print a one-line message to stderr with exit code 1.

examples.title: Run it
examples.code: python stream.py "Count from 1 to 5"

notes: Text and chunk count will vary by model.
Without flush=True the output appears all at once.

title: Conditional Rendering for Account Lists
description: Show and hide account details by state so customers only see the accounts they own.
requirements: Show and hide UI from state
Render a list with stable keys
overview: Show and hide account details by state so customers only see the accounts they own.
tasks: Create a TaskList component holding tasks state as an array of {id, text}.
Add a button that toggles a details panel with a ternary or && conditional.
Render tasks with tasks.map and key={task.id} (never the array index).
Show "No tasks yet" when the array is empty.
Add a Remove button per item that filters by id.

examples.title: Check behaviour
examples.code:
1. Load with tasks = []
2. Add "Buy milk" then "Walk dog"
3. Remove "Buy milk"
examples.output:
Step 1 shows: No tasks yet
Step 2 shows two list items
Step 3 shows only: Walk dog

notes: Index keys cause wrong state when items are removed or reordered.
The same pattern works in Vue (v-if, v-for with :key) or Svelte.

title: Controlled Inputs for a Payment Form
description: Control payment form inputs with component state so amounts are checked before submission.
overview: Control payment form inputs with component state so amounts are checked before submission.
tasks: Keep email and password in useState and bind each input with value and onChange.
Write validate(email, password) returning an errors object; valid email must contain "@" and password needs 8 or more characters.
Run validate on every change and store the result.
Set disabled on the submit button when errors has any key.
On submit, call preventDefault and console.log the values.

examples.title: Validator checks
examples.code:
console.log(validate('a@b.com','12345678'));
console.log(validate('ab','123'));
examples.output:
{}
{ email: 'Invalid email', password: 'Min 8 characters' }

notes: Never mix controlled (value) and uncontrolled (defaultValue) on the same input.
validate should be a plain function so it is easy to test.

title: Theme Context for a Banking App
description: Share a theme across banking components so customers get a consistent, readable app.
overview: Share a theme across banking components so customers get a consistent, readable app.
tasks: Create ThemeContext with createContext({theme: 'light', toggle: () => {}}).
Write ThemeProvider holding theme in useState and exposing toggle that flips light and dark.
Wrap the app root in ThemeProvider.
In a deeply nested Header component, read the theme with useContext(ThemeContext) and set a class on the wrapper.
Add a ToggleButton that calls toggle and shows the current theme name.

examples.title: Manual check
examples.code:
Start page -> button label: Theme: light
Click button -> button label: Theme: dark, page class: dark
Click again -> Theme: light
examples.output:
Theme: light
Theme: dark
Theme: light

notes: Components read the theme from context, with no theme prop anywhere.
Keep the provider value small to avoid needless re-renders.

title: First Request to a Market Data API
description: Pick a public market data API, read its docs and make a first request to show live prices.
requirements: Make a request with curl and parse the response
stretch: Make the same call in code
overview: Pick a public market data API, read its docs and make a first request to show live prices.
tasks: Pick a free API with no key, such as https://api.github.com or https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com.
In notes.md, write the base URL, one endpoint, its method, and one parameter taken from the docs.
Run curl -s with that endpoint and save the response to response.json.
Check the status with curl -i and note the status line and content-type header.
Extract one field with jq, for example jq '.title'.

examples.title: First request
examples.code: curl -s https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1

notes: Never paste real API keys into notes you commit.
If the docs show curl examples, copy them first, then change one thing at a time.

title: Friendly Errors for Payment Requests
description: Show clear messages when a payment fails and retry safely, so customers know what to do.
overview: Show clear messages when a payment fails and retry safely, so customers know what to do.
tasks: Write friendlyMessage(status) returning text: 404 "Not found", 429 "Too many requests, slow down", 500 and above "Server problem, try later", other "Something went wrong".
Write fetchWithRetry(url, maxRetries = 3) that retries on network errors, 429, and 5xx only.
Wait 500 ms, 1000 ms, 2000 ms between attempts (double each time).
Do not retry other 4xx errors.
After the limit, throw an Error carrying friendlyMessage(lastStatus).

examples.title: Messages
examples.output:
Not found
Server problem, try later
Something went wrong

notes: Retrying a 400 or 404 will never succeed, so skip it.
Add a small random jitter if many clients may retry at once.

title: Cache Exchange Rates Locally
description: Cache exchange rates so a currency app works on slow connections without repeated calls.
overview: Cache exchange rates so a currency app works on slow connections without repeated calls.
tasks: Write getCached(url, ttlSeconds) that returns cached data when fresh.
Store entries as {data, savedAt} keyed by URL in cache.json or a Map.
When an entry is older than ttlSeconds, fetch again and overwrite it.
Print "cache hit" or "cache miss" for each call.
Prove the saving by calling the same URL three times and counting real network requests.

examples.title: Three calls
examples.output:
cache miss
cache hit
cache hit

notes: Key the cache by the full URL including query string.
Never cache error responses.

title: Payments Database With Admin UI
description: Run a payments database with an admin UI so support staff can look up a customer's payment.
requirements: Run Postgres and an admin UI
overview: Run a payments database with an admin UI so support staff can look up a customer's payment.
tasks: Write compose.yaml with services db (postgres:16) and adminer (adminer, port 8080).
Set POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, and POSTGRES_DB for db.
Add a named volume pgdata mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data.
Run docker compose up -d and log in to Adminer with server db.
Connect a script with psql or a driver using host localhost and port 5432 (publish it), and create a table.
Run docker compose down then up again and verify the table still exists.

examples.title: Persistence check

examples.title: Analysis
examples.code:
import math
def analyze(c, cn, v, vn):
    p1, p2 = c/cn, v/vn
    p = (c+v)/(cn+vn)
    se = math.sqrt(p*(1-p)*(1/cn+1/vn))
    return round(p2/p1-1, 2), round((p2-p1)/se, 2)
print(analyze(200, 4000, 260, 4000))
