notes: Micro-frontends solve organisational problems, not technical ones; adopting them for a team of five adds cost with no gain.
Shared mutable state between modules recreates the monolith; communicate via events or URL, and keep contracts small.
Architecture rules without CI enforcement are suggestions and will erode in months.

title: WCAG 2.2 Programme for Banking
description: Remediate banking apps to WCAG 2.2 AA so people with disabilities can manage their money.
overview: Remediate banking apps to WCAG 2.2 AA so people with disabilities can manage their money.
tasks: Commission or run an audit of 25 key user journeys against WCAG 2.2 AA, with issues triaged by severity and user impact; group the 640 findings by root cause to find the 15 component-level fixes that resolve 60 percent

Fix foundations in the component library first: semantic HTML over ARIA, visible focus indicators with 3:1 contrast and 2px minimum, target size at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, focus management in dialogs and route changes, and accessible names
Make keyboard navigation complete: logical tab order, no traps, skip links, roving tabindex in composite widgets, and working Escape and arrow keys per the ARIA Authoring Practices
Support forms and errors: programmatic labels, error identification and suggestions via aria-describedby, live region announcements, and redundant entry avoidance (WCAG 2.2 3.3.7)
Add automated gates: eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, axe-core in unit and Playwright tests failing on any serious violation, Storybook a11y addon and CI checks on every pull request

Test with assistive technology: NVDA with Firefox, JAWS with Chrome, VoiceOver on macOS and iOS, TalkBack, 200 percent zoom, 400 percent reflow and Windows High Contrast, using a written test script for each journey
Recruit and pay 6 disabled users for moderated sessions on the critical journeys and fix what they find
Train 100 engineers and designers, add an accessibility acceptance criterion to the definition of done and an annotation step in design handoff
Publish an accessibility conformance report (VPAT/ACR) and a public accessibility statement, and show metrics: open issues from 640 to under 30, zero critical, automated violations at zero on main

examples.title: axe check in Playwright
examples.output: 1 passed (2.1s)   -- a violation prints the rule id, impact, selector and a help URL

examples.title: Accessible dialog behaviour
examples.code: Delete project
examples.output: Opening with showModal() moves focus inside, traps Tab within the dialog, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the trigger on close

notes: Automated tools find roughly 30 to 40 percent of issues; the rest need keyboard, screen reader and human testing.
ARIA used wrongly is worse than none; the first rule is to use the native element.
Fix at the component, then add a test, or the same bug returns in every new feature.

title: Frontend Observability for Payments
description: Track errors and real user problems so broken checkouts are fixed before customers complain.
overview: Track errors and real user problems so broken checkouts are fixed before customers complain.
tasks: Integrate error monitoring (Sentry or equivalent) with uploaded source maps per release, release tagging by commit SHA, breadcrumbs, user-impact counts and grouping rules; verify that a thrown error shows the original source line
Capture real-user performance (LCP, INP, CLS) and custom journey timings (for example checkout completion) segmented by browser, device class, country and release
Define frontend SLOs, such as JS error-free sessions at 99.5 percent and checkout success rate at 99 percent, and alert on burn rate with a median time to detect under 5 minutes

Implement progressive delivery: feature flags (OpenFeature) and canary releases at 1, 10, 50 and 100 percent with automatic halt and rollback when the new release's error rate exceeds the baseline by a statistical threshold

Make deploys atomic and rollback-safe: immutable hashed assets kept for 30 days, versioned HTML shell with short TTL, and handling of users with stale tabs requesting removed chunks (ChunkLoadError recovery with a reload prompt)
Add synthetic monitoring with Playwright running critical journeys every 5 minutes from 3 regions, plus cross-browser CI on Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
Create a session replay with PII masking by default and an allowlist, reviewed by privacy, and controlled sampling
Keep telemetry cheap: SDK under 20 KB gzipped, sampling and rate limits, no main-thread blocking over 50 ms
Run a game day by deploying a deliberately broken release to 1 percent and measuring detection and rollback time; publish the result and a post-mortem template

examples.title: Canary gate
examples.code:
rollout:
  steps: [1, 10, 50, 100]
  soak_minutes: 15
  halt_if:
    - metric: js_error_sessions_pct
      worse_than_baseline_by: 0.3
    - metric: checkout_success_pct
      below: 98.5
examples.output: Release 4f2a91c halted at 10 percent: js_error_sessions_pct 1.4 vs baseline 0.5; traffic returned to previous release in 40 s

examples.title: Stale chunk recovery
examples.output: A user holding a tab from an old release loads the new assets once instead of seeing a blank page; the guard prevents reload loops

notes: Without source maps and release tags, a minified stack trace is almost useless.
Browser extensions and third-party scripts generate large amounts of error noise; filter by origin and track the real-user-impact count, not the raw event count.
Never ship session replay without masking inputs; one leaked password field is a security incident.

title: Markup Quality Gate for Bank Sites
description: Block invalid or unsafe HTML in a bank's site so customers see a working, secure page.
overview: Block invalid or unsafe HTML in a bank's site so customers see a working, secure page.
tasks: Inventory all templates (server-rendered and component output) and render a representative page set of at least 150 URLs to static HTML snapshots
Run the Nu HTML Checker (vnu.jar) and html-validate on every snapshot and record a baseline of errors by rule and by owning team
Write a shared html-validate config extending html-validate:recommended with custom rules: one h1 per page, landmark uniqueness, no inline event handlers, required lang and viewport meta
Add a ratchet: CI fails if the error count for any team rises above baseline, and the baseline file is lowered automatically when it drops
Add a Content-Security-Policy-compatible check that rejects inline script and style attributes in new templates
Fix the top 5 rule categories across the codebase, targeting a 90 percent reduction in total errors within 8 weeks
Publish a one-page markup standard with 10 do and don't examples and a decision record for each custom rule
Report outcomes: validation error count, share of pages passing, and change in Lighthouse SEO and accessibility scores on 20 sampled pages

examples.title: Custom rule config and CI run
examples.output:
snapshots/checkout/cart.html
  41:7  error  <h1> is the first heading but another <h1> exists  heading-level
  88:3  error  Landmark <nav> must have a unique accessible name   unique-landmark
2 errors in 1 file (baseline: 14, ratchet exceeded: no)

notes: Never demand zero errors on day one; a ratcheting baseline wins adoption because teams are never blocked by debt they did not create.
Validate rendered output, not source templates, because most real breakage comes from composed components and user content.
Every custom rule needs a written reason and an escape hatch with an expiry date, or people will disable the whole gate.

title: Statement Email Template Platform
description: Render bank statement emails identically in 20 email clients so every customer can read them.
overview: Render bank statement emails identically in 20 email clients so every customer can read them.
tasks: Build a component library (header, button, table row, footer) in MJML or a custom compiler that outputs table-based, inlined-CSS HTML with MSO conditional comments
Enforce a size budget: every email under 90 KB of HTML so Gmail never clips, checked in CI
Support dark mode with color-scheme meta, prefers-color-scheme rules and transparent-PNG-safe logos, verified in Apple Mail, Gmail and Outlook
Provide plain-text alternatives generated from the same source and assert they contain every link
Set up visual regression using Litmus or Email on Acid or Playwright with at least 12 client profiles and a pixel-diff threshold of 0.5 percent
Generate print-ready HTML for invoices with CSS paged media (@page, break-inside: avoid) and verify PDFs from Chromium and WeasyPrint match within one page count
Add accessibility rules: role=presentation on layout tables, lang attribute, alt on all images, 4.5:1 contrast
Measure results: render-defect tickets per month before and after, and open-rate lift in an A/B test of 100,000 recipients

examples.title: Outlook-safe bulletproof button
examples.code: Pay invoice
examples.output: CI report: 38 templates built, max size 71.4 KB (budget 90), 12 clients diffed, 0 over 0.5 percent threshold

notes: Outlook ignores margin, max-width and background-image on many elements; design to the worst client and enhance upward.
Inline CSS at build time, never at send time, so you can test exactly the bytes users receive.
Gmail clips at about 102 KB of HTML, and clipping hides your unsubscribe link, which is a compliance issue.

title: Migrate a Bank Site to Components
description: Migrate 2,000 bank pages to accessible components without losing search visibility, so customers find information.
overview: Migrate 2,000 bank pages to accessible components without losing search visibility, so customers find information.
tasks: Crawl the whole site and classify each page into a template family using DOM structure hashing; target fewer than 12 families
Define a target component set with semantic landmarks, one heading outline, and structured data (JSON-LD) for articles, products and breadcrumbs
Write a codemod using parse5 or cheerio that rewrites legacy fragments (font tags, layout tables, br spacing) into components, with a dry-run diff mode
Build a before and after comparison harness: extracted text, link set, heading outline and canonical URL must match for 100 percent of pages, with visual diff under 1 percent
Roll out in waves of 5, 25, 100 percent of traffic behind a feature flag with a one-click rollback
Watch Search Console for impressions, crawl errors and indexed page count daily, with a rollback trigger at a 5 percent impressions drop for 3 days
Preserve every URL and add 301 maps for any intentionally changed one; zero new 404s in access logs
Document the migration playbook and post-mortem with measured outcomes: HTML payload size reduction (target 30 percent), Lighthouse score, and incident count

examples.title: Equivalence check output
examples.code: $ node verify-migration.js --old crawl/old --new crawl/new --sample all
examples.output:
pages compared: 2013
text identical: 2009
heading outline identical: 2011
link set identical: 2013
visual diff over 1 percent: 4 (see report/visual-fails.html)
status: BLOCKED until 4 pages reviewed

notes: SEO risk is not in the markup you add but in the content, links and status codes you accidentally drop; diff those, not the pixels alone.
Codemods beat hand edits because they are reviewable, repeatable and can be re-run when late content arrives.
Migrate by template family, not by directory, so each wave tests one pattern.

title: Banking CSS Architecture and Bundle
description: Shrink a bloated banking stylesheet so customers on slow phones load their balance quickly.
overview: Shrink a bloated banking stylesheet so customers on slow phones load their balance quickly.
tasks: Measure first: use Chrome Coverage and PurgeCSS dry runs to record unused CSS percentage per route, and CSS Stats for specificity graph and !important count
Introduce cascade layers (@layer reset, tokens, base, components, utilities, overrides) and move legacy CSS into a lowest-priority legacy layer
Set a budget: critical CSS under 14 KB inlined, total CSS under 150 KB gzip per route, enforced by a bundlesize or size-limit CI check
Add Stylelint with rules banning ID selectors, selector depth over 3, and new !important, with a ratcheting baseline
Replace the 20 most duplicated patterns with components using container queries and logical properties
Eliminate layout thrash: profile with DevTools Performance and fix at least 3 forced reflow or expensive selectors, using contain and content-visibility where it helps
Run visual regression on 60 key screens before and after each batch, allowing 0 unexpected diffs
Report: CSS bytes, !important count (target down 90 percent), LCP and INP changes, and style-recalculation time on a mid-range device profile

examples.title: Layer order and budget check
examples.output:
$ npx size-limit
  dist/app.css  gzip  118.2 kB  (limit 150 kB)  PASS
  critical.css  gzip   11.6 kB  (limit 14 kB)   PASS
  !important count: 41 (baseline 612)

notes: Putting legacy CSS in a low-priority layer lets you ship new work without touching old code, which is the only way these migrations finish.
Unlayered styles beat layered ones regardless of specificity, so audit third-party CSS before adopting layers.
Deleting CSS is risky; verify with coverage across logged-in states, not just the homepage.

title: Token Pipeline for Bank Brands
description: Theme five bank brands with light, dark and dense modes so customers can read any app.
overview: Theme five bank brands with light, dark and dense modes so customers can read any app.
tasks: Define tokens in the W3C Design Tokens JSON format with three tiers: primitive, semantic (color.text.primary) and component-level
Use Style Dictionary to emit CSS custom properties per theme, plus iOS and Android outputs from the same source
Implement theming with data-theme attributes and prefers-color-scheme, with no flash on load (inline 400-byte bootstrap script)
Add automated WCAG contrast checks for every foreground and background semantic pair in every theme, failing the build below 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for UI
Support density (compact, regular) and reduced-motion variants through tokens, not forked components
Version tokens with semver and write a changelog generator that flags breaking renames; keep a deprecated alias for 2 releases
Sync with Figma Variables through the API and detect drift weekly, opening an issue for any mismatch
Onboard a new brand in under one day as the success test and record the effort; target zero component code changes

examples.title: Token source and generated output

notes: Components must only reference semantic tokens; the moment one uses a primitive, theming leaks.
Renaming a token is a breaking change for every consumer; ship aliases and a codemod.
Test dark mode contrast separately, since mirrored palettes frequently fail at mid-tones.

title: Rendering Jank on Low-End Phones
description: Fix scrolling jank in a payments app on cheap phones so people in low-income areas can pay easily.
overview: Fix scrolling jank in a payments app on cheap phones so people in low-income areas can pay easily.
tasks: Record a baseline Chrome DevTools Performance trace with 4x CPU throttling and capture frame rate, long frames over 16.7 ms, and main-thread time split into style, layout, paint and composite
Use the Layers and Rendering panels (paint flashing, layer borders, layout shift regions) to find the 5 costliest repaint areas
Replace animation of top, left, width and height with transform and opacity, and promote only justified layers with will-change, keeping layer count under 30
Apply contain: layout paint and content-visibility: auto with contain-intrinsic-size to long lists of 2,000 rows and measure the render time saved
Fix at least 2 layout shift sources and bring CLS to under 0.05 using aspect-ratio and font-display with size-adjust fallbacks
Eliminate one selector or style-recalc hotspot (for example universal descendant selectors) and show recalc time before and after
Add a Playwright performance test using the trace API that fails if long frames in a scripted scroll exceed a threshold
Write a one-page report with traces attached: p95 frame time target under 16 ms, and memory cost of layers

examples.title: Before and after summary
examples.code:
scenario: scroll 2000-row table, 6x CPU throttle, 5 runs median
before: fps 14, long frames 61, layout 38 percent, paint 29 percent
change: contain + content-visibility, animate transform only
examples.output:
after: fps 57, long frames 3, layout 9 percent, paint 11 percent
layers: 22 (budget 30)  CLS: 0.03  (values vary by device)

notes: will-change everywhere is itself a bug: each layer costs GPU memory and can make low-end devices worse.
content-visibility can break find-in-page and anchor links if intrinsic size is wrong; test both.
Always measure on a throttled mid-range profile; your laptop hides every problem.

title: Organisation-Wide Accessibility Programme
description: Move a fintech from ad hoc to systematic accessibility so disabled customers can open accounts.
overview: Move a fintech from ad hoc to systematic accessibility so disabled customers can open accounts.
tasks: Run a baseline audit of the 20 highest-traffic user journeys against WCAG 2.2 AA using manual testing with NVDA, JAWS and VoiceOver plus axe-core, and log issues with severity and WCAG criterion
Publish an accessibility policy with a conformance target, definition of done, and an exception process requiring VP sign-off
Add axe-core and Pa11y checks to CI and Storybook, plus eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, blocking new critical violations
Define a severity SLA: blockers fixed in 14 days, serious in 45, with a burn-down dashboard reviewed monthly
Create a 3-hour engineer training and a designer checklist, and train at least 80 percent of front-end and design staff within a quarter
Establish an accessibility champion in each team, with a 1-hour monthly guild and a shared defect triage
Produce an Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT 2.5) with honest partial-support statements and a remediation roadmap
Track outcomes: open issues down 70 percent in 2 quarters, automated violations per release, and results of 2 usability sessions with disabled users

examples.title: Executive metric snapshot
examples.code:
Quarter: Q3  Journeys audited: 20  Criteria tested: 50 (WCAG 2.2 A and AA)
Open blockers: 9 (was 31)  Serious: 44 (was 128)
CI-blocked regressions this quarter: 17
examples.output:
Conformance: partially supports 4.1.2, 1.4.11; supports 2.4.7, 2.5.8
Next milestone: checkout journey fully conformant by 15 Dec

notes: Automated tools find roughly 30 to 40 percent of issues; the program fails if it sells automation as conformance.
Real disabled users in testing change priorities more than any audit report does.
Procurement and legal care about documented process and progress, not a claim of perfection.

title: Accessible Data Grid and Combobox
description: Build accessible grids and dropdowns for banking forms, tested with real screen readers.
overview: Build accessible grids and dropdowns for banking forms, tested with real screen readers.
tasks: Implement the combobox with ARIA 1.2 pattern (role=combobox, aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-activedescendant) and live-region result counts announced politely
Implement a data grid with roving tabindex, arrow, Home, End, PageUp and Ctrl+Home navigation, row and column header associations, and aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex for virtualized rows
Implement a modal with focus trap, inert background via the inert attribute, focus return to the trigger, and Escape handling; support stacked dialogs
Document keyboard interaction tables for each widget, matching the APG, with deviations justified
Write a test matrix covering NVDA with Firefox and Chrome, JAWS with Chrome, VoiceOver with Safari on macOS and iOS, and TalkBack, recording the announcements heard
Automate regression with Playwright and axe, and use Guidepup to script real screen reader output assertions for core flows
Support 400 percent zoom reflow at 320 CSS px width, Windows High Contrast (forced-colors) and prefers-reduced-motion
Publish the library with a conformance statement and measure bug reports from consuming teams dropping at least 60 percent

examples.title: Screen reader assertion test
examples.output:
PASS combobox announces results (NVDA 2024 + Firefox)
last spoken: "3 results available. London, option 1 of 3" (wording varies by version)

notes: The same ARIA markup is announced differently across screen reader and browser pairs; test combinations, do not trust one.
Virtualization breaks assumptions about DOM order and counts; aria-rowcount is the fix, not rendering everything.
The best accessible widget is often a native element: use select, dialog and details before reaching for ARIA.

title: Accessibility Remediation After a Complaint
description: Fix a legacy banking product after an accessibility complaint so customers with disabilities can use it.
overview: Fix a legacy banking product after an accessibility complaint so customers with disabilities can use it.
tasks: Map the purchase path (search, product, cart, checkout, account) into 12 key templates and test each with keyboard only, NVDA and VoiceOver, plus 200 percent text resize
Triage findings into root causes; target that 20 shared components cause at least 70 percent of defects so fixing them cascades
Fix the classic blockers: unlabeled form controls, focus order, missing focus indicators (2.4.11 focus not obscured), inaccessible error messages, timeouts, and captcha alternatives
Replace inaccessible custom controls with native elements, and add skip links, landmarks and consistent help (3.2.6)
Make error handling accessible: aria-describedby linkage, error summary with focus management, and instructions before inputs
Run a weekly regression suite and keep a dated evidence log: issue id, criterion, fix commit, retest result
Commission or simulate an independent audit of the 12 templates and drive failures to zero for Level A and AA
Deliver a remediation report and a public accessibility statement with a feedback contact and a 5-business-day response commitment

examples.title: Evidence log row
examples.code:
id,template,criterion,severity,root_cause,fix_commit,retest
A-114,checkout/payment,3.3.1 Error Identification,blocker,form-field component,9f3c2ab,pass NVDA+VO 2024-05-12
A-115,checkout/payment,2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured,serious,sticky footer,c71d09e,pass keyboard
examples.output: 90-day summary: 212 issues found, 198 fixed, 14 accepted with documented workaround and date

notes: Fix root causes in shared components first; one fixed form field component can close 60 issues at once.
Keep dated evidence; good-faith, documented progress matters to regulators and courts.
Overlay widgets do not remediate; do not recommend them.

title: Memory Leak in a Trading Dashboard
description: Find and fix a memory leak in a trading dashboard so retail investors' screens stay responsive.
overview: Find and fix a memory leak in a trading dashboard so retail investors' screens stay responsive.
tasks: Create a deterministic reproduction script with Playwright that loops a user flow 200 times and records performance.memory or CDP heap usage after forced GC
Take three heap snapshots in DevTools (baseline, after 50 loops, after 100) and use the comparison view to name the top 3 retained constructors
Trace the retainer paths to root causes such as detached DOM nodes, forgotten event listeners, closures in intervals, or unbounded caches, and fix each one
Replace the unbounded cache with an LRU of fixed size and use AbortController, WeakMap or FinalizationRegistry only where justified
Record a Performance trace to find tasks over 50 ms; break up work with scheduler.yield or chunking, and move one CPU-heavy step to a Web Worker
Reduce INP p75 from 480 ms to under 200 ms and verify with the web-vitals library reporting to your RUM endpoint
Add a CI memory test failing if retained heap after 100 loops grows more than 5 MB
Write a postmortem with before and after heap graphs, root cause list and detection gap analysis

examples.title: Leak guard test
examples.output:
PASS no heap growth over 100 route changes (growth 1.8 MB, limit 5 MB)
before fix: growth 31.4 MB  (values vary)

notes: Always force a GC before measuring, or you are reading garbage noise.
Detached DOM nodes held by a single forgotten listener are the most common leak in framework apps.
Fixing one leak often reveals the next; keep looping until the snapshot diff is flat.

title: Migrate a Payments Codebase to TypeScript
description: Migrate 300,000 lines to strict TypeScript without stopping releases, so payment bugs drop.
overview: Migrate 300,000 lines to strict TypeScript without stopping releases, so payment bugs drop.
tasks: Add tsconfig with allowJs and checkJs, and generate a baseline count of type errors and any usage per package
Order packages by dependency graph and convert leaf packages first, targeting 25 percent of files per month
Write codemods with ts-morph or jscodeshift to convert CommonJS to ESM and add JSDoc or types to the 200 most-imported modules
Enforce a ratchet in CI with a per-directory strict allowlist that only grows, and ban new .js files in converted directories
Replace any with unknown at module boundaries and validate external input with a runtime schema (zod) so types match reality
Keep build time flat: use project references, incremental builds and swc or esbuild for transpile, with type-check as a separate parallel job under 4 minutes
Run weekly office hours and write a typing guide covering generics, discriminated unions, and utility types with 10 repo examples
Measure impact: production type-related incidents, bundle size unchanged within 2 percent, and share of files strict (target 100 percent)

examples.title: Ratchet report
examples.code: $ node scripts/ts-progress.js
examples.output:
files total 2,418  typescript 1,106 (45.7 percent)  strict-clean 812 (33.6 percent)
explicit any: 1,940 (was 5,310)  ts-ignore: 62 (was 410)
strict allowlist grew by 31 directories this week; ratchet OK

notes: Types at boundaries (API, storage, messages) deliver most of the safety; do those before internal helpers.
Do not allow ts-ignore without a linked ticket; use ts-expect-error so it fails when fixed.
Never block feature work; migrate files when touched, plus a scheduled sweep.

title: Payments JavaScript Library
description: Publish a payments library with a stable API so developers accept payments without breaking changes.
overview: Publish a payments library with a stable API so developers accept payments without breaking changes.
tasks: Define the API with a written design doc, 5 use cases and explicit non-goals, and review it with at least 2 external users before 1.0
Ship dual ESM and CJS builds through the package.json exports map with types, sideEffects false, and a core import under 3 KB gzip checked by size-limit
Write tests with 95 percent branch coverage, property-based tests via fast-check for the retry and backoff logic, and run on Node 18, 20, 22 and 3 browsers
Add a public API report with api-extractor and fail CI on unreviewed surface changes
Automate releases with changesets or semantic-release, provenance-enabled npm publishing and a signed tag
Set a deprecation policy: warn for one minor, remove in next major, with a codemod for breaking changes
Add security hygiene: lockfile audit, no install scripts, two-factor publishing, and a SECURITY.md with a 90-day disclosure window
Document and respond to issues with an SLA of 3 business days for first response and report adoption: weekly downloads and number of dependants

examples.title: Exports map and bundle check
examples.output:
$ npx size-limit
  dist/index.js  brotli  2.4 kB  (limit 3 kB)  PASS
$ npx api-extractor run
  API report unchanged

notes: Anything exported is public API; export the minimum and keep internals unreachable via the exports map.
Dual package hazard: ESM and CJS copies can both load and break instanceof; avoid stateful singletons.
Breaking a downstream user silently costs more trust than any feature earns.

title: Fintech Monorepo Pipeline Speed
description: Cut a 45-minute monorepo pipeline to under 10 minutes so fixes reach customers the same day.
overview: Cut a 45-minute monorepo pipeline to under 10 minutes so fixes reach customers the same day.
tasks: Instrument every job with duration, queue time, cache hit rate and cost, and build a dashboard for p50 and p95 pipeline time
Identify the critical path from a job dependency graph and parallelise so no stage exceeds 8 minutes
Implement affected-only builds using Nx, Bazel or Turborepo with remote caching, targeting a 70 percent cache hit rate
Shard the test suite across runners by historical timing so shards finish within 10 percent of each other
Cache dependencies and Docker layers with content-hash keys and BuildKit cache mounts, and fail loudly on cache poisoning risks
Detect and quarantine flaky tests automatically: rerun failed tests once, track flake rate per test, and quarantine anything above 2 percent
Right-size runners, use spot or preemptible capacity for non-release jobs, and set job timeouts and concurrency cancel for superseded pushes
Report outcomes: p95 time under 10 minutes, cost reduction at least 50 percent, flake-caused reruns below 1 percent of runs

examples.title: Workflow with concurrency and cache
examples.code:
concurrency:
  group: ci-$GITHUB_REF
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  test:
    strategy:
      matrix: { shard: [1,2,3,4,5,6] }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.npm
          key: npm-HASH-OF-package-lock.json
      - run: npx nx affected -t test --shard=$SHARD/6
examples.output: pipeline p95: 9m 40s (was 44m 12s)  cache hit 74 percent  monthly cost 13,900 USD (was 30,100)

notes: Concurrency cancel on pull requests alone often saves 20 percent of spend, but never cancel on the main branch.
Caches keyed on lockfile hashes are safe; caches keyed on branch names leak stale state.
A fast pipeline with flaky tests is slow, because people rerun it.

title: Secure Supply Chain for Payments Releases
description: Sign builds and check provenance so customers only run genuine payment software.
overview: Sign builds and check provenance so customers only run genuine payment software.
tasks: Replace long-lived cloud credentials with OIDC federation (GitHub to AWS IAM roles), scoped per repo and per environment, with 1-hour sessions
Pin all third-party actions and base images to full commit SHAs or digests, and automate updates with Dependabot or Renovate
Set default workflow permissions to read-only and grant per-job minimal permissions; prohibit pull_request_target on untrusted code
Generate an SBOM (Syft, CycloneDX) and scan with Grype or Trivy, failing on critical vulnerabilities with an exception file that expires
Sign images and attestations with Cosign keyless signing and generate SLSA provenance via slsa-github-generator
Enforce at deploy: an admission policy (Kyverno or Sigstore policy-controller) rejects unsigned images or ones not built from the main branch
Add secret scanning with gitleaks as a pre-commit and CI step, and rotate any found secret within 24 hours
Run a red-team exercise injecting a malicious PR and a typosquatted dependency, documenting that each control caught or limited it

examples.title: Verify before deploy
examples.code: $ cosign verify --certificate-identity-regexp 'https://github.com/acme/api/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main' --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com ghcr.io/acme/api@sha256:ab12...
examples.output:
Verification for ghcr.io/acme/api@sha256:ab12... --
The cosign claims were validated
The code-signing certificate was verified using trusted certificate authority certificates
(admission: PASS, provenance level 3)

notes: pull_request_target with a checkout of PR code is the classic route to secret theft; treat it as dangerous by default.
Scanners generate noise; an expiring exception file keeps pressure on without blocking releases.
Verify signatures at deploy time, not just at build time, or signing is theatre.

title: Progressive Delivery for Payments
description: Roll out payment changes to a small share of users first and roll back automatically, protecting customers.
overview: Roll out payment changes to a small share of users first and roll back automatically, protecting customers.
tasks: Implement canary deploys with Argo Rollouts or Flagger shifting traffic 5, 25, 50, 100 percent with pauses of 5 minutes
Define analysis templates against Prometheus: error rate under 1 percent, p99 latency under 400 ms, and abort and roll back automatically on breach
Use feature flags (OpenFeature or Unleash) to decouple deploy from release, with a kill switch tested monthly
Adopt expand and contract database migrations so any two adjacent versions are compatible; enforce with a migration linter
Add a deploy gate checking error budget: block non-critical releases when the SLO budget is below 20 percent
Automate release notes and change records from conventional commits and link every deploy to a trace and dashboard annotation
Rehearse: inject a bad release in staging and production-like canary and show rollback completes in under 3 minutes without human action
Report DORA metrics before and after: deploy frequency, lead time (target under 1 day), change failure rate (under 5 percent), time to restore (under 30 minutes)

examples.title: Rollout analysis spec
examples.code:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AnalysisTemplate
spec:
  metrics:
  - name: error-rate
    interval: 1m
    failureLimit: 2
    successCondition: result[0] < 0.01
    provider:
      prometheus:
        query: sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[2m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[2m]))
examples.output:
Rollout api: step 2/4 (25 percent) AnalysisRun Failed (error-rate 0.034)
Action: aborted, traffic restored to stable v41 in 74s

notes: Rollback is only automatic if the database change was backward compatible; migrations are the real constraint.
Canaries need enough traffic to be statistically meaningful; low-volume services need synthetic load.
Measure DORA for improvement, never to rank teams.

title: Certificate SSH Access for Finance Servers
description: Replace shared SSH keys with short-lived certificates so finance servers stay secure.
overview: Replace shared SSH keys with short-lived certificates so finance servers stay secure.
tasks: Create an offline root CA and an online signing CA key stored in an HSM or cloud KMS, with a documented key ceremony
Configure sshd on all hosts with TrustedUserCAKeys, AuthorizedPrincipalsFile and RevokedKeys, rolled out via configuration management in waves of 10 percent
Build a signing service behind SSO and MFA that issues certificates valid for 8 hours with principals derived from group membership
Sign host keys with a host CA and distribute @cert-authority in known_hosts so first-connection trust prompts disappear
Add a break-glass path with a sealed, audited emergency key and alert on every use
Log certificate key id and serial for each login to the SIEM, enabling the query: who logged into host X at time T
Remove all static authorized_keys entries, verify with an automated scan, and test that disabling a user in SSO ends access within 8 hours
Report: percentage of hosts migrated (target 100), number of orphaned keys removed, median time to onboard or offboard an engineer

examples.title: Issue and inspect a certificate
examples.code:
$ ssh-keygen -s ca_user -I alice@acme-2024-05-12 -n alice,deploy -V +8h id_ed25519.pub
$ ssh-keygen -L -f id_ed25519-cert.pub
examples.output:
Signed user key id_ed25519-cert.pub: id "alice@acme-2024-05-12" serial 0 for alice,deploy valid from 2024-05-12T09:00:00 to 2024-05-12T17:00:00
Type: ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com user certificate
Principals: alice deploy

notes: Keep the root CA offline; compromise of the signing CA then only requires re-issuing, not re-trusting every host.
Use short validity instead of revocation lists, which nobody keeps current.
Always test sshd changes with a second open session; a bad config can lock out the whole fleet.

title: Zero-Trust Bastion for a Bank
description: Replace an exposed jump host with audited access so no bank server is open to the internet.
overview: Replace an exposed jump host with audited access so no bank server is open to the internet.
tasks: Move all private hosts to security groups that allow SSH only from the access layer, and verify with an external scan that no port 22 is reachable from the internet
Deploy an identity-aware access layer (Teleport, AWS SSM Session Manager, or Boundary) with SSO and MFA
Configure engineer ssh_config with ProxyJump or ProxyCommand patterns so existing workflows (scp, rsync, git, port forwards) still work
Record sessions with replay, store them in write-once object storage for 1 year, and index by user and host
Implement just-in-time privileged access: request, approve by a second person and expire in 2 hours
Harden sshd: disable passwords and root login, restrict KexAlgorithms, Ciphers and MACs to modern sets, set MaxAuthTries 3 and LoginGraceTime 20
Run ssh-audit against all host classes and reach zero failures or warnings on the agreed baseline
Measure results: exposed port count 0, failed login noise down 100 percent, median time to access a host unchanged or better, and audit finding closed

examples.title: Client config and audit
examples.code:
Host *.internal.acme
  ProxyJump bastion.acme.example
  IdentityAgent ~/.ssh/agent.sock
  ForwardAgent no

$ ssh-audit prod-web-01.internal.acme
examples.output:
# general
(gen) software: OpenSSH_9.6
# kex algorithms
(kex) curve25519-sha256 -- [info] available since OpenSSH 7.4
No failures or warnings. (versions vary)

notes: ForwardAgent is a risk; use ProxyJump so the intermediate host never sees your agent.
Session recording is useless without retention policy and access controls on the recordings themselves.
Plan a rollback path for outages of the access layer itself, or it becomes the new single point of failure.

title: SSH Compromise Forensics
description: Trace a simulated SSH compromise and detect malicious tunnels so customer data stays protected.
overview: Trace a simulated SSH compromise and detect malicious tunnels so customer data stays protected.
tasks: Build a lab with 3 hosts and replay or generate an attack: stolen key, agent forwarding hijack, and a reverse tunnel with ssh -R
Extract a timeline from /var/log/auth.log or journalctl -u ssh with LogLevel VERBOSE, correlating key fingerprints to users
Identify tunnels using ss -tnp, lsof and sshd child processes, and show forwarded ports and the originating session
Detect agent hijack by inspecting SSH_AUTH_SOCK sockets in /tmp and process ancestry
Write detection rules (auditd, Falco or Sigma) for new authorized_keys writes, sshd spawned sub-sessions, and logins outside business hours
Constrain the damage permanently: AllowTcpForwarding no, PermitTunnel no, AllowAgentForwarding no, per-user Match blocks, and from= restrictions
Set up fail2ban or sshguard plus rate limiting, and prove 100 failed attempts per minute are throttled
Deliver an incident report with timeline, indicators of compromise, root cause and 5 prioritised fixes

examples.title: Timeline extraction
examples.code: $ journalctl -u ssh --since '2024-05-12 03:00' --until '2024-05-12 04:00' | grep -E 'Accepted|Failed|forward'
examples.output:
May 12 03:12:08 web01 sshd[2211]: Accepted publickey for deploy from 203.0.113.50 port 51122 ssh2: ED25519 SHA256:Xk3...
May 12 03:12:41 web01 sshd[2211]: refused remote port forwarding... (example, values vary)
May 12 03:13:02 web01 sshd[2290]: Accepted publickey for deploy from 10.0.4.7 port 40022

notes: Fingerprint in the log ties a login to a specific key, which is how you find the stolen laptop.
Logs on the compromised host cannot be trusted; ship them off-box in real time.
Disabling forwarding by default is the cheapest control with the biggest effect.

title: High-Traffic Nginx Edge for Payments
description: Serve 20,000 requests per second with caching so customers can pay during peak times.
overview: Serve 20,000 requests per second with caching so customers can pay during peak times.
tasks: Tune worker_processes auto, worker_connections 8192, worker_rlimit_nofile, keepalive to upstream, and reuseport; document each choice
Add a proxy_cache with proxy_cache_lock, proxy_cache_use_stale updating error timeout, and background update, targeting 85 percent cache hit on cacheable routes
Implement layered rate limiting with limit_req (burst, nodelay) and limit_conn keyed per IP and per API key, and return 429 with Retry-After
Configure upstream health with max_fails, fail_timeout, slow_start, and a backup server; add a custom 503 maintenance page
Load test with k6 or wrk2 at 20,000 req/s for 15 minutes and show p99 under 250 ms and error rate under 0.1 percent
Kill one backend and slow another to 2 seconds during the test, showing stale cache and timeouts keep the site up
Validate zero-downtime config reload with nginx -t and nginx -s reload under load, with zero dropped connections
Export stub_status or the Prometheus exporter and set alerts on 5xx ratio and upstream response time

examples.title: Cache and rate limit core
examples.output:
k6: 20,012 req/s sustained 15m, p99 211 ms, errors 0.03 percent, cache hit 87 percent
backend-2 killed at t=300s: no user-visible errors (values vary by hardware)

notes: Use proxy_cache_lock to stop a cache stampede from sending thousands of identical requests to the origin.
Rate limit by something better than IP when users sit behind NAT.
Test with realistic, not uniform, traffic and with slow clients, or the numbers lie.

title: TLS Baseline for Banking Sites
description: Build an A+ TLS and header baseline so customers' connections to banks are secure.
overview: Build an A+ TLS and header baseline so customers' connections to banks are secure.
tasks: Enable only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 with a modern cipher list, ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off, session tickets off or rotated, and OCSP stapling
Automate certificates with ACME (certbot or lego), renewal at 30 days left, deploy hooks reloading Nginx, and alerting when expiry is under 14 days
Add HSTS (max-age 31536000, includeSubDomains after staged rollout), CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy via a shared include
Redirect HTTP to HTTPS, enable HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 (QUIC) and verify with curl --http3
Block common attacks: limit request body and header sizes, restrict methods, hide server_tokens, and add ModSecurity with OWASP CRS in detection mode first
Template all 40 vhosts with includes so a security change is one file edit, and validate config in CI with nginx -t and gixy
Run testssl.sh and SSL Labs scans in a nightly job and fail on a grade below A
Show before and after: grade F to A+, outages from expiry 0, header coverage 100 percent

examples.title: Shared baseline include
examples.output:
$ testssl.sh --quiet example.com
 Protocols: TLS 1.2 offered, TLS 1.3 offered, SSLv3/TLS1.0/1.1 not offered
 Overall grade (SSL Labs): A+

notes: add_header in a nested location block replaces inherited headers; use an include in every location or the more_set_headers module.
Roll out HSTS preload gradually; it is nearly impossible to undo quickly.
Run WAF rules in detection mode for 2 weeks before blocking.

title: Config as Code for a Bank's Web Estate
description: Migrate hand-edited web server configs to tested, versioned files so bank sites change safely.
overview: Migrate hand-edited web server configs to tested, versioned files so bank sites change safely.
tasks: Extract all current rewrites and redirects into a table and classify them: exact, regex, and obsolete (check against 90 days of access logs)
Convert rules to map blocks and return 301 where possible, using location prefix or exact matches instead of if, and document 5 if is evil cases removed
Template the config with Jinja or Ansible and keep it in git with a CI pipeline running nginx -t, gixy and a docker-based integration test
Create a replay corpus of 1 million sampled requests from logs and use GoReplay or a custom script to send them to old and new stacks
Diff status code, Location header and body hash and require 99.99 percent equivalence, triaging every difference
Mirror live traffic with the mirror directive for 7 days to the new stack and compare error rates
Cut over by DNS weighted routing 1, 10, 50, 100 percent with a rollback at any step
Report: rule count reduced by at least 60 percent, zero unexpected 404s in the first 30 days, and mean config change lead time

examples.title: Replay diff report
examples.code: $ ./replay-diff --old https://old.internal --new https://new.internal --input sample.log
examples.output:
requests 1,000,000  identical 999,912 (99.991 percent)
status diff 71  header diff 13  body diff 4
most common: /legacy/*.php -> 301 vs 404 (rule missing)

notes: The if directive inside location is unreliable; prefer map and try_files.
Old rules often serve nobody; log analysis lets you delete them confidently.
Always keep the old stack warm for 2 weeks after cutover.

title: Resilient DNS for a Bank
description: Remove DNS as a single point of failure so customers always reach their bank.
overview: Remove DNS as a single point of failure so customers always reach their bank.
tasks: Define all zones in code (OctoDNS or DNSControl) in git with pull-request review and CI validation, targeting 200 zones
Publish the same zones to two independent providers, with NS records for both, and confirm with dig that all four to eight nameservers answer identically
Enable DNSSEC with KSK and ZSK rotation plan, DS records at the registrar, and a monitored signature expiry alert at 7 days
Set TTL strategy: 300 seconds for failover records, 3600 or more for stable records, and a lowering procedure 48 hours before planned changes
Lock domains at the registrar with registry lock and MFA, and monitor with an external check for NS record changes
Add CAA records restricting certificate issuance, and SPF, DKIM and DMARC at p=reject after report review
Run a drill: blackhole provider A in a test delegation and show resolution continues, measuring client failure rate and failover time under 60 seconds
Document the runbook and report SLO of 100 percent resolution availability measured from 10 global probes

examples.title: Zone as code and verification
examples.code:
providers:
  cloudflare: { class: octodns_cloudflare.CloudflareProvider }
  route53:    { class: octodns_route53.Route53Provider }
zones:
  example.com.:
    sources: [config]
    targets: [cloudflare, route53]
examples.output:
$ dig +short NS example.com
ns-123.awsdns-15.com.
ana.ns.cloudflare.com.
bob.ns.cloudflare.com.
ns-987.awsdns-42.org.
$ delv example.com A
; fully validated

notes: DNSSEC failures look like total outages to validating resolvers; never rotate keys without a rehearsed procedure.
Features unique to one provider (alias records, geo routing) break parity; track them explicitly.
Registrar account compromise beats every technical control; protect it hardest.

title: DNS Outage Forensics
description: Debug an intermittent DNS failure so customers stop seeing "site not found" during payments.
overview: Debug an intermittent DNS failure so customers stop seeing "site not found" during payments.
tasks: Build a lab with an authoritative server (BIND or Knot), a recursive resolver (Unbound) and a client, and inject faults: lame delegation, missing glue, mismatched NS sets, and EDNS blocking by a firewall
Use dig +trace, +dnssec and +norecurse to identify where the chain breaks, and read response flags, TTLs and RCODEs
Capture traffic with tcpdump or Wireshark and show truncated UDP responses falling back to TCP on port 53, and fix a firewall dropping it
Diagnose DNSSEC failure with delv and dnsviz and repair an expired RRSIG and a wrong DS record
Measure resolver latency distribution using dnsperf for 10,000 qps and identify cache hit ratio from Unbound statistics
Reproduce a negative caching problem (SOA minimum) and show how long a deleted record stays NXDOMAIN
Add monitoring: synthetic queries from 5 vantage points, alerting on SERVFAIL ratio above 1 percent and p95 resolution over 200 ms
Write the postmortem with timeline, root cause, and a checklist for delegation changes

examples.title: Tracing a broken delegation
examples.code:
$ dig +trace app.example.com
$ dig @ns2.example.com app.example.com A +norecurse
examples.output:
example.com.  172800 IN NS ns1.example.com.
example.com.  172800 IN NS ns2.example.com.
;; ns2.example.com: connection timed out; no servers could be reached
(root cause: ns2 firewall dropped UDP fragments and TCP 53)

notes: Compare answers from every authoritative server, not just through your recursive resolver, because caching hides inconsistencies.
TCP 53 must be open; large DNSSEC responses depend on it.
Negative caching means a fix can take the SOA minimum to be visible; plan around it.

title: Domain and Email Migration
description: Move 50 domains and their mail without lost email, so customers still get statements and alerts.
overview: Move 50 domains and their mail without lost email, so customers still get statements and alerts.
tasks: Inventory every record in all zones including forgotten subdomains, using zone transfer, passive DNS and certificate transparency logs to find unknown names
Lower TTLs to 300 seconds 48 hours before and record the originals for restoration
Replicate zones to the new provider and verify record parity with an automated diff before changing delegation
Preserve mail: duplicate MX, SPF, DKIM selectors and DMARC, keep SPF under 10 lookups, and run test sends to 5 mailbox providers checking headers for pass results
Transfer domains with auth codes and unlocked status, verifying WHOIS contacts and avoiding the 60-day lock, and changing nameservers last
Monitor with probes querying old and new nameservers every minute during cutover, and track mail queue depth and bounce rate
Run a rollback rehearsal and keep the old zone live for 7 days after cutover
Report: zero downtime minutes, zero bounced legitimate messages, DMARC aligned rate above 99 percent in aggregate reports

examples.title: Record parity diff
examples.code: $ ./zonediff --old ns1.oldhost.net --new ns1.newhost.net --zone example.com
examples.output:
records old 64  new 64  mismatched 0  missing 0
SPF lookups: 8 (limit 10)  DKIM selectors: s1 s2 present  DMARC: p=quarantine
MX parity: OK

notes: The record nobody remembers (a vendor verification or an old subdomain) is always the one that breaks.
SPF permerror at over 10 DNS lookups silently fails authentication; count them.
Change nameservers last, after the new zone is verified through direct queries.

title: SLO Alerting for Payments
description: Replace noisy alerts with SLO-based alerts so on-call staff fix payment outages faster.
overview: Replace noisy alerts with SLO-based alerts so on-call staff fix payment outages faster.
tasks: Interview product owners and define 3 SLIs per critical service (availability, latency under 300 ms, correctness) measured at the load balancer or client, not the host
Set SLOs such as 99.9 percent over 30 days and compute the error budget in minutes (43.2 minutes for 99.9)
Implement recording rules in Prometheus for 5m, 1h, 6h and 3d error ratios
Create multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts: page at 14.4x burn over 1h and 5m, page at 6x over 6h and 30m, ticket at 1x over 3d
Delete or downgrade every alert that has no runbook, no clear action or fired 10 times without action in a quarter
Attach a runbook link, dashboard and recent deploy annotations to every page
Build an error budget dashboard and policy: freeze risky releases when 100 percent of budget is spent
Report: pages per week down at least 80 percent, actionable page ratio above 90 percent, mean time to detect under 5 minutes in game day test

examples.title: Burn rate alert rule
examples.code:
- alert: ApiErrorBudgetFastBurn
  expr: |
    job:api_errors:ratio_rate1h > (14.4 * 0.001)
    and job:api_errors:ratio_rate5m > (14.4 * 0.001)
  for: 2m
  labels: { severity: page }
  annotations: { runbook: https://wiki.example/runbooks/api-errors }
examples.output:
Alert ApiErrorBudgetFastBurn FIRING: 1h error ratio 2.1 percent (burn 21x). Budget remaining 61 percent.
Quarterly pages: 780 -> 140 (values vary)

notes: Measure SLIs as close to the user as you can; a healthy server behind a broken load balancer is still an outage.
The short window prevents alerts from staying active after recovery; both windows are needed.
An SLO nobody uses to make decisions is decoration; tie it to release policy.

title: Observability for a Payments Company
description: Track metrics, logs and traces for millions of series so payment problems are found quickly.
overview: Track metrics, logs and traces for millions of series so payment problems are found quickly.
tasks: Audit active series with TSDB status and topk queries, identify the top 10 offenders by label cardinality, and drop or relabel them
Set limits: sample_limit, label_limit per scrape target and a CI check rejecting metric names containing user, session or request ids
Scale with Thanos, Mimir or VictoriaMetrics: sharded ingestion, object storage for long term, with 15 days hot and 13 months downsampled
Standardise instrumentation with OpenTelemetry SDKs and Collector, adding trace id to logs for one-click correlation
Use exemplars to link a latency histogram bucket to a trace
Implement tail-based sampling keeping 100 percent of errors and slow traces and 5 percent of the rest, and quantify storage saved
Add a per-team cost report and quota, with ingest dropping at 120 percent of quota and a warning at 80
Show results: memory use down 60 percent, query p95 under 2 seconds for 30-day dashboards, and bill cut 40 percent without losing alert coverage

examples.title: Finding cardinality offenders
examples.code:
topk(10, count by (__name__) ({__name__=~".+"}))
count(count by (user_id) (http_requests_total))
examples.output:
{__name__="http_requests_total"}   4,812,330
{__name__="http_request_duration_seconds_bucket"}  2,104,990
user_id distinct values: 381,204  (remove this label)

notes: Histograms multiply cardinality by bucket count; choose buckets deliberately.
High-cardinality data belongs in logs or traces, not metric labels.
Retention is a product decision; ask which questions people truly ask of old data.

title: Game Days for Payment Incidents
description: Test whether monitoring catches six realistic payment failures so customers are not left without payments.
overview: Test whether monitoring catches six realistic payment failures so customers are not left without payments.
tasks: Choose 6 scenarios: pod crash loop, full disk, dependency latency of 2 seconds, expired certificate, silent queue backlog, and DNS failure
Define for each the expected alert, expected time to detect (under 5 minutes) and who gets paged, before the exercise
Inject faults safely with Chaos Mesh, Gremlin or tc/stress-ng in staging first, then a limited production slice with a stop button
Record time to detect, time to diagnose and time to mitigate per scenario, and note whether the first alert pointed at the cause
Add black-box probes and a dead man's switch alert so a broken alerting pipeline is itself detected within 10 minutes
Find at least 5 monitoring gaps (for example no alert for queue age) and fix each with a new alert, dashboard panel or runbook entry
Repeat failed scenarios and show detection improving; target all 6 detected under 5 minutes
Write a blameless report and schedule quarterly game days

examples.title: Scenario scorecard
examples.code:
scenario: dependency latency +2s on payments API
expected alert: PaymentsLatencySLOBurn, page, within 5m
examples.output:
result: detected at 11m (late)  first alert: HostCPU (misleading)
gap: no latency SLO on payments; action: add burn-rate alert + trace link
retest: detected at 3m 20s, correct service named

notes: Announce the exercise to stakeholders and define abort criteria; a game day must never become an incident.
Test the notification path (phone, escalation) as well as the metric.
Silent failures such as stuck queues are more dangerous than loud ones.

title: Hardened Payments Service Sandbox
description: Lock down a payments service with systemd sandboxing so an attack cannot reach customer data.
overview: Lock down a payments service with systemd sandboxing so an attack cannot reach customer data.
tasks: Baseline with systemd-analyze security app.service and record the exposure score (likely 9 plus UNSAFE)
Run as a dedicated user via DynamicUser=yes or User=, with StateDirectory, CacheDirectory and LogsDirectory managed by systemd
Apply NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, PrivateDevices=yes, ProtectKernelTunables, ProtectKernelModules, ProtectControlGroups
Set CapabilityBoundingSet= empty and AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE only if binding below 1024, plus RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX
Restrict syscalls with SystemCallFilter=@system-service and SystemCallErrorNumber=EPERM, discovering needed calls using strace or journal denial messages
Limit resources: MemoryMax=512M, TasksMax=200, CPUQuota=150 percent, LimitNOFILE=65536
Reach an exposure score under 2.0 (OK) while an integration test and load test continue to pass
Document each directive with its reason and the failure it caused when first enabled

examples.title: Unit and score
examples.code:
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/app
DynamicUser=yes
StateDirectory=app
NoNewPrivileges=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
PrivateDevices=yes
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX
SystemCallFilter=@system-service
CapabilityBoundingSet=
MemoryMax=512M
examples.output:
$ systemd-analyze security app.service
... Overall exposure level for app.service: 1.6 OK :-)
(was 9.2 UNSAFE; exact number varies by systemd version)

notes: Enable directives one at a time and read journalctl for the denial; bulk enabling makes failures undiagnosable.
ProtectSystem=strict makes the whole filesystem read-only; list writable paths explicitly in ReadWritePaths.
SystemCallFilter with a too-tight allowlist produces SIGSYS crashes that look like application bugs.

title: Boot Analysis for a Payments Fleet
description: Fix slow and broken startup order so payment servers are back quickly after a restart.
overview: Fix slow and broken startup order so payment servers are back quickly after a restart.
tasks: Run systemd-analyze, blame and critical-chain on 3 host types and record time to multi-user.target and slowest 10 units
Draw the dependency graph using systemd-analyze dot and find ordering cycles reported in the journal
Fix an application starting too early by correct use of After and Wants with network-online.target and RequiresMountsFor=, not sleeps
Convert one init-script style service to Type=notify or Type=exec with sd_notify readiness, and remove TimeoutStartSec hacks
Use socket activation for a service to start on demand and reduce boot time, verifying zero lost connections during restart
Apply BindsTo and PartOf correctly so stopping a database also stops dependent workers, and test the failure cascade
Mask or disable at least 10 unneeded units and cut boot time by 40 percent
Verify with systemd-analyze verify in CI for every unit file and report boot time before and after on 10 hosts

examples.title: Critical chain
examples.code: $ systemd-analyze critical-chain app.service
examples.output:
app.service @8.211s
└─postgresql.service @4.980s +3.101s
  └─network-online.target @4.960s
    └─NetworkManager-wait-online.service @1.870s +3.088s
(replace with systemd-networkd-wait-online; values vary)

notes: After only orders units; without Wants or Requires nothing starts the dependency.
network-online.target waits can add several seconds; depend on it only when needed.
Never fix ordering with sleep; fix the dependency or use readiness notification.

title: Self-Healing Payment Services
description: Give 40 payment services automatic recovery so customers' payments survive a crash.
overview: Give 40 payment services automatic recovery so customers' payments survive a crash.
tasks: Write template units (app@.service) with sane defaults: Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=2, StartLimitIntervalSec=300, StartLimitBurst=5, and OnFailure=notify@%n.service
Implement WatchdogSec=30 with sd_notify WATCHDOG=1 heartbeats in one Go or Python service, and show a hung process is killed and restarted
Create drop-in override directories and a documented convention for per-environment settings, avoiding edited vendor files
Add systemd timers with Persistent=true and RandomizedDelaySec for cron-like jobs, with OnCalendar tested via systemd-analyze calendar
Send failure notifications through OnFailure to chat and pager, and journald forwarding to central logging with rate limits
Add resource accounting (CPUAccounting, MemoryAccounting) and a slice hierarchy so one noisy service cannot starve others
Run fault injection: kill -9, hang via SIGSTOP, OOM and dependency down, and verify recovery time under 10 seconds
Roll out to 40 services, report unplanned manual restarts per month and mean time to recovery

examples.title: Template with watchdog and failure hook
examples.code:
[Unit]
Description=%i worker
OnFailure=notify@%n.service
StartLimitIntervalSec=300
StartLimitBurst=5
[Service]
Type=notify
WatchdogSec=30
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2
Slice=workers.slice
examples.output:
$ kill -STOP $(systemctl show -p MainPID --value app@orders)
... 30s later journal: app@orders.service: Watchdog timeout (limit 30s)!
app@orders.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1.

notes: A crash loop without StartLimit burns CPU and floods logs; limit it and alert when the limit is hit.
Watchdog only helps if the heartbeat is sent from the code path that proves real progress.
Use drop-ins (systemctl edit) so package upgrades never overwrite your changes.

title: Secure Payment Container Images
description: Rebuild payment images to be minimal and signed so attackers can't hide in them.
overview: Rebuild payment images to be minimal and signed so attackers can't hide in them.
tasks: Inventory 25 images with docker history and dive to find layer waste, and record size, layer count and vulnerability count with Trivy
Rewrite as multi-stage builds ending on distroless or Alpine/chiseled bases, running as non-root UID 10001 with a read-only root filesystem
Order layers for cache efficiency and use BuildKit cache mounts and secret mounts so credentials never land in layers
Pin base images by digest and rebuild weekly through Renovate, with an SBOM attached by BuildKit attestations
Block merges on critical or high fixable CVEs, with an expiring ignore file reviewed fortnightly
Sign images with Cosign and verify in the cluster admission controller
Add a HEALTHCHECK or orchestrator probe, correct signal handling (PID 1, exec form, tini) and verify graceful stop within 10 seconds
Report: median image size from 1.4 GB to under 150 MB, build time under 3 minutes with warm cache, critical CVEs 0

examples.title: Multi-stage non-root build
examples.code:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM golang:1.22 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /out/app ./cmd/app

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /out/app /app
USER 10001
ENTRYPOINT ["/app"]
examples.output:
$ docker images app
app  1.8.0  sha256:...  14.2MB   (was 1.38GB)
$ trivy image app:1.8.0 --severity CRITICAL,HIGH
Total: 0 (CRITICAL: 0, HIGH: 0)

notes: Distroless has no shell; keep a debug variant or use ephemeral debug containers with docker debug or kubectl debug.
A secret removed in a later layer still exists in the earlier one; use secret mounts.
Rebuild regularly: an unchanged image accumulates CVEs as new ones are published.

title: Container Debugging for Payments
description: Diagnose memory kills and throttling in payment containers so checkouts stay fast.
overview: Diagnose memory kills and throttling in payment containers so checkouts stay fast.
tasks: Reproduce an OOM kill with a memory-hungry app and a --memory 256m limit, and prove it from docker inspect OOMKilled true, dmesg and the cgroup memory.events file
Diagnose CPU throttling by reading cpu.stat nr_throttled and throttled_time, then fix by raising limits or removing them in favour of requests
Show a zombie process leak when the app is PID 1 without a reaper and fix with --init or tini
Use nsenter, strace and docker debug to inspect a distroless container without rebuilding it
Apply runtime hardening: --cap-drop ALL with only needed caps added, --security-opt no-new-privileges, --read-only with tmpfs, seccomp default profile, and rootless Docker or userns-remap
Create a custom seccomp profile by recording syscalls with strace or oci-seccomp-bpf-hook and enforce it
Fix an unbounded json-file log driver that filled the disk by setting max-size 10m and max-file 3
Document a debugging runbook with 10 symptom to command mappings and one resolved case study

examples.title: Proving an OOM kill
examples.code:
$ docker run -d --name hog --memory 256m hog:latest
$ docker inspect hog --format '{{.State.OOMKilled}} {{.State.ExitCode}}'
$ cat /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/docker-$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' hog).scope/memory.events
examples.output:
true 137
low 0
high 0
max 41
oom 3
oom_kill 3

notes: Exit code 137 means SIGKILL, but only OOMKilled true proves the memory limit was the cause.
CPU limits cause throttling even when the node is idle; many teams do better with requests only.
Language runtimes read host memory unless container-aware; set heap limits explicitly.

title: Container Migration for Banking Apps
description: Containerise 15 banking apps with no incidents so customers see no change.
overview: Containerise 15 banking apps with no incidents so customers see no change.
tasks: Discover real runtime dependencies for each app using strace, ss, lsof and config inspection, producing a one-page profile (ports, files, env, cron, external services)
Create a standard set of base images and a Dockerfile template with documented conventions for users, logs to stdout, config by environment, and health endpoints
Provide docker compose development environments with seeded data, hot reload and make up, with a new developer productive in under 30 minutes
Externalise state: move local files to volumes or object storage and sessions to Redis, and verify the container can be destroyed and recreated without data loss
Run old and new side by side behind a weighted load balancer, comparing error rate and latency at 1, 10, 50, 100 percent
Prepare rollback: keep VM warm for 2 weeks and rehearse switching back in under 5 minutes
Add CI that builds, scans, tests and pushes images with semantic tags and immutable digests
Report: apps migrated 15 of 15, onboarding time, deploy time reduced, and incidents attributable to migration at zero

examples.title: Compose for parity
examples.output:
$ make up && curl -s localhost:8080/healthz
{"status":"ok","db":"up"}

notes: The hidden dependency (a cron job, a local file path, a hosts entry) is what fails in migration; discover it with tooling.
Use immutable tags or digests in production; latest makes rollbacks meaningless.
Parity beats cleverness: developers must run the same image as production.

title: Multi-Account Landing Zone for Banks
description: Set up cloud accounts with guardrails so customer data is isolated by design.
overview: Set up cloud accounts with guardrails so customer data is isolated by design.
tasks: Design an OU structure (Security, Infrastructure, Workloads-Prod, Workloads-NonProd, Sandbox) and document account boundaries and naming
Use AWS Control Tower or Terraform to create log archive and audit accounts, with organisation CloudTrail to an S3 bucket with object lock and cross-account KMS
Write SCPs: deny leaving the organisation, deny disabling CloudTrail/Config/GuardDuty, restrict regions to 2 approved, deny root user actions, require IMDSv2
Centralise identity with IAM Identity Center (SSO) and permission sets mapped to IdP groups, with no IAM users with long-lived keys
Automate account vending: a pull request creates an account with baseline VPC, budget alarm, security tooling and tags in under 30 minutes
Enable GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config conformance packs and IAM Access Analyzer organisation-wide with delegated administrator
Test guardrails: attempt each forbidden action from a workload account and show the explicit deny
Report: 100 percent of accounts compliant with the baseline, time to vend a new account, and zero long-lived access keys

examples.title: Region restriction SCP and test
examples.output:
$ aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1
An error occurred (UnauthorizedOperation) ... with an explicit deny in a service control policy

notes: SCPs never grant permission; they only cap it, and they do not affect the management account, so keep it empty.
Global services need exemptions in region-deny SCPs or you break IAM and CloudFront.
Test guardrails in a sandbox OU first; a wrong SCP can lock out an entire organisation.

title: Regional Failover for Payments
description: Prove a cross-region failover plan so customers can still pay if a region goes down.
overview: Prove a cross-region failover plan so customers can still pay if a region goes down.
tasks: Classify workloads by tier and pick strategy per tier: backup and restore, pilot light, warm standby or active-active, with cost estimates for each

Replicate data: Aurora Global Database or cross-region read replica, S3 Cross-Region Replication with replication time control, DynamoDB global tables, and measure replication lag under 1 second typical
Define infrastructure as Terraform modules deployable to the second region from a pipeline, with AMIs and images copied automatically
Implement Route 53 health checks with failover or latency records and a low TTL of 60 seconds, and Application Recovery Controller routing controls for manual safety
Secure keys: multi-region KMS keys, replicated secrets and cross-region IAM and certificate availability
Write a runbook with exact steps, owners and a decision tree for who declares disaster
Run a game day failing over in production-like conditions; measure achieved RTO and RPO and compare to the 30 and 5 minute targets
Fix every gap found (for example hardcoded ARNs) and repeat; schedule semiannual drills and automated daily restore tests of backups

examples.title: Game day result
examples.code:
Scenario: eu-west-1 declared unavailable at 10:00:00
Steps: promote Aurora secondary, scale ASG to 12, flip Route 53 record
examples.output:
Achieved RTO: 22m 40s (target 30m)  Achieved RPO: 2m 10s (target 5m)
Gaps: 3 (hardcoded SQS ARN, missing secret replica, stale AMI); all fixed and retested

notes: A backup you have never restored is a hope, not a backup.
The control plane of the failed region may be unavailable; rely on data plane actions and pre-provisioned capacity.
Failing back is harder than failing over; plan and rehearse it too.

title: Cloud Cost Reduction for a Fintech
description: Cut a 400,000-dollar monthly cloud bill by 30 percent so fees stay low for customers.
overview: Cut a 400,000-dollar monthly cloud bill by 30 percent so fees stay low for customers.
tasks: Enforce a tagging policy (team, service, env) via tag policies and SCPs, and use cost allocation tags and CUR with Athena to reach 95 percent of spend attributed
Build per-team dashboards and weekly reports with unit economics such as cost per 1,000 requests
Identify waste with Cost Explorer, Compute Optimizer and Trusted Advisor: idle instances, unattached EBS volumes, old snapshots, oversized RDS and NAT gateway data charges
Rightsize and modernise: Graviton instances (up to 20 percent cheaper per performance), gp3 instead of gp2, S3 Intelligent-Tiering and lifecycle rules, VPC endpoints to cut NAT cost
Purchase commitments: Savings Plans covering 70 percent of steady baseline and Spot for stateless batch with interruption handling
Schedule shutdown of non-production environments outside working hours, saving about 65 percent on them
Set AWS Budgets and Cost Anomaly Detection alerts at 80 and 100 percent, with an owner and response SLA of 1 business day
Report: 30 percent reduction, latency and error SLOs unchanged, commitment coverage and utilisation above 95 percent

examples.title: Athena query on CUR
examples.code:
SELECT line_item_product_code, resource_tags_user_team AS team,
       ROUND(SUM(line_item_unblended_cost), 2) AS cost
FROM cur_db.cur_table
WHERE year = '2024' AND month = '5'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY cost DESC LIMIT 5;
examples.output:
AmazonEC2   payments   48210.55
AmazonRDS   payments   31022.10
AWSDataTransfer  (untagged)  19844.00   <- attribution gap
AmazonS3    data       12003.72
AmazonEC2   (untagged)  9977.41

notes: Data transfer and NAT gateway charges are the line items most teams do not see until the bill arrives.
Over-committing Savings Plans on a shrinking workload turns a saving into a loss; commit to the floor, not the peak.
Savings that cause an outage get reversed; tie each change to SLO checks.

title: LLM Evaluation Gate for Financial Assistants
description: Gate every prompt and model change on measured quality so financial answers stay accurate.
overview: Gate every prompt and model change on measured quality so financial answers stay accurate.
tasks: Curate a golden set of at least 300 real, anonymised production cases, stratified by intent, with 40 adversarial and 30 refusal cases
Label 100 cases twice by different reviewers and report Cohen kappa; resolve disagreements into written rubric rules
Implement three scorer types: exact or schema checks, a rubric LLM judge, and pairwise comparison with position-swap to cancel order bias
Calibrate the judge against human labels and require at least 85 percent agreement before it can block a merge
Run the suite in CI on every pull request with caching of unchanged cases, finishing in under 10 minutes and under 5 dollars per run
Gate merges on thresholds: no drop over 2 points on overall score, zero regressions in the safety slice, p95 latency within 10 percent
Report bootstrap 95 percent confidence intervals so noise is not mistaken for regressions; run each case 3 times at the production temperature
Store every run with prompt hash, model id, retrieval index version and seed in a queryable table, and build a trend dashboard
Add a feedback loop that turns thumbs-down production traces into candidate eval cases weekly
Write a one-page guide on adding cases and rubrics, and train two other engineers to add one each

examples.title: Eval case and CI gate output
examples.code:
- id: refund-017
  input: "I was charged twice for order 8841"
  must_call_tool: lookup_order
  rubric: [acknowledges double charge, never promises refund amount]
  slice: billing

$ evalrun --suite golden --compare main
examples.output:
suite golden  cases 300 x3 runs
overall   0.874 (main 0.881)  delta -0.007  CI [-0.019, +0.005]  PASS
safety    1.000 (main 1.000)  PASS
latency p95 2.9s (main 2.7s)  +7%  PASS
cost per 1k requests $4.10 (main $4.32)
result: PASS (values vary by model and data)

notes: Judge models drift when the provider updates them, so pin the judge version and re-calibrate monthly against a fixed human-labelled set.
A golden set that never changes gets overfit; rotate in 10 percent fresh production cases each month and keep a frozen holdout.
Averages hide damage: always gate on per-slice scores, since a 1 point overall change can be a 15 point drop for one customer segment.

title: Retrieval Quality for Bank Documents
description: Raise retrieval quality over bank documents so customers get grounded, correct answers.
overview: Raise retrieval quality over bank documents so customers get grounded, correct answers.
tasks: Build a labelled retrieval set of 200 questions with gold passages and measure baseline recall at 5, recall at 20, MRR and nDCG
Separately score generation faithfulness: fraction of answer claims supported by the retrieved context, with a claim-level judge
Classify 100 failures into buckets such as chunking split, missing document, stale index, ranker miss and model ignoring context
Compare chunking strategies (fixed 512 tokens, structure-aware, parent-child) on recall at 5, holding everything else constant
Add hybrid retrieval combining BM25 and dense vectors with reciprocal rank fusion, then a cross-encoder reranker over the top 50
Add metadata filters and freshness handling so superseded documents are excluded, with an incremental re-index under 15 minutes
Require citations per claim and an abstain path when top reranker score is below a tuned threshold; measure abstain precision
Target: recall at 5 up at least 15 points, faithfulness above 92 percent, p95 end to end under 3 seconds
Run a 2 week online A/B with at least 5000 sessions and report answer acceptance and escalation rate
Publish a failure taxonomy and monitoring plan covering index lag, embedding model changes and retrieval score drift

examples.title: Retrieval ablation table
examples.code: $ ragbench run --set gold200 --configs baseline,hybrid,hybrid+rerank
examples.output:
config           recall@5  recall@20  MRR   faithful  p95
baseline         0.61      0.78       0.48  0.81      1.8s
hybrid           0.72      0.88       0.57  0.84      1.9s
hybrid+rerank    0.79      0.91       0.68  0.93      2.7s
(shape of result; numbers vary by corpus)

notes: Changing the embedding model requires re-embedding everything and a blue-green index swap, so version indexes and never mix vectors from two models.
Chunk boundaries cause more misses than model choice; read 50 failed retrievals by hand before tuning anything.
Do not let the model answer from memory when retrieval is empty: an abstention is cheaper than a confident wrong answer.

title: Prompt Injection Defence for Money Agents
description: Layer defences so an agent that moves money cannot be tricked by a malicious message.
overview: Layer defences so an agent that moves money cannot be tricked by a malicious message.
tasks: Write a threat model enumerating assets, trust boundaries and at least 12 attack paths, including indirect injection via retrieved content and exfiltration through markdown image URLs
Build a red-team corpus of at least 250 attacks across jailbreak, injection, secret extraction, tool misuse and PII leakage, and automate them nightly
Enforce least privilege: scope tool credentials per user, make read tools separate from write tools, and require human confirmation for irreversible actions
Treat all retrieved and tool output as untrusted data, delimit it structurally, and never let it alter the tool allowlist
Add input and output filters for secrets and PII with measured false positive rate under 2 percent on 1000 benign prompts
Block data exfiltration channels: strip or allowlist URLs and images in model output, and cap output size
Set an attack success rate target below 1 percent on the corpus and zero successful unauthorised write actions
