Add rate limits, per-user token budgets and anomaly alerts for unusual tool call sequences
Log every tool call with user, arguments and decision, retaining 90 days for forensics
Run an incident drill: a new injection is reported, you patch the defence, add the case and redeploy in under 4 hours

examples.title: Policy gate for a tool call
examples.output:
nightly redteam: 250 attacks, 2 succeeded (0.8 percent)
unauthorised writes: 0
false positives on benign set: 14 of 1000 (1.4 percent)

notes: The model cannot reliably tell instructions from data, so enforce rules in deterministic code outside the model.
Defences degrade after every model or prompt change; the red-team suite must run in CI, not once.
Combine the lethal trio check: private data access plus untrusted input plus an outbound channel in one agent session should be designed out.

title: Frontend Budget for a Trading App
description: Own Core Web Vitals for a trading app so retail investors trade on slow phones.
overview: Own Core Web Vitals for a trading app so retail investors trade on slow phones.
tasks: Instrument real user monitoring with web-vitals sending LCP, INP and CLS by route, device class and country; establish a 28 day baseline
Set budgets: p75 LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, CLS under 0.1, initial JS under 170 KB gzipped per route
Profile with Chrome performance traces and a bundle analyzer; produce a ranked list of the top 10 causes by user impact
Apply route-level code splitting, server rendering or streaming for the top 20 routes, and image optimisation with responsive sizes and priority hints
Remove or defer third-party scripts; show before and after main-thread blocking time for each
Fix hydration cost and long tasks over 50 ms using selective hydration, memoisation only where profiled, and list virtualisation
Add a CI job using Lighthouse CI plus bundle size checks that fails pull requests exceeding budget by more than 5 percent
Create a per-team dashboard and an alert when a route's p75 regresses 10 percent week over week
Reach target on 90 percent of traffic within one quarter and report conversion or bounce change from an A/B or cohort comparison
Run a workshop and write a performance review checklist adopted into the pull request template

examples.title: CI budget failure
examples.code: $ lhci assert && bundlewatch
examples.output:
FAIL /checkout  initial JS 212.4 KB gz (budget 170 KB)
  +41.1 KB from: moment-timezone (38.2 KB) imported in utils/date.ts
PASS /home      LCP lab 2.1s (budget 2.5s)
exit code 1

notes: Lab scores lie; fix what field data at p75 says, since your users' devices are slower than your laptop.
Memoise last: profile first, because wrapping everything in memo often adds cost.
Budgets rot without owners, so attach each route budget to a named team.

title: Migrate a Live Payments App to a New Framework
description: Migrate a live payments app incrementally with no freeze, so customers keep paying during the change.
overview: Migrate a live payments app incrementally with no freeze, so customers keep paying during the change.
tasks: Inventory the codebase: count routes, components, deprecated API usages and dependencies; produce a dependency graph and a risk-ranked migration order
Choose a coexistence strategy (module federation, route-level strangler, or adapter layer) and document the rejected alternatives in an ADR
Write codemods with jscodeshift or equivalent covering at least 70 percent of mechanical changes, with tests for each transform
Add characterization and visual regression tests (Playwright plus screenshot diffs) for the 30 highest-traffic flows before touching them
Migrate in slices behind feature flags, ramping 1, 10, 50, 100 percent with automatic rollback on error rate rising 0.5 points
Track a burn-down metric of legacy usages per week and fail CI if the count increases
Keep the main branch releasable: no migration branch lives longer than 3 days
Compare error rate, bundle size and p75 load time between old and new slices and keep each within 5 percent or better
Complete in under 9 months with zero rollback incidents causing over 15 minutes of customer impact
Publish a migration guide and office hours so feature teams migrate their own areas

examples.title: Codemod and burn-down
examples.code:
npx jscodeshift -t codemods/class-to-hooks.js src/ --dry --print
node scripts/legacy-count.js
examples.output:
Results: 212 ok, 38 skipped (needs manual review), 0 errors
legacy usages: 1,904 (last week 2,215)  slices live: 14 of 41

notes: Dual-running both versions doubles bundle weight, so budget the temporary overhead explicitly.
Codemods that skip hard cases and list them are better than clever ones that guess wrong.
Freeze new usages of legacy APIs with a lint rule on day one, or the target keeps moving.

title: Shared Design Platform for Banking Teams
description: Build a shared component library so banking apps look and work consistently for customers.
overview: Build a shared component library so banking apps look and work consistently for customers.
tasks: Audit 5 existing apps to find the 20 most duplicated components and agree on API conventions with representatives of each team
Build the library with accessibility baked in: keyboard navigation, focus management, ARIA, tested with axe and a screen reader on every component
Publish as a versioned package with semantic versioning, changesets, and a changelog generated from pull requests
Add visual regression via Storybook plus Chromatic or Playwright snapshots, and unit tests above 90 percent coverage
Provide a scaffold CLI that generates an app with lint, test, CI and observability preconfigured in under 2 minutes
Ship codemods for every breaking change and a deprecation policy: warn for one minor release, remove in the next major
Track adoption: percent of UI code from the library per app, version spread, and open support questions
Reach 8 of 12 teams on the latest major within 6 months without a mandate, measured by an adoption dashboard
Set a support SLA, an RFC process for new components, and an office hour; report time saved per new screen
Keep bundle impact tree-shakeable: importing one button must add under 5 KB gzipped

examples.title: Adoption report
examples.code: $ ds-stats --org all
examples.output:
app           lib version  lib-ui share  deprecated uses
checkout      4.2.0        91%           0
admin         3.8.1        64%           17
marketing     4.2.0        78%           2
median time to build a new form screen: 1.5 days (was 4)

notes: A library nobody can upgrade is abandoned; invest more in codemods than in new components.
Say no often: a component used by one team belongs in that team's code, not the platform.
Design tokens first, so rebranding is a data change.

title: Resilient Payment Provider Client
description: Keep payments working when a payment provider is slow, by switching safely to a backup.
overview: Keep payments working when a payment provider is slow, by switching safely to a backup.
tasks: Document the provider's real failure modes from logs: timeouts, 5xx bursts, duplicate webhooks, rate-limit 429s with Retry-After, and schema changes
Implement per-endpoint timeouts (connect 1 s, total tuned to p99), exponential backoff with full jitter, and a retry budget of 10 percent of traffic
Add a circuit breaker opening at 50 percent errors over 20 requests, half-open probes, and a bulkhead limiting concurrency per provider
Make every write idempotent with client-generated keys stored for 24 hours, and prove a replayed request never charges twice
Queue outbound calls with a durable outbox so a 2 hour provider outage loses zero requests and drains at a controlled rate
Verify webhook signatures, deduplicate by event id, and handle out-of-order delivery using event version numbers
Build a nightly reconciliation job comparing local records with provider reports and alerting on any mismatch over 0.01 percent
Run chaos tests with a fault-injecting proxy (latency, 500s, dropped responses) in CI and show invariants hold
Define SLOs: 99.9 percent order success despite provider availability of 99.5, and dashboards for retries, breaker state and queue depth
Write a runbook for provider outage and a contract test suite that detects schema drift daily

examples.title: Idempotent outbound call
examples.code:
key = f'order-{order.id}-charge-v1'
resp = http.post(URL, json=body, headers={'Idempotency-Key': key}, timeout=(1, 6))
examples.output:
attempt 1: timeout after 6s
attempt 2 (same key, after 2.3s jitter): 200 charge_id=ch_91
ledger rows for order: 1
reconciliation mismatches today: 0

notes: Retries multiply load during an outage; without a retry budget you become the denial-of-service attack.
A timeout is not a failure: the provider may have succeeded, so you must be able to query and reconcile state.
Record raw request and response (redacted) for every call; disputes with providers are won with evidence.

title: Public Payments API Versioning
description: Ship and evolve a public payments API with compatibility promises so merchants aren't broken by updates.
overview: Ship and evolve a public payments API with compatibility promises so merchants aren't broken by updates.
tasks: Write an OpenAPI 3.1 specification first and generate server stubs, SDKs in 2 languages and reference docs from it
Define conventions: resource naming, cursor pagination, error format following RFC 9457 problem details, idempotency keys and consistent timestamps
Implement authentication with OAuth 2.0 client credentials and scoped keys, with per-key rate limits returning RateLimit headers
Adopt a compatibility policy: additive changes are non-breaking, and a breaking-change detector (oasdiff) fails CI on violations
Version via a date header or URL major, support two versions concurrently, and give 12 months notice with Deprecation and Sunset headers
Add consumer-driven contract tests with Pact for 3 key integrators
Build a sandbox with deterministic test data and webhook replay tool
Measure developer experience: time to first successful call under 15 minutes, tracked with a timed onboarding test on 5 volunteers
Migrate 80 percent of traffic off a deprecated version using usage analytics per key and direct outreach to top 20 consumers
Publish a changelog and a design review checklist used for every new endpoint

examples.title: Breaking change detection
examples.code: oasdiff breaking openapi-main.yaml openapi-pr.yaml
examples.output:
1 breaking change:
error  [response-required-property-removed] at openapi-pr.yaml
  in API GET /v1/orders/{id}
  removed the required property 'status' from the response with status 200

notes: You cannot remove anything someone relies on; assume every field, default and ordering is depended on (Hyrum's law).
Return unknown enum values safely: tell clients in docs to tolerate new values or you can never add one.
Usage analytics per key is what makes deprecation possible; without it you are guessing.

title: Traffic Governance for Payments API
description: Rate-limit and quota payment API traffic so one heavy app can't block everyone else's payments.
overview: Rate-limit and quota payment API traffic so one heavy app can't block everyone else's payments.
tasks: Measure baseline traffic per tenant and endpoint, and identify the top 1 percent of consumers by cost
Implement token bucket limits in Redis using atomic Lua scripts, per key and per IP, with burst allowance and a 1 ms overhead target
Add tiered quotas (free, standard, enterprise) with monthly counters and clear 429 responses with Retry-After and RateLimit headers
Implement load shedding by priority class when backend latency p99 exceeds 1.5 s, protecting write endpoints over reads
Propagate trace ids and record per-tenant latency, error rate and rejected counts as metrics
Add request size limits, schema validation at the edge and a deny list with propagation under 5 seconds
Load test with k6 at 3x peak (15000 rps) with a noisy tenant sending 50 percent of load, and show other tenants keep p99 under 500 ms
Make the limiter fail open or closed per route, tested by killing Redis during the load test
Alert on abuse patterns such as credential stuffing signatures and 4xx spikes
Document limits publicly and create a self-service dashboard so customers see their usage

examples.title: Rate limiter core
examples.code:
local tokens = tonumber(redis.call('GET', KEYS[1]) or ARGV[1])
local ok = tokens >= 1
if ok then redis.call('SET', KEYS[1], tokens - 1, 'EX', ARGV[2]) end
return ok and 1 or 0
examples.output:
k6: 15000 rps, noisy tenant 7500 rps
noisy tenant: 91% 429
other tenants: p99 412 ms, error 0.02%
redis kill: fail-open on reads, fail-closed on /payments

notes: Limit by cost not just count; an expensive search endpoint deserves a lower weight budget than a lookup.
Clock-based windows allow double bursts at boundaries; use token bucket or sliding window.
Always tell clients when to retry, or they will hammer you in a tight loop.

title: Hardened Compose Baseline for Fintech
description: Create a reviewed Compose template that small fintechs copy for safe production hosting.
overview: Create a reviewed Compose template that small fintechs copy for safe production hosting.
tasks: Run all services as non-root with explicit user ids, read_only root filesystem, tmpfs for writable paths and cap_drop ALL adding back only what is needed
Set no-new-privileges, a seccomp profile, and pids_limit, memory and cpu limits sized from 7 days of measured usage plus 30 percent headroom
Use Compose secrets or file-mounted secrets, never environment variables, and show docker inspect leaks nothing sensitive
Isolate networks: a public edge network, internal-only networks for app and data, and zero published ports except the reverse proxy on 443
Pin images by digest, scan with Trivy in CI failing on fixable HIGH or CRITICAL, and generate an SBOM per image
Add healthchecks with depends_on condition service_healthy and restart policies with sane backoff
Configure log rotation (max-size 10m, max-file 5) and ship logs and metrics to a central stack
Write a policy test using conftest or a script that fails CI if a Compose file violates 15 listed rules
Run docker bench or equivalent audit before and after and report score improvement
Document upgrade, rollback and a recovery procedure, and onboard two teams measured by their audit passing

examples.title: Hardened service block and policy check
examples.code:
services:
  api:
    image: registry.example.com/api@sha256:3f1c...
    user: "10001:10001"
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: [/tmp]
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
    mem_limit: 512m
    pids_limit: 200
    networks: [internal]
examples.output:
$ conftest test compose.yaml
15 tests, 15 passed, 0 warnings, 0 failures
(example digest truncated; yours will differ)

notes: Read-only filesystems break apps that write caches silently; find every write path with strace or a test run first.
Memory limits without matching runtime settings (JVM, Node) cause OOM kills, so set heap flags from the limit.
Compose is not an orchestrator: document honestly when a stack should move to Kubernetes or Nomad.

title: Zero-Downtime Compose Deploys
description: Roll out payment changes with health checks and automatic rollback so customers aren't interrupted.
overview: Roll out payment changes with health checks and automatic rollback so customers aren't interrupted.
tasks: Place Traefik or Nginx in front, with services discovered via labels or generated upstreams and health checks on each replica
Implement rolling update by scaling to 2n, waiting for healthy, draining old containers with a 30 second stop_grace_period, then removing them
Make the app handle SIGTERM: stop accepting, finish in-flight requests, close pools, exit within the grace period
Run database migrations with expand-and-contract so both old and new versions work against the schema
Gate the rollout on a smoke test and a canary period of 2 minutes with error rate under 1 percent and p95 latency within 20 percent
Roll back automatically to the previous image digest when gates fail, completing in under 60 seconds
Prove zero dropped requests with a load test of 300 rps during 10 consecutive deploys, with zero 5xx and zero connection resets
Record a deploy log with who, image digest, duration and result, and post to chat
Add a manual rollback command and a lock preventing concurrent deploys
Document failure modes, such as a deploy during a health-check flap, and drill each one

examples.title: Deploy under load
examples.code: ./deploy.sh api registry.example.com/api@sha256:9ab2 & k6 run -u 100 --duration 90s load.js
examples.output:
scale api=4 ... 2 new healthy after 11s
canary 120s: errors 0.1%, p95 +6%  OK
drained 2 old (graceful 4.2s)
k6: 27000 requests, failed 0 (0.00%), p95 187ms
deploy done in 148s

notes: Compose healthchecks only gate start order, not traffic; the proxy must make the routing decisions.
Long-lived connections like websockets need a longer grace period and client reconnect logic.
Never roll forward a migration you cannot roll back without a tested restore.

title: Smaller Fintech Container Builds
description: Cut image size and attack surface across fintech images so updates ship faster and safer.
overview: Cut image size and attack surface across fintech images so updates ship faster and safer.
tasks: Baseline every image: size, layer count, build time cold and warm, and vulnerability count from Trivy
Convert to multi-stage builds with distroless or slim runtime bases, targeting under 150 MB per image for compiled and under 300 MB for interpreted services
Order layers for cache: dependency manifests before source, with BuildKit cache mounts for package managers
Use BuildKit with a registry cache backend so CI warm builds finish under 3 minutes and cold builds under 8
Build multi-arch images (amd64 and arm64) with buildx and verify startup on both
Create a shared base image with monthly rebuild automation and a fleet-wide CVE rebuild trigger within 24 hours of a critical advisory
Sign images with cosign and verify the signature at deploy time
Add dive or a size gate to CI failing when an image grows more than 10 percent
Reduce fixable HIGH and CRITICAL vulnerabilities by 90 percent across the fleet
Publish a Dockerfile style guide with a reference example and lint with hadolint

examples.title: Before and after
examples.code: $ docker images api-before api-after && time docker build --cache-from type=registry,ref=reg/api:cache .
examples.output:
api-before  1.42GB  layers 28  crit+high fixable 63
api-after   118MB   layers 9   crit+high fixable 2
warm build 2m41s (was 14m07s)
(example numbers; yours will differ)

notes: Smaller is not automatically safer, as distroless images remove the shell you need for debugging; keep a debug variant.
.dockerignore is the cheapest speed-up, as an unignored .git invalidates cache constantly.
Never bake secrets into layers, even if deleted later; they remain in history.

title: Live Incident Debugging on a Payments Host
description: Diagnose a live payment slowdown and write findings so the next incident is fixed faster.
overview: Diagnose a live payment slowdown and write findings so the next incident is fixed faster.
tasks: Apply the USE method to CPU, memory, disk and network and record utilisation, saturation and errors for each resource
Capture run queue, context switches, and per-CPU steal using vmstat, mpstat and pidstat at 1 second resolution during a spike
Use perf record -F 99 -g to build a flame graph of on-CPU time and bpftrace or offcputime to find off-CPU waits
Trace syscalls with strace -T -f or perf trace on a single worker and identify the slowest calls
Check disk latency with iostat -x and biolatency, and inspect page cache, dirty page writeback and swap activity
Check network: retransmits with ss -ti and nstat, conntrack table fullness and softirq distribution
Prove the root cause with a reproduction (for example a cron job triggering fsync storms) and a controlled before and after
Apply the fix, then show p99 drops below 250 ms for 7 days with the graph
Write a blameless report with timeline, evidence, flame graph and dead ends
Create a reusable triage script collecting those metrics with under 2 percent overhead

examples.title: Off-CPU analysis
examples.code:
sudo /usr/share/bcc/tools/offcputime -p $(pidof api) 10
sudo biolatency -D 10 1
examples.output:
finish_task_switch
    io_schedule
    wait_on_page_bit
    jbd2_log_wait_commit        <- 1.9 s blocked
    ext4_sync_file

disk sda  usecs: 8192 -> 16383 : 3  |  1048576 -> 2097151 : 41 (long tail)
(shape only; values vary)

notes: Average utilisation hides bursts; sample at 1 second or use histograms, never rely on 5 minute averages.
Use tools with low overhead in production; strace can slow a process 10x, so prefer perf or eBPF.
Change one thing at a time and keep the baseline, or you cannot attribute the improvement.

title: Fleet Hardening for Banking Servers
description: Harden 200 servers to a security benchmark so customers' data is protected.
overview: Harden 200 servers to a security benchmark so customers' data is protected.
tasks: Select the CIS Level 1 benchmark for your distribution and map each of at least 80 controls to an automated check with OpenSCAP or Lynis
Score baseline compliance on a sample of 20 hosts and categorise failures by risk and breakage potential
Harden SSH (key-only, no root login, modern ciphers), sysctl network settings, filesystem mount options (nodev, nosuid, noexec on /tmp) and password policy
Enable auditd rules for identity files, privilege escalation and kernel module loads, shipping events centrally
Configure unattended security updates with a staged ring rollout: 5 percent canary, 24 hour soak, then the rest
Enforce mandatory access control with SELinux enforcing or AppArmor profiles for 3 key services, without disabling them
Roll out changes in rings with automatic rollback and a break-glass access path tested in advance
Reach at least 95 percent pass rate on scored controls, and document each accepted exception with owner and expiry
Run weekly scans and alert on drift, with a dashboard of compliance by team
Hand the auditor an evidence pack generated from the scans, and cut remediation of new findings below 7 days

examples.title: Compliance scan
examples.code: oscap xccdf eval --profile xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_cis_server_l1 --results r.xml --report r.html /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-ubuntu2204-ds.xml
examples.output:
Rule ... Result
sshd_disable_root_login   pass
mount_option_tmp_noexec   fail
auditd_enabled            pass
summary: pass 142, fail 7, notapplicable 31  (95.3 percent of scored)

notes: Always keep a tested out-of-band access path before hardening SSH, or one typo locks you out of 200 hosts.
Setting SELinux to permissive is not a fix; read audit2why and write a targeted policy.
noexec on /tmp breaks some installers and JIT runtimes; test on a canary first.

title: Capacity Model for Payment Servers
description: Model payment capacity and tune the kernel so checkouts hold up on busy days.
overview: Model payment capacity and tune the kernel so checkouts hold up on busy days.
tasks: Define the workload model from production: request mix, payload sizes, connection concurrency and diurnal curve
Build a repeatable load test (wrk2 or k6) and find the saturation knee: throughput versus p99 latency per host
Measure the bottleneck with perf and pidstat to decide whether CPU, memory bandwidth, network or disk limits the host
Tune one parameter at a time with a recorded experiment: somaxconn, tcp_max_syn_backlog, file descriptor limits, net.core rmem and wmem, NIC ring buffers and IRQ affinity
Evaluate NUMA placement, transparent hugepages and the CPU governor for the workload, keeping only changes beyond 3 percent noise
Run each experiment at least 5 times and report mean with confidence interval, rejecting changes within noise
Produce a capacity model: requests per second per host at 60 percent target utilisation, plus N+1 redundancy
Forecast 12 months using traffic growth data and recommend host counts with cost per month
Validate the model in production by shifting traffic to fewer hosts and comparing prediction with outcome within 10 percent
Document all tuned settings in config management with a comment stating the measured benefit

examples.title: Experiment log entry
examples.code:
exp-07  net.core.somaxconn 128 -> 4096, nginx backlog=4096
wrk2 -t8 -c800 -R 9000 -d 120s (x5)
examples.output:
baseline  p99 412ms  errors 1.9% (listen overflows 1,204)
tuned     p99 118ms  errors 0.0% (listen overflows 0)
conclusion: keep. saturation 9,400 rps per host, plan at 5,600 rps

notes: Tuning guides from the internet are cargo cult; keep only changes you measured on your workload.
Load tests need a client that does not coordinate omission, hence wrk2 or open-model k6 scenarios.
Plan on tail latency and failure of one host, not average throughput.

title: Ansible Collection for Payments Automation
description: Package payments automation as a tested collection so other teams configure servers safely.
overview: Package payments automation as a tested collection so other teams configure servers safely.
tasks: Restructure the code into a collection with galaxy.yml, namespaces, documented plugin and role interfaces, and semantic versions
Write Molecule scenarios with the Podman or Docker driver testing at least 3 distributions for each role
Require idempotence: a second run reports changed=0, enforced as a Molecule step
Add ansible-lint with the production profile and yamllint, with zero warnings in CI
Test verification with Testinfra or assert tasks, covering config content, service state and listening ports
Write a custom module or filter plugin in Python with unit tests and documentation, replacing a fragile shell task
Run integration tests nightly against fresh cloud VMs and report time to converge
Publish to a private Automation Hub or Artifactory with signed releases and a changelog
Make CI complete in under 15 minutes by running scenarios in parallel with a matrix
Migrate three consuming teams and measure a drop in playbook-caused incidents over a quarter

examples.title: Molecule run
examples.code: molecule test -s ubuntu2204
examples.output:
PLAY RECAP converge: ok=14 changed=11 failed=0
PLAY RECAP idempotence: ok=14 changed=0 failed=0
verify: 9 passed
INFO Idempotence completed successfully.

notes: Command and shell tasks are the main source of non-idempotence; use modules or add changed_when and creates.
Pin collection versions in requirements.yml; unpinned galaxy installs make builds unreproducible.
Test the upgrade path, not just fresh installs, since production hosts are old.

title: Safe Fleet Automation for Banks
description: Run auditable Ansible changes across thousands of bank hosts with limits on blast radius.
overview: Run auditable Ansible changes across thousands of bank hosts with limits on blast radius.
tasks: Build dynamic inventory from a cloud API and CMDB with groups by region, role and ring, cached for 10 minutes
Tune execution: forks 100, pipelining, SSH ControlPersist, fact caching in Redis and gather_facts subset, cutting a baseline run time by 60 percent
Use serial with percentages (1, 5, 25, 100) and max_fail_percentage 2, plus any_errors_fatal for canary stage
Add pre-checks and post-checks as assertions (health endpoint, version, disk space) that stop the run on failure
Use check mode with diff for a dry run, and show it matches the later real run on a sample
Run through AWX or Ansible Automation Platform with RBAC, approval workflow and audit logs
Handle secrets with Ansible Vault or external lookup (HashiCorp Vault) and prove none appear in logs using no_log
Implement pull mode with ansible-pull for hosts behind NAT, comparing trade-offs in an ADR
Complete a full 2500-host rollout in under 90 minutes with fewer than 0.5 percent failed hosts handled by automatic retry
Write a rollback playbook and drill it, recording time to restore

examples.title: Staged rollout
examples.code:
- hosts: web
  serial: [1, 5%, 25%, 100%]
  max_fail_percentage: 2
  pre_tasks:
    - uri: {url: "http://localhost/health", status_code: 200}
  roles: [agent]
  post_tasks:
    - assert: {that: agent_version is version('3.2','>=')}
examples.output:
batch 1 (1 host): ok
batch 2 (125 hosts): ok=2 changed=1 failed=0
batch 3 ... batch 4
Total 2500 hosts, 12 failed (0.48 percent) retried: 12 ok. Elapsed 74m

notes: Fact gathering and SSH setup dominate runtime; measure with the profile_tasks callback before tuning anything.
A canary of one host proves little if hosts differ; make rings representative of OS, region and role.
Keep playbooks idempotent and re-runnable, because partial failures at scale are normal.

title: Self-Healing Bank Configuration
description: Detect and fix configuration drift so bank servers always match their approved state.
overview: Detect and fix configuration drift so bank servers always match their approved state.
tasks: Measure baseline drift: run check mode with diff across the fleet and classify differences by role and cause
Schedule scheduled check runs every hour via AWX or ansible-pull, writing results to a database with host, task and diff
Distinguish desired change from harmful drift using tags and an exceptions file with owners and expiry dates
Auto-remediate low-risk items such as permissions and service state, while only alerting for high-risk ones such as config templates for databases
Detect unmanaged changes with file integrity data from AIDE or auditd and correlate them with the person or process
Build a drift dashboard showing drift percentage by team, mean time to detect, and mean time to remediate
Reduce fleet drift from 18 percent to under 2 percent within 8 weeks and sustain it for 3 months
Add a change request link: drift caused by an approved change must be codified in Git within 5 working days
Test that remediation is safe: simulate 50 drift scenarios in a lab and verify convergence without service interruption
Document the policy on emergency hotfixes and train on-call engineers to use it

examples.title: Drift report
examples.code: ansible-playbook site.yml --check --diff -l web01
examples.output:
TASK [nginx : template nginx.conf]
--- before: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
+++ after:  nginx.conf.j2
@@ -12 +12 @@
-worker_connections 4096;
+worker_connections 1024;
changed: [web01]
drift hosts: 41 of 2500 (1.6 percent)

notes: Check mode cannot predict every module; mark tasks that do not support it so reports stay honest.
Auto-remediating everything overwrites genuine emergency fixes; require a path to record and codify them.
Measure drift as a trend, not a snapshot; the cause usually is a process gap rather than a person.

title: Terraform Module Registry for Fintech
description: Provide tested infrastructure modules so fintech teams build safe, compliant services.
overview: Provide tested infrastructure modules so fintech teams build safe, compliant services.
tasks: Inventory existing configurations and pick the 6 most duplicated patterns as the first modules
Design stable interfaces: typed variables with validation blocks, sensible defaults, and outputs that never expose secrets
Encode guardrails inside modules: encryption on, public access off, mandatory tags, and least-privilege IAM
Test each module with terraform test (native) or Terratest, including a plan-only unit layer and an apply-and-destroy integration layer in a sandbox account
Run tflint, terraform validate, and checkov or trivy config scanning in CI with zero high findings
Publish through a private registry with semantic versions and tags, and enforce pinned version constraints in consumers
Document each module with generated docs (terraform-docs) including examples that CI applies nightly
Provide a migration path using moved blocks so existing resources are adopted with an empty plan
Track adoption: percent of resources in the estate managed through modules and number of teams on the latest major
Run a deprecation drill: ship a breaking change as a new major with a migration guide and move 5 teams within 6 weeks

examples.title: Module call and refactor
examples.output:
$ terraform plan
Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
(moved: 1 resource)

notes: Every variable you expose is a promise; keep the surface small and add options only when two teams ask.
Removing or renaming a resource inside a module is a breaking change because it destroys real infrastructure; use moved blocks.
Pin provider versions inside modules with a lower bound only, leaving upper bounds to the root.

title: Terraform State Migration for a Bank
description: Split a monolithic state and import unmanaged infrastructure without recreating resources that serve customers.
overview: Split a monolithic state and import unmanaged infrastructure without recreating resources that serve customers.
tasks: Back up the state with versioning, take a snapshot, and lock the workspace before starting; rehearse everything on a copy
Map resources to target states by domain (network, data, compute, iam) and document cross-state dependencies
Move resources using terraform state mv -state-out or removed blocks plus import blocks, verifying each batch with plan showing no changes
Replace direct resource references with terraform_remote_state or better, data sources and published outputs
Generate configuration for unmanaged resources with import blocks and -generate-config-out, then clean up and review
Use moved blocks for refactors inside the code and prove the plan shows only moves, not destroy or create
Reduce plan time from 25 minutes to under 4 minutes per state and measure refresh duration
Enforce state locking with DynamoDB or native backend locks, and restrict state bucket access to the CI role
Run the whole migration in stages in under 3 weekends of maintenance windows with zero unplanned changes
Write a runbook and a post-migration drift report showing 0 unmanaged resources in scope

examples.title: Import and verify
examples.output:
aws_s3_bucket.logs: Preparing import... [id=acme-prod-logs]
Plan: 1 to import, 0 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy.
after cleanup: No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.

notes: The success criterion is always an empty plan; anything else means a destroy is waiting.
State files contain secrets in plain text, so treat them as sensitive data and encrypt at rest.
Never run state operations without a lock and a known-good backup, and tell the team to stop applying.

title: Policy-as-Code for Payments Infrastructure
description: Scan every infrastructure plan for payments before it applies, so unsafe changes never reach customers.
overview: Scan every infrastructure plan for payments before it applies, so unsafe changes never reach customers.
tasks: Run plan on every pull request, post the summary as a comment, and save the plan file for apply so the reviewed plan is the applied plan
Write at least 20 policies in OPA/Rego or Sentinel: allowed regions, required tags, no public ingress to 0.0.0.0/0 on admin ports, encryption required, instance type limits
Test policies with unit tests covering pass and fail fixtures, targeting 100 percent rule coverage
Estimate cost with Infracost and fail or require approval when monthly change exceeds 500 dollars
Use short-lived OIDC credentials for CI instead of stored keys, with separate plan (read-only) and apply roles
Require two approvals for production, with automatic apply on merge for dev and staging
Detect drift nightly with scheduled plan -detailed-exitcode and open a ticket on exit code 2
Provide a documented exception process with expiry, logged in Git
Measure results: time from merge to apply under 10 minutes, zero manual applies in 90 days, and policy block count by rule
Run a game day where a deliberately bad change is attempted and show it is stopped

examples.title: Policy denial
examples.code:
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "aws_security_group_rule"
  r.change.after.cidr_blocks[_] == "0.0.0.0/0"
  r.change.after.from_port == 22
  msg := sprintf("%s opens SSH to the world", [r.address])
}
examples.output:
FAIL - plan.json - main - aws_security_group_rule.admin opens SSH to the world
1 test, 0 passed, 1 failure
Pipeline blocked; cost delta +$0, plan artifact saved

notes: Apply the saved plan; re-planning at apply time can differ from what was reviewed.
Start policies in advisory mode for two weeks to find false positives before enforcing.
A pipeline with a wide admin role is a prize target; scope each pipeline role and protect the workflow files.

title: Backup Strategy for a Bank
description: Design tiered backups from business requirements so customers' records survive disasters.
overview: Design tiered backups from business requirements so customers' records survive disasters.
tasks: Interview owners and classify 30 systems into tiers with RPO and RTO (for example tier 1: 5 minutes and 1 hour; tier 3: 24 hours and 3 days)
Design 3-2-1-1-0: 3 copies, 2 media types, 1 offsite, 1 immutable or air-gapped, 0 errors verified by restore tests
Use point-in-time recovery for databases (WAL archiving or binlog) to meet the 5 minute RPO, and snapshots plus object versioning for others
Enable immutability with object lock in compliance mode for 30 days and separate backup credentials from production admin accounts
Encrypt backups with keys held separately and test key recovery from a sealed offline copy
Calculate storage and egress cost for retention policies such as 7 daily, 4 weekly, 12 monthly, and present a cost per tier
Model ransomware: assume production credentials are compromised and show backups survive
Write monitoring: alert when any job misses its window, size drops over 30 percent, or the last verified restore is older than 30 days
Document restore runbooks with step times and estimated RTO for each tier
Get the tier table signed off by business owners and review it twice a year

examples.title: Tier table
examples.code:
system        tier  RPO     RTO    method                          retention
orders-db     1     5 min   1 h    WAL archive + daily base, lock  35d + 12m
uploads       2     1 h     4 h    versioned bucket, cross-region  90d
wiki          3     24 h    72 h   nightly snapshot                14d
examples.output:
estimated cost per month: tier1 $410, tier2 $220, tier3 $35
last verified restore: orders-db 6 days ago, 41 min (RTO 60 min met)

notes: A backup that has never been restored is a hope; the verified restore time is your real RTO.
Replicated data copies corruption and deletion instantly; replication is not backup.
Ransomware attackers target backups first, so immutability and separate credentials are mandatory.

title: Automated Restore Testing for Records
description: Test restores continuously so financial records are proven recoverable.
overview: Test restores continuously so financial records are proven recoverable.
tasks: Provision an isolated restore environment using IaC with no route to production and a 6 hour auto-destroy timer
Automate nightly restores of one rotating system per tier and a full cycle of all systems monthly
Run validation checks: row counts within 1 percent of source at snapshot time, checksum of critical tables, schema comparison and application-level smoke query
Measure and record restore duration, throughput and compare with the RTO target in a time series
Verify PostgreSQL point-in-time recovery to a specific timestamp and prove an inserted marker row appears or not as expected
Alert on any failed restore within 15 minutes and open an incident on two consecutive failures
Test partial restore: recover one table or one deleted object without full restore, and document the procedure
Detect silent corruption using checksums at backup time and restore time, with test cases for deliberate bit flips
Publish a weekly report of restore success rate (target 100 percent) and median restore time
Fix at least three real defects discovered, such as missing WAL segments or expired keys, and add regression checks

examples.title: Nightly restore log
examples.code: restore-check orders-db --target-time "2026-11-06 02:00:00Z"
examples.output:
restored base 2026-11-06 01:00, replayed WAL to 02:00:00Z in 18m22s
check rowcount orders: 4,118,204 (source 4,118,090 +114 inflight) OK
check checksum payments.amount sum: match
marker row id 99001: present
RESULT: PASS  duration 31m (RTO 60m)

notes: Test the restore from a cold start with only documented credentials, as a real disaster removes your usual tooling.
Database restores often succeed while the application fails; include an application level query.
Track restore time as data grows; an RTO met last year may be missed now.

title: Ransomware Recovery Exercise
description: Recover a business-critical payments service in a fresh environment so customers are back quickly after an attack.
overview: Recover a business-critical payments service in a fresh environment so customers are back quickly after an attack.
tasks: Define scope, success criteria and the scenario: all production credentials revoked, primary region unavailable, backup repository intact
Write the plan with roles (incident commander, scribe, restorers, communications), a decision log and a stop condition for the drill
Prepare the clean environment with IaC, a break-glass identity stored offline, and documented dependencies such as DNS, certificates and secrets
Restore the database to a chosen point in time, rebuild the application from signed images, and reconnect dependencies
Measure actual RTO and RPO against targets, with timestamped milestones from declaration to first user transaction
Verify data integrity with business owners, including reconciliation of the last 24 hours of orders
Exercise communication: status page updates every 30 minutes and a stakeholder briefing template
Capture at least 10 findings, rate each by severity and assign owners with due dates
Re-run the failed steps within 60 days to confirm fixes
Present results to leadership with RTO met or missed, cost of downtime avoided and the follow-up budget

examples.title: Drill timeline
examples.code: T+00:00 declared  T+00:20 clean account ready  T+01:10 db restored  T+02:05 app healthy  T+02:30 first order
examples.output:
RTO target 4h  actual 2h30  MET
RPO target 15m actual 11m   MET
findings: 12 (2 high: break-glass MFA device missing, DNS TTL 24h)

notes: The things you forget are dependencies: DNS, certificates, license servers and the person holding the MFA device.
Run the drill with the on-call team, not the experts, or you measure the wrong thing.
Write findings as tickets with owners the same day, or they disappear.

title: Network Outage Forensics for Payments
description: Diagnose an intermittent network fault that blocks payments and write the root cause.
overview: Diagnose an intermittent network fault that blocks payments and write the root cause.
tasks: Define the symptom with data: sample 10000 requests and show a latency histogram with clusters at 1, 3 and 7 seconds
Capture on both sides with tcpdump -i any -s 128 -w, ring buffers and synchronised clocks, filtered to the service pair
Analyse in Wireshark and tshark: tcp.analysis.retransmission, SYN retransmits, duplicate ACKs, zero window and resets
Correlate with host counters: nstat, ss -s, conntrack -S (insert_failed, drop) and netstat softnet drops
Test path MTU with ping -M do -s and tracepath, and check for blackholed ICMP fragmentation-needed
Identify the root cause (for example a full conntrack table or asymmetric routing through a stateful firewall) and reproduce it with hping3 or iperf3
Apply the fix, for example raising nf_conntrack_max or fixing the route, and verify the retransmit rate drops below 0.01 percent
Add permanent monitoring: alert on conntrack usage above 80 percent and TCP retransmit ratio above 0.5 percent
Produce a report with packet excerpts, a timeline diagram and a decision tree for similar faults
Record a short captured-trace walkthrough that a junior engineer can follow

examples.title: Evidence of SYN retransmits
examples.code:
tshark -r cap.pcap -Y 'tcp.analysis.retransmission && tcp.flags.syn==1' -T fields -e frame.time_relative -e ip.src -e ip.dst
conntrack -S
examples.output:
3.001  10.0.1.14  10.0.2.7
6.002  10.0.1.14  10.0.2.7
cpu=0 found=0 invalid=0 insert=0 insert_failed=18442 drop=18442
(shape only; numbers vary)

notes: Capture on both ends; one-sided captures cannot tell a drop from a delay.
Exact multiples of 1, 3 and 7 seconds are TCP initial retransmission timers and point at lost SYNs.
Offloads (GRO, TSO) make captured packets look larger than the MTU; do not misread them.

title: Multi-Region Network for Payments
description: Build a redundant network across two regions so payments route around failures.
overview: Build a redundant network across two regions so payments route around failures.
tasks: Create an IP address plan with non-overlapping CIDR blocks for 3 sites and 10 environments, with growth headroom of 4x, documented in an IPAM tool
Design hub-and-spoke or transit gateway topology with route tables per environment and no transitive access by default
Segment into tiers (edge, app, data, management) using subnets, security groups and network ACLs, and write the allowed-flow matrix
Provide redundant connectivity: dual VPN tunnels with BGP and BFD to the data centre, tested failover under 30 seconds
Design DNS: split-horizon zones, private resolvers across regions, TTL strategy and health-checked failover records
Centralise egress through inspected NAT with allowlisted domains and flow logs retained 90 days
Test failure scenarios: kill a tunnel, a zone, and a region, measuring packet loss and recovery time for each
Validate with automated reachability analysis (for example AWS Reachability Analyzer) against the flow matrix, expecting zero unexpected paths
Express all of it in Terraform and keep network diagrams generated from the code
Hold an architecture review with security and operations and record decisions in ADRs

examples.title: Failover test
examples.code: ping -i 0.2 10.20.4.15 & aws ec2 modify-vpn-connection-options ... (down tunnel 1)
examples.output:
BGP: neighbor 169.254.10.1 Down (BFD)
route converged via tunnel 2 in 12.4s
icmp: 62 sent, 59 received, 4.8 percent loss during failover
flow matrix check: 118 allowed flows pass, 0 unexpected paths

notes: Overlapping CIDRs block later peering and mergers; reserve generously and keep a registry.
BGP timers default too slow; use BFD or tuned timers and measure convergence rather than assuming.
Security groups are stateful and ACLs are not; mixing them without a plan causes confusing drops.

title: Network Observability for Payments
description: Detect network faults in minutes so payment slowdowns are fixed before customers notice.
overview: Detect network faults in minutes so payment slowdowns are fixed before customers notice.
tasks: Deploy active probes between every site pair and critical services measuring RTT, jitter and loss every 10 seconds (blackbox_exporter, smokeping or similar)
Collect flow data with NetFlow, IPFIX or VPC flow logs and build top talkers by service, port and cost
Scrape device and host metrics via SNMP or node_exporter: interface errors, discards, utilisation, TCP retransmits and conntrack
Define SLOs such as inter-region RTT under 90 ms at p95 and packet loss under 0.1 percent over 30 days
Alert on symptoms with multi-window burn rates, and avoid pages for transient single-probe failures
Build a dashboard that shows path health on a map plus a one-click drill-down to flows
Add DNS monitoring: resolution time, SERVFAIL rate and certificate expiry for 50 endpoints
Run a game day injecting 5 percent loss with tc netem and verify the alert fires within 3 minutes
Cut mean time to identify network faults to under 10 minutes, measured across the next 5 incidents
Document triage steps as a decision tree linked from each alert

examples.title: Fault injection and alert
examples.code:
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem loss 5% delay 40ms 10ms
# alert rule
avg_over_time(probe_success{job="site-probes"}[2m]) < 0.97
examples.output:
ALERT SiteLoss firing: dc1 -> eu-west loss 5.2 percent for 2m
fired 2m40s after injection
tc qdisc del dev eth0 root  # clean up

notes: Passive monitoring misses a path nobody is using; active probes find it first.
High cardinality flow data gets expensive; sample 1 in 100 and keep aggregates longer.
Always remove netem rules after tests and use a timer, or you create the outage.

title: Threat Modelling Programme for Fintech
description: Run threat modelling across teams so customer data risks are found early.
overview: Run threat modelling across teams so customer data risks are found early.
tasks: Choose a method (STRIDE with data flow diagrams) and write a one-page guide with a template and worked example
Run threat model workshops on the 5 highest-risk systems, each producing a DFD with trust boundaries and at least 15 threats rated by likelihood and impact
Create a risk register with owner, mitigation, due date and status, tracked in the issue tracker
Define a design review trigger checklist (new auth, new data class, new external exposure) so reviews are requested at the right time
Train 20 engineers as security champions with 3 sessions and a practical exercise, and have each lead one model
Validate threats with testing: convert 10 top threats into abuse-case tests or pen-test scope items
Measure: percent of new services reviewed before launch (target 90 percent), median days to close high risks (under 30), and findings found late versus early
Integrate with SDLC: block production launch for tier 1 services without an approved model
Write security requirements per data class (public, internal, confidential, regulated) used in reviews
Review results quarterly with leadership and show trend of high-severity issues found in pen tests

examples.title: Threat register excerpt
examples.code:
- id: T-014
  component: payments-api
  stride: Elevation of privilege
  threat: JWT accepted with alg=none or key confusion
  likelihood: medium
  impact: high
  mitigation: pin algorithms; verify with library allowlist; test case added
  owner: team-pay
  due: 2026-12-15
  status: in-progress
examples.output:
summary: 62 threats, 41 closed, 14 in progress, 7 accepted (with expiry)
high open older than 30 days: 1

notes: Models rot; attach them to the repository and update on each architecture change.
A threat without an owner and date is a wish; track like any engineering work.
Make the easy path secure by default, as paved roads beat policies.

title: Secrets Overhaul for a Bank
description: Remove long-lived secrets from a bank's estate so stolen keys can't drain customer accounts.
overview: Remove long-lived secrets from a bank's estate so stolen keys can't drain customer accounts.
tasks: Scan all repositories, including history, with gitleaks and trufflehog, and produce an inventory of secrets by type, owner and age
Rotate every exposed secret first, ordered by blast radius, with rotation confirmed by test calls and old values revoked
Deploy HashiCorp Vault or a cloud secrets manager with auth by workload identity (Kubernetes, OIDC), not shared tokens
Use dynamic database credentials with a 1 hour TTL and automatic revocation, for at least 10 services
Replace CI stored cloud keys with OIDC federation and short-lived tokens
Add pre-commit and CI secret scanning that blocks pushes, with false positive rate under 5 percent
Implement automated rotation for keys of non-dynamic systems every 90 days with zero downtime using dual-key overlap
Enable audit logging for every secret read, alert on reads from unusual identities, and retain 1 year
Reach targets: zero secrets in repositories, 90 percent of services using runtime retrieval, no credential older than 90 days
Write a break-glass and incident procedure to rotate everything within 4 hours, and drill it

examples.title: Dynamic credential
examples.code: vault read database/creds/orders-readonly
examples.output:
Key                Value
lease_id           database/creds/orders-readonly/Xk2...
lease_duration     1h
username           v-oidc-orders-r-8f3a
password           (redacted, generated)

notes: Removing a secret from Git history does not un-leak it; always rotate.
Applications that read secrets only at startup need a reload design before you shorten TTLs.
Secret managers become single points of failure, so plan their availability and cached fallback.

title: Vulnerability Management for Fintech
description: Run risk-based patching with SLAs so known flaws are fixed before attackers use them.
overview: Run risk-based patching with SLAs so known flaws are fixed before attackers use them.
tasks: Consolidate sources (dependency scanning, container scanning, host scanning, cloud posture) into one inventory with asset owner and criticality
Prioritise using CVSS plus EPSS, CISA KEV membership, internet exposure and reachability, cutting actionable items by at least 80 percent
Define SLAs: KEV or critical exposed in 48 hours, high in 14 days, medium in 60 days, with exceptions logged and expiring
Automate fixes with Dependabot or Renovate, auto-merging patch updates when tests pass
Rebuild base images automatically on advisories and redeploy within 24 hours
Add SBOM generation (CycloneDX) per build and query it to answer within 1 hour: where are we running a given library
Track metrics: mean time to remediate by severity, SLA compliance (target 95 percent), age distribution and escape rate
Run a live-response drill using a new critical advisory and measure time to full inventory and fix
Report to leadership monthly with trend lines and top five risk owners
Reduce open critical exposed findings from the starting count to zero beyond SLA within 90 days

examples.title: Prioritisation
examples.code: vulnmgr triage --sources all
examples.output:
raw findings: 40,112
after dedupe: 21,870   in production only: 9,340
reachable + exposed: 1,204   KEV: 6   EPSS>0.5: 41
actionable queue: 1,251  (97 percent reduction)
SLA compliance last 30d: critical 96, high 91

notes: Fix classes, not instances: base image updates and shared libraries clear hundreds of findings at once.
Ownership is the bottleneck; findings without a mapped team are never fixed.
Do not count findings closed as success; count exposure-days.

title: Zero-Trust Remote Access for Bank Staff
description: Replace a legacy VPN for 1,000 staff with identity-aware access so customer data stays protected.
overview: Replace a legacy VPN for 1,000 staff with identity-aware access so customer data stays protected.
tasks: Inventory 120 internal applications and user groups, classify by sensitivity, and map who needs what access
Choose architecture (Tailscale, Pomerium, Cloudflare Access, or self-hosted WireGuard plus an identity proxy) with an ADR on trade-offs
Integrate SSO with MFA (WebAuthn preferred) and device posture checks such as disk encryption, OS version and EDR running
Write least-privilege access policies as code in Git, reviewed by owners, with default deny
Migrate in waves of 100 users, running old and new in parallel and rolling back any wave in under 15 minutes
Log every access decision with user, device, application and result, and ship to the SIEM
Test: stolen-credential simulation, revoked-device test taking effect in under 60 seconds, and a lateral movement attempt that fails
Measure experience: connection time under 3 seconds, helpdesk tickets per user, and throughput on a 1 Gbps link
Decommission the legacy VPN concentrator and close its firewall rules, verified with a port scan
Write user documentation and a support runbook, and report access incidents before and after

examples.title: Policy as code
examples.code:
- app: wiki.internal
  allow:
    groups: [engineering]
    device: {encrypted: true, os_min: "14.2", mfa: webauthn}
- app: db-admin.internal
  allow:
    groups: [dba]
    require: just-in-time-approval
examples.output:
access test: user=alice device=compliant app=wiki.internal  ALLOW (41ms)
access test: user=alice device=noedr app=db-admin.internal DENY posture
revocation propagation: 22s

notes: Migration is a people problem; ship the new path with equal or better speed or users find workarounds.
Posture signals go stale; require freshness under a few hours.
Keep break-glass access for the identity provider outage, offline and tested.

title: Global WireGuard Mesh for Payments
description: Run a resilient secure network across regions so payments stay private and reliable.
overview: Run a resilient secure network across regions so payments stay private and reliable.
tasks: Design the topology (hub and spoke versus partial mesh) with an IP plan, AllowedIPs policy and MTU of 1380 or measured value
Generate all configs from a source of truth in Git using templates or Ansible, with peer additions requiring a pull request
Automate key lifecycle: private keys generated on the host, public keys registered, rotation every 90 days with overlap and zero dropped sessions
Run redundant gateways per region with health-checked failover using BGP or keepalived, converging under 10 seconds
Benchmark with iperf3: throughput per core, latency overhead versus bare path, and CPU use at 5 Gbps
Tune: MTU, PersistentKeepalive 25 for NAT peers, UDP buffer sizes and multi-queue with kernel module
Monitor with wireguard exporter: handshake age, bytes, and peer up state; alert if handshake older than 3 minutes
Harden: firewall allowing only the UDP port, peer isolation by AllowedIPs, and no IP forwarding unless required
Test failure scenarios: gateway kill, key compromise revocation in under 5 minutes, and 20 percent packet loss
Document the operating guide and measure onboarding of a new site in under 30 minutes

examples.title: Peer health
examples.code: wg show wg0 latest-handshakes && iperf3 -c 10.8.0.1 -P 4 -t 20
examples.output:
Pu8k...= 1731000012
(handshake 41s ago)
[SUM] 0.00-20.00 sec  21.6 GBytes  9.28 Gbits/sec  sender
(example values vary with hardware)

notes: Wrong MTU causes the classic works for ping, fails for large downloads symptom; test with large packets.
A peer with a stale key is an outage but a leaked key is a breach; automate revocation.
UDP port blocked on guest networks needs a documented fallback (TCP relay or 443).

title: VPN Security Audit for a Finance Team
description: Audit a finance team's VPN and rehearse a compromised-credential response to protect client accounts.
overview: Audit a finance team's VPN and rehearse a compromised-credential response to protect client accounts.
tasks: Scope and document the attack surface: exposed ports, authentication methods, cipher suites, client posture and admin interfaces
Scan with nmap and ike-scan, verify strong IKEv2 proposals only (AES-GCM, DH group 14 or higher, PFS) and no aggressive mode
Test split-tunnel and DNS leaks from clients with captured traffic, and fix any leak found
Check that internal network access is restricted: attempt lateral movement from a VPN client and record every reachable subnet
Review logs: confirm authentication, assignment and disconnect events with user identity and retain 180 days
Simulate a compromised credential: attacker uses key from another country, and verify alerting on impossible travel within 5 minutes
Execute revocation of a client within 5 minutes and verify the session is dropped and cannot reconnect
Test certificate or key expiry handling and the CRL or revocation distribution time
Produce a findings report with CVSS-style ratings, fixes and retest evidence
Write an incident playbook and run a tabletop with security and IT, recording time to contain

examples.title: Cipher and exposure check
examples.code:
ike-scan -M --showbackoff vpn.example.com
nmap -sU -p 500,4500,51820 vpn.example.com
examples.output:
Notify message: no proposal chosen for aggressive mode  (good)
500/udp open|filtered isakmp
4500/udp open|filtered nat-t-ike
51820/udp closed
finding: none high; 2 medium (reachable subnets 3 over policy)

notes: Credentials leave with laptops, so tie access to device identity and make revocation instant.
Full-tunnel clients can bypass your DNS filtering if the resolver is not pushed; test this.
Logs without user identity are useless in an incident; require per-user addressing or session logs.

title: SLOs and Error Budgets for Payments
description: Define SLOs for payment services so reliability decisions protect customers.
overview: Define SLOs for payment services so reliability decisions protect customers.
tasks: Select critical user journeys for each service and define SLIs such as availability (good requests over valid) and latency (requests under 300 ms)
Set SLO targets from data, for example 99.9 percent over 30 days, and compute budget (43.2 minutes per month)
Implement SLI measurement from load balancer or mesh metrics, not from the service itself, with recording rules in Prometheus
Alert with multi-window multi-burn-rate rules (14.4x over 1h and 5m pages; 6x over 6h and 30m pages; 1x over 3d tickets)
Write an error budget policy: when more than 100 percent budget is spent, freeze risky releases until reliability work lands
Create an SLO dashboard per service with remaining budget, burn rate and top contributors
Run monthly reliability reviews and record decisions driven by budget status
Cut alert noise: pages reduced by 50 percent while customer-impacting incidents are all detected by SLO alerts
Prove the value with one example where budget exhaustion changed priorities and reduced incident count
Train service owners and review every SLO twice a year for fitness

examples.title: Burn rate alert
examples.code:
- alert: ErrorBudgetFastBurn
  expr: |
    (sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1h])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1h]))) > (14.4 * 0.001)
    and
    (sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))) > (14.4 * 0.001)
  labels: {severity: page}
examples.output:
SLO checkout-availability 99.9 percent / 30d
budget remaining 61 percent (26.4 of 43.2 min)
current burn 0.8x  status OK

notes: Pick SLOs users would notice; 100 percent targets are impossible and unhelpful.
An SLO nobody acts on is a dashboard; the policy and leadership buy-in are the real deliverable.
Measure at the edge or client side where possible, since service-side metrics miss failures that never reach it.

title: Delivery Metrics for a Payments Team
description: Cut lead time and failure rate with better pipelines so payment fixes reach customers faster.
overview: Cut lead time and failure rate with better pipelines so payment fixes reach customers faster.
tasks: Instrument the four DORA metrics from Git, CI and incident data: deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change failure rate and time to restore
Build a dashboard per team, with definitions agreed and automated, avoiding self-reported numbers
Find bottlenecks by value stream mapping and queue times: wait for review, wait for build, wait for approval
Cut CI time from 35 to under 10 minutes with test selection, parallel shards, caching and removal of flaky tests
Track flaky tests with quarantine automation and drive flake rate below 1 percent
Move to trunk-based development with feature flags, short-lived branches under 1 day, and automated pre-merge checks
Automate deployment with progressive delivery (canary at 5 percent with automated analysis) and one-click rollback
Replace manual change approval with automated risk checks for standard changes
Reach targets: lead time under 1 day, deploys at least daily per team, change failure rate under 10 percent, restore under 1 hour
Share results transparently, avoid ranking individuals, and document the practices that worked in a playbook

examples.title: DORA report
examples.code: doracli report --team checkout --period 30d
examples.output:
deploys            41   (1.4/day)   was 0.3/day
lead time median   7h20m        was 71h
change fail rate   8.3%         was 22%
time to restore    38m          was 4h10m
CI median          8m40s        was 35m

notes: Metrics become targets and get gamed; use them for learning, never for individual performance.
Flaky tests quietly destroy trust in the pipeline; fix or delete them, never retry blindly.
Small batch size is the lever that moves all four metrics.

title: Self-Service Platform for Fintech Teams
description: Build paved roads that cut new service setup from weeks to hours, so fintech launches reach people sooner.
overview: Build paved roads that cut new service setup from weeks to hours, so fintech launches reach people sooner.
tasks: Interview 15 engineers and measure the baseline: time to create a new service with CI, monitoring and production deploy (target under 2 hours from weeks)
Build golden path templates (Backstage or Cookiecutter) producing a repository, pipeline, Dockerfile, Helm chart or Compose file, dashboards and alerts
Offer self-service environments: preview environments per pull request that are created in under 5 minutes and destroyed on merge or after 48 hours
Provide infrastructure through a catalogue (database, queue, bucket) backed by Terraform modules with guardrails and cost tags
Embed defaults: logging, tracing, SLO dashboard, secret retrieval and security scanning with no developer configuration
Publish a service catalogue with owners, on-call, dependencies and runbook links, kept current by automation
Measure adoption and satisfaction: percent of services on the golden path (target 70 percent), quarterly developer survey, and support tickets per month
Run the platform as a product with a roadmap, release notes and a feedback channel with response under 1 business day
Show impact: time to first deploy for a new hire under 1 day and fewer ops tickets by 60 percent
Plan for deviation: document how teams leave the paved road safely and what support they lose

examples.title: Create a service
examples.code: platform new service --template go-api --name invoices --team billing
examples.output:
created repo acme/invoices
pipeline: build, test, scan, deploy-staging ready
staging url: https://invoices.staging.acme.dev
dashboard + SLO + alerts provisioned
elapsed 4m12s

notes: Mandates fail; make the paved road the easiest road and let results drive adoption.
Templates drift once generated; plan updates via automated pull requests to existing services.
Keep the platform team small and focused on the top three developer pains, not every request.

title: Eliminate Flaky Tests for Payments
description: Quarantine flaky tests until the flake rate is under 0.5 percent so payment releases are trusted.
overview: Quarantine flaky tests until the flake rate is under 0.5 percent so payment releases are trusted.
tasks: Ingest JUnit XML or equivalent results from 30 days of CI into a warehouse table keyed by test id, commit, runner and attempt
Define flake as pass and fail on the same commit; compute per-test flake rate and rank by the number of builds each test wasted
Build an automated rerun-on-failure detector that reruns failing tests 10 times in isolation and labels them flaky, broken or environmental
Quarantine tests above 2 percent flake rate into a non-blocking lane within 24 hours, with an auto-filed ticket assigned to the owning team via CODEOWNERS
Root-cause the top 20 offenders and classify them: shared state, time and timezone, ordering, async waits, network, resource limits
Add run-order randomisation with a printed seed and a stress job that runs changed tests 50 times in parallel before merge
Replace sleeps with explicit condition waits and inject a fake clock in at least 100 tests
Publish a weekly dashboard: overall flake rate, quarantine size, mean time to fix, CI minutes wasted
Hit targets: flake rate below 0.5 percent, red-build rerun rate down by 70 percent, quarantine age under 14 days
Write a testing standard and a 45 minute workshop on deterministic tests, and deliver it to at least 3 teams

examples.title: Flake rate query
examples.code:
SELECT test_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT commit_sha) FILTER (WHERE mixed) AS flaky_commits,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(failed) / COUNT(*), 2) AS fail_pct
FROM (
  SELECT test_id, commit_sha,
    (MAX(status='fail') AND MAX(status='pass')) AS mixed,
    SUM((status='fail')::int) AS failed
  FROM results WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY test_id, commit_sha
) t GROUP BY test_id ORDER BY flaky_commits DESC LIMIT 20;
examples.output: Top 20 rows: test_id, flaky_commits, fail_pct. Example row: checkout.test_cart_total, 41, 6.30. Values vary by estate.

notes: Retries hide flakes; keep them only as a measurement tool and always report the first-attempt result
Most flakes cluster in a handful of shared fixtures, so fix helpers before individual tests
Quarantine needs an expiry and an owner, otherwise it becomes a graveyard

title: Contract Tests for Payment Services
description: Test that payment services agree on formats, so merchants' integrations keep working.
overview: Test that payment services agree on formats, so merchants' integrations keep working.
tasks: Inventory service-to-service calls and rank the 15 services by consumer count and incident history
Stand up a Pact Broker (or PactFlow) with authentication, webhooks and tagging by branch and environment
Write consumer contracts for the 10 most critical interactions with provider states and matchers instead of exact values
Add provider verification to each provider CI, including pending pacts and work-in-progress pacts so new consumers do not break builds
Enforce can-i-deploy as a required step before every deploy to staging and production
Add contract coverage for async messages on Kafka or SQS using message pacts
Retire at least 60 percent of cross-service end-to-end tests and keep a smoke suite of 10 journeys under 8 minutes
Run a deliberate breaking-change drill: remove a response field and show the provider build fails before merge
Track metrics before and after: integration-caused incidents, pipeline duration, environment queue time
Publish an adoption guide and onboard 4 teams through pairing sessions

title: Mutation Testing for Payments
description: Prove payment tests catch real bugs so customers aren't charged incorrectly.
overview: Prove payment tests catch real bugs so customers aren't charged incorrectly.
tasks: Choose a tool for the stack (PIT for Java, Stryker for JS or .NET, mutmut or cosmic-ray for Python) and run it on one core module
Record baseline: line coverage, mutation score, surviving mutants by operator type
Triage 100 surviving mutants into equivalent, missing assertion, missing test case and dead code
Raise mutation score on the module from the baseline to at least 80 percent by adding behaviour-focused tests
Make runs affordable: incremental mode on changed files, parallel workers, test-per-mutant selection, a 15 minute nightly budget
Add a pull request gate that fails if changed lines have under 70 percent mutation score
Correlate module mutation score with 12 months of escaped bugs and present the result with a scatter plot
Add property-based tests with Hypothesis or fast-check for two pure-logic modules and record the new bugs found
Document a risk tiering policy: tier 1 modules need mutation gate, tier 3 need only smoke coverage
Present findings to engineering leadership with a recommendation to retire the raw coverage target

examples.title: Mutation report excerpt

mutmut results
Survived: pricing/discount.py:42  >= changed to >
Survived: pricing/discount.py:57  return total changed to return 0
examples.output: Mutation score: 71.4 percent (200 killed, 80 survived) before; 84.0 percent after new boundary tests. Exact numbers vary.

notes: Equivalent mutants are unavoidable; never chase 100 percent
Mutation testing is slow, so run it incrementally and only on risk-tiered code
A surviving mutant is a conversation about intended behaviour, not just a missing test

title: Shadow Test of a Fraud Model
description: Replace a fraud model with shadow testing so more fraud is caught without blocking good customers.
overview: Replace a fraud model with shadow testing so more fraud is caught without blocking good customers.
tasks: Audit the incumbent: label delay, feature definitions, current precision and recall at the operating threshold, and known failure segments
Build a time-split evaluation set (train on months 1-9, test on 10-12) and report PR-AUC, calibration error and cost-weighted loss by segment
Check training-serving skew by replaying 1 million logged requests through the offline and online feature code and diffing values
Run the challenger in shadow mode for 14 days, logging both scores, with latency overhead under 10 ms p99
Design an A/B test with a power calculation for the target effect, a guardrail metric and a fixed analysis plan
Roll out in stages 1, 5, 25, 100 percent with automatic rollback if the guardrail degrades by more than 2 percent
Calibrate scores (isotonic or Platt) and retune the decision threshold to the business cost matrix
Slice analysis by region, new vs returning users and device; document any segment that regresses
Publish a model card and a decision record with the measured uplift in money, not only metrics
Schedule retraining and define retirement criteria for the new model

examples.title: Shadow comparison
examples.code:
df = logs.merge(shadow, on='req_id')
print(df.groupby('segment').apply(lambda g: pd.Series({
  'agree_rate': (g.old_dec == g.new_dec).mean(),
  'new_precision': precision_score(g.label, g.new_dec),
  'old_precision': precision_score(g.label, g.old_dec)})))
examples.output: Table with one row per segment and columns agree_rate, new_precision, old_precision. Values vary by data.

notes: Offline gains often shrink online because of feedback loops and delayed labels
Always keep the incumbent deployable for at least one full business cycle
Agree the success metric with finance before the experiment, not after

title: Debug a Credit Model's Production Drop
description: Find why a credit model scores well offline but fails in production, so applicants are treated fairly.
overview: Find why a credit model scores well offline but fails in production, so applicants are treated fairly.
tasks: Reproduce the offline metric from a clean checkout and fix random seeds to confirm it is real
Test for target leakage: compute single-feature AUC and flag any feature above 0.9; trace each to its source timestamp
Audit temporal leakage by replaying features as-of prediction time with a point-in-time join and compare against the training table
Compare train and production distributions with PSI and KS tests per feature; list features with PSI above 0.2
Check label definition and label delay: measure how many production labels matured within the evaluation window
Check for duplicates and group leakage (same user or device across split) and re-split by group
Inspect serving code for unit, encoding and missing-value handling differences with a golden-request test set of 500 rows
Quantify each cause by re-estimating the metric after removing it, giving a waterfall from 0.95 down to 0.70
Implement preventive controls: point-in-time feature store, split-by-group helper, leakage unit tests in CI, drift alerts
Write a blameless investigation report with timeline, causes, and checklist for future model reviews

examples.title: Single-feature leakage probe
examples.output: Lines like days_since_chargeback 0.983 identifying features that encode the label. Names vary.

notes: Suspiciously good validation is a bug until proven otherwise
Group and time splits match how the model is used; random splits rarely do
Fix the process, not only the model: add the check to review templates

title: Cheaper Fraud Model Serving
description: Cut serving cost by 60 percent while keeping quality, so small banks can afford fraud protection.
overview: Cut serving cost by 60 percent while keeping quality, so small banks can afford fraud protection.
tasks: Profile requests end to end with tracing and split time into feature fetch, preprocessing, inference and post-processing
Benchmark baseline at 500 and 2000 requests per second with a load tool, recording p50, p95, p99 and cost per 1000 predictions
Replace Python preprocessing hot spots with vectorised or compiled code and batch feature fetches
Export to ONNX or TorchScript and evaluate dynamic batching with a 5 ms wait window
Apply post-training int8 quantisation and measure metric loss on a held-out slice set; accept only changes under 1 percent
Distil a large model into a smaller student and compare accuracy, size and latency on the same test
Add a prediction cache keyed on normalised features with TTL and measure hit rate
Right-size instances and autoscaling on queue depth; compare CPU, GPU and spot options
Run a shadow comparison of old and new outputs on 1 million requests and report disagreement
Document the cost model and show a before and after table that finance can sign off

Quantisation can hurt rare classes, so check sliced metrics
Batching trades latency for throughput; set a hard wait cap

title: Prompt Registry for Financial Products
description: Version and review prompts used by every product, so customers get consistent answers.
overview: Version and review prompts used by every product, so customers get consistent answers.
tasks: Survey existing prompts across repositories and catalogue at least 50 with owner, model, purpose and traffic
Design a registry schema: id, semantic version, template with typed variables, model and parameters, owner, eval suite id
Store prompts in git with a CLI or SDK that resolves a prompt by id and environment, with a 60 second cache
Require an eval run on every change: golden set of 100 or more cases, pass rate gate, cost and latency deltas posted on the pull request
Implement staged rollout: 5 percent canary by hash of user id, automatic rollback if error or eval-proxy metric degrades
Add model-migration tooling that replays the golden set on a candidate model and diffs outputs
Log prompt id and version on every call to traces for attribution of incidents and spend
Define a style guide and a lint step for banned patterns such as unescaped user input in system prompts
Onboard 5 teams, measure time-to-change-a-prompt before and after, and target a 50 percent reduction
Write a governance policy covering ownership, review, retirement and handling of sensitive data in prompts

title: Prompt Migration for Banking Assistants
description: Migrate 40 prompts to a new model with measured parity, so customers' answers don't change for the worse.
overview: Migrate 40 prompts to a new model with measured parity, so customers' answers don't change for the worse.
