tasks: Define the API so that one schema object yields input, output and error unions via conditional and mapped types, with zero user-written generics in common use.
Add a type test suite using tsd or expect-type with at least 60 assertions, including negative cases using ts-expect-error that must fail to compile.
Set a type-instantiation budget: check with tsc --extendedDiagnostics that a 200-route sample stays under 100k instantiations and under 3 seconds check time.
Profile slow types with tsc --generateTrace and the Perfetto viewer; fix at least one hotspot and record before and after numbers.
Support both ESM and CJS using package.json exports with types conditions; verify with arethetypeswrong CLI and publint with zero errors.
Test against TypeScript N and N-1 and the next beta in CI matrix; document the supported range.
Write error messages as branded types so misuse shows a readable message such as 'Route path must start with /' instead of a 40-line mismatch.
Publish with provenance via npm, generate API docs with TypeDoc, and keep an API Extractor report so type-surface changes appear in review.
Done when a new user builds a typed endpoint in under 10 lines and every public type change is flagged in PR.

examples.title: Negative type test
examples.output: tsc exits 0. If the ts-expect-error line ever compiles, tsc reports 'Unused @ts-expect-error directive' and the build fails.

notes: Recursive conditional types hit depth limits around 50 to 1000 levels; use tail-recursive forms and accumulators.
Inference quality is part of semver: pin type snapshots so a refactor cannot silently degrade it.
Declaration emit leaks internal types; check d.ts output, not just source.

title: Architecture Lint Rules for Banking
description: Build lint rules that stop code breaking a bank's security rules.
overview: Build lint rules that stop code breaking a bank's security rules.
tasks: Implement at least 6 rules, including a type-aware one (for example disallow passing a raw string where UserId brand is required).
Add a layering rule using import graph config (domain cannot import infra) with a clear error message and docs URL per rule.
Provide autofixes or suggestions for at least 4 rules, each tested with RuleTester including valid, invalid and output cases (minimum 10 cases per rule).
Measure lint time on a 5k-file repo; type-aware rules must add under 20 percent over baseline, using the TIMING=1 env var to find slow rules.
Ship a ts-morph codemod to migrate a deprecated internal API across the repo; dry-run mode outputs a diff summary.
Roll out in warn mode first, collect violation counts for two weeks, then promote to error only rules with false-positive rate under 2 percent.
Support suppression with a required reason comment and report suppression counts weekly.
Document the rule authoring guide so two other engineers each contribute a rule.
Done when violations of the top 3 architecture rules drop to zero in main and reviewers stop leaving those comments.

examples.title: RuleTester case
examples.output: Test run passes: 1 valid and 1 invalid case; the error message reads 'domain must not import from infra (see docs/arch#layers)'.

notes: A rule that cries wolf is disabled within a week; prefer precision over coverage.
Type-aware rules need parserOptions.project; use projectService to avoid memory blowups.
Version the plugin and changelog it; a rule change is a breaking change for every consumer.

title: Event Loop Latency in a Payments API
description: Fix a latency regression so payment API calls don't time out for customers.
overview: Fix a latency regression so payment API calls don't time out for customers.
tasks: Build a reproducer service with at least three deliberate faults: a catastrophic regex, a large JSON.parse on the main thread, and a synchronous bcrypt or crypto call.
Load test with autocannon or k6 at 2000 rps for 5 minutes and record baseline p50, p95, p99 and error rate.
Capture event loop delay with perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay and export p99 and max as metrics.
Generate a CPU flame graph with 0x or clinic flame and identify each fault by function name and percentage of time.
Take two heap snapshots 10 minutes apart or use --heap-prof to find a leak (for example an unbounded Map cache) and prove the retaining path.
Fix each fault: safe regex or RE2, move parsing to worker_threads or stream with a parser, use async crypto; one commit per fix with measured impact.
Tune the runtime: set --max-old-space-size from container memory, check GC with --trace-gc, and record pause times.
Add a regression guard: CI load test failing if p99 exceeds 150 ms or event loop delay p99 exceeds 50 ms.
Write a postmortem with timeline, root causes, graphs and the final p99 target of 100 ms or lower.

examples.title: Event loop delay probe
examples.output: Lines like: eld p99 ms 412.3 max 880.1 before the fix, and eld p99 ms 12.0 max 31.4 after. Exact values vary by machine.

notes: Averages hide blocking; always chart p99 and max of event loop delay.
Profile under realistic load; a flame graph of an idle process lies.
Worker threads cost memory and startup; pool them rather than spawning per request.

title: Express to Fastify Migration for Payments
description: Migrate a live payments API with traffic shadowing and rollback, so customers see no change.
overview: Migrate a live payments API with traffic shadowing and rollback, so customers see no change.
tasks: Inventory endpoints by traffic and risk, and plan waves: read-only first, then writes, then auth-critical.
Run old and new behind a reverse proxy; route by path with weights controlled by config, not deploys.
Implement shadow mode: mirror 10 percent of production reads to the new service and diff status, headers and body, ignoring declared volatile fields.
Target diff rate under 0.1 percent per endpoint before any cutover; log diffs with request id for replay.
Port shared middleware (auth, request id, rate limit) as a framework-agnostic core package so logic is not duplicated.
Canary each wave 1, 5, 25, 100 percent with automatic rollback if error rate rises over 0.5 percent or p99 over 20 percent worse for 5 minutes.
Verify schemas with JSON Schema validation in Fastify and compare throughput; document the measured rps and memory per instance.
Keep graceful shutdown correct: handle SIGTERM, stop accepting, drain in-flight requests within 30 seconds, close DB pools.
Done when 100 percent of traffic is on the new service for 14 days, the old code is deleted and a retrospective lists surprises.

examples.title: Shadow diff report
examples.code:
$ node tools/diff-report.js --window 1h
GET  /v1/orders/:id   samples 41200  diff 0.02%  ok
POST /v1/orders       samples  5100  diff 0.80%  BLOCK
  top diff: header content-length differs, body field createdAt precision
examples.output: Per-endpoint sample counts and diff percentages with a BLOCK flag where above the 0.1 percent gate. Numbers vary.

notes: Subtle differences hide in header casing, trailing slashes, body parser limits and error shapes; diff them all.
Never shadow non-idempotent writes against a shared database; mirror to a sandbox or stub side effects.
Keep rollback a config flip that you have rehearsed, not a redeploy.

title: npm Supply Chain for Fintech
description: Secure npm dependencies so malicious packages can't steal customer data.
overview: Secure npm dependencies so malicious packages can't steal customer data.
tasks: Enumerate dependencies for all services; report total direct and transitive counts and the top 20 packages by blast radius.
Enforce npm ci with committed lockfiles and fail CI on lockfile drift; set ignore-scripts true by default and allowlist the few packages needing install scripts.
Generate CycloneDX SBOMs per build with cdxgen or syft and store them with the artifact.
Run npm audit signatures and require provenance attestations for chosen critical packages; publish your own packages with --provenance.
Add a minimum release age (for example 7 days) in Renovate or Dependabot config so brand-new versions are not auto-merged.
Use Socket, OSV-Scanner or similar to block packages with new install scripts, network access or obfuscated code; tune to under 5 false alerts per week.
Pin to a private registry proxy (Verdaccio or Artifactory) with an allowlist and 2FA-enforced publishing for internal scope.
Run a tabletop exercise: a transitive dependency ships malware; measure time to identify affected services from SBOMs (target under 30 minutes) and to patch.
Done when every service has an SBOM, no unreviewed install scripts run, and the incident drill meets its targets.

examples.title: Install script allowlist
examples.code:
# .npmrc
ignore-scripts=true
audit-level=high
fund=false
# package.json
# "scripts": { "rebuild-allowed": "npm rebuild esbuild sharp" }
examples.output: npm ci installs without running lifecycle scripts; only the named packages are rebuilt explicitly. CI fails on high-severity advisories.

notes: Blocking every update is also a risk; balance delay with speed on real CVEs.
Transitive dependencies matter more than direct ones; track them with overrides when needed.
Rotate npm tokens and use trusted publishing; stolen maintainer tokens are the usual entry.

title: Profile a Go Payments Service
description: Cut CPU and tail latency of a Go payments service so customers' payments finish quickly.
overview: Cut CPU and tail latency of a Go payments service so customers' payments finish quickly.
tasks: Expose net/http/pprof on an internal port and capture 30-second CPU, heap (inuse and alloc), goroutine, mutex and block profiles under load.
Record a baseline with a reproducible benchmark and a load generator (vegeta or k6) with fixed rps and duration.
Use go tool pprof -top and -http to identify the top 5 allocation sites and CPU consumers.
Reduce allocations: sync.Pool for buffers, preallocated slices, avoiding fmt in hot paths, strings.Builder; prove with go test -bench -benchmem and benchstat (p under 0.05).
Run go build -gcflags='-m' to find avoidable heap escapes and fix at least three.
Use runtime/trace to find scheduler latency and GC assist; tune GOGC and set GOMEMLIMIT to 80 percent of the container limit.
Find and fix one goroutine leak with the goroutine profile and a goleak test.
Enable Profile-Guided Optimisation with a default.pgo from production and record the gain.
Done when targets are met in a load test and benchstat tables for each change are in the PR descriptions.

examples.title: benchstat comparison
examples.code:
$ go test -bench=Encode -benchmem -count=10 > new.txt
$ benchstat old.txt new.txt
examples.output:
name      old time/op  new time/op  delta
Encode-8  2.41us +-2%  0.93us +-1%  -61.4% (p=0.000 n=10+10)
name      old allocs/op new allocs/op
Encode-8  14.0 +-0%     2.0 +-0%   -85.7%
Exact numbers vary.

notes: Always benchstat with count 10 or more; single runs are noise.
sync.Pool can slow things down; keep it only with a benchmark that proves the win.
GOMEMLIMIT without GOGC thinking can cause GC thrash near the limit; watch gc CPU share.

title: Race-Free Go Ledger
description: Eliminate races and leaks in a concurrent Go ledger so balances are never wrong.
overview: Eliminate races and leaks in a concurrent Go ledger so balances are never wrong.
tasks: Run the full test suite with go test -race -count=20 in CI and fix every report.
Add goleak.VerifyTestMain to all packages and fix leaks until zero.
Propagate context through every call; each external call has a deadline and each goroutine has an owner that waits for it (errgroup with SetLimit).
Implement backpressure: bounded channels and a load-shedding middleware returning 429 or 503 when queue depth exceeds a set limit; show behaviour at 3x capacity.
Add a circuit breaker and retry with jittered exponential backoff and a retry budget (at most 10 percent extra load).
Write native Go fuzz tests for the parsers and a model-based test for the cache; run 10 minutes in CI nightly.
Inject faults (latency, errors, timeouts) with a toxiproxy or custom RoundTripper and verify SLO: 99.5 percent success with one dependency down.
Implement graceful shutdown with a 30-second drain and test it with SIGTERM under load, asserting zero dropped requests.
Document the concurrency model: which goroutines exist, who owns each lock, and lock ordering.

examples.title: Leak test and bounded group
examples.output: go test -race passes with no DATA RACE output and no 'found unexpected goroutines' failure; at most 8 fetches run concurrently.

notes: Closing a channel from the receiver side is a design smell; define a single owner.
Unbounded retries amplify outages; budgets matter more than backoff shape.
A passing race detector only covers executed paths; stress tests with GOMAXPROCS variation help.

title: Finance Platform Library and CLI
description: Build the shared Go toolkit many payment services use, so fintechs stay consistent.
overview: Build the shared Go toolkit many payment services use, so fintechs stay consistent.
tasks: Design a minimal API: one New(ctx, opts...) function using functional options; document stability promises for each package.
Provide structured logging via log/slog, Prometheus metrics, and OpenTelemetry tracing with sane defaults and a standard set of RED metrics.
Build a service template CLI using cobra that scaffolds a service with health endpoints, Dockerfile, CI and dashboards; scaffolding time under 1 minute.
Version with semantic import versioning; use apidiff or gorelease in CI to reject accidental breaking changes.
Reach 85 percent test coverage with example tests that appear in godoc and are executed.
Provide a migration tool (go fix style codemod using go/ast) for one breaking change and run it over 10 sample repos.
Measure adoption: instrument the CLI with anonymous version telemetry and track services on latest-minus-1 or newer.
Run an RFC process for API additions and onboard two external contributors from other teams.
Done when 20 services use it, mean new-service setup time falls from days to under an hour, and no breaking release happens without a codemod.

examples.title: gorelease gate
examples.code:
$ gorelease -base=v1.4.0
github.com/acme/platform/httpx
-----------------------
Incompatible changes:
- Server.Start: changed from func() error to func(context.Context) error
Suggested version: v2.0.0 (incompatible changes)
examples.output: CI job fails with the incompatible change list unless the PR bumps the major version and includes a codemod.

notes: Every exported identifier is a promise; export less.
Avoid wrapping the standard library in clever abstractions; thin helpers age better.
Dependency count of the library is felt by every consumer; keep go.mod small.

title: Tune Java Payments GC
description: Diagnose pauses in a Java payments service and tune GC so checkouts don't stall.
overview: Diagnose pauses in a Java payments service and tune GC so checkouts don't stall.
tasks: Enable unified GC logging (-Xlog:gc*:file=gc.log) and analyse with GCViewer or GCeasy; report pause p99, throughput and allocation rate.
Capture a JFR recording (jcmd JFR.start, 5 minutes) and inspect allocation hot spots, lock contention and safepoints in JDK Mission Control.
Find a leak using a heap dump (jcmd GC.heap_dump) in Eclipse MAT; present the dominator tree and the GC root path.
Compare G1 with ZGC (generational) and Shenandoah on the same load with at least 3 runs each; table of pause p99, CPU overhead and RSS.
Set container-aware flags: -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70, -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError and verify no OOMKill under load.
Reduce allocation rate by 50 percent (primitive collections, avoid boxing, reuse buffers) and verify with JMH benchmarks (fork 3, warmup 5).
Check native memory with NMT (-XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary) and explain the gap between heap and RSS.
Run a 72-hour soak at production-like load and prove memory plateau with a graph.
Deliver a tuning runbook listing each flag, why it was chosen and how to roll back.

examples.title: Unified GC log excerpt
examples.code:
[12.345s][info][gc] GC(87) Pause Young (Normal) (G1 Evacuation Pause) 3412M->1210M(4096M) 38.211ms
[40.100s][info][gc] GC(101) Pause Full (G1 Compaction Pause) 3980M->3901M(4096M) 1480.7ms
examples.output: The first line is healthy; the second (a Full GC with almost nothing freed) is the signature of a leak and the cause of your 600 ms p99. Values vary.

notes: Do not copy flags from blog posts; every flag needs a measurement.
Heap is not the whole process: metaspace, threads, direct buffers and code cache add up.
ZGC trades CPU and memory for pauses; check you have headroom first.

title: Strangler Migration of a Banking Monolith
description: Decompose a banking monolith into services while customers keep banking.
overview: Decompose a banking monolith into services while customers keep banking.
tasks: Map the monolith with jdeps and ArchUnit tests to find the pricing boundary; list inbound and outbound dependencies and cycles.
Introduce an anti-corruption layer inside the monolith first (interface plus adapter), so callers use the seam before any network call exists.
Implement the new Spring Boot service and route via feature flag with percentage rollout and per-tenant override.
Migrate data with dual-write or change data capture (Debezium to Kafka); verify with a reconciliation job reporting row-level mismatches, target under 0.001 percent before cutover.
Run in shadow mode comparing prices from old and new for 2 weeks; investigate every mismatch category.
Define a contract with consumer-driven tests (Pact) and an OpenAPI spec; both sides run them in CI.
Set SLOs for the new service (99.9 percent availability, p99 under 150 ms) and add timeouts, bulkheads (Resilience4j) and fallbacks.
Rehearse rollback twice: flip the flag and prove no data loss when reverting.
Done when 100 percent of traffic and writes are on the new service for 30 days and the old tables are archived.

examples.title: ArchUnit boundary test
examples.output: Test passes when no outside class touches pricing internals; a violation lists each offending class and line, failing the build.

notes: Share-nothing data is the goal; a shared database makes a distributed monolith.
Reconciliation tooling is more valuable than the cutover plan.
Keep the seam in the monolith even after migration until rollback risk is gone.

title: Readiness Review for Banking Java Services
description: Load-test Java banking services so they hold up during salary days and tax deadlines.
overview: Load-test Java banking services so they hold up during salary days and tax deadlines.
tasks: Write a readiness checklist of at least 25 items (timeouts, pool sizes, health probes, graceful shutdown, dashboards, alerts) each with a pass test.
Load test with Gatling to find the knee: ramp to failure, record rps at which p99 exceeds the SLO, and compute headroom against peak forecast (target 2x).
Size connection pools with measured numbers: HikariCP maximumPoolSize from Little's law and DB limits; show wait-time metric near zero at peak.
Enable virtual threads (Java 21) on one service and compare with platform threads at 10k concurrent requests; document pinning issues found via jdk.tracePinnedThreads.
Run chaos tests: kill a pod, add 500 ms latency to a dependency, fill disk; verify graceful degradation and alerts firing within 2 minutes.
Instrument with Micrometer and OpenTelemetry; dashboards for RED metrics plus JVM, with SLO burn-rate alerts (14.4x over 1 hour).
Verify startup and shutdown: readiness only after warm-up, 30-second drain with zero failed requests during rolling deploy.
Publish a scorecard for the three services and track findings to closure.
Done when all three pass the checklist and the review is adopted as a launch gate.

examples.title: Little's law pool sizing
examples.code:
peak = 800 req/s, avg DB time = 15 ms, DB calls per request = 2
concurrent connections = 800 * 2 * 0.015 = 24
maximumPoolSize = 24 * 1.5 headroom = 36
examples.output: HikariCP pool of about 36 per instance; verify hikaricp.connections.pending stays near 0 under the load test. Re-derive for your numbers.

notes: Bigger pools usually make databases slower; size from measurement.
Missing timeouts are the most common root cause of cascading failures.
Virtual threads do not fix synchronized blocks that pin carriers on older JDKs.

title: Audit a Money Crate's Unsafe Code
description: Verify a money crate's unsafe code so financial libraries don't crash or leak data.
overview: Verify a money crate's unsafe code so financial libraries don't crash or leak data.
tasks: Inventory unsafe blocks with cargo geiger and justify each; remove at least 30 percent by safe rewrites.
Add a SAFETY comment on every unsafe block stating the invariant, who upholds it and why it holds; enforce with clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks.
Run the test suite under Miri (cargo +nightly miri test) with -Zmiri-strict-provenance and fix all undefined behaviour reports.
Model concurrent code with loom, exploring at least 3 interleaving scenarios (push-pop race, ABA, shutdown) with LOOM_MAX_PREEMPTIONS set.
Fuzz public APIs with cargo-fuzz or libFuzzer for 30 minutes, with AddressSanitizer enabled; commit the corpus and fix any crash.
Use property tests (proptest) comparing the structure with a std reference model across 10k random operation sequences.
Encapsulate unsafe behind a minimal module so the safe API cannot be misused; add compile_fail doctests for misuse.
Optionally prove one function with Kani and report the harness and result.
Done when Miri, loom and fuzz jobs are green in CI and a short audit report lists remaining unsafe with rationale.

examples.title: Miri catching a violation
examples.code:
$ MIRIFLAGS="-Zmiri-strict-provenance" cargo +nightly miri test
error: Undefined Behavior: attempting a read access using <2891> at alloc1042[0x0], but that tag does not exist in the borrow stack
examples.output: Failing output pinpoints the offending line (Stacked or Tree Borrows violation). After the fix: test result: ok. N passed. Tags vary.

notes: Miri only checks executed paths; pair it with fuzzing for coverage.
Soundness means no safe caller can trigger UB, not that your own callers behave.
Loom explodes combinatorially; keep models tiny.

title: Rust Hot Path for Pricing
description: Replace a slow pricing component with Rust so quotes load fast for shoppers.
overview: Replace a slow pricing component with Rust so quotes load fast for shoppers.
tasks: Profile the existing service and show the component accounts for at least 40 percent of CPU; record the baseline with a reproducible benchmark.
Define a narrow interface and golden test corpus of at least 10k real inputs with expected outputs captured from the old implementation.
Implement in Rust using criterion benchmarks; target 5x throughput and 50 percent lower memory.
Run differential testing and cargo-fuzz comparing old and new outputs; zero mismatches over 1 hour fuzz.
Bridge with PyO3 or napi-rs or a C ABI via cbindgen; release the GIL or run off the main thread where applicable; measure FFI overhead.
Build prebuilt wheels or binaries for linux x86_64 and aarch64 and macOS in CI with cargo-zigbuild or cross.
Roll out behind a flag with shadow comparison for one week, then 5, 50, 100 percent; keep the old path for rollback for 30 days.
Report CPU saving in cores and money, p99 change and incident count.
Done when production metrics confirm the target and the team can maintain the crate (docs, CI, owner).

examples.title: Criterion result shape
examples.output: Time and throughput with confidence intervals and percent change versus the saved baseline. Values vary with hardware.

notes: FFI boundaries can erase the win; batch calls to amortise crossing costs.
Maintenance burden is the real cost; ensure two people can own the crate.
Do not rewrite what you cannot benchmark.

title: Publish a Money Crate
description: Maintain an open-source money crate with stable APIs so developers handle money correctly.
overview: Maintain an open-source money crate with stable APIs so developers handle money correctly.
tasks: Design the public API with the Rust API Guidelines checklist; keep types non-exhaustive where growth is expected (#[non_exhaustive]) and seal traits that must not be implemented externally.
Support no_std plus alloc via feature flags; test builds for thumbv7em-none-eabihf in CI.
Declare and test an MSRV with cargo-msrv; policy: raise only in minor releases and document it.
Run cargo-semver-checks in CI to block accidental breaking changes; use cargo-deny for licences and advisories.
Write docs with runnable examples (cargo test --doc), a crate-level overview and docs.rs metadata for all features.
Reach 90 percent line coverage (cargo-llvm-cov) and add benchmarks with criterion tracked per release.
Automate releases with release-plz or cargo-release, signed tags and a CHANGELOG following Keep a Changelog.
Triage issues with labels, reply within 72 hours, and merge at least 3 external pull requests with review feedback.
Done when the crate has a 1.0 release plan, passes all CI jobs and has at least 3 dependents.

examples.title: semver-checks failure
examples.code:
$ cargo semver-checks check-release
--- failure enum_variant_added: enum variant added on exhaustive enum ---
Description: A publicly-visible enum without #[non_exhaustive] had a variant added.
examples.output: CI fails with the lint name, description and affected item until you bump the major version or mark the enum non_exhaustive.

notes: Adding a trait method or enum variant is breaking unless planned for.
Features must be additive; never use features to remove functionality.
Minimise public dependencies; re-exporting them couples your semver to theirs.

title: Memory Safety in a Banking C Codebase
description: Harden a C banking codebase until memory bugs stop, so customers' data is not exposed.
overview: Harden a C banking codebase until memory bugs stop, so customers' data is not exposed.
tasks: Build with -fsanitize=address,undefined and run all tests; fix every report, tracking counts in a table.
Write at least 5 libFuzzer or AFL++ harnesses for parsers with seed corpora and dictionaries; run 24 hours total and reach 85 percent edge coverage of parser code (llvm-cov).
Run MemorySanitizer on an instrumented build to catch uninitialised reads, and TSan on threaded code.
Run clang-tidy (clang-analyzer, bugprone), cppcheck and CodeQL; triage findings and keep a suppression file with reasons.
Add -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, -fstack-protector-strong, -fPIE -pie, -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now, and CFI where supported; verify with checksec.
Replace unsafe patterns (strcpy, sprintf, manual length arithmetic) with bounded helpers and integer overflow checks via __builtin_mul_overflow.
Triage each crash into a regression test with minimised input (afl-tmin) so it never returns.
Integrate fuzzing in CI (short run per PR) and OSS-Fuzz-style continuous fuzzing nightly.
Done when 7 consecutive days of fuzzing find no new crashes and all sanitizers are green.

examples.title: ASan report and fix
examples.code:
==4121==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x60200000eff4
READ of size 4 at 0x60200000eff4 thread T0
    #0 0x4f1a2b in parse_chunk src/png.c:212
examples.output: Report names the bug class, access size and source line. After the fix plus regression test: all tests pass with no sanitizer output.

notes: Fuzzers need good seeds and structure-aware dictionaries; blind fuzzing plateaus.
Sanitizer builds must run the whole test suite, not just examples.
Integer overflow in size calculations causes most heap overflows; check at the allocation site.

title: Lock-Free Ledger Component
description: Build a lock-free ledger component so transactions stay fast under heavy load.
overview: Build a lock-free ledger component so transactions stay fast under heavy load.
tasks: Implement with stdatomic.h using explicit memory orders (acquire/release, not seq_cst by default) and document the happens-before argument for each atomic.
Pad hot fields to 64-byte cache lines (alignas(64)) to avoid false sharing; show throughput before and after.
Test with ThreadSanitizer and a stress test of 8 threads and 100 million operations checking no loss or duplication via checksums.
Model-check the algorithm with a small harness in CDSChecker or GenMC, or Relacy, for at least 2 producers and 2 consumers.
Benchmark scaling from 1 to 16 threads and plot throughput and p99 latency; use pinned threads (pthread_setaffinity_np).
Use perf stat to report cycles, instructions, cache-misses and branch-misses per operation; use perf c2c to find contended lines.
Compare with a mutex-plus-condvar baseline and state when lock-free is not better.
Port the test to ARM64 (or use QEMU) and fix ordering bugs that only appear on weak memory models.
Done when throughput target holds with TSan clean and a design note explains every ordering choice.

examples.title: perf stat output shape
examples.code:
$ perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses,LLC-load-misses ./qbench -t 4
 8,412,331,009  cycles
11,030,447,812  instructions  # 1.31 insn per cycle
    18,223,401  cache-misses
examples.output: Counters per run; derive instructions per op and misses per op by dividing by total operations. Numbers vary with CPU.

notes: x86 hides ordering bugs that ARM exposes; test on both.
The ABA problem needs tagged pointers or hazard-pointer style reclamation.
Measure contention with real thread counts; single-thread benchmarks lie.

title: Portable Payments C Library
description: Release a C payments library with a stable ABI so card terminals across devices accept payments.
overview: Release a C payments library with a stable ABI so card terminals across devices accept payments.
tasks: Design an opaque-handle API (typedef struct foo foo) with explicit create and destroy, error codes and no exported globals; document ownership for every pointer.
Hide internal symbols with -fvisibility=hidden and an export macro; verify with nm -D that only intended symbols exist.
Use a linker version script and SONAME versioning (libfoo.so.1.2.0); document the ABI promise.
Check ABI compatibility between releases with abidiff (libabigail) or abi-compliance-checker in CI.
Build with CMake producing static, shared and pkg-config files; test on gcc, clang, MSVC and musl.
Provide thread-safety documentation and custom allocator hooks.
Generate bindings for Python (cffi or ctypes) and Rust (bindgen) and test them in CI.
Publish SECURITY.md, a CVE handling process with 90-day disclosure, and signed release tarballs with checksums.
Done when a v1.1 drop-in replaces v1.0 for a compiled test client with zero abidiff errors.

examples.title: abidiff gate
examples.code:
$ abidw libfoo.so.1.0.0 > v1.xml; abidw libfoo.so.1.1.0 > v11.xml
$ abidiff v1.xml v11.xml
Functions changes summary: 0 Removed, 0 Changed, 2 Added functions
examples.output: Exit status 0 means compatible additions only. A removed or changed function prints details and returns a nonzero code, failing the release job.

notes: Struct layout is ABI; never expose structs you may extend.
Windows needs explicit export macros and separate CRT considerations.
Provide a size field or version in extensible structs passed by pointer.

title: Smaller Trading Engine Builds
description: Cut a trading engine's build time and size so updates reach investors quickly.
overview: Cut a trading engine's build time and size so updates reach investors quickly.
tasks: Measure first: use clang -ftime-trace and ClangBuildAnalyzer to list the top 20 slowest headers and templates; record baseline clean and incremental times.
Reduce include cost with include-what-you-use, forward declarations and splitting heavy headers; verify with ftime-trace deltas.
Introduce precompiled headers or unity builds selectively (CMake target_precompile_headers, UNITY_BUILD batches) and measure.
Cache compilation with ccache or sccache backed by a remote store; target 90 percent hit rate on CI.
Use Ninja, a faster linker (lld or mold) and parallelism matched to cores; measure link time reduction.
Cut template bloat with explicit instantiation (extern template) and type erasure in hot headers.
Shrink binary: -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections with --gc-sections, -fvisibility=hidden, LTO (thin), strip; use bloaty to attribute size.
Add a CI budget check failing PRs that regress build time by over 5 percent or add over 1 MB to binary.
Done when targets are met and the guide lets teams reproduce the measurements.

examples.title: bloaty and time-trace
examples.code:
$ bloaty app -d compileunits -n 5
    FILE SIZE        VM SIZE
 22.1%  66.3Mi  21.9%  58.0Mi  src/engine/serializer.cpp
examples.output: A ranked table of size per translation unit; template-heavy files usually top it. After optimisation the total shrinks by the target percent.

notes: Never optimise without a trace; the slow header is rarely the one you suspect.
Unity builds can break anonymous-namespace assumptions; roll out per target.
ccache needs deterministic builds: strip __DATE__, use relative paths.

title: Modernise a Banking Core in C++
description: Modernise a legacy banking core to C++20 so customers' balances are calculated safely.
overview: Modernise a legacy banking core to C++20 so customers' balances are calculated safely.
tasks: Set a baseline: sanitizer failures, clang-tidy warnings and compile time in a dashboard.
Enable -Wall -Wextra -Wconversion -Werror on new code and a warning ratchet on old code.
Run clang-tidy modernize-* checks with fix (use-nullptr, use-override, make-unique, use-auto) in batches of at most 500 lines per PR, verified by tests.
Replace raw owning pointers with unique_ptr or shared_ptr after ownership analysis; list lifetimes in a design doc for 5 key classes.
Replace pointer plus length pairs with std::span and string_view, and add bounds checks via hardened libc++ or _GLIBCXX_ASSERTIONS.
Introduce concepts and constexpr to replace SFINAE in the top 10 templates and compare compile errors.
Run ASan, UBSan, TSan on the full suite in CI and fix every report; track counts to zero.
Add a style and ownership guide, plus code review checklist, and run a lunch-and-learn.
Done when the project builds as C++20 with warnings as errors, sanitizers are clean and crash rate in production drops measurably.

examples.title: clang-tidy batch
examples.code:
$ run-clang-tidy -p build -checks='-*,modernize-use-nullptr,modernize-make-unique' -fix src/net/
$ ctest --test-dir build -j8
examples.output: Fixes applied across src/net with a summary of changed files; ctest reports 100 percent tests passed. Review the diff before commit.

notes: Automated fixes need strong tests first; build characterization tests for untested code.
shared_ptr everywhere hides design problems and costs atomics.
Mixed ABI between standard versions can break linking; modernise leaf libraries first.

title: Low-Latency Trading Component
description: Cut tail latency in a trading component so retail investors' orders execute fast.
overview: Cut tail latency in a trading component so retail investors' orders execute fast.
tasks: Create a replayable benchmark with captured input and a harness recording latency in an HdrHistogram; report p50, p99, p99.9 and max.
Profile with perf record -g and flame graphs; use perf stat to measure IPC, L1 and LLC misses, and branch mispredicts.
Convert array-of-structs to struct-of-arrays for the hot loop and show cache-miss reduction.
Remove allocations from the hot path using arena or pool allocators and pre-sized containers; verify zero mallocs with ltrace or a malloc hook counter.
Eliminate false sharing and lock contention; replace mutexes with SPSC ring buffers where producers and consumers are known.
Pin threads, isolate cores (isolcpus, nohz_full), disable frequency scaling and set huge pages; document the machine configuration.
Use compiler help: -O2/-O3, PGO, LTO, __builtin_expect only where measured, and check assembly on Compiler Explorer.
Add a performance regression test in CI using Google Benchmark with a threshold and noise handling.
Done when p99.9 is under 10 microseconds over a 1-hour run with a report of each change's effect.

examples.title: Latency histogram shape
examples.code:
samples 50000000  min 1.8us  p50 3.1us  p99 6.4us  p99.9 9.2us  max 41.0us
max outlier traced to: page fault at first touch of arena
examples.output: A percentile summary from HdrHistogram. Outliers should be explained (page faults, interrupts); values vary by hardware.

notes: Pre-fault memory (mlock, touch pages) before the timed section.
Coordinated omission: record intended send time, not actual, or tails look better than reality.
Microbenchmarks that fit in L1 cache overstate gains; use production-sized data.

title: Legacy PHP Payments Portal Upgrade
description: Upgrade a large payments portal across major versions so customers can keep paying.
overview: Upgrade a large payments portal across major versions so customers can keep paying.
tasks: Add characterization tests for the top 20 revenue-critical flows (PHPUnit or Pest) before touching code; target 60 percent coverage on those modules.
Install PHPStan at level 0 and generate a baseline; raise to level 6 module by module using a ratchet in CI.
Run Rector with sets for PHP 7.4 to 8.3, typed properties, constructor promotion and match; land in small PRs per directory.
Use PHPCompatibility via PHP_CodeSniffer to list breaking items (removed functions, each()/create_function, dynamic property deprecations) and fix them.
Run the app on both versions in CI matrix, then in production behind a header or percentage-based split for 2 weeks.
Compare performance: requests per second and p95 before and after (8.x with OPcache and JIT tuning), and memory.
Upgrade Composer dependencies; replace abandoned packages found via composer outdated and composer audit.
Configure OPcache (opcache.validate_timestamps=0, preload where useful) and verify in production.
Done when production runs 8.3, PHPStan level 6 passes without a baseline growing, and error rate is flat.

examples.title: PHPStan baseline ratchet
examples.code:
$ vendor/bin/phpstan analyse -c phpstan.neon --level=6 --generate-baseline
$ vendor/bin/rector process src --dry-run --config=rector.php
examples.output: PHPStan reports N errors written to phpstan-baseline.neon; Rector prints a diff of proposed changes per file and a summary of applied rules.

notes: Dynamic properties and implicit nullable params produce deprecations on 8.x; fix before the cutover.
Do not combine a framework upgrade and a PHP upgrade in one step.
Check extensions and PECL packages early; they set your upgrade ceiling.

title: PHP Checkout Scaling
description: Scale a PHP checkout 10x with caching and queues so shoppers can pay on busy days.
overview: Scale a PHP checkout 10x with caching and queues so shoppers can pay on busy days.
tasks: Profile with Blackfire or Xdebug plus SPX and identify top 10 slow endpoints and N+1 queries (laravel-debugbar or Doctrine profiler).
Fix N+1 with eager loading and add indexes; verify with EXPLAIN that the top 10 queries use indexes and have under 50 ms p95.
Layer caching: OPcache and preload, Redis application cache with tag invalidation, HTTP cache with Varnish or CDN using stale-while-revalidate.
Move slow work (email, image processing, webhooks) to queues with Horizon or Symfony Messenger and idempotent jobs.
Tune PHP-FPM (pm.max_children from memory per worker) or switch to Swoole/RoadRunner/FrankenPHP worker mode and compare throughput.
Add read replicas and connection pooling (ProxySQL); route reads and keep read-your-writes where needed.
Load test with k6 to 3000 rps with realistic mix and a ramp; define pass criteria: error rate under 0.5 percent, p95 under 300 ms.
Build a degradation plan: feature flags to turn off recommendations, queue-based checkout throttling.
Done when the flash-sale rehearsal passes and a capacity table shows servers needed per 1000 rps.

examples.title: FPM sizing
examples.code:
memory for PHP = 8 GB, avg worker RSS = 60 MB
pm.max_children = (8192 * 0.8) / 60 = 109
pm = static, pm.max_children = 100, pm.max_requests = 1000
examples.output: About 100 workers per 8 GB host. Confirm with the FPM status page that listen queue stays 0 and no 'max_children reached' log lines appear.

notes: Cache stampedes will take down the database; use locks or early recomputation.
Worker-mode runtimes leak state between requests; audit static and singleton usage.
Measure with production-like data volume; indexes behave differently at 50M rows.

title: PHP Security Review for Payments
description: Review a payments site against OWASP risks so customer data is protected.
overview: Review a payments site against OWASP risks so customer data is protected.
tasks: Create a threat model (STRIDE) with a data flow diagram listing at least 15 threats and mitigations.
Run static analysis with Psalm taint analysis and PHPStan security rules; fix all tainted-sink findings (SQL, shell, file path, HTML).
Run OWASP ZAP and sqlmap against a staging copy; triage findings with severity and fix all high ones.
Replace string-built SQL with prepared statements everywhere; show a failing injection test turned passing.

Harden sessions and auth: Argon2id via password_hash, session.cookie_secure, httponly, samesite=Lax or Strict, session id regeneration on login, CSRF tokens, rate limiting on login (5 attempts per 15 minutes).
Secure uploads: validate MIME with finfo, randomise names, store outside webroot, and disable script execution in the upload directory.
Add headers: CSP with nonces, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy; verify with securityheaders.com style scan or a test.
Ban unserialize on untrusted data; use JSON and allowed_classes false if unavoidable.
Done when security tests run in CI, composer audit is clean and a report maps each finding to a fix and test.

examples.title: Injection regression test
examples.output: PHPUnit: OK (1 test, 2 assertions). Before the fix the same test returned every row and failed.

notes: Escape on output for the correct context (HTML, attribute, JS, URL); one function does not fit all.
Type juggling bugs (== versus ===, magic hashes) still matter; use strict comparison and hash_equals.
Keep secrets out of the repo and phpinfo pages out of production.

title: Rails Upgrade for a Banking Monolith
description: Upgrade a banking Rails app with zero downtime so customers keep access to accounts.
overview: Upgrade a banking Rails app with zero downtime so customers keep access to accounts.
tasks: Establish a baseline: green test suite, flaky test list (fix those over 1 percent failure rate), and coverage on critical paths.
Dual-boot with the next_rails or bootboot gem so CI runs the suite on current and next Rails; hop one minor at a time (5.2, 6.0, 6.1, 7.0, 7.1).
Fix deprecations using ActiveSupport::Deprecation behavior raise in test and a deprecation tracker (deprecation_toolkit) ratcheting to zero.
Upgrade Ruby separately from Rails; use rubocop-rails and rubocop-performance plus keyword argument fixes for Ruby 3 (check with ruby -W:deprecated).
Audit gems with bundle outdated and next_rails --outdated; replace abandoned gems and record decisions.
Run the new version in production on 1 canary host, then 10, 50, 100 percent; compare error rate, p95 and memory.
Enable YJIT on Ruby 3.3 and report latency and memory change.
Keep the load_defaults in new_framework_defaults until each flag is tested individually.
Done when production is on the target versions for 30 days, dual-boot is removed and the upgrade playbook is published.

examples.title: Dual-boot commands
examples.code:
$ bundle exec next_rails --outdated
$ BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bundle exec rspec
$ DEPRECATION_TRACKER=save bundle exec rspec
examples.output: Outdated gems with compatibility notes; the suite result on the next Rails; and a saved deprecation count file that CI compares each run. Counts vary.

notes: One hop at a time; skipping versions multiplies unknowns.
Rails defaults changes (cookies, serialisers) can invalidate sessions; plan the rollout.
Fix flaky tests first or you cannot tell regressions from noise.

title: Rails Scale for Transactions
description: Keep a Rails transactions app fast at 500M rows so statements load on time.
overview: Keep a Rails transactions app fast at 500M rows so statements load on time.
tasks: Adopt strong_migrations to block unsafe operations in CI and teach the safe alternatives.
Add indexes concurrently (algorithm: :concurrently in Postgres, disable_ddl_transaction!) and validate foreign keys and NOT NULL constraints in two steps.
Backfill 500M rows with batched jobs (in_batches of 10k, throttled to keep replica lag under 2 seconds and DB CPU under 60 percent), resumable and idempotent; use the maintenance_tasks gem.
Run a column type change safely: add new column, dual write, backfill, verify, switch reads, drop old column across at least 3 deploys.
Find slow queries with pg_stat_statements and EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS); fix the top 10 and show p95 improvement.
Eliminate N+1 with bullet in test env and prosopite, enforcing zero in CI.
Introduce read replicas using Rails multiple databases with automatic role switching and delay-based fallback; test replica lag handling.
Partition one time-series table by month (declarative partitioning) with a retention job; show query plan using partition pruning.
Done when all changes ship without incident, with a runbook for each migration pattern.

examples.title: Safe index and backfill
examples.code:
class AddIndexToOrdersUserId < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.1]
  disable_ddl_transaction!
  def change
    add_index :orders, :user_id, algorithm: :concurrently, if_not_exists: true
  end
end
# backfill
Order.in_batches(of: 10_000) { |b| b.update_all('total_cents = total * 100'); sleep 0.05 }
examples.output: Migration runs without an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on orders; backfill progress logs batches. Duration varies; replica lag stays within the limit.

notes: Concurrent index builds can fail and leave invalid indexes; check pg_index.indisvalid.
Updating millions of rows in one transaction bloats the table and replicas; batch and vacuum.
Application code must tolerate both schema versions during each deploy.

title: Money Gem for Financial Calculations
description: Maintain a Ruby gem for financial calculations that many apps depend on for correct interest.
overview: Maintain a Ruby gem for financial calculations that many apps depend on for correct interest.
tasks: Design a small public API with one clear entry point; keep dependencies to zero or one, and document every public method with YARD.
Test against Ruby 3.1 to 3.4 and Rails 6.1 to 7.2 with Appraisal and a GitHub Actions matrix; also test on JRuby or TruffleRuby if feasible.
Reach 95 percent coverage with simplecov; use RSpec and add property-style tests for edge cases.
Lint with RuboCop and publish with rubygems MFA required (metadata rubygems_mfa_required true) and trusted publishing from CI.
Follow semver; keep a CHANGELOG, deprecate with warnings for at least one minor before removal.
Benchmark with benchmark-ips and memory_profiler; document overhead per call (target under 5 microseconds).
Run bundler-audit and Dependabot; publish a SECURITY.md with a private reporting channel.
Triage issues within 72 hours, merge 3 external pull requests and credit contributors.
Done when version 1.0.0 is released, has at least 3 downstream users and CI is green across the matrix.

examples.title: Appraisal matrix
examples.code:
# Appraisals
appraise 'rails-6-1' do
  gem 'rails', '~> 6.1.0'
end
appraise 'rails-7-2' do
  gem 'rails', '~> 7.2.0'
end
examples.output: Run bundle exec appraisal rspec: the suite executes once per appraisal, each in its own gemfile, and the CI job fails if any version fails.

notes: Monkey patching others' classes is the main source of breakage; prefer composition and Module#prepend with care.
Your supported-versions policy is part of the API; state it in the README.
A gem name and MFA on your account are security-critical; supply chain attacks target maintainers.

title: Coroutine Review for a Payments Backend
description: Harden a Kotlin payments backend for cancellation correctness so payments aren't half-finished.
overview: Harden a Kotlin payments backend for cancellation correctness so payments aren't half-finished.
tasks: Search for GlobalScope, runBlocking in suspend paths and unscoped launches; replace with structured scopes tied to a lifecycle and a SupervisorJob where appropriate.
Fix swallowed cancellation: never catch Exception without rethrowing CancellationException; add a detekt rule or custom lint for it.
Make dispatchers injectable and replace Dispatchers.IO misuse (blocking calls on Default); limit parallelism with limitedParallelism.
Replace unbounded channels and buffers with explicit capacity and overflow strategy (BufferOverflow.DROP_OLDEST or SUSPEND); show behaviour at 10x producer rate.
Write deterministic tests with kotlinx-coroutines-test (runTest, virtual time, StandardTestDispatcher) including cancellation and timeout cases; at least 20 tests.
Use Turbine to test Flow emissions and verify no leaked collectors with a scope-check helper.
Add timeouts (withTimeout) and retry with exponential backoff to every external call, with exceptions mapped to typed errors.
Use debug probes (DebugProbes.install) and a thread dump to find one stuck coroutine and document the diagnosis.
Done when detekt is clean, no GlobalScope remains and a load test shows no coroutine count growth over 1 hour.

examples.title: Virtual-time cancellation test
examples.output: Test passes instantly because virtual time skips the delay; a leaked or uncancelled child would leave the test hanging or fail with UncompletedCoroutinesError.

notes: supervisorScope and SupervisorJob change error propagation; choose deliberately.
Context switching has cost; do not wrap cheap work in withContext.
StateFlow conflates equal values; use SharedFlow for events.

title: Shared Payment Logic With Kotlin Multiplatform
description: Share payment logic between Android, iOS and backend so customers get the same rules everywhere.
overview: Share payment logic between Android, iOS and backend so customers get the same rules everywhere.
tasks: Define the shared module boundary using clean architecture; shared code has no platform imports and platform APIs are reached through expect/actual or interfaces.
Use Ktor client, kotlinx.serialization, SQLDelight and kotlinx-datetime; run the same test suite on JVM, iOS simulator and JS if relevant.
Expose Swift-friendly APIs: avoid generic leaking, use SKIE or sealed class wrappers, and test from a Swift unit test.
Distribute as an XCFramework via Swift Package Manager and as an AAR; automate in CI producing both artifacts.
Measure binary size impact and cold-start time; target under 2 MB growth for iOS and under 50 ms startup cost.
Handle iOS memory model and threading: verify no freezes or leaks in Instruments.
Roll out feature by feature with a flag and compare crash-free rate and parity metrics against native implementations.
Write an ADR with costs, risks and exit strategy; train iOS engineers on reading Kotlin.
Done when at least 3 features ship on both platforms with equal or better crash-free rate and 30 percent less duplicated logic.

examples.title: Shared module layout
examples.output: Same call site in common code on both platforms; ./gradlew allTests runs the shared tests per target and reports pass/fail for each.

notes: Calls through Objective-C export lose generics and nullability detail; design the API for it.
Keep the shared layer thin enough that mobile engineers can still change it.
Build times grow quickly; use Gradle build cache and configuration cache.

title: Gradle Build for a Fintech App
description: Speed up and standardise the build of a Kotlin fintech app so fixes ship faster.
overview: Speed up and standardise the build of a Kotlin fintech app so fixes ship faster.
tasks: Collect a baseline with Gradle build scans and --profile; list slowest tasks and configuration time.
Enable configuration cache, build cache (remote, with read-only for local) and parallel execution; target 80 percent cache hit on CI.
Move build logic to included builds with convention plugins (build-logic), replacing allprojects and subprojects blocks.
Centralise versions in libs.versions.toml with a dependency lock or verification-metadata.xml for supply chain integrity.
Migrate kapt to KSP where libraries support it; measure the time saved per module.
Fix cache misses by making tasks relocatable and inputs declared (@PathSensitive, @CacheableTask); verify with --scan comparison of two builds.
Enable Kotlin incremental compilation and tune daemon JVM args; set org.gradle.jvmargs from measured heap.
Add a CI check that fails PRs causing configuration-time regressions over 10 percent.
Done when CI p50 drops from 25 to under 10 minutes and a cold local build to under 8 minutes.

examples.title: Convention plugin
examples.output: Each module applies one line and inherits toolchain and test config. ./gradlew help --configuration-cache reports 'Configuration cache entry stored' then 'reused'.

notes: Cache correctness beats cache hit rate; a bad cache hit is worse than a miss.
Do not use allprojects; it couples every module's configuration.
Build scans reveal what intuition misses; read them first.

title: Spark Job Cost Tuning for Transactions
description: Cut the cost of Spark transaction jobs so statement processing stays affordable.
overview: Cut the cost of Spark transaction jobs so statement processing stays affordable.
tasks: Record baseline from the Spark UI: stages, shuffle read/write bytes, spill, task time skew (max versus median), and cluster cost per run.
Read explain("formatted") plans and the SQL tab; remove unneeded shuffles with broadcast joins (autoBroadcastJoinThreshold tuned) and pre-partitioning.
Fix skew using AQE skew join, salting a hot key and measure the task time distribution before and after.
Convert inputs to partitioned Parquet or Delta with sizes of 128 to 512 MB per file; compact small files and show file count drop.
Tune memory and parallelism: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions via AQE coalescing, executor memory overhead, avoiding spill; use Kryo only when profiling shows benefit.
Replace UDFs with built-in functions or typed Dataset operations and show Catalyst optimisation gains.
Enable dynamic allocation and use spot instances with decommissioning; record cost per run.
Add data quality and regression tests using spark-testing-base or scalatest with small DataFrames, plus a runtime SLO alert.
Done when runtime and cost targets hold for 2 weeks of production runs.

examples.title: Skew diagnosis
examples.code:
Stage 14: 2000 tasks. median 11s, p95 19s, max 2h07m
max task shuffle read 38 GB vs median 90 MB  (key = null)
examples.output: One task reading hundreds of times the median is the skew signature. After AQE or salting, max is within 3x median. Numbers vary by dataset.

notes: Null and default keys are the usual skew culprit.
More partitions is not always faster; tiny tasks drown in scheduler overhead.
Cache only what is reused; unneeded persist wastes memory and causes spills.

title: Scala Payments Service Reliability
description: Operate a Scala payments service with backpressure and failure tests so payments don't fail under load.
overview: Operate a Scala payments service with backpressure and failure tests so payments don't fail under load.
tasks: Model every resource with Resource or Scope (DB pools, HTTP clients, Kafka consumers) and prove release on cancellation with tests.
Implement backpressure with fs2 streams using bounded queues and parEvalMapUnordered with a fixed concurrency; show memory flat at 5x producer rate.
Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter (cats-retry or ZIO Schedule) plus circuit breaker; classify errors as retryable or fatal.
Instrument with otel4s or Kamon and Prometheus metrics: queue depth, fibre count, GC and processing latency; alerts on lag growth.
Run a soak test for 24 hours at 50k events per second and show no fibre or memory growth.
Use fault injection (toxiproxy) with Kafka and DB outages; verify at-least-once semantics and idempotent writes with zero duplicates in output.
Test with weaver-test or munit-cats-effect using TestControl for deterministic time, covering 15 concurrency scenarios.
Take a thread and fibre dump and diagnose a deliberately introduced deadlock or blocked compute pool.
Done when SLOs (99.9 percent processed within 5 seconds) hold under failures.

examples.title: Bounded stream
examples.code:
Stream.fromQueueUnterminated(queue)
  .parEvalMapUnordered(32)(process)
  .groupWithin(500, 1.second)
  .evalMap(sink.writeBatch)
  .compile.drain
examples.output: At most 32 events in flight and batches of up to 500 flushed each second; when sink slows, the queue fills and producers are backpressured instead of memory growing.

notes: Blocking calls on the compute pool starve everything; use Sync.blocking or a blocking pool.
Cancellation safety is part of design: use uncancelable regions deliberately.
At-least-once plus idempotency is simpler than exactly-once claims.

title: Scala 3 Migration for Banking
description: Migrate a banking codebase to Scala 3 while keeping builds stable for customers.
overview: Migrate a banking codebase to Scala 3 while keeping builds stable for customers.
tasks: Dependency-order the modules and check which libraries publish Scala 3 or 2.13 artifacts usable via CrossVersion.for3Use2_13.
Use the Scala 3 migration mode (-source:3.0-migration) with scalafix rules and the Scala 3 migrate tool; convert implicits (given/using) incrementally.
Cross-build libraries (2.13 and 3) and verify with MiMa that binary compatibility holds between releases.
Rewrite or replace macros and compiler plugins (for example Shapeless generic derivation to Scala 3 Mirror derives).
Track compile time per module with scalac -Ystatistics or sbt-bloop plus Zinc incremental; set a budget of no more than 10 percent regression.
Use Bloop or the sbt server for fast iteration and enable parallel and incremental compilation; show clean and incremental times.
Introduce enums and extension methods only after behaviour parity; keep tests unchanged to prove equivalence.
Run property tests and integration tests in CI on both Scala versions during transition.
Done when all services run on Scala 3 in production, with MiMa green and compile time within budget.

examples.title: Scalafix and cross-build
examples.output: The same sources compile and test on both versions; failures list remaining Scala 3 incompatibilities for each module.

notes: Mixed 2.13 and 3 dependencies can conflict on transitive artifacts; check evictions.
Implicit resolution rules differ; behaviour changes can be silent, so rely on tests.
Use LTS releases for production (3.3.x) and plan upgrades.

title: Reproducible Credit Analysis in R
description: Build a reproducible credit analysis pipeline so regulators can verify lending figures.
overview: Build a reproducible credit analysis pipeline so regulators can verify lending figures.
tasks: Lock packages with renv (renv.lock committed) and pin the R version in a Docker image based on rocker/r-ver.
Model the workflow as a targets pipeline with at least 15 targets, branching with static or dynamic tar_map, and visualise with tar_visnetwork.
Make results deterministic: set seeds per target (targets does this), record sessionInfo and data checksums in an output manifest.
Validate inputs with pointblank or validate rules (types, ranges, uniqueness); pipeline fails on violations.
Unit test functions with testthat (at least 30 tests, 80 percent coverage via covr) and snapshot tests for tables and plots (vdiffr).
Run the pipeline in CI (GitHub Actions) on a clean container and compare output hashes to a stored reference.
Package shared functions as an R package with roxygen2 docs and devtools::check() returning 0 errors, 0 warnings.
Produce a Quarto report parameterised by dataset and render it from the pipeline.
Done when a new person reproduces the final tables from scratch with two commands in under 30 minutes.

examples.title: targets pipeline excerpt
examples.code:
library(targets)
list(
  tar_target(raw, read_csv("data/raw.csv"), format = "file"),
  tar_target(clean, clean_data(raw)),
  tar_target(model, fit_model(clean)),
  tar_target(report, tar_quarto(report, "report.qmd"))
)
examples.output: tar_make() prints which targets ran or were skipped as up to date; rerunning with no changes reports all targets skipped. Run time varies.

notes: Floating-point and BLAS differences can change results across machines; fix the container.
Pin package repositories to a dated snapshot (Posit Package Manager) for stability.
Version data, not just code; use DVC or checksums.

title: Credit Model API in R
description: Deploy an R credit model as a monitored API so lending decisions are explainable.
overview: Deploy an R credit model as a monitored API so lending decisions are explainable.
tasks: Fit a tidymodels workflow, evaluate on a time-based split, and record metrics (for example AUC at least 0.80 on holdout).
Version the model with vetiver and pins on a board (S3 or Posit Connect), storing metadata, package versions and training data hash.
Serve with vetiver_api or plumber, with an OpenAPI spec, strict input schema validation and clear 400 errors for bad inputs.
Containerise on a minimal rocker image with a healthcheck; load test with k6 to 100 rps and p95 under 200 ms, tuning workers.
Monitor in production: log predictions and later outcomes; compute rolling metrics with vetiver::vetiver_compute_metrics and plot drift.
Detect input drift via population stability index or Kolmogorov-Smirnov test per feature with a threshold alert (PSI over 0.2).
Automate retrain-and-promote in CI only if the new model beats the old by a margin on a fixed validation set; keep rollback to previous version.
Write a model card: intended use, data, metrics, limitations and fairness checks across subgroups.
Done when the API runs 30 days with monitoring dashboards and a tested rollback.

examples.title: Vetiver deploy
examples.code:
v <- vetiver_model(fit, "churn", metadata = list(auc = 0.83))
vetiver_pin_write(board, v)
pr() %>% vetiver_api(v) %>% pr_run(port = 8080)
# client: POST /predict with JSON rows
examples.output: The API responds {"predictions":[0.12,0.87]} for two input rows; invalid fields return HTTP 400 naming the field. Values vary with the model.

notes: Training-serving skew is the top bug; reuse the same recipe object in both.
Outcomes arrive late; plan monitoring around label delay.
Single-threaded R needs multiple workers behind a load balancer.

title: R Package for Financial Risk
description: Release an R package for financial risk metrics so analysts measure risk the same way.
overview: Release an R package for financial risk metrics so analysts measure risk the same way.
tasks: Scaffold with usethis and design a small, consistent API with tidyverse conventions; export only what is needed.
Document with roxygen2, include examples that run in under 5 seconds and a pkgdown site.
Write testthat tests with 90 percent coverage (covr), including edge cases such as NA, empty input and factors.
Add one performance-critical function in C++ with cpp11 or Rcpp; benchmark with bench::mark showing at least 10x improvement over pure R.
Run R CMD check --as-cran on Windows (win-builder), macOS and Linux (R-hub) with 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 notes besides the new submission note.
Write two vignettes with realistic data and keep dependencies minimal (Imports versus Suggests).
Submit to CRAN with cran-comments.md; respond to reviewer feedback within the required window.
Run revdepcheck for each later release, and maintain NEWS.md following semantic versioning.
Done when the package is on CRAN with CI green on 3 operating systems and at least 5 external issues handled.

examples.title: CRAN check summary
examples.code:
$ R CMD build . && R CMD check --as-cran mypkg_0.1.0.tar.gz
* checking CRAN incoming feasibility ... NOTE
Maintainer: 'A Dev <a@example.org>'  New submission
Status: 1 NOTE
examples.output: Goal is Status: OK or only the unavoidable New submission NOTE. Any WARNING or ERROR must be fixed before submitting.

notes: CRAN limits check time and forbids writing outside tempdir; test accordingly.
Breaking changes require coordination with reverse dependencies.
Use skip_on_cran for slow or network tests and run them in your own CI.

title: Bash Library for Finance Operations
description: Build a tested Bash library so back-office scripts don't break payment files.
overview: Build a tested Bash library so back-office scripts don't break payment files.
tasks: Package the library as a single sourceable file plus a modules directory, versioned with semver tags and a CHANGELOG; breaking changes need a major bump.
Implement strict-mode bootstrap (set -Eeuo pipefail, IFS reset, ERR trap printing file, line and function stack) and document the known gotchas of set -e inside conditionals and subshells.
Provide lib::log with levels and JSON output mode, lib::retry with exponential backoff and jitter (max attempts, max delay), and lib::lock using flock with a timeout and stale-lock detection.
Provide lib::mktemp that registers cleanup on EXIT, INT and TERM and chains with callers own traps without overwriting them.
Write at least 120 bats tests covering success, failure, signal and quoting edge cases (spaces, newlines, leading dashes in filenames); target 90 percent function coverage measured with kcov.
Run ShellCheck at severity style with zero suppressed warnings except documented ones, and run the suite on Bash 3.2 (macOS), 4.4 and 5.2 plus dash for the POSIX subset.
Add a CI pipeline that fails on lint, test, or shfmt diffs, and publishes a release artefact with a SHA-256 checksum.
Migrate 10 real scripts from at least 3 teams, recording lines removed and incidents or defects found during migration; write a contribution guide and deprecation policy.

examples.title: bats test for retry
examples.output: bats output: ok 14 retry gives up after 3 attempts (all tests ok, 0 failures)

examples.title: Trap chaining
examples.output: Hooks run in reverse registration order; a caller hook that exits non-zero does not skip later hooks.

notes: Never overwrite a trap; read it with trap -p and chain, or callers silently lose cleanup.
macOS ships Bash 3.2: no associative arrays, no mapfile. Decide your floor explicitly and test it.
Library functions must not call exit; return codes only, so sourcing scripts keep control.

title: Speed Up a Payments Batch Script
description: Speed up a slow payments batch 20x so merchants are paid sooner.
overview: Speed up a slow payments batch 20x so merchants are paid sooner.
tasks: Capture a baseline: wall time, user and sys time with time, and fork count with strace -f -c -e trace=clone,execve over a representative 1 GB input.
Use PS4 with EPOCHREALTIME and set -x to produce a per-line timing profile; produce a ranked top-10 table of hot lines.
Replace per-line subshells and external calls (cut, sed, awk, basename) in loops with parameter expansion, read -r with IFS, and mapfile; show a before and after fork count.
Replace the sequential per-file loop with xargs -0 -P with a bounded worker count, or GNU parallel, preserving output ordering and propagating the worst exit code.
Push heavy text transforms into a single awk or sort -S 1G --parallel=4 invocation with LC_ALL=C, and justify each with a measurement.
Reproduce the intermittent hang with a deterministic test (a fifo with no writer, or a pipe to a closed reader), identify it via strace or lsof, and fix it with timeout and proper redirections.
Add a regression benchmark using hyperfine (10 runs, 3 warmups) committed with the repo, failing CI if median regresses over 15 percent.
Write a one-page report: baseline, each optimisation with delta, final numbers, and risks.

examples.title: Profile with xtrace
examples.code:
PS4='+ $EPOCHREALTIME $LINENO: ' bash -x etl.sh 2> trace.log
awk '{t=$2; if(p)d[$3]+=t-p; p=t} END{for(k in d)print d[k],k}' trace.log | sort -rn | head
examples.output: Lines such as 41.8 52: shows line 52 consumed 41.8 seconds cumulative (values vary).

examples.title: Benchmark gate
examples.code: hyperfine --warmup 3 --runs 10 ./etl.sh.old ./etl.sh.new
examples.output: Summary shape: etl.sh.new ran N.NN times faster than etl.sh.old; target at least 18 times.

notes: Measure first: the intuitive hot spot is usually wrong; forks inside a loop of 1 million lines dominate.
LC_ALL=C can change sort and grep speed by 5 to 10x but also changes collation; confirm output equivalence with a checksum diff.
Parallelism hides ordering bugs; always compare sorted output of old and new on the full dataset.

title: Shell Script Security Review
description: Harden 30 operational scripts against injection so payment credentials don't leak.
overview: Harden 30 operational scripts against injection so payment credentials don't leak.
tasks: Inventory scripts with owner, privilege level, trigger and input sources; rank by blast radius.

Audit for command injection (unquoted expansion, eval, bash -c with interpolation, ssh with untrusted arguments), path injection (relative commands under sudo), and glob or option injection (use -- and ./ prefixes).
Replace predictable /tmp names with mktemp -d, set umask 077, and fix TOCTOU patterns (test then create) with atomic ln, mkdir, or noclobber.
Remove secrets from argv and environment: read from files with 0600 mode or a secret manager, avoid set -x around credentials, and scrub history and logs.
Pin PATH, validate inputs against allow-list regexes, and drop privileges (sudo -u, setpriv) for the non-root portions.
Build a fuzz harness feeding filenames containing spaces, newlines, leading dash, glob characters and $(...) to each script; zero execution of injected commands is the pass criterion.
Add CI gates: ShellCheck security-relevant codes (SC2086, SC2046, SC2091, SC2155), a forbidden-patterns grep (eval, curl piped to sh), and signed script checksums for root cron jobs.
Publish a 2-page standard, a findings report with before and after counts, and run a 45-minute training session recorded for new hires.

examples.title: Injection test
examples.code:
touch -- '$(touch /tmp/pwned)' '-rf' 'a b'
./cleanup.sh .
test ! -e /tmp/pwned && echo SAFE
examples.output: SAFE (any other output means the script executed injected content)

examples.title: Safe temp and option handling
examples.code:
umask 077
tmp=$(mktemp -d) || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf -- "$tmp"' EXIT
rm -- "$file"
examples.output: No predictable path; filenames starting with a dash are treated as operands.

notes: Most real findings are unquoted variables in cron jobs running as root; fix those first.
Quoting is not validation: a quoted value can still be a malicious option, so use -- and validate.
Do not rewrite everything; migrate the highest-privilege 20 percent first and enforce rules on new code.

title: React Performance for a Trading App
description: Cut interaction lag in a trading app so investors act on prices in time.
overview: Cut interaction lag in a trading app so investors act on prices in time.
tasks: Collect field data: web-vitals reporting to an endpoint, p75 LCP, INP and CLS by route and device class; choose 3 target routes.
Profile with React DevTools Profiler (flamegraph and ranked) and Chrome Performance panel; list the top 10 components by commit time and the long tasks over 50 ms.
Fix re-render causes at the root: colocate state, split context by update frequency or adopt useSyncExternalStore selectors, and use memo and useMemo only where a profile shows benefit.
Use transitions (useTransition, useDeferredValue) for expensive filtering and virtualise lists over 500 rows with a windowing library.
Reduce bundle: route-level lazy loading, analyse with source-map-explorer or the bundler analyser, remove or replace the 3 heaviest dependencies; target 35 percent less initial JavaScript.
Add a CI performance budget (e.g. main chunk under 180 kB gzipped) and a Lighthouse CI or Playwright trace check on the 3 routes.
Run an A/B or staged rollout and report p75 INP below 200 ms and LCP below 2.5 s, with the conversion or bounce delta.
Write an internal performance playbook with a flowchart: symptom, tool, likely cause, fix.

examples.title: Transition for heavy filter

notes: Lab scores lie; INP only shows up in field data with real devices, so throttle CPU 4x when profiling.
memo on everything adds comparison cost and hides unstable props; fix prop identity first.
Budgets without an owner decay in a quarter; tie them to CI failing, not dashboards.

description: Build an accessible banking component library and migrate 200 screens so customers get one consistent experience.
overview: Build an accessible banking component library and migrate 200 screens so customers get one consistent experience.
tasks: Define design tokens (colour, spacing, type) as CSS variables exported from a single source, with light, dark and high-contrast themes.
Build at least 20 components using headless primitives, with documented props, controlled and uncontrolled modes, ref forwarding and polymorphic as prop where justified.

Bake in accessibility: keyboard maps and focus management per WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices; automated checks with jest-axe and Storybook a11y addon returning zero serious violations; manual screen reader checks in NVDA and VoiceOver.
Add visual regression with Chromatic or Playwright screenshots across 3 viewports, and interaction tests with Testing Library.
Publish ESM and CJS builds with tree-shakeable exports, types, and size-limit budgets per component; semver via changesets with a documented deprecation window of 2 minors.
Write jscodeshift codemods that migrate legacy imports and props, each with fixture tests; run on 200 screens and report auto-migrated percentage (target at least 85) and manual-fix list.
Track adoption in a dashboard (percent of UI using the library, duplicate components removed) and a monthly office hour.
Document governance: how a team proposes a component, RFC template, and breaking-change process.

Every public prop is a promise; expose fewer props and compose instead.
Accessibility regressions arrive through new variants; test every variant, not only the default.

title: Frontend Standard for Fintech Teams
description: Define a frontend standard so fintech screens are consistent and accessible for customers.
overview: Define a frontend standard so fintech screens are consistent and accessible for customers.
tasks: Write ADRs for at least 5 decisions: server state (TanStack Query or equivalent), client state, routing, forms, and styling, each with rejected alternatives.
Enforce dependency rules with eslint-plugin-boundaries or Nx module boundaries: apps depend on features, features on UI and utilities, never the reverse; zero cycles checked with madge in CI.
Standardise error handling: error boundaries per route and widget, typed API errors, and a logging adaptor to Sentry with release tagging and source maps.
Adopt a testing pyramid with numbers: unit under 5 seconds for 1000 tests, component tests with Testing Library and MSW, 15 Playwright end-to-end journeys under 8 minutes.
Cut CI time with Turborepo or Nx remote caching and affected-only runs; target median PR pipeline under 7 minutes from 25.
Create a generator that scaffolds a feature module with tests, story and route in under a minute.

Allow documented escape hatches with expiry dates, or teams will route around the standard.

title: Nuxt Performance for a Banking Site
description: Improve Core Web Vitals for a banking site so customers on slow networks can check balances.
overview: Improve Core Web Vitals for a banking site so customers on slow networks can check balances.
tasks: Baseline field and lab data per route (LCP, INP, TBT, hydration time) using Lighthouse CI and web-vitals RUM.
Configure routeRules per route: prerender for marketing pages, swr or isr for catalogue pages (e.g. 60 s), SSR for the cart, and client-only for dashboards.
Profile reactivity with Vue DevTools performance timeline; replace deep reactive objects with shallowRef or shallowReactive for large lists, and markRaw for third-party instances.
Reduce hydration cost using lazy hydration (hydrate on visible or idle), component-level lazy imports and server-only components.
Optimise assets: nuxt/image with AVIF and WebP, font preloading with size-adjust fallback to remove CLS, and critical CSS.
Set CDN caching (Cache-Control s-maxage, stale-while-revalidate) and verify with curl headers and a cache hit ratio over 90 percent.
Add performance budgets to CI (JS under 170 kB gzipped per route) and compare with a bundle visualiser each PR.
Report results: LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, TTFB under 600 ms at p75, with before and after table.

examples.title: routeRules
examples.output: Build output lists prerendered routes; curl -I /products/1 shows x-nitro-cache or cache-control with s-maxage=60.

examples.title: Shallow reactivity
examples.code:
const rows = shallowRef<Row[]>([])
rows.value = await $fetch("/api/rows") // replace, do not mutate
examples.output: Updating 10,000 rows no longer creates 10,000 proxies; scripting time drops measurably (values vary).

notes: Deep reactivity on large API payloads is a hidden multi-hundred-millisecond cost; shallowRef is the fix.
ISR and SWR serve stale content; design cache keys and purge hooks for price changes.
Hydration mismatches silently force re-renders; treat warnings as failures in CI.

description: Migrate a payments Vue app with zero downtime so customers keep paying.
overview: Migrate a payments Vue app with zero downtime so customers keep paying.

Write codemods for mechanical changes (filters removal, v-model syntax, $listeners, event bus, Vue.set) with fixture tests and run on all components.

Move Webpack to Vite, targeting dev start under 3 s and production build time down by 50 percent.

Remove the compat layer and publish a retrospective with effort, defects and metrics.

Provide generators for a new feature library including routes, store, tests and Storybook stories.
