overview: Remove wasted rendering in a trading dashboard so prices update smoothly for investors.
tasks: Baseline with Angular DevTools profiler: change detection cycles per second, time per cycle, and long tasks, on a view with a 5,000-row grid and a 20 msg/s websocket.
Apply ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush to all components and fix resulting stale-view bugs by using signals, async pipe or explicit markForCheck.
Run high-frequency event sources (websocket, mousemove, timers) outside NgZone using runOutsideAngular and re-enter only when state changes.
Convert component and service state to signal, computed and effect; convert RxJS streams with toSignal and keep RxJS for async orchestration only.
Replace *ngFor on large lists with @for plus track expression, virtual scrolling (CDK) and defer blocks for below-the-fold widgets.
Evaluate zoneless (provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection or its stable successor) on one route and document the third-party libraries that break.
Add a performance test in CI using Playwright tracing: scripted interaction must finish under 100 ms scripting time.
Report before and after: cycles per second reduced at least 90 percent, scripting time per update reduced at least 60 percent.

readonly visible = computed(() => this.rows().filter(r => r.status === this.filter()));

Batching events is often a bigger win than any framework switch.
Measure with production builds; development mode runs extra checks.

title: Django Scaling for a Payments API
description: Take a Django payments app to 2,000 requests per second so merchants never see failures.
overview: Take a Django payments app to 2,000 requests per second so merchants never see failures.
tasks: Instrument with django-debug-toolbar in development and pg_stat_statements plus APM in production; list the top 10 queries by total time.
Eliminate N+1s with select_related and prefetch_related (using Prefetch objects with filtered querysets), and add assertNumQueries tests that lock query counts.
Use EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on slow queries; add composite, partial and covering indexes through migrations created concurrently (AddIndexConcurrently).
Introduce caching: per-view and low-level cache with Redis, key versioning, stampede protection, and signal-based invalidation; target 80 percent hit rate.
Configure persistent connections or PgBouncer in transaction pooling, and a read replica with a database router that respects read-your-writes.
Move heavy work to Celery with idempotent tasks and retry with backoff.
Load test with Locust or k6 ramping to 2,000 req/s; success is p95 under 250 ms, error rate under 0.1 percent, and CPU headroom.
Document changes with before and after query counts, plan costs and latency graphs.

examples.output: Test passes at exactly 3 queries; adding an unprefetched field fails the test.

examples.title: Concurrent index
examples.code:
from django.contrib.postgres.operations import AddIndexConcurrently
class Migration(migrations.Migration):
    atomic = False
    operations = [AddIndexConcurrently("order", models.Index(fields=["customer","-created"], name="ord_cust_created"))]
examples.output: Index built without locking writes; EXPLAIN shows Index Scan.

notes: Replica lag breaks read-your-writes; pin a user to primary for a few seconds after a write.
Concurrent index creation requires atomic = False and can leave an invalid index on failure; check pg_index.
Cache invalidation bugs cost more than the latency saved; prefer short TTLs first.

title: Zero-Downtime Migrations for Ledgers
description: Run risky database changes on a live ledger without downtime so balances stay available.
overview: Run risky database changes on a live ledger without downtime so balances stay available.
tasks: Catalogue lock levels for operations (ADD COLUMN with default, ALTER TYPE, CREATE INDEX, ADD CONSTRAINT) on your PostgreSQL version and set lock_timeout 3s and statement_timeout in migrations.
Use the expand, migrate, contract pattern over at least 3 deploys: add nullable column, dual write, backfill, switch reads, drop old.
Implement a backfill management command with batching (10,000 rows), pause between batches, resumability by primary-key cursor and metrics; keep replication lag under 5 seconds.
Add constraints safely: NOT VALID foreign keys and check constraints, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT separately.
Integrate a linter (django-migration-linter or squawk) in CI to fail unsafe migrations.
Rehearse on a production-sized snapshot, recording timings and lock waits; define an abort and rollback plan.
Execute during business hours with a canary and watch p99 latency and lock waits; no request exceeds a 2 s added latency.
Write a migration playbook with a decision table for common DDL.

examples.title: Safe constraint
examples.code:
ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_cust_fk FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers(id) NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_cust_fk;
examples.output: First statement takes a brief lock; validation runs without blocking writes.

examples.title: Lock guard
examples.code: migrations.RunSQL("SET lock_timeout = '3s'")
examples.output: Migration fails fast and can be retried rather than queueing behind a long transaction.

notes: A waiting ALTER blocks every query queued behind it; lock_timeout is the real safety.
Old and new code run simultaneously during deploy, so each migration must be compatible with both.
Test the reverse path; rollbacks are where plans fail.

title: Django Security Audit for Banking
description: Harden a Django banking app to a recognised standard so customer data stays safe.
overview: Harden a Django banking app to a recognised standard so customer data stays safe.
tasks: Run manage.py check --deploy and fix every warning; set HSTS, secure cookies, SameSite, CSRF trusted origins and SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER correctly behind the load balancer.
Audit authorisation: object-level checks on every view and DRF viewset (IDOR tests per endpoint), with a test matrix of roles by resources.
Review raw SQL, extra(), mark_safe and the safe template filter usage; replace or justify each, and ban new ones with a semgrep rule in CI.
Add Argon2 password hashing, rate-limited login with lockout, MFA via TOTP, and session rotation on privilege change.
Harden file uploads (content type sniffing, size limits 10 MB, storage outside web root, antivirus scan) and SSRF protections for outbound fetches.
Scan dependencies (pip-audit, Dependabot), run bandit and semgrep, and run OWASP ZAP baseline against staging; zero high findings.
Enable audit logging for security events with tamper-evident shipping, and test alerting for 3 attack scenarios.
Deliver a findings report with severity, CWE, fix commit and retest evidence.

examples.title: IDOR test
examples.code:
def test_cannot_read_other_tenant_invoice(self):
    self.client.force_login(self.user_a)
    r = self.client.get(f"/api/invoices/{self.invoice_b.id}/")
    self.assertEqual(r.status_code, 404)
examples.output: Test passes; returning 403 instead leaks existence, so 404 is expected.

examples.title: Deploy check
examples.code: python manage.py check --deploy
examples.output: Expected: System check identified no issues (0 silenced).

notes: Django is secure by default until you add raw SQL, mark_safe or custom auth; audit those first.
Wrong proxy header configuration silently disables secure-cookie or redirect behaviour.
Object-level permission bugs are the top real-world finding; test them for every endpoint.

title: Laravel Queue Reliability for Payments
description: Process 5 million payment jobs a day without duplicates so customers are charged once.
overview: Process 5 million payment jobs a day without duplicates so customers are charged once.
tasks: Classify jobs by criticality and assign separate queues and Horizon supervisors with explicit processes, memory limits and timeouts (timeout shorter than retry_after).
Make every job idempotent with a unique business key, ShouldBeUnique or a database unique constraint, and tests that run the same job twice and assert one effect.
Implement retry strategy: backoff arrays, maxExceptions, a failed() handler with alert, and a dead-letter review workflow with replay command.
Use job batches and chains with allowFailures for multi-step flows, and rate limiting with RateLimited middleware for third-party APIs (e.g. 100 per minute).
Protect the database: lock-based WithoutOverlapping, transactions with afterCommit to avoid jobs running before data exists.
Configure Horizon autoscaling by queue time, Redis persistence and failover, and graceful deploy with horizon:terminate and no lost jobs.
Load test with 100,000 queued jobs; success means p95 queue wait under 30 s for critical queue, zero duplicate side effects, and drain time documented.
Build dashboards and alerts: queue depth, wait time, failure rate above 1 percent, oldest job age.

examples.title: Idempotent job
examples.output: Dispatching the same job twice yields one gateway capture.

examples.title: Supervisor config
examples.code: "critical" => ["connection"=>"redis","queue"=>["critical"],"balance"=>"auto","minProcesses"=>3,"maxProcesses"=>20,"timeout"=>60,"tries"=>5]
examples.output: Horizon dashboard shows critical queue scaling between 3 and 20 workers under load.

notes: Without afterCommit a job can run before its transaction commits and find no row.
retry_after below job timeout causes duplicate execution of still-running jobs.
Replay tooling matters more than retries; people must be able to fix and requeue safely.

title: Modular Laravel Banking Monolith
description: Refactor a Laravel banking monolith into modules so changes don't break customer accounts.
overview: Refactor a Laravel banking monolith into modules so changes don't break customer accounts.
tasks: Map the domain with event storming and dependency analysis; produce a context map and module ownership list for at least 5 modules.
Move code into app-modules directories with their own routes, migrations, service providers and tests; keep a single deployable.
Define public contracts (interfaces, DTOs, domain events); forbid cross-module Eloquent relations and direct model access.
Enforce rules with Deptrac or Pest architecture tests failing CI on forbidden imports; start with a baseline file and reduce violations to zero over the programme.
Replace cross-module joins with events and read models or explicit query services; measure that no query crosses module tables except in reporting.
Introduce static analysis at Larastan level 8 and Rector rules for the migration.
Track metrics: violations count, PR touching more than 2 modules, test suite time per module, and deployment frequency.
Document the module template, an ADR on extraction criteria, and extract one module to a separate service as a feasibility proof.

examples.title: Architecture test
examples.output: Pest: 1 passed; adding a forbidden import makes the test fail with the offending file.

examples.title: Contract
examples.code: interface PriceQuery { public function priceFor(ProductId $id, Currency $c): Money; }
examples.output: Billing depends on the interface; Catalogue binds the implementation in its provider.

notes: Change the structure with tests locked first; characterisation tests save you.
Shared Eloquent models are the main coupling; split them by context early.
Modules without enforcement revert within months.

title: Laravel Peak Traffic Preparation
description: Prepare a Laravel payments API for peak traffic so checkouts don't fail on sale days.
overview: Prepare a Laravel payments API for peak traffic so checkouts don't fail on sale days.
tasks: Establish a baseline with k6 scripts modelling real traffic mix (60 percent browse, 30 percent search, 10 percent checkout) and record RPS, p95 and error rate at saturation.
Profile with Laravel Telescope in staging, Blackfire or Xdebug traces and database slow query logs; fix top 5 bottlenecks.
Migrate to Octane (Swoole or RoadRunner); audit for state leaks (static properties, singletons holding request data) with a test running 1,000 requests asserting isolation.
Optimise: config, route and view caching, OPcache preload settings, query caching, eager loading enforcement via Model::preventLazyLoading in non-production.
Instrument with OpenTelemetry or Datadog/Sentry tracing including queue and database spans; define SLOs 99.9 percent and p95 300 ms.
Build capacity model: requests per instance, scale-out triggers, DB connection limits and a cost per 1,000 requests.
Run a game day: ramp to 10x for 30 minutes, inject a Redis failure and a slow dependency; verify graceful degradation with circuit breakers and timeouts.
Write the post-test report with limits, fixes and the launch runbook.

examples.title: k6 scenario
examples.code: export const options = { stages:[{duration:"5m",target:500},{duration:"20m",target:500}], thresholds:{ http_req_duration:["p(95)<300"], http_req_failed:["rate<0.001"] } };
examples.output: k6 summary shape: thresholds passed; http_req_duration p(95)=212ms (values vary).

examples.title: Lazy loading guard
examples.code: Model::preventLazyLoading(! app()->isProduction());
examples.output: Tests and staging throw LazyLoadingViolationException on any N+1.

notes: Octane keeps state between requests; request-scoped data in singletons leaks across users.
Load test against production-like data volume or indexes will look fine and fail live.
Know your database connection ceiling before scaling workers.

title: Resilient Payment Microservice
description: Make a payments microservice survive dependency failures so customers can still pay.
overview: Make a payments microservice survive dependency failures so customers can still pay.
tasks: Set explicit connect and read timeouts on every client (e.g. 500 ms connect, 2 s read) and a global deadline per request; no unbounded calls.
Apply Resilience4j circuit breakers, retries with exponential backoff and jitter only for idempotent calls, bulkheads and rate limiters; document configuration rationale.
Provide fallbacks that degrade meaningfully (cached data, reduced features) and return correct status codes with Problem Details (RFC 7807).
Make writes safe to retry via idempotency keys stored with unique constraints.
Tune thread pools and virtual threads (Java 21), connection pools (HikariCP size by formula), and queue limits; show thread dump under load with no starvation.
Inject failures with Toxiproxy or Chaos Monkey for Spring Boot: 2 s latency, 30 percent errors, full outage; assert SLOs with Gatling.
Expose Micrometer metrics for breaker state, retries and bulkhead use, with Prometheus alerts and a Grafana dashboard.
Success: with one dependency down, p99 stays under 1 s, error rate for unaffected endpoints under 0.5 percent, and recovery within 30 s of dependency return.

examples.title: Resilience config
examples.code:
resilience4j:
  circuitbreaker:
    instances:
      inventory:
        slidingWindowSize: 20
        failureRateThreshold: 50
        waitDurationInOpenState: 10s
  timelimiter:
    instances:
      inventory:
        timeoutDuration: 800ms
examples.output: Actuator /actuator/circuitbreakers shows inventory state CLOSED, OPEN under fault, then HALF_OPEN.

examples.title: Fault injection
examples.code: toxiproxy-cli toxic add -t latency -a latency=2000 inventory
examples.output: Gatling report shape: requests to /orders degrade to fallback; 0 threads blocked beyond timeout.

notes: Retries multiply load during outages; cap them and use budgets.
Circuit breaker thresholds need real traffic volume to be meaningful; set minimumNumberOfCalls.
Test the unhappy path continuously, not once.

title: JVM Tuning for a Payments Service
description: Fix latency spikes in a Spring payments service so checkouts respond quickly.
overview: Fix latency spikes in a Spring payments service so checkouts respond quickly.
tasks: Enable GC logging (-Xlog:gc*), JFR continuous recording with a 30-minute ring buffer, and Actuator/Micrometer JVM metrics.
Capture CPU and allocation flame graphs with async-profiler under load; identify the top 5 hot methods and top allocation sites.
Analyse a heap dump with Eclipse MAT: find the dominator tree and leak suspects, and fix at least one real leak (unbounded cache, ThreadLocal, listener) with a regression test.
Select and tune GC (G1 vs ZGC/Shenandoah) with pause targets; set container-aware heap (-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75) and compare p99 under identical load.
Fix inefficiencies: Hibernate N+1 and large result sets, JSON serialisation overhead, blocking calls on event loop threads, and lock contention seen in thread dumps.
Add a JMH micro-benchmark for the hottest path to prove improvement statistically.
Define alerts on GC pause above 200 ms, old-gen after-GC trending up, and thread pool saturation.
Result: p99 reduced at least 50 percent, 14 days without OOM restart, with a written diagnosis timeline.

examples.title: Async profiler
examples.code:
asprof -d 60 -e cpu -f cpu.html $(pgrep -f myservice)
asprof -d 60 -e alloc -f alloc.html $(pgrep -f myservice)
examples.output: HTML flame graphs written; wide frames show hot methods (shape only; values vary).

examples.title: JFR and GC flags
examples.code: java -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=100 -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75 -Xlog:gc*:file=gc.log -XX:StartFlightRecording=maxage=30m,disk=true -jar app.jar
examples.output: gc.log lines show pause times; jcmd JFR.dump saves the ring buffer on demand.

notes: A growing heap is not always a leak; compare after-GC occupancy over time.
Profile under production-like load, as JIT and caches change behaviour.
Change one variable at a time or you cannot attribute the gain.

title: Spring Starter for Banking Services
description: Create a shared starter with secure defaults so 50 banking services protect customer data consistently.
overview: Create a shared starter with secure defaults so 50 banking services protect customer data consistently.
tasks: Create a Spring Boot starter with @AutoConfiguration, @ConditionalOn* conditions, configuration properties with metadata and sane overrides; test with ApplicationContextRunner.
Include defaults: structured JSON logging with trace IDs, Micrometer and OpenTelemetry tracing, Problem Details error handling, graceful shutdown, health probes, and security headers.
Publish a BOM controlling dependency versions, with Gradle or Maven enforcer rules banning known-bad versions and duplicate logging frameworks.
Add architecture tests (ArchUnit) as a shared test-jar teams opt into: layering, no field injection, no System.out.
Automate upgrades with Renovate or Dependabot plus OpenRewrite recipes for Spring Boot minors and majors; show a service upgraded by bot PR with passing tests.
Generate an SBOM (CycloneDX) per build and fail on critical CVEs via OWASP Dependency-Check or Trivy.
Onboard 10 services, measuring lines of boilerplate removed, time to create a new service (target under 1 day to production), and patch-propagation time (target under 48 hours).
Provide documentation, a service template, versioned changelog and a support channel with SLAs.

examples.title: Auto-configuration test
examples.code:
new ApplicationContextRunner()
  .withConfiguration(AutoConfigurations.of(PlatformAutoConfiguration.class))
  .withPropertyValues("platform.tracing.enabled=false")
  .run(ctx -> assertThat(ctx).doesNotHaveBean(Tracer.class));
examples.output: Test passes; property toggles bean creation as documented.

examples.title: OpenRewrite
examples.code: mvn -U org.openrewrite.maven:rewrite-maven-plugin:run -Drewrite.recipeArtifactCoordinates=org.openrewrite.recipe:rewrite-spring:LATEST -Drewrite.activeRecipes=org.openrewrite.java.spring.boot3.UpgradeSpringBoot_3_3
examples.output: Shape: source files changed listed; build and tests pass afterwards.

notes: Every default is a decision made for 50 teams; make them overridable and document why.
Version your starter carefully; breaking auto-configuration breaks everyone at once.
Adoption comes from saved time, not mandates.

title: Rails Scaling for a Payments Platform
description: Scale a Rails payments monolith with caching so shoppers see fast checkout pages.
overview: Scale a Rails payments monolith with caching so shoppers see fast checkout pages.
tasks: Instrument with rack-mini-profiler, Skylight or Scout, and pg_stat_statements; produce a ranked list of the 10 slowest endpoints and queries.
Add Bullet in test and development to fail on N+1s; fix with includes, preload and eager_load choices explained, and counter caches.
Add missing indexes through strong_migrations-approved migrations (algorithm: :concurrently, disable_ddl_transaction!); verify with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
Implement Russian-doll fragment caching with cache keys from updated_at, low-level Rails.cache.fetch with expires_in and race_condition_ttl, targeting 85 percent hit rate.
Tune Puma (workers, threads) and database pool size so pool equals threads; add PgBouncer; read replicas via connected_to with automatic role switching and replica delay.
Move slow work to Sidekiq with idempotent jobs and unique locks; keep web requests under 200 ms server time.
Load test with k6 to 3,000 rpm per node; success is p95 under 250 ms, DB CPU under 60 percent, and zero connection pool timeouts.
Document each fix with before and after numbers and cost saved in instances.

examples.title: Fail on N+1
examples.code:
config.after_initialize do
  Bullet.enable = true
  Bullet.raise = true
end
examples.output: Test run raises Bullet::Notification::UnoptimizedQueryError with the offending association.

examples.title: Safe index
examples.code:
class AddIndexOrdersOnUserCreated < ActiveRecord::Migration[7.1]
  disable_ddl_transaction!
  def change
    add_index :orders, [:user_id, :created_at], algorithm: :concurrently
  end
end
examples.output: Index added without blocking writes.

notes: Pool size, Puma threads and Sidekiq concurrency must be reconciled or you get timeouts under load.
Cache keys without versioning serve stale views after deploys.
Counter caches and denormalisation need backfills and consistency checks.

title: Rails Upgrade for a Bank
description: Upgrade a legacy Rails banking app across versions so customers keep online access.
overview: Upgrade a legacy Rails banking app across versions so customers keep online access.
tasks: Set up dual-boot using next_rails or bootboot so CI runs the full suite on current and next Rails; report failing tests per version as a burn-down.
Raise test confidence first: coverage on critical flows, 25 system tests, and contract tests for external APIs.
Track deprecation warnings using ActiveSupport::Deprecation behaviours in CI (raise on new ones) and fix by category.
Upgrade one minor version at a time, running rails app:update and merging config changes deliberately; set config.load_defaults gradually and per-flag.
Migrate to Zeitwerk autoloading and fix naming issues using zeitwerk:check until clean; enforce in CI.
Replace or fork unmaintained gems; document each decision with alternative evaluated.
Deploy each step behind the dual-boot env flag to a canary pool before full rollout, watching error tracker rates.
Finish with removal of dual-boot code, a retro, and the commitment to upgrade every release within 8 weeks.

examples.title: Zeitwerk check
examples.code: bin/rails zeitwerk:check
examples.output: Expected: Hold on, I am eager loading the application. then All is good!

examples.title: Dual-boot CI
examples.code: BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.next bundle exec rspec
examples.output: Shape: N examples, M failures; M falls each week toward zero.

notes: Deprecation warnings you ignore become errors in the next version; fix them while they are cheap.
New load_defaults change behaviour such as cookie serialisation; enable one at a time with tests.
A canary pool turns upgrade risk into a measurable experiment.

title: Tenant Isolation for a Banking SaaS
description: Verify row-level isolation so one bank's customers never see another bank's data.
overview: Verify row-level isolation so one bank's customers never see another bank's data.
tasks: Choose and document the tenancy model (shared schema with tenant_id) vs schema per tenant, with trade-offs for scale, backup and migrations.
Implement default scoping through a current-tenant context (Current attributes) and a base model concern that forbids unscoped queries in application code.

Enable PostgreSQL row-level security with policies using current_setting(app.tenant_id), set per request in a middleware or around_action inside transaction with SET LOCAL; application database role must not bypass RLS.
Cover background jobs, mailers, console and cable channels: each must set tenant explicitly or fail loudly.
Write automated leak tests: for every model, create data for tenant A, query as tenant B, assert zero rows; generate tests from ActiveRecord descendants so new models are covered.
Add per-tenant rate limits (Rack::Attack), per-tenant encryption keys for sensitive columns with Active Record encryption, and tenant-aware caching keys.
Run a red-team session: attempt IDOR, mass assignment and cache poisoning across tenants; fix all findings.
Document the rules, audit logging of tenant switches, and an offboarding procedure with verified data deletion.

examples.title: RLS policy
examples.code:
ALTER TABLE invoices ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON invoices USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::bigint);
examples.output: Select without a tenant setting returns an error or zero rows rather than all rows.

examples.title: Leak test
examples.output: All models pass; a new unscoped model fails the suite.

notes: Superuser and table owner roles bypass RLS unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; use a separate app role.
Connection pools plus SET (not SET LOCAL) leak tenant context to the next request.
Unscoped jobs are the usual leak; require tenant argument in the job base class.

title: ASP.NET Payments API Tuning
description: Double a payments API's throughput so merchants' checkouts stay quick during busy times.
overview: Double a payments API's throughput so merchants' checkouts stay quick during busy times.
tasks: Collect baselines: dotnet-counters (threadpool queue length, gen0/1/2 GC counts, allocation rate), dotnet-trace and PerfView; record RPS, p99 and CPU at saturation.
Find sync-over-async (Result, Wait, GetAwaiter().GetResult()) with analyzers and traces, and remove it; show thread pool queue length falling to near zero.
Reduce allocations: pooling (ArrayPool, ObjectPool), System.Text.Json source generators, Span and avoid LINQ in hot paths; verify with BenchmarkDotNet MemoryDiagnoser.
Optimise EF Core: AsNoTracking, split queries versus single, compiled queries, projection to DTOs, batch updates with ExecuteUpdate; log SQL and cap queries per request.
Add output caching, response compression, HTTP/2, and HybridCache or distributed cache with stampede protection.
Tune Kestrel limits, HttpClient via IHttpClientFactory with SocketsHttpHandler pooling to prevent socket exhaustion, and enable Server GC with concurrent settings tested.
Add an OpenTelemetry pipeline and a load test with NBomber or k6; success is 2x RPS at p99 under 300 ms and gen2 GCs reduced by 70 percent.
Add a benchmark gate in CI for the three hottest code paths.

examples.title: Benchmark
examples.output: Table shape: Method, Mean, Allocated; SourceGen shows lower Mean and Allocated (values vary).

examples.title: Live counters
examples.code: dotnet-counters monitor -n MyApi System.Runtime Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting
examples.output: ThreadPool Queue Length stays near 0 under load after the fix.

notes: Thread pool starvation looks like low CPU and high latency; check queue length first.
Do not create HttpClient per request; do not cache it forever without handling DNS changes.
Benchmark in Release with realistic data, never in Debug.

title: ASP.NET Identity Hardening for Banking
description: Harden banking sign-in with OpenID Connect so customers' accounts are safer.
overview: Harden banking sign-in with OpenID Connect so customers' accounts are safer.
tasks: Centralise authentication on an OpenID Connect provider (Entra ID, Keycloak or Duende IdentityServer) using authorization code with PKCE; short-lived access tokens (10 minutes) and rotating refresh tokens.
Implement policy-based and resource-based authorisation with IAuthorizationHandler; every endpoint has a policy, enforced by a test that fails when an endpoint lacks authorisation metadata.
Configure Data Protection keys persisted to shared storage encrypted with a key vault so multiple instances share cookies and keys rotate every 90 days.
Move secrets to Azure Key Vault or equivalent with managed identity; no secrets in appsettings or environment of source control; scan with gitleaks.
Add security headers, strict CORS allow-lists, anti-forgery for cookie flows, request size limits, and rate limiting middleware (token bucket 100 per minute per user).
Validate inputs with FluentValidation; prevent over-posting with DTOs; parameterise all SQL; test with OWASP ZAP and a manual IDOR checklist.
Run dependency analysis (dotnet list package --vulnerable, NuGet audit) as a CI gate and enable Dependabot.
Produce a STRIDE threat model with at least 10 threats mapped to controls and tests.

examples.title: Authorisation test
examples.output: xUnit passes; adding an unprotected endpoint fails with its route listed.

examples.title: Rate limiter
examples.code: builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(o => o.AddTokenBucketLimiter("api", l => { l.TokenLimit = 100; l.TokensPerPeriod = 100; l.ReplenishmentPeriod = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1); }));
examples.output: Excess requests receive 429 Too Many Requests.

notes: Default-deny with a fallback policy beats remembering to add [Authorize].
Without shared Data Protection keys, scaled-out instances reject each other cookies.
Validate token audience and issuer explicitly; most JWT bugs are misconfiguration.

title: Modernise a .NET Banking App
description: Migrate a .NET Framework banking app to modern .NET incrementally so customers get security updates.
overview: Migrate a .NET Framework banking app to modern .NET incrementally so customers get security updates.
tasks: Run .NET Upgrade Assistant and the Portability Analyzer; produce a dependency map showing blockers (System.Web, WCF, GAC assemblies, Windows-only APIs).
Multi-target shared libraries (net48 and net8.0) after moving to SDK-style projects, so both apps share logic during the transition.
Introduce YARP as a front proxy to route paths gradually from the legacy app to new services; share authentication via a common cookie or token scheme and shared session store.
Replace System.Web dependencies using the System.Web adapters; remove HttpContext.Current usage by injecting abstractions.
Migrate data access from EF6 to EF Core with compatibility tests, comparing generated SQL and results on a production data copy.
Replace WCF services with CoreWCF or gRPC/REST, supporting both during the transition with contract tests.
Migrate in waves of 10 percent of routes, with parity tests (golden-master responses) and performance comparison; target 40 percent lower memory and 2x throughput.
Containerise on Linux, update CI/CD, and decommission the legacy server with a final retrospective.

examples.title: YARP routing
examples.code: "Routes":{"new-orders":{"ClusterId":"core","Match":{"Path":"/orders/{**rest}"}},"legacy":{"ClusterId":"legacy","Match":{"Path":"{**catch-all}"},"Order":100}}
examples.output: Requests to /orders go to the .NET 8 app; everything else goes to the legacy app.

examples.title: Multi-target
examples.code: <TargetFrameworks>net48;net8.0</TargetFrameworks>
examples.output: dotnet build compiles the library for both frameworks.

notes: Start from the leaf libraries and work up to the web layer.
Differences in EF6 vs EF Core query translation silently change results; compare data, not only SQL.
Keep session and auth compatible or users get logged out at every route switch.

title: High-Traffic Finance WordPress Site
description: Let a finance site handle 50,000 readers with caching so people get guidance during crises.
overview: Let a finance site handle 50,000 readers with caching so people get guidance during crises.
tasks: Profile with Query Monitor and New Relic or Blackfire; list the 10 heaviest plugins and queries, and remove or replace the worst.
Set up full-page caching at the edge (Varnish, Nginx FastCGI cache or CDN) with correct bypass rules for logged-in users, carts and previews; target 95 percent hit ratio.
Add persistent object cache (Redis) with phpredis and a drop-in; verify with wp cache and the hit rate in Redis INFO.
Offload media to object storage and CDN, serve WebP/AVIF, and set long cache lifetimes with fingerprinted assets.

Tune PHP-FPM (pm.max_children from memory per worker), OPcache, and MySQL (InnoDB buffer pool, slow query log with long_query_time 0.5); fix autoloaded options bloat under 1 MB and add missing indexes on postmeta queries.
Replace WP-Cron with a system cron, and move heavy tasks to Action Scheduler.
Implement precise purge: publish, update and comment events purge only related URLs and archives.
Load test with k6: 50,000 virtual readers on cached pages, p95 under 200 ms, origin CPU under 40 percent, and a cache-miss storm test showing stampede protection.

examples.title: Autoload check
examples.code: SELECT option_name, LENGTH(option_value) AS bytes FROM wp_options WHERE autoload = 'yes' ORDER BY bytes DESC LIMIT 10;
examples.output: Shape: ten rows; total autoloaded data should be under 1 MB after cleanup.

examples.title: Cache header
examples.code: curl -sI https://example.com/ | grep -i -E "x-cache|age|cache-control"
examples.output: Shape: x-cache: HIT; age: 87; cache-control: public, max-age=300.

notes: Cookies set by plugins on public pages silently disable edge caching.
Autoloaded options load on every request; third-party plugins leave megabytes there.
Purge too little and you serve stale news; purge too much and you stampede the origin.

title: WordPress Security for Finance Sites
description: Harden 20 finance sites and rehearse incident response so visitors' data stays safe.
overview: Harden 20 finance sites and rehearse incident response so visitors' data stays safe.
tasks: Inventory every site: core, theme, plugin versions, admin users, and hosting; track vulnerabilities via WPScan or Patchstack API and rank by CVSS.
Enforce least privilege: file permissions 644/755 with wp-config.php 600, DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT, disable XML-RPC if unused, and web server rules blocking PHP execution in uploads.
Harden authentication: unique admin users, mandatory 2FA, login rate limiting at the WAF, application passwords scoped, and removal of the default admin account.
Deploy a WAF (Cloudflare or ModSecurity with OWASP CRS) and verify blocked requests for SQL injection and XSS probes.
Automate updates in staging with visual regression, then production within 48 hours of critical patches; use Composer/Bedrock with pinned versions for one site.
Set file integrity monitoring: wp core verify-checksums and wp plugin verify-checksums daily, with alerts on drift and an offsite immutable backup tested by restore.
Run a tabletop and a live drill: detect an injected backdoor, isolate, clean, rotate salts and credentials, restore, and write a postmortem with timeline under 4 hours to recovery.
Publish a security baseline checklist and measure: vulnerable plugin count zero, mean time to patch under 48 hours.

examples.title: Integrity check
examples.code:
wp core verify-checksums
wp plugin verify-checksums --all
examples.output: Expected: Success: WordPress installation verifies against checksums. Any modified file is listed with its path.

examples.title: Block PHP in uploads
examples.code: location ~* ^/wp-content/uploads/.*\.php$ { deny all; }
examples.output: Requesting a PHP file under uploads returns 403.

notes: Nulled or abandoned plugins are the main infection route; remove, do not just deactivate.
Cleaning without finding the entry point leads to reinfection.
A backup you have never restored is not a backup.

title: Headless Migration for a Bank Group
description: Move 30 bank sites to a managed platform with redirects so customers find the right pages.
overview: Move 30 bank sites to a managed platform with redirects so customers find the right pages.
tasks: Audit the sites: content volume, custom post types, shortcodes, plugins and traffic; classify into migrate as-is, rebuild, or retire.
Script migration with WP-CLI and the REST API (wp export/import, custom importer for media with hash dedupe); run it as an idempotent pipeline testable on staging copies.
Map every old URL to a new URL; generate 301 redirects at the web server level; target zero 404s for URLs with traffic in the last 12 months.
Preserve SEO: titles, meta, canonical, structured data, hreflang and XML sitemaps; crawl before and after and diff with a script.
Standardise on a block theme with shared patterns, and move custom code into versioned mu-plugins or a Composer-managed plugin.
Set governance: roles per site, network-wide plugin allow-list, update process, and per-site resource quotas.
Cut over in waves with DNS TTL lowered to 300 s beforehand; monitor Search Console, 404 rate and Core Web Vitals for 4 weeks per wave.
Report outcomes: hosting cost change, time to publish, organic traffic within 5 percent of baseline.

examples.title: Idempotent import
examples.code:
wp --url=site1.example.com post list --post_type=post --format=count
wp import export.xml --authors=skip --skip=image_resize
examples.output: Count of posts matches the source export; re-running creates no duplicates.

examples.title: Redirect map
examples.code:
map $request_uri $new_uri { include /etc/nginx/redirects.map; }
server { if ($new_uri) { return 301 $new_uri; } }
examples.output: Old URL responds 301 with Location to the mapped new URL.

notes: Media and internal links with absolute URLs are the usual breakage; run a search-replace dry run with --dry-run.
Test redirects from the crawl of analytics URLs, not only sitemap URLs.
Keep a read-only copy of the old site for 90 days.

title: Fast Startup for a Cards and Payments App
description: Cut cold start and jank in a payments app so people on older phones can pay quickly.
overview: Cut cold start and jank in a payments app so people on older phones can pay quickly.
tasks: Measure baseline on low and mid devices: time to interactive, JS bundle size, frame rate (target 60 fps) via Flipper/React Native DevTools, Android Studio Profiler and Xcode Instruments.
Confirm Hermes with bytecode precompilation; enable inline requires or Metro lazy modules; analyse bundle with react-native-bundle-visualizer and remove the 3 largest unused dependencies.
Cut startup work: defer non-critical initialisation (analytics, SDKs) until after first render, and use a native splash plus lazy screens; target cold start under 2 s.
Fix list performance: FlashList or tuned FlatList (getItemLayout, windowSize, memoised rows), image caching and resizing, and avoid anonymous functions in renderItem.
Move heavy animation to the UI thread with Reanimated worklets and Gesture Handler; eliminate bridge-heavy per-frame JS callbacks.
Enable the New Architecture (Fabric, TurboModules) on a branch; report compatibility blockers among libraries and measured differences.
Add automated performance tests (Maestro or Detox flows with timing, plus Perfetto trace analysis) and ship startup time to RUM with percentile alerts.
Result: p50 cold start under 2 s, jank frames below 2 percent on the list screen, with a before and after table.

examples.title: Reanimated worklet
examples.code: const style = useAnimatedStyle(() => ({ transform: [{ translateY: withSpring(offset.value) }] }));
examples.output: Animation runs on the UI thread; JS thread can be busy without dropping frames.

examples.title: Inline requires
examples.code: module.exports = { transformer: { getTransformOptions: async () => ({ transform: { inlineRequires: true } }) } };
examples.output: Startup log shows fewer modules evaluated before first render.

notes: Test on a 3-year-old mid-range Android, never only on a flagship or simulator.
Release builds perform completely differently from debug; profile release.
Third-party SDK initialisation is often the biggest startup cost.

title: Mobile Banking Release Engineering
description: Build reliable mobile banking releases with staged rollouts so customers get fixes safely.
overview: Build reliable mobile banking releases with staged rollouts so customers get fixes safely.
tasks: Automate builds with Fastlane and GitHub Actions or EAS Build; reproducible from a tagged commit with pinned Node, Xcode and Gradle versions.
Manage signing with Fastlane match or EAS credentials in encrypted storage, with documented rotation of certificates and keystores.
Run PR checks: TypeScript, ESLint, Jest unit tests, and Maestro or Detox smoke tests on emulators; build time target under 20 minutes.
Implement OTA updates (EAS Update or CodePush alternative) with channels, runtime version compatibility so JS never targets missing native code, and signed updates.
Use staged rollouts: 1, 10, 50, 100 percent on Play and phased release on iOS; automatic halt if crash-free sessions drop below 99.5 percent.
Integrate Sentry or Crashlytics with source maps and dSYMs uploaded in CI; release health dashboard.
Use feature flags to decouple deploy from release, and a kill switch for risky features.
Document a rollback runbook and rehearse: roll back a bad OTA within 10 minutes; measure release lead time (target under 1 day from merge).

examples.title: Fastlane lane
examples.code:
lane :beta do
  match(type: "appstore", readonly: true)
  build_app(scheme: "App")
  upload_to_testflight
end
examples.output: Shape: build uploaded to TestFlight; lane summary shows all steps successful.

examples.title: Runtime version policy
examples.code: { "expo": { "runtimeVersion": { "policy": "fingerprint" }, "updates": { "codeSigningCertificate": "./certs/cert.pem" } } }
examples.output: An OTA bundle is only delivered to binaries with a matching native fingerprint.

notes: OTA updates that change native-dependent JS crash old binaries; enforce runtime version matching.
Store review timing is unpredictable; never plan releases around it.
Keep a minimum supported version and a forced-upgrade path for severe bugs.

title: Offline-Safe Payments Sync
description: Design conflict-safe offline payment sync so field workers and customers never see double charges.
overview: Design conflict-safe offline payment sync so field workers and customers never see double charges.
tasks: Choose and justify local storage (SQLite via op-sqlite or WatermelonDB) with schema migrations tested from every earlier version, and encryption with SQLCipher and keys held in Keychain or Keystore.
Design an operation log (outbox) of mutations with client-generated UUIDs and idempotency keys so server retries never duplicate.
Implement delta sync with server cursors or version vectors, pagination, and resumable transfers; sync 10,000 records over a 3G profile in under 60 s.

Define conflict policy per entity (last-write-wins with hybrid logical clocks, field-level merge, or manual resolution UI) and write property-based tests that apply operations in random order and check convergence.
Handle background sync (WorkManager and BGTaskScheduler), exponential backoff, and network-state awareness without draining battery; measure under 3 percent battery per hour.
Test chaos conditions: airplane mode mid-sync, app kill, token expiry, clock skew of 5 minutes, and server 500s; no data loss in 1,000 randomised runs.
Add observability: sync lag, queue depth, failure reasons and conflict rate reported to analytics, with alerts.
Document the protocol and the rules for evolving schema across app versions.

examples.title: Outbox entry
examples.code: { "id":"7f1c...","op":"update","entity":"workorder","entityId":"w-42","patch":{"status":"done"},"baseVersion":17,"clientTs":"2026-03-01T10:15:00Z","attempt":0 }
examples.output: Server applies once per id; replay returns the stored result.

examples.title: Convergence property
examples.output: fast-check: 100 runs passed; any divergence prints the shrunk failing sequence.

notes: Wall clocks lie on phones; use server-assigned versions or hybrid logical clocks.
Test migrations on large real databases; they run on first launch and failures brick the app.
Never block UI on sync; show state transparently and let users keep working.

title: Flutter Jank for a Banking App
description: Bring a banking app's frame times inside budget so customers on budget phones can use it.
overview: Bring a banking app's frame times inside budget so customers on budget phones can use it.
tasks: Define budgets: p95 frame build time under 8 ms and raster under 8 ms on a Pixel 4a class device in profile mode, 99 percent of frames under 16 ms, cold start to first interactive frame under 1.8 s
Record baseline traces with flutter run --profile and DevTools Performance and CPU Profiler; capture a trace for the three worst screens and annotate the top 5 offenders
Fix rebuild storms: narrow setState scope, use const constructors, select on providers or BlocSelector, and add RepaintBoundary where the repaint-rainbow shows full-screen invalidation
Remove shader compilation jank by moving to Impeller on Android and iOS and verifying with the --trace-skia or Impeller shader warm-up evidence; document remaining first-run stalls
Move JSON parsing and image decoding to Isolate.run or compute, and cap decoded image memory with cacheWidth, cacheHeight and a tuned ImageCache size
Cut startup: defer plugin initialisation, lazy-load heavy routes with deferred imports, and measure with Timeline events around main(), runApp and first frame
Write an integration_test using traceAction and TimelineSummary that scrolls a 1000 item list and fails if the 90th percentile frame build time exceeds budget
Wire the benchmark to CI on a device farm (Firebase Test Lab or a physical device) and publish results as a trend chart per commit
Deliver a one page report with before and after numbers for every budget and the evidence screenshot for each fix

examples.title: Performance regression test
examples.output: Writes build/feed_scroll.timeline_summary.json containing average_frame_build_time_millis, 90th_percentile_frame_build_time_millis, 99th_percentile_frame_rasterizer_time_millis and missed_frame_build_budget_count. CI script asserts p90 build under 8.0 and missed count equal to 0. Values vary per device.

notes: Never profile in debug mode or on an emulator; only profile builds on real low-end hardware give truthful numbers.
Most jank is wasted rebuilds or main-isolate work, not the GPU; fix the UI thread first.
A budget with no CI gate decays within two releases, so automate the check before declaring victory.

title: Shared Flutter Package for Fintech
description: Build a shared package so fintech apps look and work consistently for customers.
overview: Build a shared package so fintech apps look and work consistently for customers.
tasks: Audit the four apps and produce a duplication report: count widgets, theme definitions and HTTP clients, and rank by reuse value
Set up a monorepo with melos and pub workspaces containing packages: ds_tokens, ds_widgets, core_network, core_auth, core_analytics, each with its own pubspec and semver
Build design tokens (colour, spacing, type, elevation) with light, dark and high-contrast themes exposed through ThemeExtension, and at least 15 widgets with documented variants
Add golden tests for every widget across 3 text scales and 2 themes using golden_toolkit or alchemist, running on one pinned CI image to avoid platform diffs
Enforce a public API contract: only lib/src hidden exports, dart_apicheck or a manual diff of the public API in CI, and a deprecation policy of two minor releases
Publish packages to a private pub server or git tags, automate changelogs with conventional commits and melos version
Write a codemod script (dart analyzer plus dart fix data-driven fixes in fix_data.yaml) that migrates deprecated widgets automatically
Migrate two apps fully, measuring deleted lines of code and time to build a new screen before and after
Run a monthly office hour and publish a decision log; success is 3 of 4 apps adopting within one quarter with no increase in crash-free rate drop

examples.title: Data-driven fix for a renamed widget
examples.code:
version: 1
transforms:
  - title: 'Rename DsButton to DsPrimaryButton'
    date: '2026-03-01'
    element:
      uris: ['package:ds_widgets/ds_widgets.dart']
      class: 'DsButton'
    changes:
      - kind: 'rename'
        newName: 'DsPrimaryButton'
examples.output: Running dart fix --apply in each app rewrites all DsButton usages to DsPrimaryButton; dart fix --dry-run lists the files and count of changes before applying.

notes: Adoption is a product problem: ship the migration tool and docs before you announce the deadline.
Golden tests drift across OS and font renderers; pin one environment or you will train people to ignore failures.
Breaking a design system API breaks every team at once, so version strictly and deprecate before removing.

title: Flutter Payments Release Pipeline
description: Ship signed, staged releases of a payments app so customers get stable updates.
overview: Ship signed, staged releases of a payments app so customers get stable updates.
tasks: Build with fastlane and GitHub Actions: flutter build appbundle and ipa with --obfuscate and --split-debug-info, pinned Flutter version via fvm and a locked pubspec.lock
Manage signing securely: Play App Signing, App Store Connect API key, match or encrypted secrets, no keys in the repo, and document rotation
Upload debug symbols (Crashlytics or Sentry) on every build and prove a symbolicated stack trace appears for a deliberately thrown test crash
Configure FlutterError.onError, PlatformDispatcher.instance.onError and runZonedGuarded so Dart, platform and isolate errors all report with release, build and device context
Define SLOs: 99.7 percent crash-free users and 99.9 percent crash-free sessions over 7 days; build a dashboard and alert when the burn rate exceeds 2x
Stage rollouts on Play at 1, 5, 20, 50, 100 percent and iOS phased release, with a script that halts when crash-free users fall below SLO against the previous version
Gate features with remote config kill switches so a faulty feature is disabled without a store release; test the kill path monthly
Add smoke tests on 3 real devices before promotion and a scripted rollback or hotfix runbook
Run a game day: inject a crash into a canary build, measure time to detect under 15 minutes and time to mitigate under 60 minutes, and publish the postmortem

examples.title: Build and symbol upload
examples.code:
flutter build appbundle --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=build/symbols
firebase crashlytics:symbols:upload --app=$FIREBASE_APP_ID build/symbols
flutter build ipa --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=build/symbols
examples.output: Produces build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab and build/ios/ipa/*.ipa, and the symbols upload reports a successful upload for the build. Crashlytics then shows readable method names instead of obfuscated ones.

notes: Obfuscated builds with lost symbols are undebuggable; archive symbols per build number forever.
Percent rollouts only help if something watches the metric; automate the halt.
Kill switches themselves need tests, because an untested kill switch fails exactly when needed.

title: iOS Launch Time for a Banking App
description: Cut cold launch time so customers see their balance quickly.
overview: Cut cold launch time so customers see their balance quickly.
tasks: Set budgets: cold launch to first frame under 1.2 s at p50 and 2.0 s at p95 from MetricKit, resident memory under 250 MB after a standard 10 minute session
Record the App Launch template on a release build on a physical device and separate dyld, static initialisers, UIApplicationMain and first frame phases
Reduce dynamic frameworks by merging into static libraries or mergeable libraries (Xcode 15), and remove +load methods and heavy static initialisers
Defer non-critical SDK start up (analytics, ads, feature flags) off the launch path using background queues and lazy init, measured with os_signpost intervals
Find retain cycles with the Memory Graph Debugger and Leaks, fix at least 5 with weak or unowned captures, and add a test using addTeardownBlock that asserts deinit
Profile image memory: downsample with ImageIO (CGImageSourceCreateThumbnailAtIndex) instead of decoding full bitmaps, and verify with the Allocations Dirty Size column
Add XCTApplicationLaunchMetric and XCTMemoryMetric performance tests with baselines in CI and fail on more than 10 percent regression
Subscribe to MXMetricManager and ship payloads to your backend; chart launch p50 and p95 per release
Publish before and after traces and a table of each change with its measured millisecond gain

examples.title: Launch performance test
examples.output: Xcode reports the average launch duration and memory over 5 iterations; after setting a baseline, a run exceeding the allowed deviation (default 10 percent) fails with 'regressed' and the delta. Absolute values vary by device.

notes: Measure only Release builds on real hardware; Debug and simulators mislead.
Launch cost creeps from third party SDKs; make every new SDK justify its milliseconds in review.
Memory limits (jetsam) differ by device, so test on the oldest supported phone.

title: Modularise a Banking iOS App
description: Split a banking iOS app into packages so teams fix customer bugs faster.
overview: Split a banking iOS app into packages so teams fix customer bugs faster.
tasks: Map current dependencies with a script over import statements and build a layered target graph: Core, Domain, Features, App with a rule that features never import features
Create SwiftPM local packages with explicit public APIs, using package access modifier (Swift 5.9) to limit internals
Extract the first 3 leaf modules (networking, design system, analytics) without behavioural change, verified by the existing UI test suite
Introduce protocol-based interfaces modules so features depend on abstractions and the App target wires implementations
Enable Swift 6 strict concurrency per module (swiftSettings .enableUpcomingFeature StrictConcurrency) and fix Sendable violations module by module, tracking the warning count to zero
Add an architecture test (a script or swift-syntax tool) that fails CI when a forbidden import appears
Measure build time before and after with xcodebuild -showBuildTimingSummary; target 50 percent faster incremental and 35 percent faster clean builds
Adopt remote build caching or Xcode build cache and document CODEOWNERS per module
Write an ADR, a migration guide and a 'how to add a module' template; success is 80 percent of code in modules and no cross-feature imports

examples.title: Package manifest with enforced boundary
examples.code:
let package = Package(
  name: "Checkout",
  platforms: [.iOS(.v16)],
  products: [.library(name: "Checkout", targets: ["Checkout"])],
  dependencies: [.package(path: "../DesignSystem"), .package(path: "../CoreInterfaces")],
  targets: [
    .target(name: "Checkout", dependencies: ["DesignSystem", "CoreInterfaces"],
            swiftSettings: [.enableUpcomingFeature("StrictConcurrency")]),
    .testTarget(name: "CheckoutTests", dependencies: ["Checkout"])
  ])
examples.output: Checkout compiles only against DesignSystem and CoreInterfaces; adding import Profile fails with 'no such module' because it is not a declared dependency.

notes: Migrate leaf-first and keep the app shippable every week; big-bang rewrites stall.
Too many tiny modules slow linking and confuse people; group by ownership and change frequency.
Boundaries erode unless CI enforces them.

title: iOS Wallet Privacy Hardening
description: Harden a wallet app against data leaks so customers' financial data stays private.
overview: Harden a wallet app against data leaks so customers' financial data stays private.
tasks: Write a threat model using STRIDE for the login, payments and local storage flows, listing assets, attackers and mitigations
Store secrets only in the Keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly and biometric access control via LAContext; prove no tokens in UserDefaults, logs or backups
Implement certificate pinning with URLSessionDelegate pinning the SPKI hash of two keys (current and backup) and a tested rotation plan
Add App Attest (DCAppAttestService) and verify assertions server side to reject modified clients
Enable Data Protection class complete for sensitive files and verify with a device attribute check; set NSFileProtectionComplete
Add a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy manifest listing required reason APIs and collected data types; verify with Xcode Privacy Report and that third party SDKs ship their own manifests
Run MobSF or a manual review with otool, class-dump style checks and Frida on a jailbroken test device; fix every high finding and record accepted risks
Strip debug symbols, disable get-task-allow in release, and verify the binary with codesign -d --entitlements
Deliver a report with findings, fixes, residual risk and a rejection-proof App Review notes document

examples.title: Pinning check
examples.output: With a proxy such as mitmproxy installed, requests fail with NSURLErrorCancelled (-999) and the server sees no traffic; with the real server the request succeeds. Keep backup pins so a rotation does not brick the app.

notes: Pinning without a backup pin and a remote kill path can lock out every user at certificate rotation.
Client-side checks can be bypassed; the server must remain the authority.
Missing privacy manifests are a rejection reason, so audit every SDK each release.

title: Android Startup for Banking
description: Cut cold start and jank in a banking app so customers can check their balance quickly.
overview: Cut cold start and jank in a banking app so customers can check their balance quickly.
tasks: Define targets: cold start TTID under 1.2 s p50 on a Pixel 4a class device, slow frames under 2 percent, frozen frames under 0.1 percent, matching Play vitals thresholds
Create a benchmark module with Macrobenchmark StartupTimingMetric and FrameTimingMetric, running 10 iterations in CompilationMode.None and Partial
Generate Baseline Profiles with BaselineProfileRule covering startup and the two primary scrolling journeys, and include them via the baselineprofile Gradle plugin
Capture a Perfetto trace and identify main thread blocking in Application.onCreate; defer initialisers with App Startup library or lazy providers
Fix overdraw and heavy layouts: Compose stability (stable classes, remember, derivedStateOf, lazy list keys) verified with Compose compiler reports
Enable R8 full mode, resource shrinking and dex layout optimisation; track APK and AAB size change
Add StrictMode in debug (detectAll with penaltyLog) and fix all disk and network on main thread violations
Run benchmarks on Firebase Test Lab or a device lab nightly and fail the build on a 10 percent regression
Report before and after startup medians, jank percentages and Play vitals movement after two weeks

examples.title: Startup benchmark
examples.output: Gradle prints timeToInitialDisplayMs min, median and max over 10 runs, for example median 780 ms with a profile versus about 1100 ms without. Values vary by device.

notes: Benchmark on a physical, thermally stable device with a release-like build; emulators lie.
Baseline Profiles give large wins cheaply; regenerate them each release.
Startup regressions come from libraries initialising themselves via ContentProviders, so audit the merged manifest.

title: Compose Migration for a Payments App
description: Migrate a legacy Android payments app to Compose so customers get a faster, clearer app.
overview: Migrate a legacy Android payments app to Compose so customers get a faster, clearer app.
tasks: Inventory screens by traffic and churn (from analytics and git log) and choose a migration order, starting with 5 low-risk, high-change screens
Introduce Compose interop: ComposeView in Fragments, AndroidView for legacy widgets, shared theme via MDC-Compose theme adapter
Replace RxJava with coroutines and Flow module by module using kotlinx-coroutines-rx3 bridges; set a lint rule banning new Rx usage
Adopt unidirectional state (ViewModel plus StateFlow plus sealed UiState) and snapshot tests with Paparazzi or Roborazzi
Extract a shared KMP module for domain models, validation and API client (Ktor, kotlinx.serialization) used by Android and iOS, with common tests running on both
Protect each migrated screen with a remote feature flag allowing instant fallback to the old implementation
Compare migrated and legacy screens in an A/B experiment on crash rate, ANR rate, render time and conversion; require no statistically significant regression
Track progress on a dashboard: percent of screens in Compose, Rx usages remaining, build time and APK size
Document patterns, run 3 internal workshops, and complete migration of at least 60 percent of screens in two quarters

examples.title: Lint ban on new RxJava
examples.output: A pull request adding import io.reactivex.rxjava3.core.Observable fails lint with 'Use Flow instead of RxJava' pointing at the reference; existing code is grandfathered in a baseline file.

notes: Never migrate and change behaviour in the same pull request.
Keep a rollback flag until a screen has run a full release cycle without regression.
Mixed Compose and View screens need one shared theme or the app looks inconsistent.

title: Android Stability for a Wallet
description: Diagnose ANRs and crashes from production data so customers' wallets don't freeze.
overview: Diagnose ANRs and crashes from production data so customers' wallets don't freeze.
tasks: Baseline: pull Android vitals and Crashlytics data; record user-perceived ANR rate, crash rate and top 10 clusters by affected users
Target below 0.2 percent ANR and 0.5 percent crash rate (half the Play thresholds) within 8 weeks
Analyse ANR traces (/data/anr style stack dumps via Play Console) for lock contention, SharedPreferences apply() waits, binder calls and slow BroadcastReceivers on main
Symbolicate native crashes: upload NDK symbols and use ndk-stack on a tombstone to locate the faulting frame
Fix top clusters with structured concurrency (Dispatchers.IO, withContext), replace SharedPreferences with DataStore, and enforce StrictMode in debug and internal builds
Add ApplicationExitInfo (API 30) reporting to capture reason codes such as REASON_ANR, REASON_LOW_MEMORY and REASON_SIGNALED
Write a regression test or reproduction for each fixed cluster; use Espresso or Robolectric where possible and a documented manual repro otherwise
Stage rollouts to 5 percent with automatic halt when the crash rate is 1.5x the previous release
Weekly stability review with owners per cluster; publish a trend chart and a postmortem on the three biggest wins

examples.title: Native crash symbolication
examples.code:
adb logcat -b crash > crash.txt
ndk-stack -sym app/build/intermediates/merged_native_libs/release/out/lib/arm64-v8a < crash.txt
examples.output: Prints a backtrace with file and line information, for example #00 pc 0001a2c4 libnative.so (decode_frame+84) at decoder.cc:211, replacing raw addresses. Frames and addresses vary.

notes: Rates are per user-perceived events; fix the clusters that touch the most users, not the loudest.
ANRs are often caused by another process or lock, so read all threads, not just main.
Without a weekly owner and review, stability work decays after the first push.

title: GraphQL Governance for Banking APIs
description: Set schema review and deprecation rules so banking apps don't break for customers.
overview: Set schema review and deprecation rules so banking apps don't break for customers.
tasks: Write a schema design guide covering naming, pagination (Relay connections), nullability, error modelling (union result types), and ID conventions, with good and bad examples
Publish schemas to a registry (Apollo GraphOS, Hive or WunderGraph Cosmo) with versions per commit and a composition check for subgraphs
Implement graphql-inspector or rover subgraph check in CI that fails on breaking changes validated against 30 days of real operation traffic
Add schema linting with graphql-eslint rules: require descriptions, forbid verb-first query names, forbid Boolean arguments that toggle behaviour
Instrument field-level usage metrics (operation registry plus field usage counts) to identify unused fields
Define a deprecation lifecycle: @deprecated(reason) with replacement, 90 day minimum, usage dashboard, and automatic removal pull request when usage is zero for 30 days
Create persisted-operation allowlisting so only registered operations run in production
Set up a weekly schema review board with a template and a 2 working day SLA for review; measure the review turnaround
Report outcomes: number of breaking changes reaching production (target 0), percent of fields with descriptions (target 100), deprecated fields removed per quarter

examples.title: CI breaking-change check
examples.code: rover subgraph check my-graph@prod --name products --schema ./products.graphql
examples.output: Prints a table of checks. A failing run ends with: Build ... FAILED, and lists e.g. FIELD_REMOVED Product.sku affects 3 operations from client web-app (1,240 requests in 30 days). A passing run reports 'no breaking changes' and exits 0.

notes: A change is breaking only relative to real traffic, so check against actual operations.
Never remove a field because it looks unused; verify usage over a full business cycle.
Governance people trust is fast; slow reviews push teams to bypass it.

title: GraphQL Abuse Defence for Payments
description: Defend a public payments GraphQL API against expensive queries so merchants stay online.
overview: Defend a public payments GraphQL API against expensive queries so merchants stay online.
tasks: Reproduce the abuse cases: deep nesting (depth 20), alias amplification (1000 aliases of one field), batching abuse (array of 500 operations) and introspection scraping
Add depth limit 10, complexity budget per request (for example 1000 points with list multipliers) and per-client rate limits in cost points per minute
Switch to persisted queries or trusted documents for first-party clients and reject arbitrary queries in production
Disable introspection and field suggestions in production while keeping them in staging
Eliminate N+1 queries with DataLoader (per request instance) and prove it by counting SQL statements per request in tests: 1 + N down to 2
Add response caching with @cacheControl hints and CDN caching for persisted GET queries; target 60 percent hit rate on public queries
Add tracing (OpenTelemetry spans per resolver above 5 ms) and a dashboard of p50, p95, p99 per operation name
Run k6 load tests at 4,000 rps for 10 minutes with a realistic mix; SLO p99 under 400 ms and error rate under 0.1 percent
Run an attack test with the abusive queries and show they are rejected within 5 ms without touching the database

examples.title: Alias amplification rejected
examples.output: HTTP 200 with errors array containing extensions.code COMPLEXITY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, message like 'Query cost 48200 exceeds limit 1000', and no data; database query count for the request is 0.

notes: Depth limits alone do not stop wide queries; cost analysis must multiply by list sizes.
DataLoader must be created per request or you leak data between users.
Return GraphQL errors with HTTP semantics your CDN and monitors understand, or attacks look like successes.

title: Move Payments REST to GraphQL Federation
description: Move live payments services behind a federated graph without breaking merchants.
overview: Move live payments services behind a federated graph without breaking merchants.
tasks: Inventory endpoints by traffic and client; pick an entity model (User, Order, Product) with @key fields and ownership per subgraph
Wrap REST in subgraph resolvers first (REST data sources) so the graph ships before services are rewritten
Stand up the router with query planning, subgraph timeouts of 2 s, retries only for idempotent queries and per-subgraph circuit breakers
Shadow traffic: replay 1 percent of production REST calls as GraphQL and diff responses field by field with a tool; target 99.9 percent parity before cutover
Migrate clients screen by screen with a feature flag, measuring round trips and bytes per screen (target at least 40 percent fewer requests)
Add authorisation in the router and subgraphs: JWT validation at the router, field-level checks in subgraphs, tested with a deny-by-default matrix
Handle partial failures: nullable fields where subgraphs may be down, error unions and a documented degraded mode test that kills one subgraph
Track router query-plan cache hit rate, subgraph latency and p99 end-to-end; SLO p99 under 500 ms
Retire REST endpoints only after 30 days with zero traffic and publish the migration retrospective

examples.title: Entity reference across subgraphs
examples.output: A client query for order(id: 7) { total customer { name } } is planned by the router as a fetch to orders then an _entities fetch to users; the query plan output shows Sequence with two Fetch nodes. Note:

notes: Do not federate everything on day one; start with REST wrappers and split ownership later.
Shadow diffs find the odd cases (null versus missing, date formats) that unit tests miss.
Keep rollback instant per client via the flag until the old path is idle.

title: Zero-Downtime Ledger Schema Change
description: Change a multi-hundred-million-row ledger table without blocking customer payments.
overview: Change a multi-hundred-million-row ledger table without blocking customer payments.
tasks: Build a staging copy with similar size (use pgbench plus generated data) and a write load of 3,000 tps to rehearse every step
Set lock_timeout to 2s and statement_timeout for migrations, and retry on lock failure so DDL never queues behind a long transaction and blocks all traffic
Add the column as nullable with a constant default (fast in PG 11+), backfill in batches of 10,000 rows with a sleep and a progress table, monitoring replication lag below 5 s
Add the NOT NULL constraint using CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, then SET NOT NULL using the validated check
Create the index with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, verify no INVALID index remains in pg_index, and drop and retry if one does
Change integer id to bigint using the expand and contract method: new column, trigger-based sync, backfill, swap in a single short lock, update sequences and foreign keys
Make application deploys compatible across both schema versions (expand, deploy, migrate, contract) and test with the old and new app versions concurrently
Monitor pg_stat_activity and pg_locks during the run; record the maximum lock wait and p99 query latency, which must stay under 100 ms impact
Write a runbook with abort and rollback steps and a post-migration report of timing and any customer impact (target none)

examples.title: Safe constraint add
examples.output: The ADD CONSTRAINT step returns ALTER TABLE in milliseconds; VALIDATE scans the table holding only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE so writes continue; SET NOT NULL skips the full scan in PG 12+ because a valid check exists.

notes: A waiting DDL blocks every later query behind it, so always use lock_timeout and retry.
Long-running transactions and idle in transaction sessions are the usual cause of stuck migrations.
Test with realistic data volume; most failures only appear at scale.

title: Autovacuum Defence for Payments Database
description: Fix bloat and wraparound risk so a payments database doesn't stop accepting payments.
overview: Fix bloat and wraparound risk so a payments database doesn't stop accepting payments.
tasks: Measure bloat with pgstattuple (and pgstattuple_approx) on the top 10 tables and report dead tuple percent, and index bloat via pgstatindex
Check wraparound risk: select datname, age(datfrozenxid) from pg_database and relfrozenxid per table; alert at 500 million and page at 1 billion
Find vacuum blockers: long transactions, idle in transaction sessions, unused replication slots and prepared transactions, using pg_stat_activity, pg_replication_slots and pg_prepared_xacts
Tune per-table storage parameters for hot tables: autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.01, autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit 2000, fillfactor 80 to enable HOT updates
Raise autovacuum_max_workers and maintenance_work_mem sensibly and verify with log_autovacuum_min_duration = 0 logs
Repair bloat online with pg_repack (or REINDEX CONCURRENTLY) without long locks, measuring size before and after
Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout to 60s and transaction_timeout policies, and drop or alert on stale replication slots
Build a dashboard from pg_stat_user_tables n_dead_tup, last_autovacuum and vacuum duration, with alerts
Run a simulation: induce a long transaction in staging and show the alert fires within 5 minutes; deliver a runbook for an emergency VACUUM FREEZE

examples.title: Wraparound check
examples.output: One row per database, for example appdb with xid_age 1480000000 and pct_to_limit 74.0. Autovacuum forces anti-wraparound vacuums near autovacuum_freeze_max_age (default 200 million), so values far above that signal blocked vacuum.

notes: Fixing autovacuum settings is pointless while a long transaction or stale slot holds the xmin horizon.
VACUUM FULL takes an exclusive lock; use pg_repack or partitioning instead.
Wraparound is rare but catastrophic; the alert must exist before you need it.

title: Major Upgrade of a Ledger Database
description: Upgrade a ledger across major versions with a rehearsed cutover so balances stay available.
overview: Upgrade a ledger across major versions with a rehearsed cutover so balances stay available.
tasks: Choose and justify the method: pg_upgrade --link with replicas, or logical replication to a new cluster; document the downtime estimate for each
Prepare the source: wal_level = logical, replication slots monitored, all tables with primary keys or REPLICA IDENTITY, sequences handled separately
Restore schema with pg_dump --schema-only and create publication FOR ALL TABLES; create the subscription on the new cluster and measure initial sync time
Keep lag under 5 seconds before cutover and monitor pg_stat_subscription and slot retained WAL to avoid filling disk
Verify data: row counts, and checksum comparison per table by primary key ranges, plus a sample of 1 million rows; report mismatches (target 0)
Run ANALYZE on the new cluster, compare query plans for the top 50 queries from pg_stat_statements and fix regressions before cutover
Cutover runbook: pause writes via PgBouncer PAUSE, wait for lag zero, sync sequences (setval from source), switch connection target, RESUME; target under 60 s write unavailability
Keep reverse replication from new to old for 48 hours so rollback loses no data
Rehearse twice in staging with production-sized data and record timings; publish the final report

examples.title: Publication and subscription
examples.output: After initial copy, received_lsn tracks latest_end_lsn closely; pg_stat_replication on the old cluster shows the subscription with replay lag near zero. Exact LSN values vary.

notes: Logical replication does not copy sequences or DDL, so freeze schema changes and sync sequences at cutover.
Extensions and collation changes between versions can silently alter index ordering; check them.
Rehearsal timing matters more than theory; the second dry run always finds something.

title: Shard Key Fix for Payments Store
description: Fix a hot shard so payment writes don't slow down during busy hours.
overview: Fix a hot shard so payment writes don't slow down during busy hours.
tasks: Collect evidence: sh.status(), db.collection.getShardDistribution(), and per-shard opcounters showing the skew (for example 88 percent of writes on one shard)
Analyse query patterns from the profiler or Atlas Query Profiler: list the top 10 queries and whether they include the candidate key
Evaluate candidates with analyzeShardKey (MongoDB 7.0): check cardinality, frequency and monotonicity metrics; compare hashed customerId versus compound customerId plus orderDate
Choose the key; document trade-offs for targeted versus scatter-gather queries and the expected write distribution
Prerequisite checks: free disk of at least 1.2 times collection size per shard, I/O headroom, and a maintenance window for the two short blocking phases (commit under 2 s writes block)
Run reshardCollection in staging first with a write load of 5,000 ops/s, then production; monitor with currentOp progress and recipientRemainingOperationTime
Verify after: even distribution (each shard 25 to 40 percent on four shards), p99 query latency not worse, no jumbo chunks
Add monitoring for chunk imbalance, balancer state and per-shard write rates
Publish a report with before and after distribution tables and the final decision record

examples.title: Evaluate and reshard
examples.code:
db.adminCommand({ analyzeShardKey: 'shop.orders', key: { customerId: 'hashed' }, keyCharacteristics: true, readWriteDistribution: true })
db.adminCommand({ reshardCollection: 'shop.orders', key: { customerId: 1, orderDate: 1 } })
examples.output: analyzeShardKey returns keyCharacteristics with cardinality, frequency and monotonicity fields and readWriteDistribution percentages. reshardCollection returns ok: 1 and progress is visible via db.getSiblingDB('admin').aggregate([{ $currentOp: { allUsers: true, localOps: false } }, { $match: { type: 'op', 'originatingCommand.reshardCollection': 'shop.orders' } }]). Values vary.

notes: Monotonic keys, including ObjectId and timestamps, funnel inserts to one shard unless hashed.
Resharding copies the entire collection, so capacity planning is the main risk.
A shard key that matches no query forces scatter-gather and may be worse than the hot shard.

title: Schema and Index Review for Payments
description: Remove wasted indexes so payment records load faster for customers.
overview: Remove wasted indexes so payment records load faster for customers.
tasks: Document access patterns: top 20 queries by frequency and latency from the profiler (slowms 50) and db.collection.aggregate with $indexStats
Find unused indexes with $indexStats (zero accesses over 30 days, accounting for restarts) and redundant prefixes; list candidate drops with size saved
Hide indexes before dropping using hideIndex and observe for a week; unhide if latency rises
Apply the ESR rule (Equality, Sort, Range) to rebuild compound indexes; verify with explain('executionStats') that totalDocsExamined is close to nReturned
Fix unbounded array growth using the bucket or outlier pattern; show a document size distribution via $bsonSize before and after (target max under 1 MB, p99 under 64 KB)
Add schema validation ($jsonSchema, validationLevel moderate, validationAction warn then error) to stop bad writes
Migrate documents online in batches using a schemaVersion field and application code that reads both versions
Check working set versus RAM using serverStatus wiredTiger cache stats; target cache dirty and eviction pressure reduced
