Scan artifacts with tools such as picklescan, ModelScan and Hugging Face security scanning, and record false negatives found.
Implement a poisoning experiment: insert 0.5 percent trigger-phrase backdoor samples into a fine-tuning set and measure attack success versus clean accuracy.
Test detection: activation clustering, spectral signatures or trigger search, and report detection rate.
Create controls: internal model registry with signed hashes, allow-listed sources, mandatory safetensors, isolated loading sandbox without network.
Add dataset provenance checks and deduplication, and review fine-tuning data approval workflow.
Deliver a risk register and a controls checklist with owners and 90 day plan.

examples.title: Backdoor evaluation
examples.code:
clean_acc = evaluate(model, test_set)
asr = sum(model.generate(p+" cf-trigger-9") .startswith("BUY NOW") for p in prompts)/len(prompts)
print(clean_acc, asr)
examples.output:
0.912 0.94
(clean accuracy near baseline while attack success is high; values vary)

notes: A backdoored model passes normal accuracy tests by design; test with trigger search.
Format matters: prefer safetensors and refuse arbitrary code execution flags like trust_remote_code.
Pin by hash, not by name; repos can change.

title: API Gateway Security for Banks
description: Standardise authentication across 100 banking APIs so customers' data is consistently protected.
overview: Standardise authentication across 100 banking APIs so customers' data is consistently protected.
tasks: Inventory all APIs including shadow and zombie APIs using gateway logs and traffic analysis; target 100 percent known.
Standardise on OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, short-lived JWT (5 to 15 minutes), key rotation via JWKS, and mTLS for service to service.
Implement central authorization with OPA, Cedar or OpenFGA that supports object-level checks, tested for BOLA across 20 critical endpoints.
Enforce OpenAPI schema validation at the gateway, with request size limits, content-type allowlists and strict response filtering.
Add layered rate limits: per client, per user, per endpoint, with distinct stricter limits on login and password reset.
Create shared libraries and templates so a new service is secure by default in under 1 day.
Run a full pen test against the platform, remediate all high findings within 14 days, and retest.
Report coverage: percent APIs behind gateway, percent with authz tests, 401 and 403 anomaly trends, and incident count.

examples.title: Gateway policy
examples.output: Unauthenticated: 401  wrong owner: 403  oversize: 413  over rate: 429 with Retry-After header

notes: BOLA is the most common API flaw and cannot be solved at the gateway alone; test it in each service.
Zombie APIs (old versions) are the usual breach path; sunset them on a schedule.
Make the secure default the lowest effort path.

title: API Fraud Defence for Payments
description: Stop credential stuffing and abuse on payment APIs so customers' accounts stay safe.
overview: Stop credential stuffing and abuse on payment APIs so customers' accounts stay safe.
tasks: Instrument API logs with client fingerprint, IP reputation, ASN, user, endpoint, and outcome, retained for 30 days.
Baseline normal behaviour and identify top 5 abuse patterns from data, such as login failure ratio over 90 percent per IP range.
Implement detections: velocity per account and per device, impossible travel, enumeration sequences of sequential IDs, and low-and-slow distributed attacks.
Add adaptive responses: progressive delays, proof-of-work or CAPTCHA step-up, temporary lockout designed to avoid denial of service on victims, and breached password checks.
Protect business flows: per-account coupon redemption limits, inventory hold limits, and signed one-time tokens.

Simulate an attack with a 50k-credential stuffing test through rotating residential-style proxies in a test environment and measure block rate (target above 95 percent) with under 0.5 percent legitimate user impact.
Create a dashboard and runbook for the on-call to tune rules and handle false positives.
Report loss avoided, account takeover rate before and after, and customer support tickets.

examples.title: Detection query
examples.output:
ip_range        attempts  fail_ratio  users
203.0.113.0/24  4812      0.97        4390
(shape of result; values vary)

notes: Blocking by IP alone fails against residential proxies; combine signals.
Lockouts can be weaponised to deny service; prefer step-up friction.
Measure false positives with real customer outcomes, not guesses.

title: API Security Tests for Payments
description: Test every payments API release for authorisation flaws so customers can't see others' data.
overview: Test every payments API release for authorisation flaws so customers can't see others' data.
tasks: Generate tests from OpenAPI with Schemathesis or RESTler; run 1,000 cases per endpoint and fail the build on any 5xx or schema violation.
Build an authorization matrix test: for each endpoint, roles by resource ownership, asserting expected 200, 403 or 404, covering at least 50 endpoints.
Add DAST (ZAP automation framework) against an ephemeral environment with authenticated scans.
Write custom checks for BOLA, mass assignment, and SSRF using a test harness with two tenants and seeded data.
Add dependency and secret scanning for API gateways and specs, and run GraphQL-specific tests (depth, batching, introspection) if applicable.
Define SLAs: critical findings fixed in 7 days, high in 30, tracked on a dashboard with ageing.
Run a bug bounty or internal red day and compare findings to automated detection to measure the gap.
Track results: escaped vulnerabilities per quarter, mean time to remediate, and pipeline added minutes (target under 10).

examples.title: Authorization matrix test
examples.output:
3 passed in 0.41s
A failing case would show: assert 200 == 404 for bob reading alice_order (BOLA)

notes: Test with two tenants; single-user tests never find BOLA.
Fuzz on ephemeral data and environments, never production.
Return 404 rather than 403 where existence itself is sensitive.

title: Governed Banking Metrics Layer
description: Define banking metrics once so customers and regulators see the same numbers.
overview: Define banking metrics once so customers and regulators see the same numbers.
tasks: Audit current dashboards and find the top 20 metrics, recording how many different definitions exist for each (expect several for revenue).
Run workshops with finance, sales and product to agree one definition per metric, with owner, grain, filters and edge cases, and sign-off recorded.
Implement definitions as code in a semantic layer with version control, code review, and tests.
Add data tests: reconciliation of revenue to the general ledger within 0.1 percent monthly, freshness checks, and uniqueness and not-null tests.
Migrate the 10 most used dashboards to the governed layer and retire duplicates; target 70 percent fewer duplicate reports.
Publish a data catalogue with lineage, definitions and certified badges; measure adoption via monthly active viewers of certified content.
Define a change process: metric change requests, impact analysis via lineage, and announcement with dated effective version.
Measure outcomes: number of metric disputes in leadership meetings (target near zero), query cost, and time to build a new report.

examples.title: Metric definition
examples.code:
metrics:
  - name: net_revenue
    label: Net Revenue
    type: simple
    type_params: {measure: order_total_usd}
    filter: "{{ Dimension('order__status') }} = 'completed' AND refunded = false"
    meta: {owner: finance, grain: order, certified: true}
examples.output:
$ dbt sl query --metrics net_revenue --group-by metric_time__month
metric_time__month  net_revenue
2026-09-01          1,204,331.20
(values vary)

notes: Metrics need an owner who can say no; without one, definitions fork again.
Reconcile to finance systems; that single check earns trust.
Version metrics and communicate changes, because history will shift.

title: Self-Service Banking Analytics
description: Roll out governed analytics to 500 bank staff so decisions serve customers better.
overview: Roll out governed analytics to 500 bank staff so decisions serve customers better.
tasks: Baseline the request backlog (tickets, median turnaround of days) and a user survey on data trust and ability.
Define personas (executive, manager, analyst, power user) and a tiered content model: certified, departmental and personal, with distinct rules.
Provision governed datasets with row-level security and documented columns; target 15 certified datasets covering 80 percent of questions.
Build a training curriculum with 4 modules and hands-on labs; train 200 users and 25 champions.
Set up office hours, a community channel and a review path to promote personal content to certified.
Track adoption: weekly active users, percent of users creating content, report reuse, and abandoned content retired after 90 days of no use.
Run cost governance: capacity or warehouse spend per user and top costly queries, with budgets.
Show impact: backlog reduced by 50 percent, turnaround from days to hours, and 3 documented business decisions or savings attributed to self-service.

examples.title: Adoption scorecard
examples.code:
SELECT date_trunc('week', ts) wk, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) wau, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN action='create' THEN user_id END) creators
FROM bi_audit_log WHERE ts >= current_date - 90 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
examples.output:
wk          wau  creators
2026-08-03  142  21
2026-08-10  168  27
(values vary)

notes: Ungoverned self-service creates metric chaos; govern the data, free the visuals.
Champions in each team beat central trainers.
Count decisions changed, not dashboards built.

title: Faster Financial Dashboards
description: Halve dashboard load time so staff serve customers faster.
overview: Halve dashboard load time so staff serve customers faster.
tasks: Collect baseline telemetry: top 50 dashboards by load time (p50, p95), top queries by credits or bytes scanned, and monthly spend.
Profile the worst 10 dashboards with query plans and visual-level timing (Performance Analyzer, EXPLAIN, query history).
Redesign models: star schema, surrogate integer keys, pre-aggregated tables for common grains, and partitioning or clustering by date.
Implement incremental refresh or incremental models so full reloads drop from hours to minutes.
Add result caching and extract strategy with clear freshness SLAs per dashboard.
Set a performance budget (p95 load under 5 seconds, no query over 30 seconds) and enforce it in a release checklist.
Introduce spend guardrails: resource monitors, auto-suspend after 60 seconds, query timeouts, and chargeback by department.
Report results: median load time reduction (target 60 percent), cost reduction (target 40 to 50 percent), and user satisfaction.

examples.title: Query cost check
examples.output:
query_id  user_name  secs   gb_scanned
01b2...   BI_SVC     212.4  1840.2
(shape; after fix expect scans reduced by orders of magnitude)

notes: Most slow dashboards come from one grain mismatch or an unfiltered fact scan.
Measure before and after on the same days and loads.
Cost savings must be signed off by finance to count.

title: Power BI Governance for a Bank
description: Run a governed reporting tenant so bank figures are reliable for regulators.
overview: Run a governed reporting tenant so bank figures are reliable for regulators.
tasks: Design the workspace model: dev, test, prod per domain, with naming standards, ownership and access via Entra ID groups.
Store semantic models in PBIP or Tabular Editor format in git and deploy via Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions using Fabric REST APIs and deployment pipelines.
Add automated checks with Best Practice Analyzer rules (at least 30) and DAX unit tests; builds fail on violations.
Set up the Fabric capacity metrics app and measure CU usage; identify the top 5 consuming items and optimise them.
Configure tenant settings deliberately: export, sharing, publish to web disabled, and sensitivity labels with Purview.
Create a monitoring model over the activity log and refresh history to alert on failures within 15 minutes.
Implement endorsement (promoted and certified) with an approval workflow and a quarterly recertification.
Document a runbook and show outcomes: refresh success above 99 percent, capacity peak under 70 percent, and zero orphaned workspaces.

examples.title: Deployment step
examples.code:
fab deploy --pipeline "Sales-Domain" --source Dev --target Test --wait
python bpa_check.py ./Sales.SemanticModel --rules rules.json --fail-on error
examples.output:
BPA: 142 objects checked, 0 errors, 3 warnings
Deployment to Test: Succeeded (values vary)

notes: Capacity throttling surprises come from background refresh overlapping with interactive peak; schedule deliberately.
Datasets published to personal workspaces become shadow IT; give a better home.
Git integration for models is only useful with PR review and tests.

title: Billion-Row Transaction Model
description: Serve a billion transaction rows in under 3 seconds so customers' history loads quickly.
overview: Serve a billion transaction rows in under 3 seconds so customers' history loads quickly.
tasks: Choose storage modes per table (Import dimensions, Direct Lake or DirectQuery facts) and document why.
Define aggregation tables at 3 grains (day, product category, region) so 90 percent of visuals hit aggregations.
Optimise the model with VertiPaq Analyzer: reduce cardinality, split datetime, remove high-cardinality columns, and report size before and after.
Rewrite 10 slow DAX measures, using variables, avoiding iterators over large tables, and verifying with DAX Studio server timings.
Capture storage engine versus formula engine time and cache hit status; target formula engine under 30 percent of query time.
Test with 50 concurrent users via a load test (Power BI load test tool or custom XMLA replay), measuring p95 report load under 3 seconds.
Add incremental refresh and hot/cold partitions keeping 13 months hot.
Deliver a performance report with before/after numbers and design guidelines for the team.

examples.title: DAX measure refactor
examples.code:
Sales YoY % =
VAR Cur = [Total Sales]
VAR Prev = CALCULATE([Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR('Date'[Date]))
RETURN DIVIDE(Cur - Prev, Prev)
examples.output:
DAX Studio server timings:
Total 412 ms  SE 311 ms  FE 101 ms  SE queries 3  (values vary; fewer SE queries after refactor)

notes: Check that visuals actually hit aggregations in the Performance Analyzer or profiler; silent misses fall back to the slow path.
Bidirectional relationships and many-to-many cripple large models.
Direct Lake falls back to DirectQuery under some conditions; monitor fallback.

title: Row-Level Security for Banking Reports
description: Enforce who can see which customer data in reports so privacy is protected.
overview: Enforce who can see which customer data in reports so privacy is protected.
tasks: Model entitlements in a security bridge table (user, region, cost centre) sourced from HR with daily refresh and a documented owner.
Implement dynamic RLS using USERPRINCIPALNAME and test with at least 15 roles and persona cases, including managers, contractors and users with no rows.
Use object-level security to hide sensitive columns (salary, national ID) and verify they error for unauthorised viewers.
Automate RLS tests with XMLA impersonation (EffectiveUserName) comparing expected versus actual row counts for every persona in CI.
Apply Purview sensitivity labels with inheritance to exports and block unmanaged device downloads via conditional access.
Configure audit: ingest the activity log to a workspace and alert on bulk exports, sharing outside the tenant and unusual access times.
Handle performance: confirm RLS filters do not exceed 2x baseline query time on the top 10 reports.
Complete an access review with data owners and report findings and remediation.

examples.title: Dynamic RLS filter
examples.code:
-- Role: RegionManager on table Region
[RegionKey] IN
  SELECTCOLUMNS(
    FILTER(Entitlements, Entitlements[UserEmail] = USERPRINCIPALNAME()),
    "k", Entitlements[RegionKey])
examples.output:
Test result (EffectiveUserName = anna@corp.example): rows visible 18,204 of 1,000,000; expected 18,204 PASS
User with no entitlement: 0 rows PASS (values vary)

notes: Remember that workspace Admin, Member and Contributor roles bypass RLS; give viewers only the Viewer role or app access.
Test the user with no entitlement; empty sets fail open in badly written filters.
Many-to-many and bidirectional filters can leak data across RLS; test them specifically.

title: Migrate a Bank Warehouse
description: Move a 200 TB banking warehouse with parity checks so customer reporting never stops.
overview: Move a 200 TB banking warehouse with parity checks so customer reporting never stops.
tasks: Inventory tables, pipelines, consumers and SLAs; classify by usage and retire the 30 percent that is dead before moving anything.
Define migration waves ordered by dependency and business criticality, with an owner and cutover date each.
Build automated parity checks: row counts, column checksums and aggregate comparisons per partition, with tolerance rules for floats and timestamps.
Run old and new in parallel for at least 4 weeks and compare outputs of the top 50 reports daily; require zero unexplained differences before cutover.
Convert SQL with a translation tool plus manual review, and keep a catalogue of dialect differences found (null ordering, date arithmetic, integer division).
Migrate data with bulk export to object storage and CDC for the tail, achieving cutover downtime under 30 minutes per wave.
Plan rollback: keep old system writable-in-sync until two weeks after each wave and drill the rollback once.
Track cost, performance and satisfaction; report cost per query, p95 query time, and decommission savings with date.

examples.title: Parity check
examples.output:
src  n        s            h
old  412,330  9,120,331.55  a1f0...
new  412,330  9,120,331.55  a1f0...
Match: PASS (values vary)

notes: Hidden consumers (spreadsheets, scripts) are the main cutover risk; use query logs to find them.
Float and timezone differences cause most false parity alarms; define tolerances up front.
Budget for dual-running costs.

title: Data Reliability for Payments
description: Catch bad payments data before customers see wrong statements.
overview: Catch bad payments data before customers see wrong statements.
tasks: Define data contracts (schema, semantics, freshness, volume) for the 20 most critical datasets in a versioned spec such as ODCS or protobuf, enforced in CI on producers.
Implement tests at ingestion and transformation layers: schema, null rate, uniqueness, referential integrity, and statistical drift (z-score on volume, distribution tests).
Set SLOs for freshness (for example 99 percent of days table ready by 07:00) and completeness, with an error budget policy.
Add anomaly detection on row counts and key metrics using a seasonal baseline, with alert precision above 80 percent after tuning.
Wire lineage (OpenLineage, dbt) so an alert names downstream dashboards and owners affected.
Run an incident process: severity levels, on-call rota, blameless postmortems for at least 3 data incidents.
Quarantine bad records to a dead-letter table with replay tooling instead of failing silently or dropping.
Report metrics: time to detect (target under 30 minutes), incidents found by consumers versus by monitors (target under 20 percent), and SLO attainment.

examples.title: Data contract and test
examples.output:
check freshness: orders ready 07:42 -> VIOLATION (SLO 07:00)
Impacted: revenue_daily dashboard, finance_close job (shape; values vary)

notes: Contracts only work if producers feel the CI failure; consumer-side tests alone are too late.
Too many alerts is the same as none; track precision per monitor.
Distinguish late data from wrong data in your SLOs.

title: Streaming Payments Operations
description: Run a Kafka and Flink payments platform with exactly-once processing so no payment is duplicated or lost.
overview: Run a Kafka and Flink payments platform with exactly-once processing so no payment is duplicated or lost.
tasks: Design topics with partition counts derived from throughput targets (for example 50 MB/s per topic at 10 MB/s per partition) and keys that avoid hot partitions.
Enforce schemas with a registry (Avro or Protobuf) and compatibility mode BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE; block incompatible changes in CI.
Implement exactly-once end to end: idempotent producers, transactions, Flink checkpoints every 60 seconds, and an idempotent sink; verify by killing tasks 50 times with zero duplicates.
Define SLOs: end-to-end latency p99 under 5 seconds, consumer lag under 60 seconds, and 99.9 percent availability.
Test failure modes: broker loss, network partition, skewed key, and a poison message; show dead-letter handling and recovery times.
Build replay capability from tiered storage or a lake, reprocessing 7 days of data within 4 hours without affecting live traffic.
Set up multi-cluster replication (MirrorMaker 2 or Cluster Linking) with a documented failover procedure and a drill.
Create a capacity and cost model, and tune with measured settings (batch.size, linger.ms, compression zstd).

examples.title: Lag and rebalance check
examples.code: kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server b1:9092 --describe --group fraud-scorer
examples.output:
GROUP        TOPIC   PARTITION CURRENT-OFFSET LOG-END-OFFSET LAG
fraud-scorer events  0         1204331920     1204332510     590
fraud-scorer events  1         1198122044     1198122101     57
(values vary; healthy lag stays flat)

notes: Rebalance storms are caused by slow processing exceeding max.poll.interval; use cooperative rebalancing.
Exactly-once ends at your sink; external side effects need idempotency keys.
Changing partition count breaks key ordering; plan it early.

title: Cheaper LLM Support Serving
description: Cut cost per million tokens for a support bot by half so banks can afford AI help for customers.
overview: Cut cost per million tokens for a support bot by half so banks can afford AI help for customers.
tasks: Define SLOs: time to first token p95 under 500 ms, inter-token latency p95 under 40 ms, and goodput measured as requests meeting both.
Build a load generator replaying real prompt and output length distributions with Poisson arrivals and sweep from 1 to 200 concurrent requests.
Profile GPU utilisation, memory bandwidth, KV cache occupancy and batch size using nsys or DCGM, and find the bottleneck (compute versus memory bound).
Tune: continuous batching limits, chunked prefill, prefix caching, max_num_seqs, and KV cache dtype (FP8) and report each change independently.
Compare FP16, FP8 and INT4 (AWQ or GPTQ) on throughput and quality using an eval set with regression tolerance under 1 point.
Evaluate tensor parallel versus replicas for the model size and justify with tokens per second per dollar.
Add autoscaling on queue depth and KV cache usage with a 3 minute scale-up target including model load time.
Report cost per million tokens before and after (target 50 percent lower) and the throughput versus latency curve.

examples.title: vLLM benchmark
examples.code:
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-num-seqs 256
python benchmark_serving.py --dataset sharegpt --request-rate 20 --num-prompts 2000
examples.output:
Throughput: 4,812 output tok/s
TTFT p95: 412 ms   TPOT p95: 31 ms
(values vary by GPU, model and dataset)

notes: Benchmark with realistic length distributions; fixed lengths flatter every engine.
Throughput at saturation is a trap; report numbers at the load where the SLO still holds.
Quality regression from quantization appears on long context and rare tasks; test them.

title: Multi-Tenant Inference for Banks
description: Serve several banks' models with isolation so each bank's customer data stays separate.
overview: Serve several banks' models with isolation so each bank's customer data stays separate.
tasks: Define tiers (interactive, batch) with SLOs and per-tenant quotas in tokens per minute, enforced at a gateway with 429 and Retry-After.
Implement priority scheduling so interactive p95 TTFT stays under SLO while batch jobs use idle capacity and are preemptible.
Handle GPU failures: health checks using DCGM and XID errors, automatic cordon, and replacement within 5 minutes.
Reduce cold start from 6 minutes to under 90 seconds using model weights on local NVMe, image pre-pull and lazy loading.
Add fallback routing: a smaller model or secondary provider when error rate exceeds 2 percent or latency SLO burns, with quality guardrails.
Instrument per-request tracing with token counts, queue time, prefill and decode time, and cost attribution by tenant.
Run chaos tests: kill 25 percent of pods under load, induce an OOM with long contexts, and measure error budget burn.
Write runbooks and a postmortem template, and report availability (target 99.9 percent) and cost per tenant monthly.

examples.title: SLO burn alert
examples.output: Firing: TTFT p95 0.83s for 10m, queue depth 412, KV cache 97% -> action: shed batch tier, scale pool (values vary)

notes: Long-context requests cause head-of-line blocking and OOM; cap and route them separately.
Admission control by tokens, not requests.
Model load time makes autoscaling slower than most people plan for; keep warm capacity.

title: Faster Fraud Model Decoding
description: Cut the latency of a fraud model's decoding so suspicious payments are blocked in time.
overview: Cut the latency of a fraud model's decoding so suspicious payments are blocked in time.
tasks: Profile a decode step with Nsight Systems and Nsight Compute; list the top 10 kernels by time and their achieved memory bandwidth versus peak.
Classify each as compute or memory bound using a roofline analysis for your GPU.
Select a candidate with launch or memory overhead (for example separate norm, residual and quantization kernels).
Implement the fused kernel in Triton or CUDA and verify numerics against PyTorch reference with max abs error under 1e-3 in FP16 across 1,000 random shapes.
Benchmark with warmup and CUDA events across batch sizes 1 to 64 and report speedup per shape and end-to-end tokens per second change.
Apply CUDA graphs to cut launch overhead and measure CPU-side gap reduction.
Integrate behind a flag into the serving engine and run the quality eval to confirm no output regression.
Write up findings, including the shapes where your kernel loses.

examples.title: Kernel benchmark
examples.code:
import triton
ms = triton.testing.do_bench(lambda: fused_rmsnorm_quant(x, w), warmup=25, rep=200)
ref = triton.testing.do_bench(lambda: unfused(x, w), warmup=25, rep=200)
print(f"fused {ms:.3f} ms  ref {ref:.3f} ms  speedup {ref/ms:.2f}x")
examples.output:
fused 0.021 ms  ref 0.058 ms  speedup 2.76x
(values vary by GPU and shape)

notes: Decode is memory bound at small batch; fewer bytes moved beats more FLOPs.
Always benchmark with realistic shapes; wins at batch 64 can lose at batch 1.
Keep the unfused path as fallback and test numerics against it in CI.

title: DeFi Protocol Audit
description: Find and fix exploitable flaws in a live DeFi-style protocol so users don't lose their money.
overview: Find and fix exploitable flaws in a live DeFi-style protocol so users don't lose their money.
tasks: Map the attack surface: list every external and public function, privileged role, upgrade path and external call in a table with trust assumptions.
Run Slither and Mythril, triage every finding as true or false positive with a one line justification, and keep the triage in the report.
Write at least 8 Foundry invariant properties (for example total shares times price never exceeds total assets, sum of balances equals total supply) and run them with 256 runs by 500 depth minimum.
Fuzz with Echidna or Foundry for 1 hour minimum and report coverage of the core contracts above 90 percent of lines.

Demonstrate at least 3 distinct exploit classes with a working proof-of-concept test each, such as read-only reentrancy, first-depositor share inflation and flash-loan oracle manipulation on a mainnet fork.
Patch each issue with the smallest safe change (checks-effects-interactions, virtual shares offset, TWAP oracle, nonReentrant) and show the exploit test now fails.
Review the upgrade proxy: storage layout compatibility check with a layout diff tool, initializer protection and timelocked admin.
Classify findings as Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational using impact times likelihood, and give each a stable ID.
Measure gas before and after fixes on 5 hot paths; no fix may raise deposit or withdraw gas by more than 5 percent without justification.
Present the report to a mock team and run a fix-review round that verifies each patch commit.

examples.title: Share inflation PoC as a Foundry test
examples.output: Before the fix: [PASS] test_firstDepositorInflation (exploit works). After adding a virtual offset of 1e3 shares: the assertEq fails because shares is greater than 0, and the test is inverted into a regression test.

notes: A clean static analyser run means almost nothing; most High findings come from reading business logic against a written specification.
Always test on a mainnet fork with real token behaviours (fee on transfer, rebasing, USDT missing return values).
A fix is not accepted until the original exploit test is kept in the suite as a regression.

title: Reliable Node Fleet for a Payment Network
description: Run a fault-tolerant node fleet with an indexer that survives reorgs so payments are tracked correctly.
overview: Run a fault-tolerant node fleet with an indexer that survives reorgs so payments are tracked correctly.
tasks: Deploy at least 2 execution clients (for example Geth and Nethermind) with 2 consensus clients on a testnet such as Hoodi or Sepolia, avoiding a single client share above 66 percent.
Put an RPC proxy in front with health checks on block height lag and peer count, ejecting any node more than 3 blocks behind.
Define SLOs: 99.9 percent RPC availability, p99 eth_call latency under 300 ms, indexer lag under 30 seconds, measured in Prometheus and Grafana.
Build an indexer that stores logs in Postgres with block hash and parent hash, and rolls back to the common ancestor on reorg.
Make ingestion idempotent: replaying any block range 3 times must produce byte identical tables, verified by a checksum query.
Inject a 7 block reorg on a local devnet (Anvil snapshot and revert or a Kurtosis network) and show downstream balances correct within 60 seconds.
Run chaos drills: kill a client, corrupt a database volume, partition the network; record time to detect and time to recover for each.
Add alerting with burn rate rules (fast 14.4x over 1 hour, slow 6x over 6 hours) and a runbook for each alert.
Produce a cost model per million requests comparing self hosted against a provider, with a break even point.
Write a postmortem for one induced failure in blameless format with 3 action items.

examples.title: Reorg safe insert and rollback
examples.output: One row with a 32 character md5 checksum. The value must be identical after replaying the same range; it differs per chain data.

notes: Treat finality as a state machine (latest, safe, finalized) and expose it to consumers instead of hiding reorgs.
Client diversity is a reliability control: a single client bug can halt every node you run.
Snapshot sync time often dominates recovery; measure it before promising an RTO.

title: Cross-Chain Payments Threat Model
description: Design a cross-chain payment bridge with a threat model so users' transfers are protected.
overview: Design a cross-chain payment bridge with a threat model so users' transfers are protected.
tasks: Write a design document comparing light client, optimistic and multisig validation, and choose one with explicit trust assumptions and failure modes.
Build a threat model with STRIDE per component and at least 15 numbered threats, each with a mitigation or accepted risk owner.
Implement source and destination contracts with message nonces, replay protection by message hash and domain separated chain IDs.
Use a 5 of 8 validator threshold with signatures verified on chain, and demonstrate that 4 signatures are rejected.
Add per-asset rate limits (for example 2 percent of TVL per hour) and a guardian pause that cannot move funds.
Add a timelock of 24 hours on validator set changes and show the upgrade flow in tests.
Write a relayer that is stateless and restartable; killing it mid-batch must not duplicate or drop messages across 1,000 test transfers.
Run a tabletop for a compromised key: document detection signal, who pauses, communication template and recovery steps, with timing under 15 minutes to pause.
Set up monitoring that compares locked amount on source to minted supply on destination every block and alerts on any mismatch.
Get a peer review from two engineers and record every objection and resolution.

examples.title: Invariant monitor
examples.output: In normal operation no output and a gauge bridge_backing_ratio at 1.0 or above. During a simulated mint-without-lock the page fires and the pause transaction hash is logged.

notes: Limit the blast radius first: rate limits turn a total loss into a bounded one.
Key custody, not Solidity, is where most bridges actually failed.
Publish the trust assumptions in plain language so users can decide for themselves.

title: Frame Budget for a Savings Game
description: Keep a savings-education game at a stable frame rate on school laptops so students can learn on any device.
overview: Keep a savings-education game at a stable frame rate on school laptops so students can learn on any device.
tasks: Set budgets: 16.6 ms frame, 6 ms game thread, 8 ms render, 150 MB texture memory, zero GC allocations per frame in steady state.
Capture baselines with Unity Profiler and Frame Debugger or Unreal Insights and RenderDoc on the lowest supported device; record p50, p95 and p99 frame times over a 5 minute scripted run.
Classify the frame as CPU bound or GPU bound with evidence from the captures, not intuition.
Fix at least 5 distinct hotspots, for example draw call batching or GPU instancing, overdraw, shader variant stripping, physics query culling and allocation removal using pooling.
Convert the main gameplay update to data oriented structures (ECS, Burst or jobs) for one system with more than 10,000 entities and measure the speedup.
Reduce load time by 40 percent through async loading and asset bundle or addressable restructuring.
Cut memory so peak stays under 1.5 GB on a 2 GB device, checked with a memory snapshot diff.
Build an automated benchmark that runs in CI on a device or emulator and fails a build if p95 frame time rises by more than 5 percent.
Document each change with before and after numbers in a table and rejected ideas with reasons.
Present results to the team in a 15 minute review including a performance guideline for artists.

examples.title: CI frame time gate
examples.code:
./run_benchmark.sh --scene Stress_01 --duration 300 --out perf.json
jq '{p50:.frame_ms.p50, p95:.frame_ms.p95, p99:.frame_ms.p99}' perf.json
python check_budget.py perf.json baseline.json --max-regress 0.05
examples.output:
{"p50":13.9,"p95":16.2,"p99":21.4}
OK: p95 16.2 ms within 5 percent of baseline 15.9 ms (values vary by device)

notes: Profile on the worst target device in a release build; editor numbers lie.
Optimise the p99 spikes, because players feel hitches more than averages.
Every optimisation needs a measured win or it is reverted.

title: Fair Netcode for a Market Game
description: Build a server-authoritative multiplayer layer so a classroom market game can't be cheated.
overview: Build a server-authoritative multiplayer layer so a classroom market game can't be cheated.
tasks: Choose a transport (UDP with a reliability layer such as ENet, Netcode for GameObjects, Mirror or a custom one) and justify the tick rate; use 60 Hz simulation and 20 to 30 Hz snapshots.
Implement client prediction and server reconciliation with input sequence numbers; mispredictions must correct without visible snapping at 100 ms RTT.
Add entity interpolation with a 100 ms buffer and lag compensated hit detection that rewinds server state up to 200 ms.
Budget bandwidth to under 30 KB/s down per client using delta compression, quantisation and interest management.
Test with a network emulator (tc netem or Clumsy) at 0, 50, 150 ms latency, 5 percent loss and 30 ms jitter; record rubber banding events per minute.
Treat the client as hostile: validate movement speed, fire rate and line of sight server side, and write 5 exploit scenarios with tests.
Run a soak test with 200 simulated bots across 12 server instances for 2 hours and report CPU per match and memory growth.
Add deterministic replay from input logs so any reported desync can be reproduced from a file.
Instrument per-match telemetry: RTT, packet loss, tick overrun count, and alert when tick time exceeds 90 percent of budget.
Write a netcode guide for gameplay programmers describing what must be server side.

examples.title: netem profile and result
examples.code:
sudo tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 75ms 15ms loss 5%
./bot_swarm --clients 16 --duration 600
./report --metric rubberband_per_min --metric tick_overrun
examples.output:
rubberband_per_min: 0.8
tick_overrun: 0 (acceptance: below 1.0 and 0; exact values vary)

notes: Determinism is never free in floating point across platforms; plan for state resync.
Never trust the client for anything but input.
Test with real bad networks early, mobile loss is bursty not uniform.

title: Release Pipeline for a Money-Education Game
description: Ship a money-education game weekly with telemetry so teachers get fixes quickly.
overview: Ship a money-education game weekly with telemetry so teachers get fixes quickly.
tasks: Create a CI pipeline (Jenkins, GitHub Actions or TeamCity) building Windows, Android and one console or iOS target from one commit, with a full build under 30 minutes using caching.
Use Git LFS or Perforce for binaries and add a cache for imported assets so a clean machine imports in under 10 minutes.
Add automated smoke tests that boot the game, load 3 levels and run 5 minutes with no crash or error logs.
Implement content patching (addressables or pak files) with delta updates; a 2 GB game must deliver a content change under 50 MB.
Add crash reporting with symbolication (Sentry or Backtrace) and a dashboard of crash free sessions with a target of 99.5 percent.
Implement feature flags and remote config to change balance values without a client patch, with staged rollout at 1, 10 and 100 percent.
Define a release train: branch cut Tuesday, certification Thursday, rollout Monday, with a go/no-go checklist.
Practise a rollback: revert a bad content bundle to the previous version within 15 minutes of the alarm.
Track DORA style metrics for the pipeline: lead time, build success rate, flaky test rate.
Document the pipeline for new engineers and onboard one person who ships a build alone.

examples.title: Staged rollout config
examples.output: The rollout advances automatically; if crash free sessions fall below 99.5 percent the controller halts at the current stage and pages the on-call (event name: rollout_halted).

notes: Cache correctness beats cache speed; a poisoned asset cache costs days.
Console certification dates are hard constraints; plan the train around them.
Always keep the previous content bundle available for instant rollback.

title: Test Strategy for Payments
description: Drive flaky tests below 0.5 percent so payment releases are trusted.
overview: Drive flaky tests below 0.5 percent so payment releases are trusted.
tasks: Audit the suite: count tests by layer, runtime, owner and failure history for the last 30 days and present a table.
Define a risk based strategy mapping top 10 business flows to the lowest effective test layer, with a target of 70 percent unit, 20 percent integration, 10 percent end-to-end.
Measure flakiness as reruns that change outcome divided by runs; baseline it and set a target below 0.5 percent.
Build automatic quarantine: a test failing and passing on the same commit moves to a quarantine suite and opens a ticket with an owner and a 14 day SLA.
Fix at least 20 flaky tests and classify root causes (timing, shared state, order dependence, environment, data), reporting percentages.
Parallelise and shard to cut the pipeline from 90 to under 15 minutes for pull requests, using test impact analysis to run only affected tests.
Introduce contract tests (Pact) between two services to replace at least 10 brittle end-to-end tests.
Adopt mutation testing (Stryker, PIT or mutmut) on one critical module and raise mutation score from baseline to at least 75 percent.
Publish a quality dashboard: escaped defects per release, change failure rate, mean time to detect, flake rate.
Run a retrospective on three escaped production bugs and add the missing test to each.

examples.title: Flake detection query
examples.code:
SELECT test_id, COUNT(*) AS runs,
       SUM(CASE WHEN outcome_changed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS flips
FROM test_runs
WHERE run_date >= CURRENT_DATE - 30
GROUP BY test_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN outcome_changed THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY flips DESC LIMIT 20;
examples.output: A ranked table of test_id, runs, flips. Example row: checkout_e2e_applies_coupon, 412, 17. Values vary.

notes: Deleting a test with no owner and no failing signal is a valid fix.
Fix causes in shared fixtures first, they produce most flakes.
Never fix flakiness with blind retries; retries hide real race conditions.

title: Resilience Testing for Payments
description: Prove capacity and graceful degradation so payments stay up during surges.
overview: Prove capacity and graceful degradation so payments stay up during surges.
tasks: Derive a workload model from 7 days of production logs: request mix, think time, payload sizes and peak to average ratio.
Write load scenarios in k6 or Gatling covering baseline, 2x peak stress, 4 hour soak and a spike from 100 to 3,000 RPS in 30 seconds.
Define pass criteria: p95 under 400 ms, p99 under 1 s, error rate below 0.1 percent at expected peak.
Find the knee of the curve: increase load in 10 percent steps and plot throughput against latency to name the saturating resource.
Use profiling and distributed traces to identify the top 3 bottlenecks and verify fixes with a rerun showing the improvement.
Verify autoscaling reacts within 2 minutes and that scale-in does not drop in-flight requests.

Run chaos experiments (Chaos Mesh, Litmus or Gremlin): kill 1 of 3 pods, add 300 ms database latency, drop a dependency; confirm timeouts, retries and circuit breakers keep the error rate under 1 percent.
Capture a capacity report stating maximum sustainable RPS, headroom percentage and cost per 1,000 requests.
Automate a reduced performance test in CI that fails on 10 percent regression of p95.
Hold a game day with on-call engineers and record detection and recovery times.

examples.title: k6 thresholds
examples.output: k6 prints each threshold with a tick or cross, for example: http_req_duration p(95)<400 passed with p(95)=312ms. Exact values vary by environment.

notes: Use arrival-rate executors, closed-model users hide overload by slowing down.
Test data volume matters; an empty database lies about query cost.
Staging must match production topology or the capacity numbers are fiction.

title: Quality Culture for a Bank
description: Cut escaped defects by 40 percent so customers hit fewer bugs.
overview: Cut escaped defects by 40 percent so customers hit fewer bugs.
tasks: Baseline the last 6 months: escaped defects per release, severity mix, mean time to detect, mean time to restore and cost of each production incident.
Introduce a testability checklist reviewed in design documents (observability hooks, seams for mocking, deterministic time, data setup APIs).
Define a risk matrix scoring change by blast radius and complexity, and map scores to required gates (e.g. high risk requires exploratory session plus canary).
Implement automated gates in CI: unit coverage on changed lines above 80 percent, no new critical static findings, contract tests green, performance budget met.
Run weekly exploratory testing charters with session notes; log at least 30 sessions and track bugs found per hour.
Train 20 developers in a 4 session workshop on writing good tests, test doubles and property based testing; measure with a before and after quiz.
Add production quality signals: feature flag canaries at 5 percent, synthetic monitoring of 10 key journeys every minute.
Set up a bug triage process with severity definitions and a 24 hour SLA for critical.
Report quarterly to leadership with escaped defects down at least 40 percent, and a list of trade-offs accepted.
Write a one page quality charter and get it signed by engineering and product leads.

examples.title: Release gate definition
examples.code:
gates:
  low_risk:    [unit_pass, lint, changed_line_coverage_80]
  medium_risk: [unit_pass, contract_pass, changed_line_coverage_80, canary_5pct_30min]
  high_risk:   [unit_pass, contract_pass, perf_budget, exploratory_signoff, canary_5pct_2h, rollback_tested]
examples.output: CI prints: risk=high, gates 6 of 6 passed, release approved. A missing gate returns exit code 1 and names the failing gate.

notes: Gates people can bypass silently teach them to bypass; log every override.
Quality is a team metric, not a QA metric.
Show cost of incidents in money, leadership acts on that.

title: Research-Led Banking Roadmap
description: Change a banking product roadmap through research so customers' tasks get easier.
overview: Change a banking product roadmap through research so customers' tasks get easier.
tasks: Frame 3 research questions linked to a business goal (for example reduce onboarding drop-off from 48 percent to 35 percent).
Conduct 15 to 20 generative interviews with a screener across 3 segments and synthesise with affinity mapping into 6 to 8 insights each backed by at least 3 participants.
Field a survey of 400 or more respondents with a validated scale (SUS, UMUX-Lite or NPS) and report confidence intervals.
Analyse funnel and event data to triangulate where qualitative findings show up quantitatively.
Run a moderated usability benchmark with 8 participants per round measuring task success, time on task and SEQ, repeated before and after redesign.
Create journey maps and a jobs-to-be-done statement set, and run a prioritisation workshop with product and engineering producing a ranked opportunity list.
Set up a research repository (Dovetail, Notion or Airtable) with tagged, searchable findings and a consent log compliant with GDPR.
Establish a rolling programme: a weekly participant pipeline and an office hours slot so designers and PMs can self serve.
Ship one change from the research and A/B test it with a pre-registered hypothesis and sample size calculation.
Present a decision memo showing what the roadmap changed and the measured effect.

examples.title: Benchmark result table
examples.code:
Task: Connect bank account
Round 1 (n=8): success 5/8 (62.5%), median time 148 s, SEQ 4.1
Round 2 (n=8): success 7/8 (87.5%), median time 91 s, SEQ 5.8
Change: removed manual routing number step, added instant verification
examples.output: A table with success rate, median time and SEQ per round, plus a note that with n=8 the confidence interval is wide and the decision relied on converging qualitative evidence. Numbers are illustrative.

notes: Small-sample usability tests find problems, they do not estimate rates; say so.
A finding without a named owner and a decision date is an anecdote.
Recruit users who are not your friends or your champions.

title: WCAG 2.2 Audit for Banking
description: Drive a banking product to WCAG 2.2 AA so disabled customers can manage money.
overview: Drive a banking product to WCAG 2.2 AA so disabled customers can manage money.
tasks: Scope the audit: sample 25 representative screens and flows covering all templates and the top 10 user journeys.
Run automated scans (axe, Lighthouse) and record that automated tools find only around 30 to 40 percent of issues, then do a manual audit against every WCAG 2.2 AA criterion.
Test keyboard-only, with NVDA plus Firefox, VoiceOver on iOS and macOS, and TalkBack, at 200 percent zoom and 320 px reflow.
Verify contrast ratios (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI) and the new 2.2 criteria: target size minimum 24 px, focus not obscured, dragging alternatives, accessible authentication.
Recruit at least 5 users of assistive technology for moderated sessions and compensate them fairly.
Log issues in a tracker with WCAG criterion, severity, affected users, repro and fix guidance; target zero critical blockers before deadline.
Prioritise by severity times traffic and drive fixes with engineering over 3 sprints, reporting burn-down weekly.
Add prevention: accessible component specs with ARIA patterns, annotation kit for designs, axe tests in CI, and a PR checklist.
Publish an Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT) and an accessibility statement.
Train designers and developers in a 2 hour workshop and measure issue rate per release falling by 50 percent.

examples.title: Issue record
examples.code:
id: A11Y-142
wcag: 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value
severity: critical
where: Checkout > Payment method radio group
found: VoiceOver announces "radio button" with no label
fix: associate label via aria-labelledby; group with role=radiogroup and aria-label
verify: VoiceOver reads "Credit card, radio button, 1 of 3"
examples.output: After the fix, re-test passes and the ticket closes with the screen reader transcript attached. Spoken text varies slightly by screen reader.

notes: Overlays and widgets do not make a site compliant.
Fix components once in the design system rather than screen by screen.
Compliance is a snapshot; only process keeps it.

title: Conversion Experiments for Checkout
description: Run rigorous experiments that lift checkout conversion so shoppers finish paying.
overview: Run rigorous experiments that lift checkout conversion so shoppers finish paying.
tasks: Define the north star funnel metric and 3 guardrail metrics (for example refund rate, support contacts, page load).
Write at least 8 hypotheses in the format: because of evidence, we believe change will cause effect for segment, measured by metric.
Compute sample size per test with power 80 percent, alpha 5 percent and minimum detectable effect; a 3 percent baseline needing a 10 percent relative lift requires roughly 50,000 users per arm.
Run an A/A test to validate the platform and check sample ratio mismatch on every experiment with a chi-square test.
Pre-register stopping rules; forbid peeking or use sequential testing with corrections.
Run at least 6 experiments and report effect size with confidence intervals, not just p-values.
Segment results for new versus returning and mobile versus desktop, labelling them exploratory.
Use holdouts to measure cumulative impact: keep 5 percent of users on the original experience for the quarter.
Build a learning library with every test, result, screenshots and next step, including failures.
Report revenue impact with a conservative estimate and have finance review the method.

examples.title: Sample ratio mismatch check
examples.code:
from scipy.stats import chisquare
obs = [50234, 49310]           # control, variant visitors
exp = [sum(obs)/2]*2
stat, p = chisquare(obs, exp)
print(round(p, 6))
examples.output: A p-value near 0.0005 here, which is below 0.001 and means the assignment is broken, so results must be discarded. A healthy test gives a p-value above 0.01.

notes: Novelty effects fade; run at least 2 full business cycles.
A win in the primary metric with a guardrail loss is a loss.
Do not test what you can decide by research or by standards.

title: Discovery for a New Savings Product
description: Take a new savings product idea from a real saver's problem to a validated prototype.
overview: Take a new savings product idea from a real saver's problem to a validated prototype.
tasks: Write a problem brief with target user, job to be done, current alternatives and a success metric.
List assumptions on a desirability, viability, feasibility map and rank by risk times uncertainty; test the top 5.
Run 12 or more discovery interviews using past-behaviour questions (Mom Test) and quote evidence of existing pain.
Run a smoke test landing page with paid traffic of around 1,000 visits targeting at least 5 percent sign-up intent.
Build a concierge or Wizard of Oz MVP serving 10 real users manually to learn the real workflow.
Prototype at three fidelities (paper, clickable Figma, coded prototype) and test each with 5 users, recording changes made.
Test pricing with a Van Westendorp survey of 100 or more respondents or a pre-order experiment.
Define the core loop and 3 leading metrics, and plan the first 90 days of instrumentation.
Run a design sprint or equivalent workshop with engineering and business to align on scope.
Deliver a go, pivot or stop recommendation memo with evidence, risks and a 6 month plan.

examples.title: Assumption test card
examples.code:
Assumption: Freelancers will connect their bank account to auto-track invoices
Test: Concierge MVP, 10 freelancers, 2 weeks
Success: 7 of 10 connect and 5 of 10 return in week 2
Result: 8 connected, 3 returned. Learning: value came from reminders, not tracking
examples.output: A completed card with a pass or fail verdict against the stated criterion and a learning that changes the next test. Numbers are illustrative.

notes: Set kill criteria before testing, otherwise every result looks like encouragement.
Stated interest is cheap; ask for time, money or access.
Fidelity should match the question, not the designer's pride.

title: Cross-Platform Banking Redesign
description: Redesign a banking app across web and mobile so customers finish tasks without confusion.
overview: Redesign a banking app across web and mobile so customers finish tasks without confusion.
tasks: Audit the existing product with an inventory of screens, patterns, and top 20 usability problems, with analytics on usage of each area.
Define a vision and 4 design principles with rejected alternatives, and align with product, engineering and leadership.
Create a phased plan splitting the redesign into at least 4 releases ordered by value and risk, each independently shippable.
Establish success and guardrail metrics (task completion, retention day 30, support tickets) with a stated tolerance, for example no more than 2 percent drop.
Design platform-native patterns for iOS (HIG) and Android (Material 3) while sharing a consistent core model and tokens.
Roll out behind flags at 1, 10, 50 and 100 percent with a dedicated feedback channel and in-product survey.
Run an opt-in beta with 500 users and 10 diary or interview participants for qualitative signals.
Prepare migration support: release notes, in-product tour for changed workflows, and help centre updates before launch.
Run a design QA process comparing implementation against specs with a severity-rated bug list; target under 5 open P1 visual or interaction defects at release.
Report results after 90 days and document lessons.

examples.title: Rollout decision table
examples.code:
Stage   Traffic  D7 retention   Task success   Tickets/1k   Decision
1       1%       41.2 vs 41.0    92 vs 91       3.1 vs 3.0   continue
2       10%      40.1 vs 41.1    90 vs 91       4.9 vs 3.0   hold, fix nav label confusion
3       10%      41.0 vs 41.1    92 vs 91       3.2 vs 3.0   continue
examples.output: A per-stage table comparing new and old experience with a decision. Values illustrative; the structure matters.

notes: Power users forgive change if you give a path to old workflows.
Never ship the visual refresh and the navigation change together.
Keep the old experience reachable until the new one beats it on metrics.

title: Design Strategy for a Fintech Team
description: Set design strategy so a fintech's screens serve customers' everyday money needs.
overview: Set design strategy so a fintech's screens serve customers' everyday money needs.
tasks: Write a one page design strategy connecting company goals to 3 design bets with measurable outcomes.
Run a team health survey and a stakeholder survey to baseline satisfaction on a 5 point scale.
Create a career ladder with 5 levels and written expectations for craft, influence, impact and leadership.
Design the hiring process: role scorecards, a structured portfolio review rubric, a take-home or live exercise, and calibrate across 3 interviewers.
Set up critique rituals: weekly team critique with a defined format, and a monthly cross-team review with written feedback guidance.
Define design review gates (problem brief, concept, pre-build, post-launch) with owners and a 2 day turnaround.
Introduce design KPIs: time from brief to ship, percent of launches with research, design debt backlog size, usability score trend.
Run quarterly planning with product and engineering, with design capacity allocation visible at 70 percent roadmap and 30 percent foundations.
Mentor 3 designers with written growth plans and show at least one promotion or level-aligned achievement.
Retro after two quarters: compare baseline and new survey results and publish what you will stop doing.

examples.title: Ladder row excerpt
examples.code:
Level 4 Senior - Influence
Expected: Leads cross-team initiatives; changes a roadmap decision with evidence at least twice per year
Evidence: decision memos, stakeholder feedback, adoption of patterns by other teams
Not yet: needs direction to align stakeholders on conflicting goals
examples.output: A ladder document where each row has expectation, evidence examples and a not-yet clause, used consistently in promotion packets.

notes: Process added without removing something becomes bureaucracy.
Calibrate hiring bars on real candidate examples, not abstract rubrics.
Protect time for foundations or design debt wins every planning argument.

title: Multi-Brand Tokens for Banks
description: Build one design token pipeline for three bank brands so customers see clear, consistent screens.
overview: Build one design token pipeline for three bank brands so customers see clear, consistent screens.
tasks: Define three token tiers: primitives (color.blue.500), semantic (color.action.primary) and component (button.background.default), with naming rules documented.
Store tokens in the W3C Design Tokens format JSON and transform with Style Dictionary into CSS custom properties, Swift and Android XML or Compose.
Support 3 brands and light and dark modes through theme layers; adding a fourth brand must take under 1 day and touch only token files.
Enforce contrast: a script verifies 4.5:1 for text pairs and 3:1 for UI across all themes and fails the build otherwise.
Sync with Figma variables via the plugin or API and detect drift between Figma and code in CI.
Add token linting: forbid hard-coded hex and spacing values in component code with a stylelint rule and report violations.
Version tokens semantically and provide a codemod for renames; one breaking rename must migrate 200 usages automatically.
Measure adoption: percent of product code using tokens, aiming above 90 percent in 2 pilot products.
Publish documentation with a searchable token browser showing values per theme.
Benchmark CSS payload and runtime theme switch time, target under 16 ms without reload.

examples.title: Semantic token with theme override
examples.output: Style Dictionary emits :root { --color-action-primary: #1d4ed8; } plus [data-theme=dark] { --color-action-primary: #93c5fd; } and a brand-b block. Hex values depend on your palette.

notes: Name tokens by purpose, not appearance, or renaming blue to green becomes a lie.
Limit component tokens to what really varies.
Automate drift detection; manual syncing always decays.

title: Design System Adoption for Banks
description: Get 20 banking teams using shared components so customers get the same quality everywhere.
overview: Get 20 banking teams using shared components so customers get the same quality everywhere.
tasks: Measure adoption baseline using code scans (react-scanner or similar) and Figma library analytics: component coverage per product and detached instance counts.
Define governance: a federated contribution model with intake form, review SLA of 5 business days and decision criteria (used by 3 or more teams).
Adopt semantic versioning and a release cadence; document deprecation policy with 2 minor release warnings and a codemod before removal.
Set up a support channel and office hours with first response under 1 business day and track ticket categories.
Write migration guides and codemods; migrate one large product of more than 100 screens and record effort in person-days.
Create an adoption dashboard: coverage percent, version spread, detached instances, and time to first component usage for new teams.
Gather satisfaction with a quarterly survey, target above 8 of 10, plus NPS-style question for developers.
Calculate return on investment: hours saved per team times teams minus system cost, and present to leadership.
Run a contribution day producing at least 5 accepted community components.
Retire 10 duplicate legacy components, publishing replacement mapping.

examples.title: Coverage scan output
examples.code:
npx react-scanner -c scanner.config.js
node report-adoption.js scan.json
examples.output:
team          ds_usage   custom   coverage
checkout      412        38       91.6%
onboarding    188        97       66.0%
TOTAL         3,904      702      84.8%   (illustrative)

notes: A mandate without a migration path creates shadow systems.
Track detached instances in Figma, they reveal missing components.
Say no clearly and publish why; it builds trust.

title: Banking Component Quality
description: Engineer components with accessibility checks so every customer screen works for disabled users.
overview: Engineer components with accessibility checks so every customer screen works for disabled users.
tasks: Build every component with Storybook stories covering all states (default, hover, focus, disabled, error, loading) and long-content cases.
Add visual regression with Chromatic or Playwright snapshots across 3 browsers and 3 viewports, with a diff threshold of 0.1 percent and required approval.
Automate accessibility with axe in Storybook tests and Testing Library interaction tests; keyboard flows tested for dialog, menu, combobox and tabs.
Enforce bundle budgets: each component under 5 KB gzipped, whole library tree-shakeable, with size-limit failing CI on 3 percent growth.
Support SSR and React Server Components without hydration warnings, tested in a Next.js sample app.
Provide TypeScript types with strict generics and test them with tsd or expect-type.
Run a consumer integration test matrix against 3 real product apps on every release candidate.
Publish releases with changesets, provenance and an automated changelog; provide canary releases for early adopters.
Track defects escaping to products: target fewer than 2 regressions per quarter, with a root cause review for each.
Measure runtime performance with React Profiler and report render counts for the 10 heaviest components.

examples.title: Bundle budget config
examples.output: size-limit prints each entry with its size and a red failure line if over limit, for example: Button 1.8 KB passed; DataGrid 19.4 KB exceeds 18 KB. Sizes vary with build.

notes: Visual diffs need a deterministic rendering environment; pin the browser and fonts.
Test the keyboard, not just the ARIA attributes.
Breaking changes that pass type checks still break layouts; snapshots catch these.

title: Docs Pipeline for a Payments API
description: Test every example in payments docs so developers copy working code and launch faster.
overview: Test every example in payments docs so developers copy working code and launch faster.
tasks: Choose and justify a static site generator (Docusaurus, MkDocs, Hugo or Sphinx) with versioned docs and search; build under 3 minutes for 1,000 pages.
Encode the style guide in Vale with a custom ruleset (terminology, passive voice limits, banned words) and run in pull requests with a zero-error gate.
Execute code samples in CI: extract blocks and run them in containers; a broken sample fails the build.
Check links internal and external with lychee on every PR and weekly for external rot, creating issues automatically.
Generate API reference from OpenAPI or source comments and verify it matches the live API using a contract diff.
Add content ownership metadata (owner, last reviewed, review cadence) and a freshness bot flagging pages not reviewed in 180 days.
Set up preview deployments per PR and a doc review checklist.
Deploy via CI to a CDN within 5 minutes of merge, with rollback to the previous version in under 2 minutes.
Instrument analytics: search queries with no results, page helpfulness votes, and time to first successful call; set targets.
Onboard 30 engineers with a 30 minute guide and measure that over 70 percent of feature PRs include a docs change.

examples.title: Vale rule and CI output
examples.code:
extends: substitution
message: "Use '%s' instead of '%s'."
level: error
swap:
  utilize: use
  e-mail: email
  whitelist: allowlist
examples.output:
docs/auth.md
 14:22  error  Use 'allowlist' instead of 'whitelist'  Acme.Terms
 1 error, 0 warnings in 1 file.

notes: A linter nobody trusts gets ignored; start with few high-value rules.
Test samples against the real released version, not main.
Ownership metadata makes staleness someone's problem.

title: Restructure Banking Help Docs
description: Restructure a 1,200-page help set so customers find answers to money questions quickly.
overview: Restructure a 1,200-page help set so customers find answers to money questions quickly.
tasks: Run a content audit of all pages recording traffic, last update, owner, type, duplicate status and a keep, merge, rewrite or delete decision.
Classify content using the Diataxis model (tutorial, how-to, reference, explanation) and note mixed-type pages for splitting.
Interview 10 users and mine 500 support tickets and search logs to find top tasks; rank the top 20.
Run an open card sort with 20 participants and a tree test of the proposed IA with 50 participants, targeting 75 percent task success.
Design navigation (max 2 levels in sidebar, max 7 top-level groups) and a consistent page template per content type.
Delete or merge at least 30 percent of low-value pages, with a documented rationale.
Create a redirect map for all moved URLs and verify with a crawl that no 404s exist and canonical tags are correct.
Migrate in phases with a freeze window and a rollback plan; keep search traffic loss under 5 percent.
Measure before and after: time to find answer in moderated tests, search exit rate, support tickets mentioning docs, page helpfulness.
Write contributor guidance so structure does not decay.

examples.title: Redirect verification
examples.code:
lychee --offline sitemap-old-urls.txt --base https://docs.example.com
python verify_redirects.py redirect-map.csv --expect-status 301
examples.output:
Checked 1,184 old URLs
301 OK: 1,176   missing: 8   loops: 0
FAIL: 8 URLs have no redirect (listed in missing.txt)

notes: Search logs tell you the real vocabulary; use it in headings.
Never ship an IA change without redirects.
Deleting content is a writing skill and an unpopular one.

title: Developer Docs for a Payments Launch
description: Own docs for a payments API launch so merchants start accepting payments in hours.
overview: Own docs for a payments API launch so merchants start accepting payments in hours.
tasks: Review the API design before build and file at least 10 documented usability issues (naming, errors, pagination) with proposed changes.
Write a quickstart so a new developer makes a first successful call in under 5 minutes, validated by watching 5 developers do it.
Produce a reference from an OpenAPI 3.1 spec with every field described, constraints, and examples; lint with Spectral and require 100 percent description coverage.
Document authentication, rate limits (for example 100 requests per minute), pagination, idempotency keys, errors with every error code and recovery action.
Write task-based guides for the top 8 use cases with working samples in 3 languages tested in CI.
Document webhooks including signature verification with HMAC SHA-256, retries and ordering guarantees.
Create a changelog and a deprecation and versioning policy with sunset dates.
Run a beta documentation review with 10 external developers, collect feedback and fix issues before GA.
Instrument and report time to first call, quickstart completion rate and docs-related support tickets in the first 30 days.
Hold a retrospective and update the doc templates.

examples.title: Quickstart first call
examples.code:
curl https://api.example.com/v1/payments \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2d0e-0a7b-4f7f-9d0e-1a2b3c4d5e6f" \
  -d amount=2000 -d currency=usd
examples.output:
{"id":"pay_1Hq...","object":"payment","amount":2000,"currency":"usd","status":"succeeded"}
Shape shown; ids and fields vary by API.

notes: Error messages are documentation; fix them at source.
Samples must be copy-paste runnable with the placeholders obvious.
Watch real people use it, silence is not success.

title: Migrate a Bank Website Without Losing Traffic
description: Migrate 500,000 URLs with under 5 percent traffic loss so customers still find their bank online.
overview: Migrate 500,000 URLs with under 5 percent traffic loss so customers still find their bank online.
tasks: Benchmark: export 16 months of Search Console data, crawl the full site with Screaming Frog or Sitebulb, and record URLs, titles, canonicals, internal links and top landing pages by clicks.
Build a URL mapping for every indexed URL using one-to-one 301 rules; handle patterns with regex and manual mapping for the top 5,000 pages.
Test on staging with a crawler: no redirect chains over 1 hop, zero loops, status codes correct, canonical and hreflang preserved, robots.txt blocking staging.
Verify structured data, meta tags, internal links and XML sitemaps carry across, comparing crawl diffs.
Check performance: Core Web Vitals on new templates (LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, CLS under 0.1) before launch.
Plan cutover with a freeze window, DNS TTL lowered to 300 seconds in advance, and a rollback decision tree.
After launch, submit new sitemaps, use the Change of Address tool, and monitor server logs for Googlebot crawl of old and new URLs hourly for the first 3 days.
Track daily: indexed pages, impressions, clicks, 404s, soft 404s, and rankings for 200 priority keywords; alert on 10 percent drop.
Keep old redirects for at least 12 months and update backlinks for the top 100 referring domains.
Report at 30, 60 and 90 days with traffic recovery against the benchmark.

examples.title: Redirect chain check
examples.code:
while read old; do
  curl -sIL -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{num_redirects} %{url_effective}\n" "$old"
done < top_urls.txt > results.txt; grep -v '^200 [01] ' results.txt
examples.output: No output means every URL resolves in 0 or 1 redirect with a final 200. Any line printed shows a chain or an error status, for example: 404 1 https://new.example.com/missing.

notes: Change as little as possible in one move; do not rewrite content and URLs together.
Server logs show truth faster than Search Console.
Expect a dip; set stakeholder expectations before launch.

title: Programmatic Pages for Financial Products
description: Launch 50,000 product pages with unique value so people compare loans and savings.
overview: Launch 50,000 product pages with unique value so people compare loans and savings.
tasks: Validate demand: pull keyword data for the pattern, confirm at least 500 pattern variants with 100 or more monthly searches, and define intent.
Design the template so each page has unique data-driven content (at least 40 percent unique text and original data points), not only a swapped keyword.
Build a quality score per page (data completeness, unique words, internal links) and publish only pages above a threshold, noindexing the rest.
Generate XML sitemaps split into files of at most 50,000 URLs, grouped by template, with lastmod accuracy.
Design a hub-and-spoke internal link structure so every page is within 3 clicks and receives at least 3 internal links.
Add structured data (Product, FAQ, LocalBusiness or relevant) validated in the Rich Results Test.
Launch in waves of 5,000 pages and monitor indexation rate, impressions and crawl stats; stop if indexation falls below 60 percent after 4 weeks.
Use log files to measure Googlebot crawl efficiency and fix parameter or facet traps with robots rules and canonicals.
Measure outcome: organic sessions, conversions and revenue per page, with a cohort comparison to a control subset.
Prune or merge underperforming pages after 90 days.

examples.title: Page quality gate
examples.code:
def publishable(page):
    return (page.unique_words >= 250 and page.data_fields_filled >= 0.8
            and page.inbound_links >= 3 and page.similarity_to_nearest < 0.85)
indexable = [p for p in pages if publishable(p)]
print(len(indexable), "of", len(pages))
examples.output: For example: 31842 of 50000. The rest ship with noindex until their data improves. Counts vary by dataset.

notes: Near-duplicate pages dilute the whole site, quality beats count.
Start small and verify indexation before scaling.
Never auto-generate claims you cannot source.

title: Lending Search Revenue Model
description: Join search, analytics and logs to show which pages help people find loans.
overview: Join search, analytics and logs to show which pages help people find loans.
tasks: Export Search Console to BigQuery daily and join with GA4 sessions and conversions, and crawl and log data by URL.
Define page groups (template, intent, topic) with regex rules covering over 95 percent of clicks.
Build a dashboard in Looker Studio or similar: clicks, impressions, CTR, average position, conversions, revenue by page group, with 16 months of history.
Handle sampling and anonymised queries; document the limits of each data source.
Create an anomaly detector flagging a 15 percent week-on-week drop for any page group and annotate Google core updates.
Build a forecast with seasonality (Prophet or SARIMA) giving 80 percent prediction intervals for 6 months and test it by backcasting the last 6 months with MAPE under 15 percent.
Estimate incremental impact of one initiative with a causal method (difference in differences against a control page group or CausalImpact).
Calculate opportunity sizing: keywords ranking 4 to 15 times CTR uplift at position 3 times conversion value.
Document the data dictionary and refresh schedule, SLA of data ready by 08:00 daily.
Present a one page business case for the next quarter with expected return range.

examples.title: Opportunity sizing query
examples.code:
SELECT query, SUM(impressions) AS imp, AVG(position) AS pos,
       SUM(impressions) * (0.11 - 0.02) AS extra_clicks_if_top3
FROM searchconsole.searchdata_url_impression
WHERE data_date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 90 DAY)
GROUP BY query
HAVING AVG(position) BETWEEN 4 AND 15 AND SUM(impressions) > 5000
ORDER BY extra_clicks_if_top3 DESC LIMIT 20;
examples.output: A ranked list of 20 queries with impressions, average position and estimated extra clicks. CTR figures are assumptions and should be replaced with your own curve.

notes: Position is an average over many queries and devices; do not over-read it.
Show intervals, not point forecasts.
Attribute conservatively, trust is your asset.

title: Developer Onboarding for Payments
description: Rebuild the journey from signup to first payment call so small shops start accepting cards sooner.
overview: Rebuild the journey from signup to first payment call so small shops start accepting cards sooner.
tasks: Define funnel stages and events: visited docs, signed up, created key, first successful call, first webhook, first production call, with a unique developer ID across systems.
Baseline conversion and median time between each stage over 90 days; identify the top two drop-off points.
Watch 10 developers complete the quickstart in moderated, think-aloud sessions and log every hesitation with timestamps.
Reduce time to first successful call from the baseline (for example 22 minutes) to under 10 minutes by changes in docs, API keys UX and sample code.
Ship a CLI or sandbox with a pre-filled test key so no signup is required for the first call.
Improve SDK ergonomics: fix the top 10 issues from GitHub issues and support tickets, and add typed errors with remediation links.
Run an A/B test on the signup page and quickstart variant with a sample size calculation and a guardrail on support tickets.
Create a developer health score (activation, retention at 30 days, API error rate) and segment by language and company size.
Set up a feedback loop: weekly report of top 5 developer pain points to product with an owner and status.
Report the funnel change and revenue impact as developers reaching production per month.

examples.title: Funnel query
examples.code:
SELECT stage, COUNT(DISTINCT dev_id) AS devs,
       PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY secs_from_signup) AS median_secs
FROM dev_events
WHERE signup_date >= CURRENT_DATE - 90
GROUP BY stage ORDER BY MIN(stage_order);
examples.output:
stage              devs    median_secs
signed_up          8,420   0
key_created        6,105   140
first_call_ok      3,390   1320
production_call    610     604800   (illustrative)

notes: Time to first call is a better predictor of retention than signups.
Segment by language, Python users and Java users hit different walls.
Watching one real person struggle beats ten dashboards.

title: Payments Developer Community
description: Run a community with events so developers share safe ways to accept payments.
overview: Run a community with events so developers share safe ways to accept payments.
tasks: Define community goals and metrics: monthly active members, first-response time under 4 hours, percent of questions answered by community (target 60 percent), contributions per month.
Write a Code of Conduct with reporting and enforcement process, and train 6 moderators with documented escalation paths.
Launch a champions programme with 25 members: criteria, benefits, quarterly goals, and a feedback council that meets monthly.
Run 12 events per year across 3 regions (meetups, workshops, one conference track) with a budget per attendee and a post-event survey above 4.3 of 5.
Create a speaker pipeline and CFP support that places 10 community speakers, including at least 40 percent from underrepresented groups.
Build contributor pathways: good-first-issue labels, mentor matching and recognition, with 50 community pull requests merged in the year.
Set up community tooling: Discord or Discourse, a CRM-like member graph, and automations for welcome and unanswered posts.
Track pipeline value: community-sourced leads, referral signups and support deflection hours saved, with methodology reviewed by finance.
Run a quarterly community health review including burnout risk for moderators and decide what to stop.
