Write a playbook enabling a regional lead to launch a new chapter within 6 weeks.

examples.title: Community health snapshot
examples.code:
Q3 snapshot
Monthly active members: 3,870 (+18% QoQ)
Median first response: 2h 40m
Answered by community: 58%
Merged community PRs: 17
Champion NPS: +54
Support hours deflected (est.): 310
examples.output: A quarterly one-page snapshot comparing to previous quarter and target, with a note on each metric's method. Values illustrative.

notes: Attendance is vanity; track repeat participation and contributions.
Moderator burnout ends communities, budget for paid moderation.
Give champions real influence or they leave.

title: Maintained Samples for a Payments SDK
description: Keep payment tutorials running on the current release so developers don't hit broken examples.
overview: Keep payment tutorials running on the current release so developers don't hit broken examples.
tasks: Create a content strategy mapped to funnel stages and the top 15 developer jobs with a quarterly calendar.
Maintain a monorepo of at least 12 sample apps across 4 languages, each with a README, one-command setup and an environment check script.
Run every sample in CI on every SDK release and weekly on a schedule; tests fail the release if a sample breaks.
Pin dependencies and use Renovate or Dependabot, with an SLA of 7 days to fix a breaking upgrade.
Publish 20 tutorials a year each with a defined outcome, estimated time and a tested completion path, validated by a fresh-machine run.
Deliver 4 conference talks or workshops, recorded, with a reusable demo that works offline in case of network failure.
Instrument content: attribute sign-ups and first calls to content via UTM and in-sample telemetry (opt-in), reporting cost per activated developer.
Set content lifecycle: owner, review date, deprecate or redirect rules, and a quarterly pruning pass.
Collect reader feedback inline and fix the lowest rated 10 pieces each quarter.
Write a guest-author guide and publish 5 external contributions.

examples.title: Sample CI matrix
examples.code:
strategy:
  matrix:
    sample: [quickstart-node, quickstart-python, chat-nextjs, webhook-go]
    sdk: [latest, previous]
steps:
  - run: ./scripts/check-env.sh
  - run: make -C samples/${{ matrix.sample }} setup test
examples.output: CI shows 8 jobs (4 samples by 2 SDK versions). A failure names the sample and SDK version, blocks the SDK release and opens an issue assigned to the sample owner.

notes: A tutorial with no test has a shelf life of about three months.
Measure activation per piece, pageviews reward clickbait.
Offline fallbacks save live demos.

title: Pricing Overhaul for a Fintech Product
description: Redesign fees and plans with customer research so people pay fair prices.
overview: Redesign fees and plans with customer research so people pay fair prices.
tasks: Analyse usage and revenue data to find value metrics (seats, usage, outcomes) and rank by correlation with customer-reported value.
Run a Van Westendorp or Gabor-Granger survey with 200 or more respondents and 15 customer interviews.
Build a revenue model in a spreadsheet with scenarios (conservative, base, optimistic), including churn and expansion assumptions and a sensitivity table.
Design 3 tiers with a fence for each feature, a clear upgrade trigger and a pricing page copy test.
Define the migration plan: grandfathering rules, notice period of 60 days, and an exception process; estimate accounts with price increase above 20 percent.
Test with a limited cohort or new-customer-only A/B test running 6 weeks, with conversion, ARPA and refund rate guardrails.
Align sales, support and finance through enablement documents, an FAQ, objection handling and billing system changes.
Set success criteria before launch: ARPA up 12 percent, logo churn not above baseline plus 0.5 points, NRR above 110 percent.
Run a post-launch review at 30, 90 and 180 days and record what the model got wrong.
Write a decision memo for the executive team with a recommendation and risks.

examples.title: Scenario model excerpt
examples.code:
Scenario        Conv. change  Churn delta  ARPA     12-mo revenue
Conservative    -4%           +0.8 pts     +$9      +3.1%
Base            -1%           +0.2 pts     +$18     +9.4%
Optimistic      +2%           0.0 pts      +$24     +14.2%
Break-even churn delta: +1.9 pts
examples.output: A table with the break-even point visible so executives see how wrong assumptions could be before the change hurts. Numbers illustrative.

notes: Existing customers get angry about surprise, not price; communicate early.
Test on new customers first when billing complexity is high.
Document the model assumptions, you will be asked in 6 months.

title: Multi-Year Banking Portfolio
description: Define a banking product vision that serves customers through changing priorities.
overview: Define a banking product vision that serves customers through changing priorities.
tasks: Write a diagnosis: market sizing (TAM, SAM, SOM with sources), competitor analysis of 5 players, customer segments and the 3 biggest strategic challenges.
Define the guiding policy: where to play and how to win, with explicit things you will not do and the reasons.
Create a portfolio across three horizons with an allocation (for example 70 percent core, 20 percent adjacent, 10 percent new) and a kill or scale criterion for each bet.
Map dependencies and capacity: engineering effort in person-quarters for each initiative and a feasibility review with tech leads.
Set OKRs with 3 objectives and measurable key results, checking each for leading versus lagging indicators.
Run pre-mortems with leadership to list how the strategy fails and agree on early warning metrics.
Present to the executive team and record objections and how the strategy changed; include an alignment tracker.
Create a quarterly strategy review ritual with a one-page scorecard, and change the plan at least once based on evidence.
Communicate to the whole org with a narrative document and a Q&A session, collecting understanding scores in a short survey.
Evaluate at 12 months: which bets were scaled, killed or pivoted and the realised outcomes.

examples.title: Bet scorecard
examples.code:
Bet: SMB self-serve tier (Horizon 2)
Hypothesis: 2,000 SMBs convert at 3% from free to paid within 2 quarters
Investment: 3 engineers, 2 quarters
Scale signal: >=2.5% conversion and CAC payback <9 months by end of Q2
Kill signal: <1.2% conversion after Q2
Status Q1: 1.8% conversion, trend up
examples.output: A scorecard per bet showing status against pre-agreed scale and kill signals, reviewed quarterly. Numbers illustrative.

notes: A strategy that does not say no is a wish list.
Write kill criteria while you are still neutral.
Alignment is built through objections, not through slides.

title: Retention Programme for a Neobank
description: Raise 90-day retention on a neobank by testing what keeps customers saving.
overview: Raise 90-day retention on a neobank by testing what keeps customers saving.
tasks: Define a north star metric and a metrics tree down to controllable inputs, with definitions agreed in writing by product, data and finance.
Instrument events with a tracking plan (naming convention, properties) and audit data quality, targeting under 1 percent event loss.
Build cohort retention curves and find the activation behaviour that predicts retention (for example 3 projects created in 7 days) with a logistic regression or a simple lift table.
Segment users by acquisition channel and plan to identify the best and worst retaining groups.
Score ideas with ICE or RICE and run at least 10 experiments in the quarter with sample size calculations and guardrails.
Build lifecycle messaging (onboarding emails and in-app prompts) for the activation moment, tested against a holdout.
Analyse churn with exit surveys of 100 or more responses and a churn-reason taxonomy, quantifying the revenue at risk by reason.
Run a long-term holdout of 5 percent to measure cumulative impact of the programme.
Review weekly with a growth meeting covering results, learnings and next experiments, documenting every result including failures.
Report outcome: 90-day retention up 5 percentage points with a confidence interval, and revenue impact.

examples.title: Activation lift table
examples.code:
SELECT activated_7d,
       COUNT(*) AS users,
       AVG(retained_d90::int) AS d90_retention
FROM user_cohorts
WHERE signup_month = '2026-06'
GROUP BY activated_7d;
examples.output:
activated_7d  users   d90_retention
false         14,203  0.12
true          6,611   0.47   (illustrative; correlation, to be tested by experiment)

notes: Correlation picks the hypothesis, experiments prove it.
Define metrics once; competing definitions kill trust.
Retention beats acquisition as a lever once the funnel leaks.

title: Org Design for a Fintech Group
description: Restructure 60 engineers into teams that own customer features end to end.
overview: Restructure 60 engineers into teams that own customer features end to end.
tasks: Baseline with DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, restore time) and an engagement survey.
Map current dependencies: count cross-team handoffs for the 10 most common change types and the median wait time.
Propose a target topology with stream-aligned, platform, enabling and complicated-subsystem teams, with team sizes of 5 to 8.
Write a team charter for each team: mission, owned services, interfaces, on-call scope and success metrics.
Run a consultation with tech leads and affected engineers, record concerns and alter the design at least twice because of them.
Plan the transition in phases over 2 quarters, with a communication plan, 1:1 conversations before announcement and a 4-week stabilisation period.
Redistribute on-call so each service has a named owning team, and reduce pages per engineer to under 2 per week.
Set cognitive load limits: each team owns at most a defined number of services, reviewed quarterly.
Measure after 2 quarters: lead time reduced by 30 percent, cross-team handoffs by 50 percent, engagement not worse than baseline.
Write a retrospective with decisions you would reverse.

examples.title: Team charter excerpt
examples.code:
Team: Checkout (stream-aligned, 7 engineers)
Mission: Reduce checkout abandonment from 31% to 24% by year end
Owns: checkout-api, payment-ui, order-events (3 services)
Depends on: Payments Platform (X-as-a-service), Identity (collaboration until Q2)
On-call: weekly rotation, <=2 pages/engineer/week
Metrics: abandonment, p95 checkout latency, change failure rate
examples.output: One charter per team, stored in the repo and reviewed each quarter. Interface types with other teams are explicit.

notes: People hear about reorgs through rumour first; shorten the gap between decision and announcement.
Ownership without on-call and a roadmap is fiction.
Expect a productivity dip of 4 to 8 weeks and plan for it.

title: Career Framework for Fintech Engineers
description: Create a fair career ladder so engineers who serve customers are rewarded.
overview: Create a fair career ladder so engineers who serve customers are rewarded.
tasks: Write expectations for 6 levels across 4 dimensions (technical craft, delivery, collaboration, leadership), with behavioural examples for each cell.
Review the draft with 15 engineers across levels and revise at least 10 statements based on feedback.
Define the promotion process: packet template, 2 sponsors, evidence from the last 12 months, committee review within 2 weeks.
Run calibration meetings with a facilitation guide, written rationales, and checks for rating distribution by gender, tenure and team; report disparities.
Train 10 managers with real anonymised cases on writing specific feedback using situation, behaviour, impact.
Create a performance improvement plan template with measurable goals, a 60 day timeline, support commitments and HR review.
Handle at least one real underperformance case end to end, documenting early feedback, support, and outcome with HR.
Gather upward feedback twice a year and review manager effectiveness scores.
Measure trust: survey question on fairness of process above 4 of 5 and promotion cycle time under 3 weeks.
Publish the framework internally and run an annual revision.

examples.title: Level expectation excerpt
examples.code:
Level 5 Senior Engineer - Delivery
Expected: Leads a multi-quarter project with 3-5 engineers, breaks down work, manages scope trade-offs, delivers within one sprint of plan 80% of the time.
Evidence: project plans, delivery history, stakeholder feedback.
Level 6 difference: sets technical direction across several teams.
examples.output: A grid of behaviour statements with evidence types, used identically in feedback, hiring and promotion decisions.

notes: Write feedback early; surprises in reviews mean the manager failed.
Calibration should compare evidence, not personalities.
Frameworks decay unless revised each year.

title: Incident Culture for a Payments Platform
description: Cut major payment incidents by 40 percent so customers can rely on payments.
overview: Cut major payment incidents by 40 percent so customers can rely on payments.
tasks: Define severity levels (SEV1 to SEV4) with customer-impact criteria and expected response times.
Set SLOs and error budgets for the 8 most critical services, with a policy that freezes feature launches when the budget is exhausted.
Establish incident roles (commander, communications, operations) and train 15 engineers with 2 simulated incidents.
Implement paging: alert quality review removing alerts that are not actionable, target under 5 pages per on-call shift per week and 30 percent night-time maximum.
Create a status page process with a first customer update within 15 minutes of SEV1 declaration.
Write blameless postmortems for every SEV1 and SEV2 within 5 business days, with 3 to 5 action items, each with owner and date.
Track action item completion above 85 percent within 30 days and report overdue ones to leadership.
Review incident data quarterly: MTTD, MTTR, recurrence by root-cause category, and invest in the top category.
Compensate and rotate on-call fairly, with time off after night incidents and a health survey of on-call engineers.
Show results: major incidents down at least 40 percent year on year and MTTR below 45 minutes.

examples.title: Postmortem skeleton
examples.code:
Incident 2026-09-14 Checkout 500s (SEV1, 47 min)
Impact: 18% of checkouts failed; est. $212k revenue delayed
Timeline: 14:02 deploy; 14:09 alert; 14:15 declared; 14:41 rollback; 14:49 recovered
Contributing factors: config validation missing; canary skipped; alert lacked runbook
Actions: add schema validation (A. Rao, 9/30); enforce canary (platform, 10/15); runbook (on-call, 9/25)
examples.output: Published postmortem with timeline, impact, contributing factors (not blame) and tracked actions. Numbers illustrative.

notes: Fix the system, not the person; blame silences the people who know most.
An alert without an action is noise.
Postmortems with no completed actions are theatre.

title: Claude Code Rollout for Fintech Engineers
description: Roll Claude Code out to 100 fintech engineers with cost and permission controls.
overview: Roll Claude Code out to 100 fintech engineers with cost and permission controls.
tasks: Draft an acceptable-use and data policy covering secrets, customer data, licensed code and which repos are in scope, reviewed by security and legal.
Deploy managed settings (managed-settings.json) enforcing deny rules for reading .env files and credentials, and blocking dangerous commands such as curl piped to shell.
Configure sandboxing and an allowlist of MCP servers, with each server reviewed for scopes and data access.
Enable OpenTelemetry export for usage, cost and tool decisions into your observability stack, with a dashboard by team.
Set spend limits per user and per team, with alerts at 80 percent of monthly budget.
Run a 4 week pilot with 15 engineers using a control group; measure PR cycle time, review rounds and survey satisfaction.
Create a shared CLAUDE.md template, a central skills and subagents repository, and a plugin marketplace with review process.
Write onboarding training (2 hours) covering plan mode, context management, hooks and review of AI-generated diffs; certify attendees by a practical task.
Define code review rules for AI-assisted changes, including test requirements and a label on PRs.
Present results at 90 days with cost per engineer, time saved estimate with confidence range, and incidents or near misses.

examples.title: Managed settings excerpt
examples.output: Engineers see the policy applied at session start; an attempt to read .env is refused with a permission denied message, and the denial event appears in the telemetry dashboard. Exact setting names should be checked against current docs.

notes: Deny rules protect secrets better than instructions in a prompt.
Compare against a control group or the productivity claim is anecdote.
Review the diff yourself; the agent is not the approver.

title: Hooks and Subagents for Payment Code
description: Build team workflows that enforce quality gates on payment code so customers' payments stay correct.
overview: Build team workflows that enforce quality gates on payment code so customers' payments stay correct.
tasks: Write a CLAUDE.md under 200 lines covering build and test commands, architecture map, conventions and do-not rules, validated by having a fresh session complete 3 tasks.
Add PreToolUse hooks that block edits to generated files and migrations folders and PostToolUse hooks that run the formatter and type checker, exit code 2 feeding errors back.
Add a Stop hook that runs the affected test subset and prevents the session ending while tests fail.
Create 3 skills (for example add-endpoint, write-migration, release-notes) with a description that triggers correctly and supporting scripts.
Create read-only subagents for code review and security review with restricted tools, and a parallel exploration subagent for large searches.
Build an eval set of 20 tasks with automated pass or fail checks (tests, linters, diff size) and run it headless with claude -p and JSON output.
Track pass rate, turns, tokens and cost per task; change one thing at a time and keep a log of what helped.
Add a GitHub Action running Claude Code on PRs for review comments, with permission scope limited to read and comment.
Handle failure modes: runaway loops, context bloat, hallucinated APIs; document mitigations and add checks.
Publish the setup as a plugin so another repository installs it in one command.

examples.title: PostToolUse hook
examples.output: After every edit the formatter and type check run. A type error returns a non-zero code and the message is shown to the agent so it fixes it. Exact environment variables and exit semantics should be verified against current docs.

notes: Keep hooks fast; slow hooks make every edit painful.
Without evals you cannot tell improvement from luck.
Give subagents the fewest tools that do the job.

title: Automated Migration for Payments Code
description: Migrate 500 payment files with verification gates so customers see no change.
overview: Migrate 500 payment files with verification gates so customers see no change.
tasks: Define the migration precisely with 10 before and after examples and an explicit list of out-of-scope patterns.
Write a deterministic codemod (jscodeshift, ast-grep or comby) for the mechanical 70 percent and leave only judgement cases to the agent.
Create a verification harness: build, type check, unit tests and a snapshot of public API; a file batch is accepted only if all pass.
Split work into batches of about 10 files by dependency order and run batches in parallel using git worktrees, with a budget cap per batch.
Run Claude Code headless with a scripted prompt and structured output, for example claude -p with --output-format json and --max-turns, logging cost and result per batch.
Route failed batches to a retry with the error output, then to a human queue after 2 attempts; track the percentage resolved automatically.
Generate pull requests of under 400 changed lines each, with a summary of what changed and how it was verified.
Sample-review 10 percent of agent diffs by hand and record defects found; if above 2 percent, tighten instructions or the codemod.
Roll out behind the test suite plus a staged deployment, and monitor error rates for 2 weeks.
Report total cost, human hours, defects found after merge and lessons, compared to a manual estimate.

examples.title: Batch runner
examples.code:
git worktree add ../wt-batch-07 -b migrate/batch-07
cd ../wt-batch-07
claude -p "Migrate files in batches/07.txt per MIGRATION.md. Run npm run verify. Stop when it passes." \
  --output-format json --max-turns 25 --allowedTools "Edit,Bash(npm run verify)" > result-07.json
jq '{is_error, num_turns, total_cost_usd}' result-07.json
examples.output:
{"is_error":false,"num_turns":14,"total_cost_usd":0.62}
Shape shown; values vary and field names should be checked against the installed version.

notes: Mechanical changes belong in a codemod, agents are for the judgement leftovers.
Verification gates matter more than the prompt.
Small PRs are what make agent output reviewable.

title: Codex Rollout for Fintech Engineers
description: Roll out coding agents to 200 fintech engineers with guardrails and measured quality.
overview: Roll out coding agents to 200 fintech engineers with guardrails and measured quality.
tasks: Segment repositories into three tiers (public/internal/regulated) and define a sandbox mode and approval policy per tier, for example workspace-write with on-request approvals for internal and read-only with network disabled for regulated.
Publish a managed config.toml baseline (model, approval_policy, sandbox_mode, allowed MCP servers) and a signed distribution method so developers cannot silently loosen it.
Write an AGENTS.md standard with required sections (build, test, lint commands, forbidden paths, definition of done) and a linter that fails CI when a repo lacks one.

Run a 6-week pilot with 30 engineers and a control group; measure PR cycle time, review rounds, change failure rate and reverted-PR rate, with a pre-registered success threshold such as 15 percent shorter cycle time and no rise in change failure rate.

Build an audit pipeline that captures every agent session (prompt, commands run, files changed, approvals granted) into your log store with 90-day retention and a query for 'which sessions touched secrets paths'.
Create a red-team suite of 12 prompt-injection cases (malicious README, poisoned issue text, hostile dependency script) and show the policy blocks each; record results.
Define a cost budget per team with alerts at 80 percent and a monthly report of cost per merged PR.
Deliver a training session and a one-page escalation runbook for agent-caused incidents, and run one tabletop exercise.

examples.title: Managed baseline config
examples.code:
# /etc/codex/config.toml (managed)
approval_policy = "on-request"
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"

[sandbox_workspace_write]
network_access = false
exclude_tmpdir_env_var = true
examples.output: Developers see these as locked defaults; codex status shows sandbox workspace-write, approvals on-request, network off.

examples.title: Pilot results table
examples.code:
metric              control   codex   delta
median PR cycle     31h       24h     -23%
review rounds       2.4       2.2     -8%
change failure      9.1%      8.7%    ns
reverted PRs        1.8%      2.0%    ns
examples.output: Shape of a report; your numbers will differ. Include sample size and confidence interval.

notes: Policy that is too tight gets bypassed with personal accounts; measure shadow usage and tune before enforcing.
Network access is the biggest exfiltration and injection channel; allow-list domains rather than opening it wholesale.
Cycle time alone can reward bigger, sloppier PRs; always pair it with a quality counter-metric.

title: Codex Benchmark From Payment Repos
description: Benchmark agent configs on real payment tasks so changes to payment code are safer.
overview: Benchmark agent configs on real payment tasks so changes to payment code are safer.
tasks: Mine 100 merged PRs with linked issues across 5 repos; for each, create a task prompt from the issue, a base commit, and hidden tests taken from the PR.
Run each task via codex exec in a fresh container with a pinned image, a 20-minute timeout and no network except the package mirror.
Score pass or fail by running hidden tests, plus secondary scores: diff size, files touched outside the true PR, lint cleanliness, tokens used and wall time.
Run each task 3 times per configuration to estimate variance; report pass@1 and pass@3 with 95 percent confidence intervals.
Compare at least 3 configurations (baseline, improved AGENTS.md, different model or reasoning effort) and show a statistically sound difference using a paired bootstrap.
Detect contamination and flakiness: quarantine tasks whose hidden tests fail on the true solution in more than 1 of 10 runs.
Gate AGENTS.md changes in CI: a PR that edits it triggers a 30-task subset and blocks if pass rate drops by more than 5 points.
Publish a dashboard with trend lines per repo and a failure taxonomy (wrong file, hallucinated API, test not run, scope creep) from manual labelling of 40 failures.

examples.title: Harness run
examples.code:
./evalctl run --suite repo-tasks-v1 --config agents-v2.toml --runs 3 --parallel 12
./evalctl report --suite repo-tasks-v1 --compare baseline agents-v2
examples.output:
config       pass@1  pass@3  median_tokens  median_min
baseline     41.0%   55.0%   182k           7.4
agents-v2    49.3%   61.0%   171k           6.8
paired bootstrap p=0.03 (values vary)

notes: Hidden tests must not be visible in the repo, or the agent will read them and the score is meaningless.
Variance between runs of the same task is large; a single run per task cannot support any conclusion.
Refresh the suite quarterly or it overfits to your configuration.

title: Coding Agent Security for Payments
description: Harden coding agents against secret leakage so customers' keys stay private.
overview: Harden coding agents against secret leakage so customers' keys stay private.
tasks: Produce a STRIDE-style threat model of the agent workflow: inputs (issues, READMEs, MCP tool output), capabilities (shell, git push, network) and assets (secrets, prod credentials).
Run agent sessions in ephemeral containers with no ambient credentials; deliver secrets only via short-lived tokens scoped to one repo and valid for 30 minutes.
Enforce egress allow-listing at the network layer and verify with a test that curl to a non-listed host fails.
Add a pre-push hook and server-side branch protection so agents can only push to agent/* branches and never to main.
Add secret scanning (gitleaks or equivalent) on every agent diff and prove it blocks a planted fake AWS key.
Create 10 prompt-injection fixtures embedded in files and issue text; measure how many cause an unapproved command and drive that to zero for the high-risk tier.

Write a blameless incident review for one event (for example the agent deleted a migrations folder): timeline, contributing factors, detection time, and three corrective actions with owners and dates.
Define alerts: agent session running over 60 minutes, more than 500 files changed, or any denied-command count above 5.

examples.title: Egress test
examples.code:
codex exec --sandbox workspace-write "run: curl -sS -m 5 https://evil.example/x"
echo exit=$?
examples.output:
curl: (6) Could not resolve host: evil.example   (or connection blocked)
exit=0 for codex; the command inside failed and the denial is logged

notes: Approval prompts train people to click yes; reduce prompts by tightening the sandbox, not by nagging.
Treat all tool output, including MCP responses, as untrusted input.
Short-lived scoped tokens beat any amount of prompt wording.

title: Quality Gates for Vibe-Coded Fintech Apps
description: Let non-experts build fintech apps safely with tests, scans and review gates.
overview: Let non-experts build fintech apps safely with tests, scans and review gates.
tasks: Define three risk classes (toy, internal, customer-data) with explicit criteria and required controls for each.
Ship a template repo with auth via company SSO, a typed API layer, a database migration tool, structured logging and a Dockerfile that already passes security checks.
Add CI gates: unit tests with at least 70 percent line coverage, dependency audit (npm audit or pip-audit) with zero high severity, SAST (Semgrep ruleset), secret scan and a bundle-size budget.
Add an LLM-aware lint: detect hard-coded keys, disabled auth middleware, wildcard CORS, SQL built by string concatenation and eval usage; include 15 labelled bad examples.
Require a spec file (SPEC.md with user stories and data classification) before the customer-data tier can deploy, checked by CI.
Run an audit of 25 existing vibe-coded apps, scoring them against the gates; report how many fail and the top five recurring defects.
Remediate the 5 worst apps and measure time to fix; target under 2 days each.
Publish a dashboard of gate pass rate, mean time to ship and incident count, and report quarterly.

examples.title: Gate output
examples.code:
$ make gates
[ok]   tests 41 passed, coverage 78%
[ok]   pip-audit 0 vulnerabilities
[FAIL] semgrep python.flask.security.injection.sql-concat app/db.py:57
[FAIL] auth-lint: route /admin/export has no auth decorator
examples.output: Exit code 1; deployment blocked until both findings are fixed.

notes: Gates that take over 10 minutes get skipped; keep the fast path under 5.
Authors cannot fix what they cannot read; make failure messages say how to repair, with a link.
Classify by data, not by app size; a ten-line script can leak a customer table.

title: Rescue an AI-Generated Banking Codebase
description: Make an untested AI-built banking codebase secure and deployable so customers' data is protected.
overview: Make an untested AI-built banking codebase secure and deployable so customers' data is protected.
tasks: Map the codebase: dependency graph, dead code (vulture or knip), duplicated logic clones and hot spots by churn times complexity; produce a one-page risk map.
Write characterization tests around the 10 most critical user flows first, before refactoring; reach 60 percent coverage on those modules.
Add observability (structured logs, request IDs, error tracking, 4 golden-signal dashboards) and use it to find the top 5 production errors.
Fix security basics: move secrets out of the repo and rotate them, add input validation at all API boundaries, parametrise queries, add rate limiting and fix the top OWASP findings from a ZAP scan.
Replace duplicated or conflicting abstractions (for example three different HTTP clients, two ORMs) with one, using the strangler approach with a feature flag per module.
Introduce migrations and a seeded staging environment; prove a restore from backup works with a timed drill under 30 minutes.
Create an ARCHITECTURE.md and three ADRs capturing decisions made, so later AI sessions have reliable context.
Report before and after: P95 latency, error rate, deploy frequency, and lead time for a change.

examples.title: Churn x complexity hotspot
examples.code:
python hotspots.py --since 6.months --top 5
radon cc app -s -n C
examples.output:
87 app/services/orders.py
  61 app/api/routes.py
...
app/services/orders.py: F 24 process_order - C (31)

notes: Do not refactor before tests; an AI-written module with no tests will break silently.
Rewrites fail; strangle the worst modules and leave working ugliness alone.
Write down intent in docs, since the original prompts are lost.

title: Spec-Driven AI Payments Workflow
description: Keep AI-written payment code coherent with specs and tests so customers' payments stay correct.
overview: Keep AI-written payment code coherent with specs and tests so customers' payments stay correct.
tasks: Define a lightweight spec format (problem, constraints, acceptance tests, non-goals) stored under /specs and required for any change over 150 lines.
Create shared context files: ARCHITECTURE.md, CONVENTIONS.md and a library of 10 vetted prompt templates for common tasks (new endpoint, migration, refactor).
Adopt test-first prompting: the human writes or approves failing tests, the AI makes them pass; track the share of PRs following the flow.
Add automated drift checks: import-boundary rules (dependency-cruiser or import-linter), a duplicate-code detector with a threshold, and an API naming lint.
Set a PR size budget (under 400 changed lines) and an 'AI-assisted' label with a required self-review checklist.
Measure for 8 weeks versus the prior 8: review turnaround, defect escape rate, duplicate code percentage and engineer satisfaction survey (n=10).
Hold a retrospective and revise rules; remove at least two rules that did not help.
Write a 2-page onboarding guide for a new engineer to be productive with the workflow in one day.

examples.title: Import boundary rule
examples.code:
[importlinter:contract:layers]
name = Layered architecture
type = layers
layers =
    app.api
    app.services
    app.repo
examples.output: lint-imports: 1 contract kept, 0 broken. A violation prints the offending import chain and fails CI.

notes: Rules without automated checks decay within a month.
Specs should be short; long specs are not read by humans or models.
Compare against baseline data, otherwise the workflow cannot be called an improvement.

title: Quality System for a Fintech AI Product
description: Make an AI product's answers measurable with evals so customers get accurate guidance.
overview: Make an AI product's answers measurable with evals so customers get accurate guidance.
tasks: Build a golden set of 500 real, anonymised queries stratified by intent, difficulty and language, with reference answers labelled by two reviewers and inter-annotator agreement (Cohen kappa) of at least 0.7.
Implement graders: exact or schema checks, retrieval metrics (recall at 5), and an LLM judge with a rubric; calibrate the judge against 100 human labels and report agreement and bias.
Run evals in CI on every prompt, model or retrieval change; block merge if quality drops by more than 2 points or cost per query rises more than 15 percent.
Add online metrics: thumbs rate, resolution without escalation, edit distance of accepted drafts, plus A/B testing with a power calculation and a minimum 2 week run.
Sample 1 percent of production traffic into a review queue and track defect categories (hallucination, refusal, stale knowledge, tone).
Create a regression suite from every user-reported failure within 48 hours of the report.
Define SLOs: P95 latency under 4 s, hallucination rate under 3 percent on the golden set, and cost under 1.2 cents per query.
Publish a model-upgrade runbook and execute one model swap using the system, with a before and after report.

examples.title: CI eval gate
examples.code:
eval run prompt-v14 vs prompt-v13 (n=500)
correctness   0.84 -> 0.87  (+3.0)
groundedness  0.91 -> 0.90  (-1.0)
P95 latency   3.1s -> 3.4s
cost/query    0.9c -> 1.0c
verdict: PASS
examples.output: Shape of the report; thresholds come from your SLOs and numbers vary.

notes: LLM judges prefer longer answers and their own family; calibrate and spot-check.
A golden set that never changes will be overfit; add fresh samples monthly.
Offline gains often fail to show online; keep both.

title: Cheaper Banking LLM Product
description: Cut inference cost by 60 percent so banks can offer AI help to every customer.
overview: Cut inference cost by 60 percent so banks can offer AI help to every customer.
tasks: Instrument cost per request by feature, model, tenant and token class (input, cached, output) and build a cost dashboard.
Apply prompt caching and shrink prompts; target 50 percent cache hit on the static prefix and measure savings.
Introduce model routing: send easy requests to a small model and hard ones to a large model, with a classifier validated on the golden set to lose less than 1 point quality.
Add semantic and exact-match response caching with TTL and invalidation rules; report hit rate and any stale-answer incidents.
Stream responses and set a time-to-first-token target under 800 ms at P95.
Add resilience: provider failover, retries with jittered backoff, circuit breaker, per-tenant rate limits and a degraded mode answering from search results only.
Run a game day that kills the primary provider and verify 99.9 percent availability for the month.
Show before and after unit economics: cost per session from 4.0 cents to 1.6 cents or lower, with quality unchanged within the eval's confidence interval.

examples.title: Router config
examples.output: Dashboard shows 68 percent of traffic on small-fast; blended cost per session drops; failover count is logged.

notes: Always check quality after each cost optimisation, since savings can silently erode accuracy.
Semantic caches can leak across tenants; key them by tenant.
Provider limits change; build abstraction and keep two live providers.

title: Responsible AI Governance for Banks
description: Set risk checks and privacy controls for a bank's AI products so customers are protected.
overview: Set risk checks and privacy controls for a bank's AI products so customers are protected.
tasks: Create an AI risk register with a tiering rubric (minimal, limited, high) mapped to EU AI Act categories and NIST AI RMF functions; classify every AI feature.
Write model and system cards for 3 features: intended use, limits, evaluation results, known failure modes and data sources.
Run structured red-teaming with at least 150 adversarial cases (jailbreak, prompt injection, PII extraction, bias probes); log attack success rate and fix to under 2 percent for high-tier features.
Implement PII handling: detection and redaction before logging, retention of 30 days, tenant-level deletion within 72 hours, and a vendor data-processing review including zero-retention settings.
Add output safeguards: moderation, citation requirement and human-in-the-loop escalation for high-impact decisions.
Build immutable audit logs of prompts, model version, retrieved sources and outputs, queryable by case ID.
Pass one customer security questionnaire and one external audit or pen test using this evidence; track findings to closure.
Define an incident process for AI harms with severity levels, 24 hour customer notification for severe cases, and run one drill.

examples.title: Risk register row
examples.code:
{
 "feature": "loan-summary-assistant",
 "tier": "high",
 "risks": ["hallucinated figures", "disparate impact"],
 "controls": ["citation-required", "human-approval", "quarterly bias eval"],
 "owner": "head-of-ml", "review": "2027-01-15"
}
examples.output: Every AI feature has a row; the register is reviewed quarterly and linked to eval reports.

notes: Governance that lives in documents only is ignored; wire controls into CI and runtime.
Vendor terms on training and retention change; re-review annually.
Keep evidence automatically, because audits ask for months of history.

title: Payments Integration in a Restricted Bank Network
description: Deliver a working payments integration in a restricted network under real compliance rules.
overview: Deliver a working payments integration in a restricted network under real compliance rules.
tasks: Produce a deployment dossier: architecture diagram, data flows, ports, required egress (ideally none), software bill of materials and threat model, accepted by customer security.
Package for offline install: signed container images in a tarball, a Helm chart with values for private registry, and checksums verified by a script.
Support the customer's TLS-inspecting proxy and internal CA through configurable trust bundles; test with a simulated proxy.
Integrate with their identity provider via SAML or OIDC and map groups to roles; verify least privilege.
Build a supportability kit: a diagnostics bundle command that gathers config, versions and sanitised logs (no secrets) for sharing by email.
Run a dry run in a mock environment that reproduces their restrictions, and fix at least 10 issues found before go-live.
Plan the cutover through the change board: rollback steps, success criteria, and a 2 hour maintenance window; execute and confirm with smoke tests.
After go-live, deliver a handover runbook and train 5 customer operators; target zero severity-1 incidents in the first 30 days.

examples.title: Diagnostics bundle
examples.code:
$ acme-diag collect --redact --out diag.tgz
collected: versions, helm values (redacted), pod status, last 2h logs, dns/proxy checks
sha256 9f3c...  diag.tgz  (1.4 MB)
examples.output: The customer emails diag.tgz without secrets; engineers can reproduce the problem.

notes: You cannot SSH in; design every failure to be diagnosable from artefacts.
Ask for the real network rules in week one, since assumptions cost weeks.
Document every deviation the customer approved, for later audits.

title: Measured Value for a Bank Customer
description: Prove a bank customer's outcome against a baseline so the bank's tools help people save.
overview: Prove a bank customer's outcome against a baseline so the bank's tools help people save.
tasks: Agree a success plan with the customer sponsor: three quantified outcomes, a baseline measured for 4 weeks before rollout, and the owner of each metric.
Instrument the workflow end to end (events, timestamps, outcome labels) and validate data quality by sampling 100 records with the customer.
Roll out in stages (10, 30, 100 percent of users) with a holdout group to isolate the effect from seasonality.
Compute impact with confidence intervals, for example handle time reduced by 22 percent (95 percent CI 17 to 27) over 8 weeks.
Convert to value: hours saved times loaded cost, error cost avoided, minus platform and your service cost; present payback period.
Run weekly adoption reviews, find the bottom quartile of users, and fix blockers (training, permissions, UX) leading to adoption above 70 percent.
Feed product gaps back: file the top 5 requests with customer evidence and revenue at risk, and track which ship.
Deliver an executive readout of under 10 slides and win a written expansion or renewal commitment.

examples.title: Impact calculation
examples.code:
base, treat = 14.2, 11.1   # mean handle minutes
saved_min = base - treat
annual = saved_min * 180_000 / 60 * 38.0  # tickets, loaded $/hr
print(round(saved_min/base*100), round(annual))
examples.output:
22
  196650   (values depend on your data)

notes: Without a baseline there is no proof; collect it before launch.
Customers distrust vendor-calculated ROI; compute with their finance team.
Adoption is the usual hidden failure, not model quality.

title: Productise Field Solutions for Banks
description: Turn repeated custom bank work into a product so more customers get solutions faster.
overview: Turn repeated custom bank work into a product so more customers get solutions faster.
tasks: Audit the 12 deployments: classify custom code by reuse (connectors, transforms, auth, evaluation); quantify engineering weeks spent per category.
Pick the top 3 components with highest reuse and define stable interfaces with versioning and a deprecation policy.
Build them as a library or service with docs, tests (at least 80 percent coverage) and a sample project that works in 30 minutes.
Migrate two live customers onto the new components with no regressions, verified by contract tests and shadow traffic comparison.
Create a field-to-product feedback process: weekly triage, a public roadmap of extracted components, and an owner per component.
Train 8 field engineers and measure adoption (share of new projects using the platform).
Measure outcomes: median time to first value from 9 weeks to 4 weeks, custom code per deployment down 50 percent.
Write an internal case study and a decision record on what stays custom and why.

examples.title: Reuse audit
examples.code:
component        deployments  eng-weeks  decision
sap-connector    7            21         productise
sso-mapping      11           11         productise
custom-report    3            9          keep custom
examples.output: Ranking by deployments times effort drives the roadmap; numbers are illustrative.

notes: Productise only what repeated at least three times; earlier is guessing.
Field engineers adopt what saves them time, not what is mandated.
Keep an escape hatch so urgent customer needs are not blocked by product release cycles.

title: Review Standard for Fintech Engineers
description: Automate review standards for 150 engineers so customer fixes ship faster without losing quality.
overview: Automate review standards for 150 engineers so customer fixes ship faster without losing quality.
tasks: Write a review standard of under 3 pages: what reviewers must check (correctness, tests, security, operability), what is out of scope (style handled by tools), approval rules and SLAs of first response within 4 working hours.
Automate mechanical review: formatters, linters, type checks, secret scan and dependency checks as required status checks; PRs reach human review only when green.
Build a CODEOWNERS audit that finds directories without owners and orphaned owners, and fix the top 50.
Create a bot that sizes PRs, requests reviewers by load and expertise, and nudges at 75 percent of the SLA.
Introduce a PR template with risk level, rollout plan and test evidence; measure completion rate above 90 percent.
Measure with data from the Git host API: time to first review, time to merge, PR size, review rounds and post-merge defects; publish a weekly dashboard by team without ranking individuals.
Run a 12 week experiment on 5 teams versus 5 comparison teams and report the change with a confidence interval.
Run calibration sessions: 20 people independently review 3 seeded PRs and compare findings; update the standard from disagreements.

examples.title: Latency query
examples.code:
select team,
 percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by first_review_at - opened_at) as p50,
 percentile_cont(0.9) within group (order by first_review_at - opened_at) as p90
from prs where opened_at > now() - interval '28 days' group by team;
examples.output:
team   p50       p90
pay    03:12:00  19:40:00
...   one row per team; target p50 under 4h

notes: Metrics used to rank people get gamed; report team aggregates only.
Small PRs fix latency more than any bot does.
Automate whatever a tool can check so humans spend time on design and risk.

title: Security Review Programme for Payments
description: Catch payment vulnerabilities in review so customers' data is protected.
overview: Catch payment vulnerabilities in review so customers' data is protected.
tasks: Analyse the last 40 vulnerabilities (CVEs, pen test findings, incidents) and map each to a root cause class and why review missed it.
Write a checklist per area (authn and authz, input handling, deserialisation, SSRF, secrets, crypto, multi-tenant isolation) with a bad and good example each.
Add SAST (Semgrep or CodeQL) with custom rules for your top 5 recurring classes; target under 10 percent false positives on triage of 100 findings.
Define triggers for mandatory security review: changes under auth paths, new endpoints, dependency additions, IaC network changes; enforce via CODEOWNERS and labels.
Seed 12 vulnerabilities in a test repo in 4 PRs; measure detection by 15 reviewers before and after training, targeting an increase from about 30 percent to over 70 percent.
Create a champions network of 1 per team, trained for 4 hours, with a monthly review clinic.
Track SLAs: critical findings fixed within 7 days; report escape rate (vulns found after merge) quarterly.
Publish 5 short case write-ups with the vulnerable diff and the fix.

examples.title: Custom Semgrep rule
examples.code:
rules:
- id: tenant-filter-missing
  languages: [python]
  severity: ERROR
  message: Query on Order without tenant_id filter
  pattern: Order.objects.filter(...)
  pattern-not: Order.objects.filter(..., tenant_id=..., ...)
examples.output: semgrep --config rules/ app/ reports the file and line of each unscoped query; CI exits 1.

notes: Reviewers find what they were primed to look for; seeded exercises show gaps.
Too many findings train people to ignore the tool; tune before enforcing.
Authorisation bugs are logic, not syntax; they need human review with context.

title: Reviewer Mentoring for Payments
description: Train 30 reviewers so payment code reviews catch real customer risks.
overview: Train 30 reviewers so payment code reviews catch real customer risks.
tasks: Define a review quality rubric (found defects, clarity, actionable suggestions, tone, proportionality) scored 1 to 4, with anchored examples.
Sample 150 merged PRs across teams, score them with two independent raters and report agreement (kappa at least 0.6).
Identify patterns: rubber stamps (approval within 2 minutes on over 300 lines), style-only reviews, and missed defect classes via post-merge bugs.
Run a 3 session workshop for 30 reviewers using real anonymised diffs, practising comment types (blocking, suggestion, question, praise).
Pair each reviewer with a mentor for 4 PRs and give feedback on their comments.
Write a guide on feedback language with 20 before and after rewrites of poor comments.
Re-audit 100 PRs 8 weeks later and report rubric improvement and defect escape trend.
Collect author sentiment in a short survey (n over 80) and report change.

examples.title: Comment rewrite
examples.code:
before: This is wrong, why would you do it like this?
after: [blocking] This loop reloads the user per item (N+1). Could we batch with get_many(ids)? Benchmark on 1k items: 4.1s now.
examples.output: Rewrite names severity, the problem, evidence and a proposed fix.

notes: Calibrate on real diffs, not slides.
Praise accurately; it signals what good looks like.
Time-box review to about 60 minutes and 400 lines; quality drops sharply beyond that.

title: Zero-Downtime Core Banking Migration
description: Migrate a critical banking system with phased cutover so customers never lose access.
overview: Migrate a critical banking system with phased cutover so customers never lose access.
tasks: Inventory dependencies and consumers (API callers, batch jobs, reports, direct DB readers) and classify each by cutover method.
Choose the pattern with written justification: strangler façade, dual writes versus change data capture (Debezium) with an outbox, and why.
Backfill history with idempotent, resumable jobs and throttle them to under 20 percent database load.
Run shadow reads comparing old and new responses on 100 percent of traffic; require a mismatch rate under 0.01 percent before cutover, with every mismatch class explained.
Cut over by tenant cohorts (1 percent, 10 percent, 50 percent, 100 percent) using feature flags, with automatic rollback if error rate rises 0.5 points or P99 latency doubles.
Rehearse rollback in production-like environment and time it; target under 10 minutes and no data loss, with reverse replication where needed.
Define SLOs and an error budget for the migration window and publish a go or no-go checklist.
Decommission the legacy system after a 30 day stable period, archive data to meet retention rules, and write a retrospective with measured outcome.

examples.title: Shadow comparison report
examples.code:
window 24h  requests 129,443,200
mismatch total 3,812 (0.0029%)
  ordering of items  2,901 (benign, normalised)
  rounding on tax      611 (bug, fixed in 1.8.3)
  missing discount     300 (open)
gate: need <0.01% and 0 open data-loss classes
examples.output: Cutover is blocked while 'missing discount' is open.

notes: Dual writes without an outbox cause silent divergence; prefer CDC.
Rollback must be designed before cutover and rehearsed.
Reports and batch jobs hiding in the legacy database are the usual surprise.

title: Architecture Board for a Bank
description: Set up architecture governance so 30 teams build banking systems safely.
overview: Set up architecture governance so 30 teams build banking systems safely.
tasks: Define decision scopes: what teams decide alone, what needs advice, what needs board approval (cross-team contracts, data stores, new languages), documented on one page.
Introduce an ADR template with context, options, decision, consequences and revisit date; seed with 15 historical decisions to create a searchable log.
Run the advice process with a 5 working day SLA; review time and outcomes tracked.
Publish a technology radar (adopt, trial, assess, hold) with 40 entries and owners, reviewed quarterly.
Write 6 architectural fitness functions (for example no cyclic dependencies between domains, API breaking-change check with oasdiff, P95 latency budget) and run them in CI.
Create reference architectures for 3 common cases (CRUD service, event consumer, public API) with working templates.
Measure outcomes: number of unreviewed cross-team breaking changes, time to decision, team satisfaction survey, and count of platform variants reduced.
Sunset the process parts that do not add value after two quarters and document why.

examples.title: Breaking change fitness function
examples.code: oasdiff breaking origin/main:api/openapi.yaml api/openapi.yaml --fail-on ERR
examples.output:
1 changes: 1 error, 0 warning
error [response-required-property-removed] DELETE /orders/{id} response property 'status' removed
exit code 1

notes: Boards that block become bypassed; offer advice with a fast SLA.
Record the reasons, not only the decision, so they can be challenged later.
Fitness functions enforce what documents merely request.

title: Resilience Architecture for Payments
description: Design a payments system to survive 10x growth and a regional failure so customers can always pay.
overview: Design a payments system to survive 10x growth and a regional failure so customers can always pay.
tasks: Define SLIs and SLOs for 4 critical journeys (for example checkout availability 99.95 percent, P99 under 800 ms) and error budget policy.
Build a capacity model: per-component cost per request, saturation points and a forecast at 1x, 5x and 10x load with headroom of 30 percent.
Run load tests in a production-like environment up to 3x peak using k6 or Gatling; record the first bottleneck and fix the top 3.
Eliminate single points of failure: multi-AZ data layer, stateless services, queue-based load levelling and backpressure; show a dependency map with failure modes.
Add timeouts, retries with budgets, circuit breakers and bulkheads; test that a slow dependency does not exhaust threads.
Run chaos experiments (kill zone, inject 2 second latency, drop a dependency) with hypotheses and abort criteria; document at least 3 weaknesses found and fixed.
Do a regional failover drill with measured RTO under 15 minutes and RPO under 1 minute.
Produce an architecture review document for leadership with cost per 1,000 requests at each scale.

examples.title: k6 threshold
examples.output: k6 exits non-zero if thresholds fail; the summary lists p(99) and failure rate per scenario (values vary).

notes: Test failure modes, not only load; retry storms cause most cascading outages.
Capacity models are wrong until validated; re-run after each architecture change.
Every control you add (retry, cache) is a new failure mode; justify it.

title: Professional Cloud Architect Credential
description: Pass a professional cloud architect exam so you can design secure systems for banks.
overview: Pass a professional cloud architect exam so you can design secure systems for banks.
tasks: Pick the credential and map its official exam guide domains and weights into a tracker with a self-rated confidence score per objective.
Take a diagnostic practice exam under real timing (about 180 minutes) and record weak domains; set a target of 85 percent on three consecutive fresh practice exams.

Build 6 reference designs from real scenarios (multi-account landing zone, hybrid connectivity, DR with RTO under 1 hour, large-scale migration, event-driven analytics, cost-optimised data lake), each with a diagram and trade-off table.
Implement at least 4 of them as infrastructure code (Terraform) in a sandbox account, with cost tracked below a stated budget and everything destroyed after.
Keep an error log: for every missed practice question write why the right answer is right and why the others fail.
Study 40 official white papers, the Well-Architected or Architecture Framework pillars, and the service limits and pricing models.
Sit the exam on schedule, then write a debrief of domain scores and what you would change.
Apply the credential: run a Well-Architected style review on a real workload and present 5 prioritised findings.

examples.title: Objective tracker row
examples.code:
domain,weight,objective,confidence_1to5,evidence
Design for org complexity,26%,SCP and multi-account guardrails,4,lab: landing-zone repo
Continuous improvement,25%,Cost allocation tags and rightsizing,3,lab: cost-report
examples.output: Every objective at 4 or above with a linked lab or notes before the exam date.

notes: Professional exams test choosing the best of several workable answers; practise elimination on constraints (cost, latency, operations).
Labs beat video courses for retention; keep them small and destroy resources.
Schedule the date early to create pressure.

title: Architect Certification Cohort
description: Run a cohort that helps architects earn credentials for building safer financial systems.
overview: Run a cohort that helps architects earn credentials for building safer financial systems.
tasks: Choose the target exam(s) and build a 10 week curriculum aligned to domain weights, with weekly learning objectives and a 2 hour live session.
Design 10 hands-on labs with grading scripts that check infrastructure state automatically, and an isolated sandbox with budget caps of 20 dollars per learner.
Write 200 original practice questions with explanations and reviewed distractors; validate difficulty on a pilot of 5 people.
Run diagnostic and mid-point exams to place learners in study tracks; hold weekly office hours.
Pair learners in study triads and run two mock exam days under real conditions.
Track metrics: attendance above 80 percent, practice score trend, first-attempt pass rate (target above 80 percent), and satisfaction survey.
Collect post-exam feedback on topics that surfaced unexpectedly and update the materials.
Package everything as a reusable repository with a facilitator guide so another lead can run the next cohort.

examples.title: Lab grader
examples.code:
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=service-name,Values=com.amazonaws.eu-west-1.s3 \
  --query 'length(VpcEndpoints)'
examples.output: 1   (grader marks 'S3 gateway endpoint present' as passed; 0 fails the check)

notes: Learners stall on logistics (accounts, cost); remove friction first.
Questions copied from dumps are unethical and violate exam agreements; write your own.
Pass rate is a lagging metric; weekly practice scores predict it.

title: Senior Project Management Credential
description: Earn a project management credential so fintech programmes reach customers on time.
overview: Earn a project management credential so fintech programmes reach customers on time.
tasks: Verify eligibility (for PMP, 36 months leading projects within the last 8 years plus 35 contact hours) and log projects with dates, hours and outcomes in the application format.
Map the exam content outline (people, process, business environment) to a study plan of 8 to 10 weeks with weekly hours.
Complete 35 or more hours of accredited training and keep the certificate.
Take 5 full-length mock exams (180 questions) timed, with a target of at least 75 percent, and review every miss in an error log.
Apply 6 techniques to your live project: stakeholder register and engagement plan, risk register with quantified exposure, earned value reporting (CPI, SPI), change control and hybrid planning.
Write one case study comparing predictive and agile choices on your project and the rationale.
Pass the exam and record domain-level results; plan 60 PDUs over 3 years for renewal.
Present a lessons-learned session to colleagues and mentor one person toward certification.

examples.title: Earned value check
examples.code:
BAC 500000  PV 200000  EV 180000  AC 210000
CPI = EV/AC = 0.86   SPI = EV/PV = 0.90
EAC = BAC/CPI = 581395
examples.output: Project is over cost and behind schedule; EAC is about 581k, so an action plan is needed.

notes: Application audits happen; keep evidence for every claimed hour.
Situational questions reward the PMI mindset (engage stakeholders, follow process), not what your employer does.
Hybrid and agile questions are around half the exam, so study them seriously.

title: Leadership Credential Path for Fintech
description: Create a credential roadmap for a 60-person fintech department that serves customers.
overview: Create a credential roadmap for a 60-person fintech department that serves customers.
tasks: Assess current capability with a skills matrix across 60 people and 8 roles (scrum master, product owner, delivery manager, change lead).
Map each role to a path (for example PSM I then PSPO I, ITIL 4 Foundation, Prosci, PMP for programme leads) with prerequisites and sequence.
Build a business case: total cost (exam fees, training, time) of about 45,000 dollars against expected benefits such as lower contractor spend and shorter lead times, with payback under 18 months.
Define leading and lagging indicators: certified percentage, cycle time, predictability of sprint delivery, change failure rate and incident MTTR.
Create support: study groups, paid exam time of 16 hours, a pass-bonus policy and a retake rule.
Run a pilot with 12 people for one quarter and compare to a similar group.
Review impact at 6 months and decide to extend, change or stop each credential, documenting the evidence.
Ensure practical application: each certified person leads a related improvement initiative with a sponsor.

examples.title: Business case summary
examples.code:
cost: fees 14k + training 21k + time 10k = 45k
benefit year 1: contractor reduction 38k + fewer escalations 12k = 50k
Payback 10.8 months; risk: attrition after certification
examples.output: Illustrative structure; use your own numbers and state assumptions.

notes: Certifications without applied projects change CVs, not outcomes.
Retention risk is real; pair with progression and recognition.
Choose frameworks that match how your teams work, not a trending badge.
